articles.title: OPXrayNet: a high-precision, explainable AI framework for transformative opportunistic osteoporosis screening utilizing multi-site X-ray imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate OPXrayNet, an automated deep-learning framework for opportunistic osteoporosis (OP) screening using multi-site skeletal X-ray images, to address the limitations of single-site analysis and poor interpretability in existing methods. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter diagnostic study utilized 16,347 annotated X-ray images from 2186 patients. The reference standard was OP diagnosis based on DXA T-score (≤ -2.5). OPXrayNet integrated YOLOv8 for automated region-of-interest detection, a spatial-frequency joint focusing architecture for feature enhancement, a feature pyramid network for multi-scale fusion, and an expert-guided loss module. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated using accuracy and AUC, comparing performance against models including DeepSeek-VL2 and DCNN via statistical tests on internal and external validation sets. RESULTS: The study included 2186 participants (mean age 69.0 ± 10.5 years; 72.3% female). On the internal test set (n = 3892), OPXrayNet achieved an accuracy of 80.1%; observed accuracy values for baseline models were lower. On the external validation set, it attained an AUC of 0.844 (95% CI: 0.821-0.867); a numerical difference of 3.9% was observed when compared with other models. Feature heatmaps suggest that the model focuses on clinically critical bone structures. CONCLUSION: OPXrayNet effectively provides accurate, automated, and interpretable opportunistic OP screening from multi-site X-ray images, showing promising performance for scalable clinical application in primary care settings. KEY POINTS: Question There is a notable absence of automated, interpretable, and highly accurate deep learning methodologies for conducting opportunistic OP screening using multi-site X-ray images. Findings The OPXrayNet model achieved an accuracy of 80.1% and an AUC of 0.844 in automated OP screening across multi-site X-rays in internal and external validation cohorts; numerical differences in performance metrics were observed when compared with baseline models. Clinical relevance This framework offers an accurate, automated, and interpretable screening tool for OP using routine X-rays, presenting substantial potential for scalable clinical application in primary care. It enables early detection without incurring additional costs or radiation exposure.

articles.title: Spatial topology on baseline PET/CT improves risk stratification in disseminated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether spatial topology features (STFs) from baseline 18 F-FDG PET/CT provide prognostic value beyond conventional burden and dissemination metrics in disseminated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). METHODS: This multicenter study included 243 patients (training, n = 161; validation, n = 82) with de novo DLBCL (≥ 4 lesions). An AI-assisted, human-in-the-loop pipeline was used to automatically detect lesions and construct 3D spatial networks. Six hierarchical models predicted 2-year progression-free survival, comparing a standard burden model (M3), a topology model (M4), and a fusion model (M5). Performance was assessed via AUC, Brier score, and calibration slope. Clinical utility was analyzed using Decision Curve Analysis (DCA), and biological correlations were tested against molecular subtypes. RESULTS: In the external validation cohort, the clinical baseline model (M0) showed limited efficacy (AUC 0.620). M4 showed similar discrimination to M3 (AUC 0.819 vs. 0.828; p = 0.68), but better specificity (76.4% vs. 67.3%). Integrating topological architecture with volumetric metrics, the fusion model (M5) significantly outperformed M3 (AUC 0.871; p = 0.032) and improved calibration (slope 0.96 vs. 0.65), providing more reliable probability estimates than purely volume-based predictions. A high LCI correlated with the non-GCB subtype (p < 0.001) and double-expressor status (p = 0.017). CONCLUSION: In disseminated DLBCL, spatial topology features function as macroscopic imaging phenotypes that capture internal tumor architecture distinct from absolute volumetric burden. Integrating this spatial dimension improved non-invasive risk stratification, while high LCI correlated with aggressive molecular phenotypes. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Tumor microenvironment remodeling following hepatic artery embolotherapy.
articles.abstract: Hepatic artery embolotherapy (HAE), which includes transarterial embolization and transarterial chemoembolization, is a standard locoregional therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Beyond inducing ischemic tumor necrosis, HAE profoundly remodels the tumor microenvironment (TME). This review presents current evidence related to HAE-induced TME remodeling and its therapeutic implications.HAE induces a complex network of interconnected hypoxic, nutrient stress, immune, and tissue repair responses, leading to dynamic remodeling of the TME. Hypoxia activates hypoxia-inducible factor-dependent pathways, thereby promoting angiogenesis, metabolic reprogramming, and treatment resistance. Nutrient deprivation induces autophagy, enabling tumor cell survival. Also, HAE exerts dual immunologic effects by stimulating antitumor immunity through tumor antigen release while simultaneously promoting immunosuppressive mechanisms including programmed death-ligand 1 upregulation, accumulation of immunosuppressive macrophages and neutrophils, and reduced cytotoxic T-cell infiltration. Furthermore, tissue repair responses activate hepatic stellate cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts, leading to extracellular matrix deposition, desmoplastic remodeling, and immune exclusion. Emerging preclinical results of several studies suggest that targeting these TME remodeling might enhance the efficacy of HAE.Understanding the dynamic biological responses following HAE might facilitate development of next-generation embolization strategies and rational combination therapies for HCC.

articles.title: Carotid near-occlusion pathophysiology: A narrative review and expanded cerebrovascular theory.
articles.abstract: The purposes of this review are to summarize the pathophysiology of carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and formulate how known hemodynamic theory can be expanded to specifically address CNO. A systematic search revealed 51 articles addressing CNO pathophysiology. ICA flow reduction and collateral pathway activation are hallmarks of CNO. While CNO is associated with a high prevalence of reduced cerebrovascular reserve (CVR), severely impaired CVR was uncommon. Hence, hypoperfusion stroke mechanism is uncommon. Embolic mechanism studies are few and with mixed results. In hemodynamic theory variant, we propose that good collateral capacity results in CNO early during stenosis severity progression and no hemodynamic stroke/TIA. Conversely, we propose that poor collateral capacity results in more severe stenosis for CNO to develop and hemodynamic stroke/TIA will occur when the stenosis is sufficiently severe. This suggested theory predicts that a mismatch between too little distal collapse given a certain stenosis severity might indicate hypoperfusion. In conclusion, CNOs are flow-reducing stenoses associated with collateral use and unclear stroke mechanism. We propose an expansion of known hemodynamic theory to specifically address CNO where collateral capacity is the key factor that determines what stenosis severity is required for CNO to form and for hypoperfusion occur (if it occurs at all).

articles.title: Navigating treatment for De novo oligometastatic breast cancer: The Assisi think tank meeting.
articles.abstract: The 2026 Assisi Think Tank Meeting, in collaboration with EUSOMA, ESTRO, and AIRO, identified de novo oligometastatic breast cancer (dnOMBC) as a clinically relevant challenge. A comprehensive review of 39 publications highlights a significant heterogeneity in locoregional treatment strategies, including varying approaches to surgical and radiation oncology management for both the primary tumour as for the metastases. The overall level of evidence is low, with only one trial, MF07-01, demonstrating a clear benefit in terms of overall survival. Therefore, we recommend applying the Advanced Breast Cancer (ABC) guidelines, considering locoregional interventions after a 3-8 months induction of systemic therapy to facilitate identification of patients with better outcomes. On longer term perspective, our findings emphasise the need for obtaining more results from ongoing and future prospective clinical trials to define the optimal role of local therapies, including surgery and radiation therapy, in improving patient outcomes. For this, we encourage a proper application of biologically driven paradigms, using advanced imaging and biomarker monitoring to better identify true oligometastatic disease, as well as to optimise outcomes by combining locoregional treatments with immunotherapy.
authors: Assisi Think Tank Meeting ATTM investigators

articles.title: Beyond the target vessel: CT pitfalls in acute chest pain.
articles.abstract: Acute chest pain computed tomography can succeed technically yet fail clinically when interpretation stops at the requested vascular territory, enhancement is inadequate, or disease evolves after a negative examination. This pictorial essay illustrates target-vessel tunnel vision, partial diagnostic success mistaken for complete exclusion, and false reassurance after an initial study. The cases emphasize review of all acquired structures, scanner-specific protocol selection, and recognition of limitations imposed by coverage, contrast timing, and cardiac phase. Wider cardiac acquisition windows and delayed myocardial imaging should be selected to answer a specific unresolved question while limiting radiation and avoiding treatment delay. Reports should identify the likely cause of symptoms, distinguish diagnostic from nondiagnostic territories, and link unresolved findings to an appropriate next step.

articles.title: Renal Multiparametric MRI for Early Detection and Longitudinal Monitoring of Metabolic Dysfunction Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Associated Kidney Injury: Histopathologic Validation and Multi-Omics Profiling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Kidney injury during metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) progression remains incompletely characterized. PURPOSE: To assess multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) for early detection and monitoring of MASLD-associated kidney injury. STUDY TYPE: Animal model. ANIMAL MODEL: Fifty male Sprague Dawley rats received high-fat diet plus very low-dose carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) underwent mpMRI before sacrifice at 0, 2, 4, 8, or 12 weeks (n = 10/time point). Ten MASLD and ten normal rats underwent serial MRI at each time point; ten CCl4-only rats served as nephrotoxicity controls. Twelve additional healthy rats underwent a scan-rescan test. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T; turbo spin-echo T2-weighted imaging, variable flip angle (VFA) gradient-echo T1 mapping, multi-echo gradient-echo blood oxygen level-dependent imaging, pulsed arterial spin labeling, echo-planar diffusion kurtosis imaging, and multi-echo Dixon imaging. ASSESSMENT: Two radiologists (5 and 13 years of experience) quantified T1, T2*, proton density fat fraction (PDFF), mean diffusivity, mean kurtosis (MK), and renal blood flow (RBF) in cortex, outer/inner stripes of outer medulla (OSOM/ISOM). Early injury was defined as a tubular injury score ≥ 2. Histopathology, immunohistochemistry, transcriptomics, and serum metabolomics were performed. STATISTICAL TESTS: Repeated-measures ANOVA; intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). p < 0.05 indicated significance. RESULTS: Scan-rescan ICCs were 0.682-0.876. OSOM MK/PDFF significantly increased by Week 2 [MK (×10-3): 0.532 ± 0.007 to 0.574 ± 0.004; PDFF (%): 2.489 ± 0.243 to 3.600 ± 0.347]; cortical RBF and OSOM T2* showed no significant changes at Week 2 (p = 0.786, 1.000) but significantly decreased from Week 4. OSOM MK/PDFF had AUCs of 0.952 and 0.905 for early renal injury. Multi-omics revealed inflammatory and lipid/bile acid alterations. Dodecanedioic/hippuric acids potentially linked MASLD severity to OSOM MK. DATA CONCLUSION: Renal mpMRI detected early kidney injury during MASLD progression. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

articles.title: Biophysical characterization of a helium beam: In-field and out-of-field microdosimetry and RBE.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Helium shows great promise in radiotherapy due to improved dose conformality and higher biological effectiveness compared to protons, but limited data on its physical and biological properties hinder its clinical potential. PURPOSE: This study aims to characterize the microdosimetric distributions of 160 MeV/u helium ions in-field and out-of-field, benchmark the measurements against Monte Carlo simulations, and investigate how the measured radiation quality propagates into radiobiological predictions from mathematical models. METHODS: Microdosimetric measurements were performed using a Tissue Equivalent Proportional Counter (TEPC) in a water phantom at various depths along the beam direction and lateral positions. The experimental data were compared with OpenTOPAS Monte Carlo simulations. The measured microdosimetric spectra and derived microdosimetric quantities were then used as physical input for two microdosimetry-based radiobiological models, the modified Microdosimetric Kinetic Model (mMKM) and the Generalized Stochastic Microdosimetric Model (GSM2), to calculate the Relative Biological Effectiveness (RBE) at each measured location. RESULTS: The microdosimetric characterization revealed increasing radiation quality parameters  y ¯ F  ,  y ¯ D  and y ∗  along the in-field direction up to the Bragg peak, followed by a decrease in the distal region. The values of  y ¯ F  range from 2.43 ± 0.19 keV/µm at 50 mm depth to 21.8 ± 1.1 keV/µm at the Bragg peak, and decreasing to 2.39 ± 0.12 keV/µm at 250 mm depth. All microdosimetric parameters declined with depth at the field-edge, while remaining approximately constant close and far out-of-field. OpenTOPAS reproduced the measured spectra with primary helium ions contributing predominantly to the higher-y region and secondary protons to the lower-y region. Although mMKM and GSM2 predicted similar trends, the RBE(0.1) values differed, with the largest variations of up to 37% relative to the mMKM occurring in the distal in-field region. The lack of corresponding in vitro measurements prevents validation of the model predictions and assessment of their accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first comprehensive experimental microdosimetric characterization of a helium beam at clinically relevant energy across in-field and out-of-field regions. The observed discrepancies with Monte Carlo simulations highlight the need for improved characterization and modeling of secondary-particle production in helium beams. The RBE calculations further illustrate how differences in the physical description and interpretation of heterogeneous radiation fields propagate into biological predictions from different models. Dedicated radiobiological measurements under these irradiation conditions are needed to validate these predictions.

articles.title: Biological target volume and tumor spread map: A combined approach for advanced radiotherapy targeting in glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) radiotherapy planning typically applies fixed margins from the Gross Tumor Volume (GTV) to define the Clinical Target Volume (CTV) and Planning Target Volume (PTV). This standardized approach ignores patient-specific patterns of microscopic tumor spread and biological abnormalities, risking under-treatment of infiltrated tissue and unnecessary exposure of healthy brain regions. PURPOSE: To address this limitation, we extended our novel Tumor Spread (TS) mapping approach, which models microscopic infiltration along white matter tracts to generate personalized CTVs, by incorporating a Biological Target Volume (BTV), derived from advanced diffusion and perfusion MRI, into the model. We then compared three radiation treatment planning strategies: (1) GTV with standard fixed-margin CTV and PTV, (2) GTV with a personalized CTV (pCTVG) and PTV (PTVG), and (3) BTV with a personalized CTV (pCTVB) and PTV (PTVB). Each was evaluated for feasibility of dose coverage, healthy tissue sparing, and recurrence overlap. METHODS: MRI data from 10 newly diagnosed GBM patients were used. BTVs were contoured using Fractional Anisotropy (FA), Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC), and relative cerebral blood volume (rCBV) maps. TS maps were generated from both GTV and BTV. Virtual volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) treatment plans were created for all three strategies. We compared target volumes, organ-at-risk (OAR) doses, and spatial overlap with recurrence regions identified in follow-up imaging. RESULTS: Both pCTVG and pCTVB were consistently smaller than the standard CTV, offering reduced irradiated volume while preserving tumor coverage. The pCTVG and pCTVB spared 59% and 49% of the standard CTV margin volume, respectively. All virtual plans met clinical conformality thresholds, and mean doses to organs at risk (OARs) were lower with both personalized strategies. At follow-up, 98% of the volume of recurrent tumor was included in the standard PTV, 95% in PTVG, and 97% in PTVB. Dose coverage of ≥80% was achieved in 99% of the recurrence volume with standard PTV, and in 98% with both PTVG and PTVB. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated the clinical feasibility and potential dosimetric benefits of MRI-derived, biology-informed personalized target volumes for radiotherapy planning of glioblastoma patients. Among the virtual personalized strategies, the approach combining the Biological Target Volume (BTV) with Tumor Spread (TS) mapping showed reduced irradiated target volume, while improving healthy tissue sparing and spatial recurrence coverage. These findings support a shift toward individualized, biology-driven radiation planning that moves beyond the traditional GTV/CTV model.

articles.title: Evolution of bubble dynamics in viscoelastic tissue during boiling histotripsy: A numerical and ex vivo experimental study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The viscoelastic properties of soft tissue and liquefied debris can influence bubble dynamics during boiling histotripsy (BH), while quantitative assessment of cavitation evolution is desirable for treatment monitoring. PURPOSE: To investigate the effects of tissue viscoelasticity and liquefaction progression on cavitation dynamics during BH and to evaluate inertial cavitation dose (ICD) as a quantitative indicator of tissue fractionation. METHODS: A modified Keller-Miksis equation coupled with a linear Voigt model was used to simulate a gas bubble within a liquid-filled cavity surrounded by viscoelastic tissue while varying acoustic power and cavity radius. Passive cavitation detection (PCD) was performed in ex vivo bovine liver (n = 20) and human breast fibroadenoma (BFA) treatment groups (n = 18). Lesion area and ICD were quantified in bovine liver, whereas B-mode sonography and histology were used to assess BFA tissue changes. Longitudinal bovine-liver data were analyzed using repeated-measures one-way ANOVA with Geisser-Greenhouse correction and prespecified paired comparisons with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment. Paired t-tests or Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank tests were used as appropriate. Effect sizes were reported as partial eta squared (  η p 2  ), Cohen's d z  , or rank-biserial correlation ( r r b   ). Spearman's rank correlation was used to assess the association between lesion area and ICD. RESULTS: Numerical simulations demonstrated that radial stress induced by bubble oscillation at the liquid-tissue interface contributes to mechanical disintegration, with interfacial stresses gradually decreasing as tissue liquefaction progresses. The PCD monitoring approach enables determination of the onset and evolution of bubble cavitation characteristics. In ex vivo bovine liver, treatment cycle had significant overall effects on lesion area [F (2.805, 53.29) = 68.42, P < 0.0001,  η p 2   = 0.783] and ICD [F (2.044, 38.84) = 109.6, P < 0.0001,  η p 2   = 0.852]. Prespecified paired comparisons showed significant increases in lesion area during Phases I ( d z  = 1.37, adjusted P < 0.0001), Phase II ( d z   = 1.50, adjusted P < 0.0001), and Phase IV ( d z   = 0.84, adjusted P = 0.0028), whereas little change was observed during Phase III ( d z    = 0.10, adjusted P = 0.6534). ICD increased significantly across all four phase boundaries, with r r b    = 1.00 during Phase I and d z   = 1.15, 0.57, and 1.55 during Phases II, III, and IV, respectively (all adjusted P  ≤  0.0190). Lesion area was strongly associated with ICD (Spearman's ρ  = 0.897, P < 0.001; power-law fit R2  = 0.82954, P < 0.001). In ex vivo BFA specimens, increasing cycle number was accompanied by stronger broadband emissions, increased ICD, expansion of hypoechoic regions, and progressive histological disruption. No histological evidence of thermal coagulation was observed in the evaluated sections. CONCLUSIONS: Liquid-cavity expansion reduced simulated interfacial stress, while PCD-derived ICD was strongly associated with lesion area in bovine liver. In BFA specimens, increasing exposure produced acoustic, sonographic, and histological evidence of progressive mechanical disruption. These findings support ICD as a potential quantitative metric for monitoring BH-induced tissue liquefaction.

articles.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391). CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

articles.title: Clinical and Venographic Distinctions Between Extrinsic and Intrinsic Dural Venous Sinus Stenosis: Implications for Venous Stenting.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dural venous sinus stenosis (VSS) is associated with intracranial hypertension and may be treated with venous sinus stenting. VSS can be either extrinsic (extramural compression related to elevated ICP) or intrinsic (narrowing typically due to arachnoid granulations), with potentially important clinical distinctions and implications for venous stenting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients evaluated with catheter venography for suspected VSS and/or cerebral venous outflow disorders from October 2021 to March 2026. Patients were categorized as having intrinsic or extrinsic venous stenosis. Clinical distinctions between groups were investigated. RESULTS: Among 162 patients (mean age, 40.2 years; 96% female), 108 (67%) had extrinsic and 54 (33%) had intrinsic stenosis. Patients with extrinsic stenosis were younger (35.6 vs. 49.5 years; P<0.0001), had higher BMI (38.1 vs. 34.8 kg/m2; P=0.018), and higher opening pressure (36.0 vs. 29.3 cmH2O; P=0.006). Extrinsic stenosis was associated with higher torcula pressure (30.1 vs. 25.7 mmHg; P=0.03), higher trans-stenotic pressure gradient (15.8 vs. 11.9 mmHg; P=0.02), and more frequent occipital emissary venous drainage (62% vs. 44%; P=0.03). Ninety patients (56%) underwent stenting. Pulsatile tinnitus clinically resolved in 20/22 patients (91%) with intrinsic stenosis versus 29/43 (67%) with extrinsic stenosis (Fisher exact P=0.065, Pearson χ2 P=0.038). Symptomatic stent-adjacent stenosis occurred in 7/58 (12%) of stented extrinsic patients and 0/32 (0%) stented intrinsic patients and was significantly different (Fisher exact P=0.048, Pearson χ2=0.041). Other stenting outcomes did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Extrinsic and intrinsic VSS have distinct clinical and venographic profiles and may have different outcomes following venous stenting, suggesting they could represent related but distinct venous outflow disorders. Further research may optimize venous stenting patient selection and inform clinical trial design.

articles.title: Sim&Size versus IFU-Based Sizing for the Artisse 2.0 Intrasaccular Device in a Multicenter Registry.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Virtual simulation is increasingly promoted for intrasaccular device sizing, but whether it changes device selection or procedural outcomes for new, highly conformable devices is unknown. We compared Sim&Size simulation with instructions-for-use (IFU) chart sizing for the Artisse 2.0 in early multicenter experience. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from the INSPIRE-A registry (November 2022-June 2024). Sim&Size use depended on software availability. We assessed agreement between sizing tools, technical success, first-device success, adjunctive devices, procedure and fluoroscopy times, complications, and the cause of each technical failure. RESULTS: Sim&Size was used in 88/123 cases (71.5%). When both methods were used (n=59), the same device was selected in 54 (91.5%). Technical success was 98.9% with Sim&Size and 85.7% without (p=0.007), whereas first-device success (86.4% vs 80.0%, p=0.41) and procedure and fluoroscopy times did not differ. Perioperative complications occurred in 4/123 (3.3%). Of the six technical failures, five were related to device fit, mostly in anatomies at the limits of the device range, and one resulted from a perforation before deployment. A dome-to-neck ratio <1 was associated with failure (3/7 vs 3/116, p=0.002). CONCLUSIONS: For the Artisse 2.0, Sim&Size and chart-based sizing selected the same device in most cases. Sim&Size use was associated with higher technical success, whereas first-device success and procedure and fluoroscopy times were comparable. Both approaches achieved high procedural success with a low complication rate and may be used according to operator preference, with simulation potentially most useful in anatomies at the limits of the device range.

articles.title: Procedural Time Independently Predicts Functional Outcome After First-Pass Reperfusion in Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Modified first-pass effect (mFPE) is an established benchmark of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) success in large-vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke, yet its clinical benefit may be time sensitive. Prior studies indicate that procedural time (PT) exceeding 30 minutes carries higher complications rates and worse outcomes. We assessed whether procedural duration exerts a continuous, dose-dependent effect on clinical outcomes among patients achieving mFPE. METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective study analyzed patients who achieved mFPE after MT for acute ischemic stroke between February 2018 and March 2024. Primary outcomes were 30- and 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2). Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), and mortality. Multivariate logistic regression models evaluated associations between PT (modeled continuously and dichotomized by a 30-minute cut-off) and clinical outcomes. RESULTS: Among 417 patients achieving mFPE, 302 (72.4%) had PT ≤30 minutes. Shorter PT was independently associated with functional independence at 30 days (aOR 1.72, 95% CI 1.06-2.80; p=0.03) but not at 90 days (aOR 1.44, 95% CI 0.89-2.32; p=0.14). Modeled continuously within each time window, PT showed no significant association with functional independence, although ordinal analysis suggested worse mRS with longer PT only in the >30-minute group at 30 days (aOR 1.18; p=0.04). Median LOS was shorter for PT ≤30 minutes (6 (3-10) vs. 7 (4-13) days, p=0.01). sICH and mortality did not differ by PT. CONCLUSION: Among patients achieving mFPE, shorter PT remained independently associated with better functional outcomes at 30 days, but not at 90 days, with no significant gradient within either window, supporting the importance of procedural efficiency even after technically successful single-pass reperfusion.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Accelerated 3D T2 CUBE MRI of the Cochlea at 1.5T and 3T: Sonic DL With AIR Recon DL Versus AIR Recon DL Alone.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Three-dimensional fast spin-echo MR cisternography (CUBE) of the internal auditory canal (IAC) and cerebellopontine angle (CPA) requires longer acquisition times that can limit clinical throughput. We evaluated whether a deep learning (DL)-based highly accelerated reconstruction technique, Sonic DL`™ (SDL), combined with a commercially available DL denoising reconstruction (AIR™ Recon DL, ARDL), preserves or improves subjective image quality and cochlear anatomy visualization relative to standard CUBE-ARDL while shortening scan time. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Consecutive patients underwent brain MRI for suspected IAC pathology at 1.5T and 3T with paired acquisition of standard 3D CUBE-ARDL and an accelerated 3D CUBE-SDL sequence. Both used the same voxel size at 1.5T (0.6x0.6x1.2 mm3) and 3T (0.6x0.6x0.6 mm3). Scan times for CUBE-ARDL versus CUBE-SDL were 2:33 versus 1:41 min at 1.5T and 1:55 versus 1:11 min at 3T. Two independent neuroradiologists blinded to MRI acquisition method scored randomized, de-identified images on a 5-point Likert scale across five domains (overall image quality, noise, sharpness, artifacts, cochlear anatomy visualization). Reader-averaged scores for CUBE-ARDL and CUBE-SDL were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with reader-specific and cumulative link mixed model (CLMM) sensitivity analyses and false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment; intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) quantified inter-reader reliability for each technique; Gwet's AC2 and weighted (Conger's) kappa with linear ordinal weights quantified pooled inter-reader agreement. RESULTS: After exclusion of 5 training cases per field strength, 49 (1.5T) and 34 (3T) patients were analyzed. CUBE-SDL scored significantly better than CUBE-ARDL for all five domains at both field strengths (all FDR-adjusted P < .001), consistently for each reader and in the CLMM. Inter-reader reliability (ICC) for CUBE-SDL was moderate-to-excellent at 3T (0.63-0.92) and moderate at 1.5T (0.65-0.74), generally exceeding CUBE-ARDL (3T: 0.35-0.61; 1.5T: 0.50-0.71). Pooled inter-reader agreement (Gwet's AC2) ranged from 0.56 to 0.89. CONCLUSIONS: A combined Sonic DL acceleration with ARDL-denoised reconstruction for 3D T2 CUBE produced significantly higher subjective image quality at both 1.5T and 3T, and, at 3T, higher inter-reader reliability than standard CUBE-ARDL, while shortening acquisition time by 34%-38%. These findings support further evaluation, including diagnostic accuracy studies, of CUBE-SDL as an alternative to CUBE-ARDL.

articles.title: A detailed analysis of First pass Reperfusion and Number of Passes in MeVO Stroke Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Reperfusion success after EVT and the number of EVT passes may be associated with clinical and imaging outcomes in patients with acute stroke due to Medium Vessel Occlusion (MeVO). MATERIAL AND METHODS: Secondary analysis of patients randomized to EVT in the ESCAPE-MeVO trial. Final reperfusion was assessed with the MeVO-expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (MeVO-eTICI) Score. First pass near-complete reperfusion was defined as MeVO-eTICI 2c-3 after 1 pass and multi-pass near-complete reperfusion as MeVO-eTICI 2c-3 after >1 pass. The primary outcome was the modified Rankin Score (mRS) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included 24-hour NIHSS and 24-hour infarct volume, among others. Associations were assessed using regression models. RESULTS: Of 255 patients randomized to EVT (48.3%), 206 remained for the final analysis. First pass near-complete reperfusion was associated with decreased infarct volume (median 12.8ml [IQR 0.15-25.3] versus: 22.4ml [6.71-56.38ml], adjusted beta-coefficient -1.68 [95%CI::-2.54-(-0.81)]) and improved 24-hour NIHSS (median 7 [2-13.5] versus: 2.5 [1-6.5], adjusted beta-coefficient -0.56 [95%CI:-0.74-(-0.38)]), but not with clinical outcomes. Similarly, improved reperfusion status was associated with lower infarct volumes and improved 24-hour NIHSS but not with clinical outcomes. Number of EVT passes was associated with higher 90-day mRS (acOR 1.41 [95%CI: 1.04-1.91] per 1-additional pass), higher 24-hour NIHSS and larger infarct volume. CONCLUSIONS: Improved first-pass reperfusion with EVT in MeVO stroke patients was associated with reduced infarct volumes and improved 24-hour NIHSS. Performing more EVT passes was associated with increased infarct volume and poorer 24-hour and 90-day outcomes.

articles.title: Association Between Tissue No-Reflow and Prognosis After successful Recanalization in Endovascular Treatment of Intracranial Atherosclerotic Occlusion: A Post Hoc Subgroup Analysis of the ANGEL-REBOOT Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: No-reflow after successful endovascular treatment (EVT) predicts poor outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) due to intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS), but its optimal evaluation and prognostic value remain unclear. This study assessed computed tomography perfusion (CTP)-defined no-reflow for predicting outcomes in ICAS-related large vessel occlusion (ICAS-LVO). METHODS: This retrospective post hoc analysis included patients from the prospective ANGEL-REBOOT trial with anterior circulation ICAS-LVO, successful eTICI 2b/3 recanalization, and postoperative 24-hour CTP. No-reflow was defined as persistent hypoperfusion (Tmax >4s or >6s) after recanalization. Outcomes included 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score (poor outcome ≥3) and 24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score. RESULTS: In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, the optimal cohort derived cutoff value for Tmax > 4s hypoperfusion volume was 95.8 mL. Among 64 patients, Tmax >4s hypoperfusion volume ≥95.8 mL best predicted poor 90-day outcome (area under the curve [AUC] 0.75). Larger Tmax >4s volumes correlated with worse 90-day mRS scores (P=0.04) and higher 24-hour NIHSS scores (P=0.006). Tmax >6s (cutoff 9.9 mL, AUC 0.690) only predicted higher 24-hour NIHSS score (P=0.001) but not 90-day outcomes (P=0.12). CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative 24-hour CTP Tmax > 4 s hypoperfusion volume showed a trend toward better prediction of 90-day poor functional outcomes compared with Tmax > 6 s in recanalized ICAS-LVO patients.

articles.title: Impact of chemical depletion of club cells on the pulmonary response to irradiation in mice.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Radiation-induced acute pneumopathy and lung fibrosis are debilitating clinical conditions that may occur following radiation therapy to the chest area. As opposed to alveolar compartment, the response of the bronchiolic epithelium and its role in tissue damage have been only sparsely addressed. Club cells reside in the bronchiolic epithelium and sustain epithelial integrity and response to trauma. Our aim was to investigate the role of club cells in radiation-induced lung damage. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used two preclinical models of X-ray radiation lung damage in mice: a model of whole thorax irradiation to 20 Gy and an accurate model irradiating 4% of the mouse lung to 80 Gy. Naphthalene-induced depletion of club cells was induced prior to irradiation and tissue damage followed by microCT analyses, histology, immunohistology and single cell RNA sequencing 1 and 6 months post-exposure. RESULTS: Exposing the whole thorax in absence of club cells resulted in severe animal mortality compared to controls. In case of small volume exposure, tentative of epithelial regeneration is observed via stem cells mobilization in the severely injured area, most likely from the margins. In absence of club cells, possible stem cells' exhaustion in response to cell depletion compromised their mobilization from the margins and may be responsible for tissue damage extension. Analyses in single cell RNA sequencing revealed interesting features of lung response to focal irradiation with increased endothelial-to-mesenchymal profile, broncho-alveolar stem cells mobilization and early foamy macrophages involvement in NA-treated tissues. CONCLUSION: Our data suggest a delay in regeneration processes when the lung is irradiated in absence of club cells. This raises interest in studying these cells in future research on the response of the healthy lungs to radiation exposure. We also may point out that pre-existing clinical conditions associated with club cell loss might be at risk for developing radiotherapy-related side effects in patients treated for thoracic tumors.

articles.title: Choroid plexus remodeling in aging and cerebrovascular disease revealed by contrast-enhanced 7T MRI.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The choroid plexus is essential for brain homeostasis, yet its in vivo morphology remains incompletely characterized. Conventional MRI visualizes only part of the choroid plexus and may therefore misrepresent age- and disease-related structural changes. We aim to develop a 7T contrast-enhanced black-blood imaging (CeBBI) framework for whole-brain visualization and quantitative morphologic characterization of the choroid plexus, and to examine its associations with aging and cerebrovascular disease. METHODS: We retrospectively included 234 participants referred for evaluation of intracranial atherosclerotic disease who underwent CeBBI. A deep learning model was trained to segment the whole choroid plexus. Choroid plexus volume, centerline-based shape features and cystic components were quantified. Segmentations derived from CeBBI were compared with those obtained using a validated T1-weighted MRI-based method. Associations with age, ventricular size and vascular imaging markers were assessed. RESULTS: 7T CeBBI enabled visualization of the choroid plexus across all ventricular compartments. The segmentation model achieved high accuracy (Dice score=0.901±0.013), and recovered more than twice the choroid plexus volume detected by the T1-weighted method. Total choroid plexus volume was not associated with age. However, with advancing age, the lateral ventricular choroid plexus became shorter (left r=-0.250, right r=-0.303, both P<0.001) and showed greater cross-sectional area (left r=0.174, right r=0.176, both P=0.007). Choroid plexus cyst number (r=0.187, P=0.004) and cyst volume (r=0.159, P=0.015) also increased with age. Cerebral microbleeds were independently associated with greater lateral ventricular choroid plexus volume (standardized β=0.178, P=0.012). CONCLUSIONS: Our method enables robust whole-brain visualization and quantitative morphologic assessment of the choroid plexus. Rather than undergoing simple age-related hypertrophy, the choroid plexus showed complex remodeling characterized by shortening, cross-sectional expansion and cystic change. The association between cerebral microbleeds and larger choroid plexus volume further supports a potential role of vascular dysfunction in choroid plexus remodeling.

articles.title: EEG-based Deep Learning Reveals Cortical Sensitivity to Small Changes in Deep Brain Stimulation Parameters.
articles.abstract: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) is an invasive procedure used to alleviate motor symptoms in Parkinson's Disease (PD) patients. Despite its effectiveness, the impact of DBS on brain activity and the way to optimise stimulation parameters remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to map the sensitivity of cortical neural response to changes in DBS parameters in real-world clinical settings. We recorded in-clinic EEG data from PD patients during their clinical DBS programming sessions, both at rest and during arm movement. A siamese variant of the EEGNet deep learning architecture was trained independently for each patient and parameter combination to determine whether two 1-sec-long EEG segments were recorded under the same or different DBS parameters, yielding 30 independently trained models. Our models achieved an average accuracy of 74% in classifying whether two 1-second EEG segments corresponded to the same or different DBS parameters. Explainability methods were then applied to extract the neural oscillations learned by the models. Ablation studies identified mid-gamma oscillations (55-90Hz) as the key band for classifying these changes. Importantly, that was not driven by 1:2 gamma entrainment. In a sub-group of patients, the theta-alpha oscillations (4-12Hz) also contributed to detecting changes in DBS parameters. We demonstrate that small DBS parameter changes modify cortical activity in a consistent manner that can be detected using shallow convolutional networks on low-density EEG. Our findings suggest that cortical mid-gamma oscillations (55-90Hz) are highly sensitive to small changes in DBS settings. Our approach and findings could be leveraged towards identifying and defining novel digital biomarkers to guide DBS programming and adaptive DBS systems.

articles.title: Reproducibility Before Treatment Decision Rules: A Targeted Scoping Review of AI-Assisted Coronary Plaque Characterization.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) can quantify plaque, whose burden predicts myocardial infarction better than stenosis severity. We reviewed evidence for artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted plaque characterization. Methods: This targeted scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) used a non-exhaustive search, mainly of MEDLINE/PubMed (July 2026, supplemented in September). AI title selection (135 of 1415 titles) and author assessment of 141 records yielded 121 included records under the revised criteria. An AI re-screen of 1280 unselected records (blind second pass on 175) found 110 further eligible records after charting; two AI passes screened 3634 confirmatory records (κ 0.93). The corresponding author accepted AI recommendations after reviewing written assessments, not blind (for the 335 confirmatory records, in one instruction). Of the 543 eligible records, 236 were charted (121 + 110 + 4 + 1; full text for 121 of the 236, abstract alone for 115) and 307 mapped from abstracts only (not fully charted). Results: In symptomatic or referred patients, AI-derived plaque burden was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (a property of the measurement, not evidence that AI improves outcomes). In one comparison, AI modestly improved discrimination over manual quantification (AUC 0.82 vs. 0.78) without significant net reclassification improvement. No randomized trial of AI-based plaque analysis reporting clinical endpoints was identified in the sources searched and assessed; TRANSFORM (NCT06112418) is recruiting. Three small same-patient comparisons found systematic between-platform differences; no adequately powered comparison of major commercial platforms was identified. Abstract-level mapping of the 307 additional records identified no randomized outcome, observed decision-impact or photon-counting prognostic study. Conclusions: AI-derived plaque measures carry prognostic information in symptomatic patients, but randomized evidence that AI-guided treatment reduces myocardial infarction or cardiovascular death in asymptomatic adults, or does so better than coronary artery calcium (CAC)-guided prevention, has not been established in the sources searched and assessed. Under the modeled effects, demonstrating benefit in the lowest-burden stage would need an impractically large trial; as a design proposal, we outline a stage-enriched randomized trial. AI-assisted plaque characterization is best understood as a throughput and within-system repeatability technology; cross-platform portability is not demonstrated, and it is not a validated treatment decision rule.

articles.title: Beyond a Symptom: A Mechanism-Based Multidisciplinary Framework for the Diagnosis and Management of Chronic Cough.
articles.abstract: Chronic cough may persist despite appropriate treatment of associated conditions, creating uncertainty about the relevance of coexisting abnormalities and therapeutic priorities. This evidence-informed narrative review draws on searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science and relevant guidelines to propose a mechanism-based multidisciplinary framework for adults, particularly those with refractory or unexplained chronic cough. The nine-step pathway integrates established disease assessment, characterization of cough hypersensitivity and laryngeal involvement, provisional weighting of treatable traits and modifiable contributors, targeted multidisciplinary input, individualized intervention, and reassessment. Within this proposed framework, findings are considered dominant, contributory, incidental, or currently inactive according to converging clinical evidence; insufficiently evaluated findings remain uncertain. Treatment response is interpreted by distinguishing improvement in the targeted trait from improvement in cough. Discordant or inadequate responses prompt reassessment of treatment adequacy and mechanistic relevance. Patient-reported outcomes, objective cough monitoring when available, and trait-specific measures inform treatment evaluation and subsequent re-phenotyping. The weighting categories and integrated pathway represent the authors' conceptual synthesis and have not been prospectively validated. Their reproducibility, feasibility, clinical effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness require evaluation.

articles.title: An Evidence Map of Pupillary Assessment in a Preselected Acute-Care Literature Archive.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined clinical purpose and acquisition method in a preselected acute-care archive of unknown representativeness. Methods: We reconciled 871 historical records using numerical adult-age evidence. Historical dual-human review, investigator-adopted dispositions for 325 unresolved records, a separate 100-record human-verified audit, and source reconciliation were distinguished. Six mapping domains and a scenario adding 274 age-unverified reports were analyzed. Results: The archive contained 355 core reports, 15 noncore records, 497 eligibility exclusions, three unresolved sources and one duplicate. Acquisition remained unestablished in 237/355 reports (66.8%): 38 remained unresolved after targeted source reconciliation, and 199 were not sampled for that acquisition audit. Any automated component was documented in 17/39 cardiac-arrest reports (43.6%), 15/27 mixed neurological/trauma reports (55.6%), and 6/116 trauma reports (5.2%). Diagnostic/physiological questions predominated in ocular and toxicological reports; neurological prognosis predominated after cardiac arrest. Adding age-unverified reports increased trauma representation from 32.7% to 39.9%. Conclusions: Clinical questions and documented acquisition profiles differ within this archive, while the numerical-age rule changes case mix. Unestablished acquisition and unequal verification limit comparisons of documented assessment methods across clinical groups. These findings do not establish field-wide coverage, clinical adoption, or comparative effectiveness.

articles.title: Presbylarynx Revisited: A Multidimensional Approach to Laryngeal Aging and Clinical Decision-Making.
articles.abstract: Background: Presbylarynx describes the structural phenotype of an aging larynx, whereas presbyphonia refers to its clinically relevant perceptual and functional expression. Although vocal fold atrophy, bowing, and glottic insufficiency are common in older adults, their presence and severity do not consistently correspond to patient-reported voice impairments. Therefore, presbylaryngeal morphology should be interpreted within the broader context of compensatory capacity, physiological reserve, systemic health, and individual communication demands. Objective: This narrative review aims to provide a clinically oriented and multidimensional synthesis of presbylarynx, encompassing its terminology, morphological and functional characteristics, relationship with systemic aging, differential diagnosis, clinical assessment, management strategies, and emerging diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. Methods: A targeted literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted in August 2026, with additional targeted searches and citation checking during revision. Relevant systematic and narrative reviews, clinical practice guidelines, consensus statements, prospective and retrospective clinical studies, translational investigations, and landmark publications addressing the presbylarynx, presbyphonia, vocal fold atrophy, laryngeal aging, assessment, and treatment were reviewed and synthesized narratively. No formal systematic review protocol, duplicate screening, standardized data extraction, or risk-of-bias assessment was performed. Results: Presbylarynx encompasses age-related alterations in the vocal fold epithelium, lamina propria, intrinsic laryngeal musculature, and neuromuscular control, which may produce vocal fold atrophy, bowing, glottic insufficiency, and reduced vibratory efficiency. However, structural findings alone neither establish the cause of dysphonia nor determine the need for treatment. Clinical expression is modified by respiratory function, frailty, comorbidities, cognition, hearing status, compensatory behavior, and communication requirements. Assessment should integrate laryngeal morphology with patient-reported, auditory-perceptual, acoustic, aerodynamic, respiratory, and systemic findings, while excluding alternative and coexisting causes of dysphonia. Management should target meaningful functional impairment and may include observation, behavioral voice therapy, injection augmentation, durable medialization, or combined approaches within a flexible, nonlinear, and patient-centered pathway. Artificial intelligence, digital voice biomarkers, regenerative interventions, advanced biomaterials, and neuromuscular stimulation represent emerging opportunities; however, their clinical application remains limited by insufficient validation and predominantly preliminary or preclinical evidence. Conclusions: The presbylarynx is not inherently pathological or an indication for treatment. Its clinical significance emerges when age-related laryngeal changes contribute to meaningful limitations in voice function, communication, or quality of life. A multidimensional, system-aware, and function-driven approach is essential for accurate interpretation and individualized management. Future research should prioritize standardized definitions, reproducible phenotyping, comparable outcome measures, prospective comparative studies, and careful validation of new technologies.

articles.title: Coronary Collateral Circulation in Coronary Syndromes: Echocardiographic Insights and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Coronary collateral circulation (CCC) represents a natural adaptive mechanism capable of preserving myocardial perfusion in the presence of obstructive coronary artery disease. Although invasive angiography remains the reference method for collateral visualization, it provides limited information regarding collateral functionality and downstream myocardial protection. Echocardiography, due to its widespread availability, lack of radiation, and advances in imaging techniques, has emerged as an attractive non-invasive tool for evaluating the myocardial consequences of collateral perfusion. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the role of echocardiography in assessing coronary collateral circulation. Conventional echocardiographic parameters, stress echocardiography, myocardial contrast echocardiography, speckle-tracking imaging, myocardial work analysis and three-dimensional echocardiography are reviewed in the context of collateral-dependent myocardial function. Emerging technologies including artificial intelligence and quantitative perfusion imaging are also discussed. Rather than directly visualizing collateral vessels, echocardiography provides complementary information on the myocardial consequences of collateral-dependent perfusion through assessment of regional function, myocardial mechanics, and, with contrast techniques, tissue perfusion. However, collateral-specific validation remains limited, particularly for emerging deformation and myocardial work indices, and echocardiographic findings should be interpreted alongside coronary anatomy and physiological or perfusion measurements. Future integration with invasive assessment, multimodality imaging, and molecular markers may improve characterization of collateral-dependent myocardium.

articles.title: Ammonia in Liver Disease: Diagnostic Utility, Preanalytical Challenges, Clinical Interpretation, and Therapeutic Implications: A Critical Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Ammonia is central to the pathogenesis of hepatic encephalopathy (HE), but blood ammonia is neither a stand-alone diagnostic test nor a reliable measure of HE grade. Its clinical value depends on the population, the question being asked, and strict control of preanalytical and analytical conditions. This critical narrative review evaluates ammonia as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in liver disease, with emphasis on standardised measurement, interpretation in altered mental status, selective monitoring, and the distinction between biochemical response and patient-important outcomes. Evidence was updated through 9 October 2026 and prioritised international guidelines, the 2026 International Society for Hepatic Encephalopathy and Nitrogen Metabolism consensus, randomised trials, prospective cohorts, systematic reviews, and verified trial registries. In cirrhosis, an elevated value is nonspecific and does not confirm HE, whereas a methodologically reliable normal value should prompt diagnostic reassessment. Ammonia may add prognostic information in stable and decompensated cirrhosis, but thresholds and risk models require population-specific validation and do not independently mandate treatment. In acute liver failure, arterial ammonia has a distinct role in assessing the risk of cerebral oedema. Fasting before planned testing, avoidance of fist clenching and prolonged tourniquet use, rapid chilled transport, prompt plasma separation, and timely analysis are essential for an interpretable result. Treatment should be guided primarily by clinical course, correction of precipitants, and prevention of recurrence rather than serial ammonia concentrations. Standardisation and clinically anchored diagnostic algorithms are necessary before ammonia-guided management can be adopted broadly.

articles.title: PSA Dynamics, Bounce, and Biochemical Recurrence Definitions After Low-Dose-Rate Brachytherapy for Prostate Cancer: A Narrative Review with Cross-Modality Comparison.
articles.abstract: Background: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) dynamics provide the earliest indicator of treatment outcome. Understanding them, including nadir kinetics and PSA bounce, is essential for refining biochemical recurrence (BCR) definitions and guiding clinical decision making. Methods: A literature search was conducted across the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. Backward citation chaining of selected references resulted in a final synthesis of 143 studies. Iodine-125 constitutes the primary radioisotope across the reviewed literature. Key Findings: Following low-dose-rate brachytherapy (LDR-BT), a PSA nadir < 0.2 ng/mL is strongly associated with long-term biochemical control. PSA bounce (defined as a rise ≥ 0.2 ng/mL above the current nadir with spontaneous resolution) occurs in approximately 30% to 50% of LDR-BT cohorts, with a median onset of approximately 1.5 years, a median duration of approximately 1 year, and a median amplitude < 1 ng/mL. Up to 18% of bounces exceed 2.0 ng/mL, accounting for nearly half of all early rises triggering the Phoenix criteria. Superior dosimetric parameters are associated with longer time to nadir and lower nadir values. Within LDR-BT cohorts, younger patient age is the most consistent predictor of bounce incidence, whereas between-study variation is primarily driven by differences in treatment modality. LDR-BT and hypofractionated regimens report higher bounce rates than those for conventional external beam radiotherapy, although unadjusted comparisons are confounded. Onset timing is the most useful feature distinguishing between bounce and BCR. Conclusions: Static, single cutoff BCR definitions post-LDR-BT may be suboptimal for surveillance. This observational synthesis suggests a hypothesis-generating, time-windowed approach (Phoenix definition during early follow-up (< 4 years) and an absolute threshold of PSA > 0.2 ng/mL thereafter) that requires prospective validation and is not a recommendation for clinical use.

articles.title: Multimodality Imaging in Contemporary Cardio-Oncology: Beyond Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract: Background: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) may develop before symptoms or a measurable decline in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Surveillance therefore requires assessment beyond LVEF alone. Content: This narrative review examines cardiotoxic mechanisms, imaging findings, and treatment-specific surveillance. Transthoracic echocardiography with LVEF and global longitudinal strain remains the first-line approach. Myocardial work may provide additional information, but oncology-specific action thresholds remain unvalidated. Cardiac magnetic resonance complements echocardiography when measurements are inconclusive or tissue characterization is required. Mapping abnormalities are nonspecific and do not independently establish treatment-related injury. Nuclear imaging addresses selected diagnostic questions; fibroblast activation protein inhibitor PET remains investigational. Artificial intelligence may support image analysis and data integration, although evidence from general cardiovascular populations requires oncology-specific validation. An algorithm and surveillance matrix link clinical findings, treatment, baseline risk, imaging, and biomarkers. Conclusions: A tiered approach organizes surveillance around specific clinical questions. Earlier detection should be distinguished from demonstrated clinical benefit: evidence that imaging-guided strategies improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes remains limited. Prospective studies are needed to validate emerging markers, AI applications, and the clinical and economic effects of integrated surveillance pathways.

articles.title: Prognostic Factors Associated with Treatment Outcomes in Endodontic/Periodontal Lesions: A Systematic Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The complex nature of endodontic/periodontal lesions complicates treatment prognosis, making long-term tooth survival challenging to predict. Identifying key prognostic factors can facilitate evidence-based clinical decision-making. This systematic review aims to evaluate the available evidence on factors associated with treatment outcomes in endodontic/periodontal lesions and to identify potential prognostic indicators. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were searched from 1 June to 1 July 2026 with no restrictions. Observational studies investigating associations between baseline prognostic factors and treatment outcomes in adults with endodontic/periodontal lesions were eligible for inclusion. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Due to substantial methodological heterogeneity, the findings were synthesized narratively rather than through meta-analysis. Results: Four retrospective studies comprising 501 teeth were included. Risk of bias was predominantly moderate to high, and certainty of evidence was low. No single factor demonstrated directionally consistent independent association across the available adjusted analyses. Conclusions: Despite limited evidence, an overall pattern suggests that endodontic/periodontal lesion prognosis may be most frequently associated with the extent of periodontal tissue destruction and the amount of remaining periodontal support. Prospective studies using standardized endodontic/periodontal lesion definitions, outcomes and appropriately adjusted multivariable prognostic models are needed.

articles.title: Legionella Pneumonia in the Molecular Diagnostics Era: From Intracellular Pathogenesis to Precision Management.
articles.abstract: Legionella pneumophila is a major cause of severe community-acquired pneumonia and one of the most lethal respiratory pathogens. Nevertheless, it remains substantially underdiagnosed because conventional diagnostic assays are slow, insensitive, or limited to specific serogroups. In this narrative review, we integrate fragmented literature regarding Legionella pneumonia, covering its intracellular pathogenesis, clinical spectrum and patient management. Evidence was identified through a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC (23 September 2026) and prioritized by design, with primary clinical and mechanistic studies and systematic reviews taking precedence over narrative summaries and with society guidelines used to anchor management recommendations. We argue that this field is undergoing a diagnostic paradigm shift fueled by culture-independent molecular assays. We first review the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system and intracellular lifecycle that allow Legionella to replicate within macrophages while evading host innate immunity. We then summarize the full clinical spectrum, ranging from self-limited Pontiac fever to fatal Legionnaires' disease complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome, as well as epidemiological characteristics including waterborne transmission and outbreak risks. The core of this review examines how metagenomic next-generation sequencing, targeted NGS, plasma microbial cell-free DNA and syndromic multiplex PCR are reshaping diagnostic workflows, and compares the strengths and limitations of these novel tools with urinary antigen testing and bacterial culture. Pooled estimates place the sensitivity of urinary antigen testing at 0.79 overall and 0.86 for serogroup 1, and that of respiratory PCR at 97.4%, with specificities of 1.00 and 0.99, respectively. We further evaluate contemporary therapeutic evidence, including fluoroquinolone versus macrolide monotherapy, combination regimens, and adjunctive corticosteroid therapy. Throughout this review, we highlight that Legionella is a pathogen whose clinical presentation, diagnostic yield and prognosis are highly dependent on host immune status, exposure setting and appropriate diagnostic stewardship. We conclude by identifying critical knowledge gaps and outlining a framework for diagnosis-driven precision antimicrobial management of this underrecognized pathogen. That framework is an evidence-informed synthesis rather than a validated pathway: no prospective study has yet shown that it improves patient outcomes, and its cost-effectiveness has not been measured.

articles.title: Retinal Vasculature as a Non-Invasive Window for Preeclampsia Prediction and Assessment: From Fundoscopy to Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Retinal Imaging.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality, and effective prevention depends on the early identification of women at risk. Because the disorder is fundamentally a state of systemic endothelial dysfunction and microvascular maladaptation, the retina has long attracted interest as a candidate in vivo biomarker. It is the only vascular bed that can be visualised directly, repeatedly and non-invasively. This review appraises retinal assessment across four modality classes, classifying each study by the timing of imaging relative to diagnosis to distinguish early prediction from diagnostic discrimination, severity assessment and long-term follow-up. Qualitative fundoscopy reliably grades hypertensive retinopathy but is subjective and insensitive in mild disease. Quantitative retinal vessel analysis links narrower retinal vessels with the hypertensive disorders of pregnancy; in one longitudinal cohort, pressure-corrected arteriolar and venular calibre was reduced from 13 weeks in women who later developed preeclampsia, although effects were modest. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography studies, almost all performed after diagnosis, report choroidal and microvascular changes of inconsistent direction and, therefore, inform diagnosis and severity assessment rather than prediction. Ophthalmic artery Doppler may offer adjunctive discrimination. Two single-centre deep learning models applied to early-pregnancy fundus photographs reported areas under the curve of 0.87-0.88 for preeclampsia, but without external validation, calibration or head-to-head comparison with established first-trimester screening. Retinal imaging is, therefore, a mechanistically grounded but unproven avenue for preeclampsia prediction. Prospective pre-diagnostic cohorts, standardised acquisition, adjustment for blood pressure and other confounders, and externally validated, calibrated models tested for incremental value over established screening are required. Only then can retinal biomarkers, particularly artificial intelligence-assisted analysis with portable fundus cameras, be adopted as a scalable screening adjunct, including in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Protein Biomarkers of Kidney Injury and Dysfunction: Emerging Evidence on Non-Coding RNAs.
articles.abstract: Background: Kidney biomarkers address different clinical questions, and their accuracy depends on the population, sample, timing, and outcome. Objective: To organize selected evidence on protein biomarkers of kidney injury and dysfunction and examine emerging clinical evidence on non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Methods: This structured comparative narrative review used PubMed and Google Scholar, with searches through 19 September 2026, supplemented by targeted source verification and literature updating during revision in October 2026. Published estimates were summarized descriptively, no new meta-analysis was performed. Filtration assessment, AKI detection, persistence, disease activity, and RNA discovery or validation were considered separately. Results: Cystatin C and proenkephalin provide filtration-related information; KIM-1, NGAL, L-FABP, and NAG address tubular injury or associated outcomes. Urinary IL-18 and serum IL-8 have limited stand-alone diagnostic value in pediatric AKI. [TIMP-2]×[IGFBP7] reflects cellular stress and near-term AKI risk. CCL14 concerns persistent AKI. uDKK3, VCAM-1, and serum cathepsin S have evidence specific to their applications. Urinary HBP and plasma 8-isoprostane describe complementary infection and oxidative-stress contexts. More recent syntheses revise previously reported estimates for KIM-1 and NGAL. Selected ncRNA studies show promising discrimination, but their populations, clinical contrasts, and validation stages differ. Conclusions: Organizing biomarkers by clinical question connects their biological information with distinct diagnostic and prognostic applications. Protein-ncRNA combinations offer a direction for prospective research, with clinical adoption requiring independent validation and added value beyond conventional assessment.

articles.title: Beyond Imaging Overuse: Reframing Appropriateness as a Framework for Value-Based and Sustainable Radiology.
articles.abstract: Diagnostic imaging is central to contemporary healthcare, but increasing demand has intensified concerns regarding inappropriate and low-value examinations. Imaging appropriateness should be understood as a multidimensional quality framework rather than a simple reduction in examination volume. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on clinical outcomes, radiation protection, healthcare costs, organizational efficiency, equity, incidental findings, and environmental sustainability. A structured PubMed search was complemented by targeted database and institutional searches and selective citation tracking. Low-value imaging may disrupt diagnostic pathways through diagnostic uncertainty, unnecessary follow-up, avoidable radiation exposure, additional costs, waiting-list pressure, and environmental burden. Mitigation strategies include referral guidelines, clinical decision support, radiologist-led vetting, standardized incidental findings management, and audit and feedback. Their effects vary by setting and outcome: improved referral scores do not necessarily reduce utilization or improve patient outcomes. Environmental estimates depend on imaging modalities, electricity supply, and assessment boundaries, while proposed artificial intelligence applications require prospective validation. We translate this evidence into an operational pathway linking examination justification, modality and protocol selection, reporting, follow-up, and service evaluation. Imaging appropriateness therefore requires reducing low-value examinations while preserving diagnostic safety and timely, equitable access to clinically beneficial imaging.

articles.title: Imaging as a Surgical Decision System in Modern Gynecologic Oncology.
articles.abstract: Imaging traditionally supports gynecologic oncology through diagnosis, staging, and estimation of resectability. Contemporary treatment, however, requires longitudinal decisions about which lesion matters, when local intervention is justified, and which modality is proportionate. This critical narrative review proposes imaging as a longitudinal surgical decision system integrating disease trajectory, treatment response, target selection, operative planning, and post-intervention assessment. We define imaging-target mismatch as discordance between the radiologically dominant lesion and the lesion with greatest clinical actionability, and operationalize the disease-modifying surgical window as open, uncertain, or closed across six decision domains. Serial imaging may reveal response-created opportunities, oligopersistence, oligoprogression, competing dissemination, or the need for tissue confirmation, while CT, MRI, ultrasound, and FDG PET/CT provide complementary decision-specific information. Three-dimensional reconstruction, intraoperative imaging, radiomics, and artificial intelligence may enhance planning, but require prospective external validation and should support rather than replace multidisciplinary judgment. Decision-oriented reporting should communicate the target, lesion-level trajectory, competing disease, anatomical feasibility, residual uncertainty, and the relevance of findings to the proposed intervention. Imaging should therefore guide not only what can be treated, but what should be treated, when, and for what therapeutic purpose.

articles.title: Atopic Dermatitis and Bone Fragility: Osteoimmunological Pathways, Therapeutic Paradoxes, and Risk-Adapted Screening Across the Lifespan.
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) has been linked to osteoporosis and fractures, but the strength, mechanisms, treatment implications, and clinical significance of this relationship remain uncertain. This review critically assesses epidemiological and osteoimmunological evidence connecting AD with skeletal fragility and proposes a lifespan-based, risk-adapted screening framework. A recent cohort-based meta-analysis found associations between AD and osteoporosis (odds ratio [OR], 1.56) and any fracture (OR, 1.08), although heterogeneity was substantial. Risk appeared higher with severe or long-standing disease and reflected interactions among inflammatory, therapeutic, nutritional, behavioral, and age-related factors. Systemic glucocorticoids were the clearest modifiable treatment-related risk, but did not fully account for the association. The RANK-RANKL-osteoprotegerin system and IL-4, IL-13, IL-31, and IL-33 offer biological plausibility, although their skeletal effects are context-dependent and supported primarily by indirect or preclinical evidence. Available data do not show that dupilumab causes osteoporosis. Emerging pediatric findings suggest improvements in growth and bone-related biomarkers, but provide no evidence of fracture prevention. AD alone does not warrant universal DXA screening. Assessment should be individualized based on age, history of fragility fractures, disease severity and duration, cumulative systemic glucocorticoid exposure, nutritional status, physical activity, muscle function, and falls. Prospective studies combining standardized AD phenotyping with longitudinal imaging, biomarkers, and adjudicated fractures are needed.

articles.title: Precision Laboratory Diagnostics for Autoimmune Encephalitis and Paraneoplastic Neurological Syndromes: Autoantibody Testing, Fluid Biomarkers, and AI-Assisted Integration.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) and paraneoplastic neurological syndromes (PNS) are leading causes of potentially reversible but frequently misdiagnosed neurological disability, and delayed recognition worsens outcomes and impedes timely tumor detection. This narrative review is written from a laboratory medicine perspective and focuses on the analytical determinants of early and accurate diagnosis: appropriate test selection, dual-method confirmation combining tissue-based and cell-based assays, phenotype-guided interpretation, and assay harmonization. We summarize the expanding spectrum of neuronal and glial autoantibodies, quantitative biomarkers of neuroaxonal injury-most notably neurofilament light chain-and investigational cerebrospinal fluid markers, including cytokine profiles, kappa free light chains, and markers of astrocytic injury, whose ability to discriminate AE from infectious mimics has not been established. We highlight novel autoantibody discovery through phage immunoprecipitation sequencing, research-stage multi-omics approaches, and early, retrospectively evaluated artificial intelligence-assisted classifiers, and we address the growing challenge of neurological adverse events triggered by immune checkpoint inhibitors. Priorities for translation into routine care include external quality assurance, certified reference materials, age-adjusted reference intervals, and prospective validation of integrated biomarker panels within reference-center networks. The review provides a structured framework to support precision laboratory diagnostics in neuroimmunology.

articles.title: From Glomerular Endothelial Remodeling to Kidney Protection: Emerging Molecular Mechanisms and Biomarker Signatures of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.
articles.abstract: Kidney-protective therapies for diabetes mellitus have evolved rapidly in recent years, with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) offering renal protection. While some recent clinical trials have shown kidney benefits of these agents that extend well beyond improvements in blood glucose levels and reductions in albuminuria, much is still unknown about the precise molecular mechanisms. In this narrative review, we critically summarize the clinical and mechanistic evidence for GLP-1RA kidney protection, focusing on renal receptor localization, changes in glomerular endothelial cells, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and extracellular matrix turnover. We highlight recent results from the FLOW trial, which showed clinically significant kidney benefits with semaglutide, and from the REMODEL trial, which combines renal imaging with single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics. Although REMODEL did not demonstrate significant improvements in its coprimary imaging endpoints, exploratory molecular analyses identified treatment-associated changes in glomerular endothelial transcriptional programs and predicted endothelial-immune cell interactions. These findings suggest that microvascular remodeling may contribute to renal protection, although direct glomerular endothelial cell GLP1 receptor expression remains to be confirmed. In experimental systems, the pathways identified also involve control of oxidative stress, inflammasome activation, regulation of mitochondrial function, podocyte health, and fibrosis-related signaling, but their causal role in human kidney disease is yet to be proven. Novel proteomic and extracellular matrix biomarkers, such as tumor necrosis factor receptors, kidney injury molecule-1, and markers of collagen turnover, may help phenotype biological treatment responses beyond classical kidney function and albuminuria measures. Finally, tissue-based molecular phenotyping, combined with circulating and urinary markers, may resolve robust molecular signatures, and separating direct receptor effects from secondary systemic effects will be critical to translating GLP-1RA-mediated kidney benefit into biomarker-based nephrology.

articles.title: Clinical Anatomy of the Descending Genicular Artery and Genicular Arterial Network for Embolization and Reconstructive Surgery: A Systematic Review and Evidence Map with Targeted Meta-Analysis.
