articles.abstract: Germline pathogenic variants in the aryl hydrocarbon receptor-interacting protein (AIP) gene are the most common identifiable genetic cause of familial isolated pituitary adenomas (FIPA) and are particularly associated with young-onset growth hormone-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). This review critically evaluates current evidence on patient selection for germline AIP testing, variant interpretation, and emerging multigene approaches. A narrative PubMed/MEDLINE search identified English-language studies published between January 2006 and April 2025, including original clinical studies, international cohorts, systematic reviews, consensus statements, and relevant guidelines. Evidence was synthesized with emphasis on diagnostic yield, genotype-phenotype correlations, clinical indications for testing, and contemporary American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) variant classification. The highest diagnostic yield is consistently observed in FIPA, pituitary gigantism, childhood- or young-onset growth hormone (GH)-secreting macroadenomas, and selected patients with aggressive or otherwise high-risk phenotypes. Contemporary ACMG/AMP classification has lowered and refined estimates of clinically actionable AIP variants compared with historical studies. Targeted AIP testing remains appropriate for characteristic phenotypes, whereas multigene panels may be useful when syndromic features, atypical presentations, or persistent suspicion of hereditary disease remain after negative AIP testing. Current evidence supports phenotype-driven rather than universal germline AIP testing in PitNETs. Integrating age at onset, family history, tumor subtype, tumor characteristics, and standardized variant interpretation may maximize diagnostic yield while limiting unnecessary testing.

articles.title: The Image-to-Intervention Workflow in Orthopaedic Surgery: A Framework for Diagnostic Certainty, Quantitative Imaging, 3D Modeling, Biomechanical Validation, and Surgical Decision-Making.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Digital orthopedic technologies are often evaluated as isolated tools even though clinical use depends on a sequence of transformations from diagnosis to intervention. This literature-informed conceptual framework defines the Image-to-Intervention (I2I) pathway and distinguishes diagnostic adequacy, geometric validity, biomechanical validity, decision relevance, execution accuracy, and patient-level outcomes. Methods: The orthopedic and cross-domain literature on imaging, segmentation, 3D modeling, additive manufacturing, computational modeling, patient-specific instrumentation, navigation, and digital twins was purposively mapped to I2I stages. Study design and validation function were recorded separately; the review was a purposive conceptual synthesis rather than a systematic evidence appraisal; no formal risk-of-bias or certainty assessment was performed. Results: The framework uses an early eligibility checkpoint before resource-intensive modeling and a later model-informed decision checkpoint. Nine provisional uncertainty and failure domains identify measurement, transformation, model-form, decision, implementation, and feedback problems without treating them as equivalent errors. A multidimensional maturity profile replaces a universal ordinal ladder. Among 81 retained research sources, 9 were systematic reviews or meta-analyses, 5 were narrative or current-concepts reviews, and 7 were randomized controlled trials; the remainder comprised non-randomized comparative, observational, case-based, technical, cadaveric, synthetic-surrogate, and computational studies. Direct empirical stage mappings were non-exclusive and were most frequent for I2I-4 and I2I-5 (33 sources each); guidance applicability was counted separately. Because the bibliography was purposively assembled, these distributions describe only the cited corpus. Conclusions: I2I complements rather than replaces established guidance for diagnostic efficacy, surgical innovation, computational-model credibility, AI reporting, and medical 3D printing. Its taxonomy, maturity profile, and reporting domains remain provisional and require consensus development and independent reliability testing before clinical or regulatory use.

articles.title: The Immune-Senescent Switch in Oral Carcinogenesis: From Premalignancy to Malignant Transformation-Does Periodontitis Tip the Balance? A Hypothesis-Driven Review.
articles.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) accounts for approximately 90% of oral malignancies, and most cases arise from oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) against a background of chronic inflammation. Periodontitis, a highly prevalent chronic inflammatory disease, is increasingly implicated as a risk factor for OSCC, yet the mechanistic link between these conditions remains unclear. This review proposes that immunosenescence-the age-related decline in immune function-may provide this link. We synthesise evidence indicating that periodontitis promotes immune ageing in oral and systemic immune compartments, encompassing T-cell exhaustion, the accumulation of senescent immune cells, and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP); together, these changes progressively weaken local immunosurveillance. On this basis, we introduce the "immune-senescent switch" as a conceptual framework-explicitly distinguished from established evidence-in which senescence is hypothesised to initially act as a tumour-suppressive barrier in early OPMDs but to be converted into a tumour-promoting force by chronic, periodontitis-driven immunosenescence. We critically evaluate the supporting evidence, including the single-arm phase 2 COIS-01 trial (n = 24), in which senolytics combined with anti-PD-1 therapy achieved a 33.3% major pathological response rate in resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, while emphasising the preliminary, hypothesis-generating nature of these data. Finally, we discuss emerging senotherapeutic strategies, translational gaps, and future research priorities.

articles.title: Exercise Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance for the Diagnosis and Phenotyping of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: In heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), functional abnormalities may emerge mainly during exercise. Resting investigations may therefore explain exertional symptoms only partly. Exercise cardiovascular magnetic resonance (Ex-CMR) measures chamber volumes, deformation and blood flow during physiological stress to assess cardiovascular reserve. This review examines the technical foundations of Ex-CMR and its applications in HFpEF diagnosis, physiological phenotyping and treatment monitoring. It considers the physiological interpretation and clinical evidence for atrial, biventricular and vascular reserve indices, with attention to standardised acquisition, multiparametric assessment and clinical translation.

articles.title: Incidence, Prognosis, and Management of Occult Endometrial Carcinoma After Hysterectomy for Benign Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Occult endometrial carcinoma, incidentally diagnosed after hysterectomy for presumed benign disease, raises concerns regarding its incidence, the prognostic effects of minimally invasive surgery and morcellation, and subsequent management. This systematic review synthesized the available evidence and performed meta-analysis where appropriate. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register were searched using a sensitivity-tested strategy. After de-duplication and screening, 76 studies met the eligibility criteria. Incidence was pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis of proportions with the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation. Subgroup analyses examined surgical contexts, including hysterectomy for benign disease, morcellation-specific cohorts, and pelvic organ prolapse surgery. Survival and management outcomes were synthesized narratively. Results: Among 68 studies with extractable denominators, the pooled incidence (proportion of hysterectomies with carcinoma on final pathology) of occult endometrial carcinoma following hysterectomy for benign disease was 0.33% (95% prediction interval, 0.04-0.87%). Incidence was lowest in selected morcellation cohorts (0.22%) and higher in unselected benign hysterectomy cohorts (0.33%) and prolapse populations (0.43%; test for subgroup differences, p = 0.03), with substantially higher rates among older patients. The pooled incidence of occult uterine malignancies, including sarcoma, was 0.54%. For endometrial carcinoma specifically, the limited observational evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between power morcellation or laparoscopic surgery and poorer survival, although confidence intervals were wide. However, morcellation was associated with increased mortality among patients with uterine sarcoma. Occult endometrial carcinomas were predominantly early-stage and low-grade, with 81.8% classified as International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics IA, and approximately 91% achieving 5-year overall survival. In a small series of selected high-risk patients, completion staging resulted in upstaging in 25% and informed adjuvant treatment decisions. Limited observational data did not demonstrate a statistically significant survival benefit of complementary lymphadenectomy, although estimates were imprecise. Conclusions: Occult endometrial carcinoma occurs in approximately 0.2-0.4% of hysterectomies performed for benign disease, with a pooled incidence of 0.33% and higher rates among older patients. The limited observational evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between minimally invasive surgery or morcellation and poorer survival, but estimates were imprecise; wide confidence intervals and potential residual confounding preclude conclusions regarding oncologic safety. Overall prognosis was favorable. These findings support age-informed preoperative counseling and appropriate endometrial evaluation, with individualized consideration of re-staging when occult carcinoma is identified.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Approaches for Gastrointestinal Bleeding Detection in Capsule Endoscopy: A Systematic Review and Critical Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding is a common, potentially life-threatening condition, and capsule endoscopy (CE) is the principal investigation for suspected small-bowel bleeding after non-diagnostic upper endoscopy and colonoscopy. Because manual review of thousands of CE frames is labor-intensive, artificial intelligence (AI) has been proposed to automate bleeding detection. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review synthesizes 15 peer-reviewed journal studies (2020-2025) applying traditional machine learning, convolutional neural networks, transfer learning, attention-based or hybrid architectures, segmentation, or object detection to GI bleeding detection in CE. Methodological quality was appraised with an AI-adapted risk-of-bias framework informed by QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Results: Frame-level classification accuracy ranged from 90.6% to 99.9% (median 98.5%; 13 studies), with the lowest values from evaluations closest to clinical practice; the segmentation and detection studies reported a mean intersection-over-union of 86.9% and an mAP@0.5 of 79.0%. Only two studies (13%) were at low risk of bias for validation strategy, none reported patient-level separation of training and test data, only four (27%) used clinical patient data, and none compared AI with conventional endoscopy or clinical outcomes. Conclusions: Current evidence demonstrates high performance on curated datasets but not yet generalizability or clinical readiness; patient-level, external, and prospective multicentre validation is required.

articles.title: Temporal Patterns of Serum Neuroprotectin D1 and Resolvin D1 After Motor and Nonmotor Epileptic Seizures: A Prospective Repeated-Measures Study.
articles.abstract: Objective: Neuroinflammatory activation is well recognized in epilepsy, whereas the temporal behavior of specialized pro-resolving mediator (SPM) responses after seizures remains poorly defined. We evaluated changes in serum neuroprotectin D1 (NP-1) and resolvin D1 (RvD1) between the early postictal period and a seizure-free period of at least 1 month and compared both time points with healthy controls. Methods: This prospective controlled repeated-measures study included 48 adults with epilepsy and 50 healthy controls. Blood was obtained within 3 h after a seizure and again after at least 1 month of seizure freedom; controls provided one sample. Serum NP-1 and resolvin D1 (RvD1) were measured using commercial enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kits. The prespecified primary analysis compared paired postictal and seizure-free measurements using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Patient-control comparisons were considered secondary/exploratory. Results: Median NP-1 increased from 50.01 ng/mL (IQR 3.58-98.62) postictally to 67.78 ng/mL (59.81-121.81) during the seizure-free period (Z = -5.333, p < 0.001, r = 0.770). RvD1 did not change significantly (326.67 [207.77-899.95] vs. 441.47 [223.67-710.81] pg/mL; p = 0.139, r = 0.215). Both mediators were lower than controls postictally (both p < 0.001). During seizure freedom, NP-1 and RvD1 remained lower than controls (p = 0.008 and p < 0.001, respectively). The absolute percentage difference from the control median was greater for RvD1 than for NP-1 during seizure freedom (60.74% vs. 42.84%; p = 0.001, r = 0.462). Conclusions: The pro-resolving response in epilepsy appears temporally heterogeneous. NP-1 showed substantial within-patient recovery, whereas Resolvin D1 remained persistently reduced. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support larger serial-sampling studies with targeted lipidomic validation rather than establishing either mediator as a diagnostic biomarker.

articles.title: Cross-Phenotype Genomics Reveals Heterogeneous Genetic Susceptibility Architecture Relevant to Menopause.
articles.abstract: Background: Menopause is accompanied by substantial interindividual variation in hormonal, metabolic, cardiovascular, skeletal, and thrombotic phenotypes. Although the genetics of reproductive ageing and individual menopause-associated traits are increasingly characterised, the cross-phenotype architecture of individual menopause-relevant germline variants remains less well defined. Methods: We performed a variant-centred genomic analysis of 31 prespecified menopause-relevant germline variants. Cross-trait evidence comprised 766 variant-trait records across 52 phenotypes and was integrated with a targeted Pan-UK Biobank phenome-wide association study (PheWAS; 1462 tests across 57 endpoints), clinically relevant outcome analyses, linkage disequilibrium assessment, FinnGen R12 venous thromboembolism (VTE) associations, regional fine-mapping, and molecular annotation. Association strength, between-study heterogeneity, phenotypic breadth and sharing, and locus resolution were evaluated as distinct evidence dimensions. Results: In total, 25 of 31 variants showed at least one cross-trait association at p < 1 × 10-5 and 21 reached genome-wide significance. Phenotypic breadth varied markedly, from restricted profiles to 16 associated phenotypes, and strong associations frequently coexisted with substantial between-study heterogeneity. In Pan-UK Biobank, 222 associations involving 25 variants met false-discovery-rate correction, spanning hormonal, reproductive, cardiometabolic, skeletal, nutritional, hepatic, and neurological phenotypes. Cross-phenotype reconstruction identified recurrent connectivity through sex hormone-binding globulin, testosterone, adiposity, lipid, and skeletal traits, while linkage disequilibrium analyses distinguished phenotypic sharing from genetic redundancy. Clinically, F5 rs6025 and F2 rs1799963 showed strong VTE associations in FinnGen (OR 2.387 and 1.921, respectively), but markedly different locus resolution: rs6025 had posterior inclusion probability (PIP) 0.979 and constituted a single-variant 95% credible set, whereas rs1799963 had PIP 0.596 within a four-variant credible set. Conclusions: Menopause-relevant germline variation exhibits heterogeneous cross-phenotype architectures in which association strength, phenotypic breadth, between-study consistency, genetic independence, and locus resolution are not interchangeable. This variant-centred framework provides a basis for evaluating inherited susceptibility relevant to menopause and hormone exposure, while prospective individual-level studies remain necessary before translation into risk prediction or treatment selection.

articles.title: Paradoxical Splenic Signal Loss on Chemical-Shift MRI in Acute Toxic Hepatitis After Occupational Petroleum Sludge Exposure: A Case Series.
articles.abstract: Background: Acute toxic hepatitis after work-related exposure to petroleum products is rare. Its imaging features are not well known. Methods: Seven men aged 18-35 years cleaned the same petroleum storage tank for two days. Symptoms began about 5 days later. Ultrasound and CT were done at admission. Non-contrast 3 T MRI with in-phase and opposed-phase imaging was done about 10 days after exposure. The splenic signal intensity ratio (SIR, in-phase/opposed-phase) was compared with that of 15 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Results: At admission, median ALT was 481 U/L, median AST 227 U/L, and median total bilirubin 6.1 mg/dL. The injury was hepatocellular by R ratio in the six patients with raised ALT. Periportal edema was seen in 6 of 7 patients. No patient had biliary obstruction or vascular thrombosis. Notably, all seven patients demonstrated paradoxical splenic signal loss on in-phase compared with opposed-phase MRI, with a median splenic signal intensity ratio (SIR) of 0.77 (IQR, 0.74-0.81; range, 0.70-0.87). Splenic SIR was lower in patients than in healthy controls (median 0.77 vs. 1.05; p < 0.001). All patients recovered with supportive care. Conclusions: In this single exposure cluster, the spleen lost signal on in-phase images. This pattern is usually linked to iron or other T2* effects. The finding is preliminary. It needs confirmation with iron measurement, hemolysis tests, and follow-up MRI.

articles.title: Urgent Endovascular Treatment of a Pancreatitis-Related Pseudoaneurysm Identified on Follow-Up CT.
articles.abstract: Visceral artery pseudoaneurysm (VA-PSA) is an uncommon but life-threatening complication of acute-on-chronic pancreatitis, particularly in the presence of walled-off necrosis (WON). Early radiological recognition is essential because of the high risk of rupture. We present the case of a 51-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis who developed a pseudoaneurysm arising from the proper hepatic artery within a pancreatic head necrotic collection. Follow-up contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a new arterial-phase enhancing focus within the WON. Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) confirmed the pseudoaneurysm, which was successfully excluded with a covered stent placed via a right transfemoral approach. Post-procedural recovery was uneventful, and short-term follow-up CT showed persistent exclusion of the lesion.

articles.title: Serum Asprosin Concentrations and Severity in Acute Pancreatitis: A Prospective Case-Control Study with Serial Measurements.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Asprosin is a fasting-induced glucogenic adipokine with pro-inflammatory effects in experimental models, but its behaviour in acute pancreatitis (AP) is unknown. In this exploratory study, we examined whether circulating asprosin differs between patients with AP and healthy controls, how it changes during hospitalisation and whether it is associated with disease severity. Methods: In this prospective case-control study, 82 patients with AP (of 183 screened, after exclusion of diabetes, hypertriglyceridaemia and morbid obesity) and 82 sex-matched healthy controls were enrolled. Serum asprosin was measured by ELISA at admission, 72 h and 120 h in patients and once in fasting controls. Severity was defined by the revised Atlanta classification. Because patients were older and heavier than controls, the group difference was adjusted for age, body mass index and sex and examined in post hoc matched subsamples. Results: Admission asprosin was 4.52 (2.94-5.89) ng/mL in patients and 3.55 (2.24-4.92) ng/mL in controls (p = 0.071); the ratio of geometric means adjusted for age, body mass index and sex was 1.17 (95% CI 0.85-1.61). Asprosin was higher in patients in post hoc age- and sex-matched pairs (median difference 1.91 ng/mL, 95% CI 0.24-3.78) but not in body mass index- and sex-matched pairs (0.96 ng/mL, -0.34 to 2.72). Asprosin changed little over five days and was not associated with moderately severe or severe AP (AUC 0.57, upper 95% confidence limits ≤0.71); only seven patients had severe AP. Conclusions: In this exploratory study, serum asprosin was modestly and non-significantly higher in patients with AP than in controls, and no statistically significant association with severity was detected. Residual confounding by age and body mass index, the exclusion of patients with diabetes or hypertriglyceridaemia (≥200 mg/dL) and the absence of in-house assay validation preclude firm conclusions. These data provide effect estimates for adequately powered, matched studies of asprosin in AP.

articles.title: Ranking Features Distinguish Vestibular Migraine with Positional Vertigo from Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo Using Machine Learning.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Vestibular migraine with positional vertigo (VMwPV) can mimic benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), leading to diagnostic challenges. This study aimed to compare clinical and nystagmus-related features between VMwPV and BPPV patients and to establish a differential diagnostic model using machine learning. Methods: 101 VMwPV and 219 BPPV patients were enrolled. The nystagmus-related features included spontaneous nystagmus (SN) and parameters during positional testing: latency, pure vertical or vertical-component positional nystagmus (PN), PN lasting <1 min, and the maximum slow phase velocity (SPVmax) of PN. Vertigo/dizziness during positional testing was also included. Using multiple machine learning algorithms, diagnostic models were constructed, and the optimal model was selected. The Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis was applied to rank the feature importance. Results: (1) Compared with BPPV, VMwPV patients were more likely to have SN and pure vertical/vertical-component PN but less likely to have latency, PN lasting <1 min, and provoked vertigo/dizziness; the SPVmax of PN was lower in VMwPV than in BPPV. (2) No statistically significant differences in area under the curve (AUC) were observed among the five models. Logistic Regression was selected as the optimal model based on its superior interpretability. (3) Vertigo/dizziness during positional testing and PN lasting <1 min were ranked as the top two most important features based on SHAP analysis. These findings should be interpreted with caution due to group selection and incorporation bias. Conclusions: Apart from the subjective provoked vertigo/dizziness, other objective variables such as PN lasting <1 min may have potential value in differentiating VMwPV and BPPV, which require multicenter studies and prospective external validation.

articles.title: Ultra-High-Resolution Imaging of Rectal Cancer with Photon-Counting Detector Computed Tomography: An Exploratory Pilot Study on the Impact of Slice Thickness and Monoenergetic Reconstruction Level on Image Quality.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To evaluate, in an exploratory pilot study, the influence of slice thickness and monoenergetic (ME) level on quantitative and qualitative image quality of ultra-high-resolution (UHR) photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) in rectal cancer (RC). Methods: This prospective pilot study enrolled 21 patients with suspected RC undergoing pre-treatment PCD-CT between July 2023 and February 2025. All underwent a QuantumPlus portal venous phase, whose 3 mm/60 keV reconstruction served as the standard reference, plus a separate pelvic UHR acquisition. Sixteen UHR reconstructions were generated (0.6-3 mm; 45-70 keV). Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and noise were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Three readers independently rated overall image quality, perceived noise, mesorectal fascia (MRF) sharpness and lesion conspicuity relative to the reference; ratings were analyzed using mixed model ordinal regression. The primary analysis was the within-UHR comparison of reconstruction settings; the comparison with the reference, which differed in contrast phase and acquisition parameters, was descriptive. Results: Nineteen patients (mean age 61.7 ± 10.7 years, 73.7% male) were included. CNR showed a significant slice thickness-ME level interaction (p < 0.001), ranging from 4.85 ± 2.43 (3 mm/45 keV) to 0.86 ± 1.04 (0.6 mm/70 keV). SNR increased and noise decreased with thicker slices, while both decreased with higher ME levels (all p < 0.001). ME level influenced all four qualitative parameters (all p < 0.001); slice thickness significantly affected overall quality and perceived noise (p < 0.001) but not MRF sharpness or lesion conspicuity (p ≥ 0.115). Overall quality was rated favorably in 82.9% at 70 keV versus 45.6% at 45 keV. Lesion conspicuity reached 71.9-86.0% favorable ratings, whereas perceived noise was consistently rated worse than the reference, and UHR SNR remained below the reference in all settings. In a descriptive pooled summary, 3 mm/60 keV (68.0%) and 2 mm/70 keV (66.2%) were rated favorably most often, with overlapping confidence intervals. Conclusions: Slice thickness and ME level markedly influence UHR PCD-CT image quality in RC. One candidate working reconstruction for future validation is 3 mm at 60 keV, with 2 mm at 70 keV as a plausible alternative. Because the reference differed in acquisition and contrast phase and no diagnostic endpoint was assessed, these results do not establish a diagnostic benefit of UHR PCD-CT.

articles.title: AI-Supported Semiquantitative CT Characterization of COVID-19 Pneumonia Across SARS-CoV-2 Wild-Type, Alpha, and Delta Variants and Its Association with Clinical Parameters.
articles.abstract: Objective: An AI-based software prototype for the detection of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pneumonia was evaluated regarding its potential to quantify pulmonary opacities across Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) variant groups, incorporating clinical and radiological parameters to facilitate faster diagnosis and therapy. Methods: Chest computed tomography (CT) examinations of 255 patients with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia were analyzed using an AI-supported semiquantitative CT software prototype between November 2020 and December 2021. The results were correlated with clinical and laboratory parameters. The cohort consisted of wild-type (n = 93), Alpha (n = 66), Beta/Gamma (n = 3), and Delta (n = 93). Beta/Gamma cases were excluded from subgroup comparisons due to the small number of patients. Results: The mean AI-derived COVID-19 probability was 0.84 ± 0.33. After exclusion of five technically non-evaluable measurements, global mean opacity attenuation differed significantly among the wild-type (-475.12 ± 116.47 Hounsfield Units (HU)), Alpha (-464.68 ± 114.80 HU), and Delta groups (-423.92 ± 112.56 HU; Kruskal-Wallis H(2) = 12.062, p = 0.002). The Volume of Opacity showed no significant differences between wild-type (984.64 ± 908.92 mL), Alpha (1161.17 ± 933.55 mL), and Delta (988.19 ± 866.20 mL) (p = 0.339). The extent of pulmonary involvement (Volume of Opacity) correlated with the duration of hospital stay (r = 0.311, p < 0.001**), duration of intensive care treatment (r = 0.468, p < 0.001**), and the laboratory parameters CRP, leukocyte count, relative lymphocyte count, and AST (p < 0.001**). It showed no significant correlation with the duration of invasive ventilation (p > 0.05). A total of 37 (14.5%) patients died and 92 (36.1%) required intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Manual corrections of lung lobe and infiltrate boundaries were performed in 221/255 datasets and were required in all assessed datasets (221/221, 100%). Conclusions: The CT Pneumonia Analysis Prototype enabled semiquantitative assessment of pulmonary opacities across different SARS-CoV-2 variants but required radiological oversight and manual correction of the automated segmentations. Given the retrospective observational design, the findings should be interpreted in light of potential confounding and heterogeneity in CT acquisition protocols. The observed associations suggest that combining semiquantitative CT parameters with clinical and laboratory data may be of potential relevance for future prognostic models, which requires further evaluation in multivariable analyses.

articles.title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Risk Stratification for Tuberculosis Infection in High-Risk Groups Receiving Immunosuppressive Therapy.
articles.abstract: Background: Individuals receiving immunosuppressive therapy, solid-organ transplant recipients, household contacts of patients with tuberculosis, and healthcare workers are at increased risk of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and progression to tuberculosis disease. However, currently available immunological tests cannot reliably distinguish tuberculosis infection from active tuberculosis disease or predict individual progression to disease. We aimed to assess the prevalence of immunological evidence of tuberculosis infection across clinically and epidemiologically distinct risk groups and to explore the potential of machine-learning methods for individualised risk stratification. Methods: In this observational study, 544 adults aged 18-75 years were assessed between 2023 and 2026. Participants included patients with pulmonary tuberculosis, tuberculosis-facility healthcare workers, healthcare workers in the general medical network, household and occupational contacts of patients with tuberculosis, patients with rheumatic diseases receiving immunosuppressive therapy, patients undergoing assessment for heart transplantation, heart-transplant recipients, and healthy controls. Participants underwent clinical, epidemiological, radiological, and immunological assessment, including interferon-γ release assays (ELISPOT and QuantiFERON-TB Gold) and the tuberculosis recombinant allergen skin test. Individuals with positive immunological tests underwent additional assessment to exclude active tuberculosis. Exploratory logistic regression and decision-tree models were developed separately for each risk group using demographic and treatment-related variables. Model performance was estimated using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (5 × 10 repeats) with bootstrap optimism correction; discrimination, calibration, sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, Cohen's kappa, and Matthews correlation coefficient were reported with 95% confidence intervals. Results: The prevalence of positive immunological tests was highest among heart-transplant recipients (15 [53.6%] of 28), followed by household contacts (12 [41.4%] of 29), patients undergoing pre-transplant assessment (5 [35.7%] of 14), and tuberculosis-facility healthcare workers (21 [22.6%] of 93). Positivity was lower among patients with rheumatic diseases receiving immunosuppressive therapy (11 [13.9%] of 79) and healthcare workers in the general medical network without documented tuberculosis exposure (7 [10.5%] of 68), and was 3 (4.4%) of 69 among healthy controls. Compared with healthy controls, positivity was significantly higher among tuberculosis-facility healthcare workers, household contacts, patients with rheumatic diseases, and pre-transplant and heart-transplant populations. Exploratory machine-learning analyses were performed separately for the two clinically most relevant immunosuppressed subgroups. In patients with rheumatic diseases (n = 71; 9 positive, 62 negative), pooled ROC AUC was 0.670 (95% CI 0.520-0.824, participant-level bootstrap); age showed 100% bootstrap sign consistency, whereas bDMARD treatment showed 84.6% and sex 55.0%. In the combined heart transplantation group (n = 41; 19 positive, 22 negative), pooled ROC AUC was 0.668 (95% CI 0.522-0.811); tacrolimus and everolimus showed the highest bootstrap sign consistency (100% and 97.6%, respectively); however, because tacrolimus and everolimus are administered predominantly to transplant recipients, these coefficients may partly reflect transplantation status rather than drug-specific effects. Because the heart transplantation group combines pre-transplant candidates and recipients, and because both subgroups had small numbers of events, these associations should be interpreted as exploratory and not as drug-specific causal effects. Conclusions: The prevalence of immunological evidence of tuberculosis infection varied substantially between risk groups and was particularly high among household contacts and heart-transplant recipients. The findings suggest that epidemiological exposure and the type of immunosuppressive therapy should be considered jointly when assessing tuberculosis infection risk. Exploratory machine-learning analyses suggested that treatment-related variables may contribute to individualised risk stratification in the combined heart transplantation group, but the models were developed in small, clinically heterogeneous subgroups and were not externally validated. They should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Prospective multicentre studies with longitudinal follow-up are required to determine whether integrated clinical, epidemiological, immunological, and treatment-related models can predict incident tuberculosis disease and improve targeted preventive strategies.

articles.title: A LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a Assay for Specific Detection of Escherichia coli in Whole Blood: Analytical Performance and Clinical Evaluation in Suspected Bloodstream Infection.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Blood culture is slow and real-time PCR (qPCR) needs a thermal cycler, while loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) is rapid but prone to non-specific amplification. We developed a LAMP assay with CRISPR/Cas12a read-out targeting the Escherichia coli dxs gene and compared it with qPCR and blood culture. Methods: Reaction conditions were optimised and specificity tested on 15 E. coli and 40 non-target isolates. The limit of detection (LOD) was determined in spiked whole blood (20 replicates per level, 1-10 CFU/mL) by hit rate and probit regression, with conversion to dxs copies by growth phase. Fifty-two patients with suspected bloodstream infection were tested by all three methods. Results: The assay detected all 15 Escherichia coli isolates tested (inclusivity 15/15; 95% CI 79.6-100) and none of 40 non-target isolates (exclusivity 40/40; 95% CI 91.2-100); the exclusivity panel did not include Shigella spp. or Escherichia fergusonii, which the in silico analysis predicts the assay would detect. The probit LOD95 was 14.2 CFU/mL (95% fiducial limits 6.7-156; ≈43 dxs copies/mL for the mid-exponential spike culture used here) for LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a and 5.8 CFU/mL (2.6-958) for qPCR; a positive was read within 5 min of starting the Cas12a detection step. LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a was positive in 19/33 qPCR-positive and 0/19 qPCR-negative patients (positive and negative percent agreement 57.6% and 100%; κ = 0.50); all 13 samples at or above the qPCR LOD95 were detected. Conclusions: LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a detects E. coli in whole blood specifically and rapidly, but its clinical sensitivity is limited by the very low bacterial loads of bacteraemia, so that it is suited to use as a rapid confirmatory test alongside blood culture rather than as a rule-out test.

articles.title: A Rare Presentation of Ranula with Supraglottic and Paraglottic Extension Managed via a Hybrid Minimally Invasive Approach.
articles.abstract: A ranula is a mucus extravasation pseudocyst typically arising from the sublingual gland, usually confined to the oral floor or submandibular space. Extension into the supraglottic and paraglottic spaces by traversing or defect-bypassing the mylohyoid muscle is an exceedingly rare phenomenon that poses a significant risk of critical airway compromise. We report an exceptional case of a right-sided ranula presenting with progressive dyspnea due to extensive posterior involvement reaching the vallecula and paraglottic region. Definitive diagnosis of the plunging ranula was established through a comprehensive framework combining clinical presentation, multimodal imaging (CT, MRI, and ultrasonography), histopathological identification of a non-epithelialized lesion with mucinous extravasation, and biochemical fluid analysis via fine-needle aspiration (FNA) confirming markedly elevated levels of salivary amylase and total protein. To mitigate surgical morbidity and avoid extensive transcervical dissection, a hybrid, minimally invasive therapeutic strategy was employed, combining intraoral sublingual gland excision with postoperative percutaneous ethanol ablation for the deep paraglottic residual pseudocystic lesion. Complete resolution of the lesion was achieved without nerve injury, recurrence, or airway complications during follow-up. This case demonstrates that a sequential combination of transoral excision and ethanol ablation is a safe, effective, and organ-preserving alternative to aggressive open neck surgery for deep-extending plunging ranulas.

articles.title: CCR2 and CCR5 Expression on Tph Cells Is Associated with IL-21 and Renal Involvement in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The increased frequency of circulating T follicular helper (cTfh) and T peripheral helper (Tph) cells in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and their association with higher disease activity have been reported. However, their role in the immunopathogenesis of SLE remains unclear. CCR2 and CCR5 have been identified on the surface of cTfh and Tph cells in autoimmune diseases such as Sjögren's Disease. Methods: This study evaluates the association between CCR2+CCR5+cTfh and CCR2+CCR5+Tph cell frequencies and serum cytokine levels in patients with SLE and lupus nephritis (LN). Results: SLE patients showed higher frequencies of cTfh and Tph cells. Overall, CCR2 and CCR5 expression was higher in Tph cells than in cTfh cells. The frequency of CCR5+Tph and CCR5+cTfh cells was higher in patients with proliferative LN than in those with mixed-type LN. IL-21 correlated with the frequency of CCR2+CCR5+ Tph cells. In renal tissue, expression of CD4, CXCR5, CCR5, and CCR2 was more prominent in tubulo-interstitial areas with predominantly chronic lesions. Conclusions: Our results provide information on the expression of CCR2 and CCR5 in cTfh and Tph cells in SLE and offer insights into the association with inducing cytokines, highlighting the potential role of these cells in LN.

articles.title: Correlation Between Clinicopathological Findings, Cervical Smear, and HPV Results: A Retrospective Study of Women Referred for Colposcopy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the association of cervical cytology, human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes, and colposcopic findings with histopathological outcomes in women referred for colposcopy. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 756 women who underwent colposcopy with cervical biopsy at a tertiary center between January 2022 and June 2025 and had HPV genotyping and conventional cytology results. The primary endpoint was cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) on biopsy; the highest grade across biopsy and conization specimens and CIN3+ were secondary endpoints. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, and diagnostic accuracy was reported according to STARD 2015. Results: CIN2+ was found in 85 women (11.2%). HPV-16 positivity (OR: 2.87; 95% CI: 1.72-4.77), epithelial cell abnormality on cytology (OR: 4.28; 95% CI: 2.05-8.92), and positive colposcopy (OR: 3.39; 95% CI: 2.00-5.73) were independently associated with higher odds of CIN2+. Adding colposcopy to a pre-colposcopy model increased the AUC from 0.730 to 0.770 (p = 0.034; optimism-corrected 0.753). Colposcopy had a sensitivity of 71.8% (95% CI: 61.4-80.2%) and an NPV of 94.6% (95% CI: 92.1-96.3%), but 24 of 85 CIN2+ cases (28.2%) had a negative colposcopic impression; results were similar for the highest-grade endpoint (92 CIN2+ cases). Conclusions: In this referral population, HPV-16, cytological abnormality, and colposcopic impression provided complementary information on the odds of CIN2+. Because more than one-quarter of CIN2+ cases were not colposcopically apparent, a negative colposcopy should not be considered sufficient to exclude high-grade disease, particularly in women with HPV-16 positivity or abnormal cytology. Prospective validation is required before these associations are used for triage.

articles.title: Integrated Assessment of Hematoma Burden, Anatomical Extension, and Mass Effect for 90-Day Functional Outcome After Spontaneous Supratentorial Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Temporal Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Objective: To assess the contribution of hematoma burden, anatomical extension, and mass effect to predicting 90-day poor functional outcome alongside clinical characteristics in spontaneous supratentorial intracerebral hemorrhage, and to evaluate temporal model performance. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 789 patients undergoing CT within six hours of symptom onset: 508 in the development cohort (2018-2022) and 281 in the temporal validation cohort (2023-2025). Poor outcome was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 4-6. Hematoma volume, deep structure involvement, and intraventricular hemorrhage were added to clinical logistic regression models, followed by midline shift. Discrimination and calibration were assessed, with 1000 bootstrap resamples for internal validation. Model coefficients remained unchanged during temporal validation. Secondary analysis replaced absolute shift with the shift/volume ratio while retaining hematoma volume. Results: Poor outcome occurred in 46.1% and 44.5% of patients, respectively. Development AUC increased from 0.798 to 0.846 with volume and extension variables (p < 0.001), then to 0.875 with midline shift (p = 0.014). Hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage, and midline shift remained associated with poor outcome. The adjusted odds ratio per millimeter of shift was 1.17 (95% CI, 1.08-1.28). Optimism-corrected and temporal validation AUCs were 0.856 and 0.854. Model ranking persisted, with generally concordant predicted and observed risks. The association between midline shift and poor outcome persisted in sensitivity analyses addressing surgery or external ventricular drainage, care limitations, and CT timing. The ratio was associated with poor outcome but yielded numerically lower AUCs in both cohorts. Conclusions: The model incorporating all three radiological features showed the highest discrimination among the three models in both cohorts, supporting joint assessment of hematoma burden and mass effect. Multicenter validation and clinical utility assessment remain necessary.

articles.title: Sensitivity of 2-Hour Gastric Emptying Scintigraphy for Delayed Gastric Emptying Confirmed at 4 Hours: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Abbreviated gastric-emptying scintigraphy (GES) protocols could save resources. We estimated how often the 2 h criterion (retention ≥ 60%) identifies patients whose delayed gastric emptying is confirmed at 4 h (retention ≥ 10%). Methods: This is a retrospective single-center study of adults with 4 h-confirmed delayed gastric emptying undergoing standardized GES at a tertiary hospital in Bogotá, Colombia (2010-2024). Sensitivity with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) was estimated overall and in exploratory subgroups. Results: Of 101 records, 97 adults were analyzed (78.4% women; 18.6% with diabetes). The median 4 h retention was 20.0% (IQR 15.0-27.0%). The 2 h criterion identified 41/97 patients (sensitivity 42.3%; 95% CI 32.9-52.2%); 56 (57.7%) would have been missed at 2 h. Sensitivity was 30.0%, 36.7% and 87.5% for mild, moderate and severe delay, respectively. It was 27.8% in patients with diabetes and 45.6% in those without (p = 0.196; underpowered comparison). Because no patient had normal 4 h retention, the specificity and predictive values could not be estimated. Conclusions: A 2 h retention below 60% does not exclude delayed gastric emptying, particularly when the delay is mild or moderate; the 4 h acquisition should be completed in these patients. Prospective studies that include patients with normal emptying are needed.

articles.title: Performance Evaluation of Deep Learning Applications in Calcaneal Fracture Diagnosis Using Separate Radiographic Views: A Comparison of CNN and Vision Transformer Architectures.
articles.abstract: Background: Calcaneal fractures are challenging to diagnose on routine radiographs and may result in missed diagnoses. Objective: This study compares Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures for detecting calcaneal fractures separately in three standard radiographic views: Anteroposterior (AP), Harris (axial), and Lateral. Methods: A balanced retrospective dataset of 178 patients with complete three-view examinations (89 with displaced calcaneal fractures and 89 controls) was used to evaluate five deep learning models: ResNet50, InceptionV3, InceptionResNetV2, XCiT, and PiT. After image-quality screening, each view underwent an approximately 8:2 image-level training-validation split; no independent test set was used. Images were preprocessed using data augmentation and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), while Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was employed to visualize model activation. Results: InceptionV3 achieved 100% sensitivity in the AP view, while ResNet50 achieved 100% specificity in both AP and Lateral views. XCiT matched ResNet50 across all five classification metrics in the AP view and matched ResNet50 and InceptionV3 in the Lateral view. PiT achieved 100% accuracy in the Harris validation set (95% CI, 89.0-100.0%). Grad-CAM visualizations showed activation over the calcaneal region in representative fracture images. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the feasibility of deep learning for identifying displaced calcaneal fractures through separate evaluations of AP, Harris, and Lateral radiographs. The model-specific performance patterns provide a foundation for further development of AI-assisted calcaneal fracture detection and future investigation of multi-view integration.

articles.title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Combined with the NLR-PMR Phenotype for Prostate Cancer Prediction and Risk Stratification in Patients with PSA 4-20 ng/mL and PI-RADS ≤ 3.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To assess contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) combined with the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio-platelet-to-monocyte ratio (NLR-PMR) phenotype for predicting prostate cancer (PCa) and clinically significant PCa (csPCa) in patients with PSA 4-20 ng/mL and PI-RADS ≤ 3. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 418 biopsy patients. Outcomes were PCa and csPCa (ISUP Grade Group ≥ 2). A continuous NLR-PMR score and CEUS were added to an age-PSA density baseline model. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Three risk strata were defined using CEUS and NLR-PMR status. Results: PCa and csPCa were detected in 60 (14.4%) and 42 (10.0%) patients. Adding NLR-PMR improved AUCs beyond age and PSA density for PCa (0.798 vs. 0.747; p = 0.025) and csPCa (0.805 vs. 0.752; p = 0.026). Combined-model AUCs were 0.798 for PCa and 0.812 for csPCa. CEUS positivity remained associated with csPCa after adjustment (OR = 2.26, 95% CI: 1.08-4.91; p = 0.033). Across low-, intermediate-, and high-risk strata, detection rates were 3.9%, 15.2%, and 34.3% for PCa and 2.0%, 8.0%, and 28.4% for csPCa. The low-risk stratum comprised 48.8% of patients, with a csPCa negative predictive value of 98.0% and no ISUP Grade Group 4-5 cancers. Dual CEUS/NLR-PMR positivity increased with pathological grade (p < 0.001). Conclusions: In this exploratory cohort, NLR-PMR improved discrimination for PCa and csPCa, and CEUS further differentiated csPCa risk among NLR-PMR-positive patients. The combined assessment identified strata with progressively increasing cancer detection rates, providing preliminary evidence for individualized pre-biopsy risk assessment. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: MRI Radiomics-Based Nomogram Integrating Skeletal Muscle Assessment for Predicting Pathologic Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Therapy in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We aim to develop and internally evaluate a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics-based nomogram integrating clinicopathologic and skeletal muscle measures for predicting pathologic complete response (pCR) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Methods: This retrospective study included 174 patients with stage II-III TNBC receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (n = 94) or chemotherapy alone (n = 80), followed by surgery. Pretreatment MRI features underwent redundancy reduction and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) selection. Six candidate models combined radiomic, clinicopathologic, and skeletal muscle predictors. Models were fitted using Firth penalized logistic regression. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples, repeating supervised feature selection, predictor selection, and final-model selection while keeping the 325 radiomic candidates fixed. Area under the curve (AUC), calibration, prediction error, and selection stability were evaluated. Results: Eighty-five patients (48.9%) achieved pCR. Seven radiomic features constituted the score. Corrected AUCs were 0.659 for the clinicopathologic model, 0.622 after adding radiomics, and 0.629 (95% CI: 0.500-0.701) for the fully integrated model (apparent AUC, 0.793). Its corrected Brier score (0.309) exceeded the constant-prevalence benchmark (approximately 0.250). Skeletal muscle density was not independently associated with pCR (p = 0.130) and did not significantly improve AUC over the radiomics-plus-clinicopathologic model (ΔAUC = 0.009, p = 0.428). The fully integrated model was selected in 50.3% of resamples, while 99.9% of selected models contained radiomic information. Conclusions: The radiomic score showed exploratory associations with pCR, but optimism-corrected performance and model stability were limited. Skeletal muscle density did not significantly improve discrimination. External validation is required before clinical application.

articles.title: Preoperative CT Assessment and Perioperative Decision-Making in Gallbladder Lesions: A Descriptive Pathway Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Preoperative CT may not reliably distinguish gallbladder malignancy from inflammatory disease, complicating surgical planning. We examined transitions from CT impressions through operative plans, intraoperative reassessment, index procedures, and subsequent treatment. Methods: This retrospective descriptive study screened 651 consecutive patients who underwent gallbladder surgery by a single surgeon at a tertiary referral center from January 2023 to December 2025. The analytic cohort included 41 patients with indeterminate or suspicious CT impressions or malignancy on final pathology. CT categories were assigned from original radiology reports independently of operative intent and pathology. Results: CT impressions were benign in six patients, indeterminate in 11, and suspicious in 24; malignancy was confirmed in six, three, and 16, respectively. Among indeterminate cases, eight had simple cholecystectomy plans, two frozen-guided plans, and one a radical-possible plan; all three malignant cases had conditional oncologic plans. Frozen section was performed in 11 patients, identifying malignancy in nine. Of 19 extended index procedures, 18 were performed under plans allowing oncologic extension; one represented an unanticipated extension. Six patients with T1b or more advanced cancer initially underwent simple cholecystectomy; three subsequently underwent completion surgery. Conclusions: Patients with the same CT impression followed different operative and subsequent management pathways. These findings highlight the clinical importance of considering diagnostic uncertainty throughout the surgical course, from preoperative planning and intraoperative reassessment to subsequent treatment decisions informed by final pathology.

articles.title: Eosinophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio as a Potential Inflammatory Marker Associated with Endometrial Cancer: An Analysis of NHANES 2017-2023 and an Independent Institutional Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluates the Eosinophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (ELR) as a systemic inflammatory marker associated with endometrial cancer using a two-stage approach combining a national population-based discovery analysis of self-reported uterine cancer (NHANES) and an independent institutional cohort of histologically confirmed endometrial cancer. Methods: In the discovery cohort, survey-weighted logistic regression was conducted among 6859 women from NHANES 2017-2023, comparing 6757 non-cancer controls with 102 women with self-reported gynecological cancers (45 cervical, 38 uterine, and 19 ovarian); the uterine cancer model was adjusted for age and BMI. In the independent institutional cohort, 901 patients with histologically confirmed primary endometrial cancer and 200 benign surgical controls were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test, unadjusted logistic regression, and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Adjusted analyses were not performed in this cohort. Results: In NHANES, mean ELR was higher in the uterine cancer group than in controls (0.1204 vs. 0.0868, p = 0.0193). After adjustment for age and BMI, ELR was associated with higher odds of self-reported uterine cancer (OR = 10.288 per 1.0-unit increase, 95% CI: 1.722-61.472, p = 0.0130; equivalent to OR = 1.26 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI: 1.06-1.51). In the institutional cohort, median ELR was significantly higher in endometrial cancer patients than in benign controls (0.1180 [IQR: 0.1380] vs. 0.0487 [IQR: 0.0574], p < 0.001). Unadjusted logistic regression showed that higher ELR was associated with endometrial cancer (OR = 2.725 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI: 2.154-3.515, p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed moderate discriminative capability (AUC = 0.7147, 95% CI: 0.6780-0.7514), with an exploratory (non-validated) cut-off of 0.0810 (sensitivity: 65.5%; specificity: 74.8%). Conclusions: Higher ELR was associated with self-reported uterine cancer in NHANES after adjustment for age and BMI, and with histologically confirmed endometrial cancer in an unadjusted institutional analysis, with moderate discriminative performance. These hypothesis-generating findings do not establish an independent association; ELR may be a candidate complementary, non-invasive marker, but its clinical utility requires confirmation in adjusted, prospective studies.

articles.title: Integrating a Transdiagnostic Clinical Approach with Whole-Exome Sequencing in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Single-Center Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodevelopmental disorders overlap in cognitive, language, motor, behavioral and social-communication features and vary widely in their genetic causes, which limits etiological research and patient stratification. We investigated whether grouping patients by data-driven clinical profiles rather than by diagnosis points to different biological pathways. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated a single-center cohort of 128 patients, grouping them into diagnosis and genetics-independent clinical profiles and into six overlapping DSM-5 diagnostic groups. In each group, the genes carrying a causative variant found by whole-exome sequencing were linked to the biological pathways they belong to. Data on variants of uncertain significance (VUS) were available for 113 of the 128 patients, in whom we counted VUS in these pathways. Each group was compared with the other patients by Poisson regression accounting for each patient's total VUS count. Analyses were repeated in patients with high-confidence profile assignments. Results: Four clinical profiles were identified (labeled C1-C4), and 89.1% of patients were assigned to one with high confidence. A pathway was considered enriched in a group when the group's patients carried more VUS in it than other patients (p < 0.05, uncorrected). The profiles yielded one enriched pathway, Transcriptional Regulation by MECP2 in profile C3 Social-Sensory/Repetitive (IRR 1.46, 95% CI 1.06-2.03; p = 0.0223); the diagnoses yielded 21, including the same pathway, which emerged in ADHD rather than in ASD, the diagnosis closest to C3. In the high-confidence subset, Myogenesis appeared in C4 Motor-Neurological, with no diagnostic counterpart. No association survived multiple testing. Conclusions: The two groupings proved complementary rather than alternative: both pointed to Transcriptional Regulation by MECP2, and each raised hypotheses the other missed. All these hypotheses require independent replication and functional or epigenomic validation.

articles.title: Serum Zinc Concentration in Relation to Asthma Control and Treatment-Step-Based Severity in Adults: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Zinc supports immune homeostasis and participates in antioxidant defense and the regulation of inflammatory responses. Lower circulating zinc has been reported in asthma, mostly in children; its relation to disease control in adults is unclear. Objective: We examined serum zinc concentrations in relation to symptom control and treatment-defined disease severity in adults with asthma and whether any association with control was independent of potential confounders. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study of 145 adults with asthma, serum zinc was compared between controlled (Asthma Control Test [ACT] > 19) and uncontrolled asthma and across treatment-step categories, using regression models adjusted for age, sex, C-reactive protein (CRP), smoking, and treatment step. Results: In the crude analysis, zinc was higher in controlled than in uncontrolled asthma (mean difference 6.7 µg/dL, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.0 to 12.3), and zinc < 70 µg/dL was more frequent in uncontrolled asthma (18.6% vs. 5.8%). After full adjustment, these associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant (mean difference 3.1 µg/dL, 95% CI -2.6 to 8.8). Zinc was lower at higher treatment steps in the unadjusted comparison (p = 0.0497), but this difference was not significant after adjustment for age (p = 0.277), and exploratory comparisons were imprecise. Conclusions: Higher serum zinc was associated with controlled asthma only in unadjusted analyses. These findings do not establish an independent or causal relationship, and whether zinc supplementation improves asthma control requires further study.

articles.title: Real-Time Machine Learning Model to Predict Cardiac Arrest Within 12 Hours in Critically Ill Patients (DeepiCARS): A Confirmatory Trial and External Validation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Continuous prediction of cardiac arrest in the intensive care unit (ICU) must be judged by considering alarm burden as well as discrimination. We evaluated DeepiCARS (iCARS), an approved recurrent-network and gradient-boosting ensemble, developed at one centre and temporally validated there, predicting in-ICU cardiac arrest within 12 h. Methods: The unchanged model was assessed in a retrospective 1:1 matched confirmatory trial at that centre (214 adults, 107 with arrest), which assigned no intervention and required no registration, and in 30,487 adult ICU admissions at an independent Korean tertiary centre (2010-2021; 2782 with an in-window arrest: 653 with cardiopulmonary resuscitation [CPR] and 2129 deaths without CPR), against seven conventional scores, per subject in the trial and per prediction point externally, on discrimination, sensitivity at matched alarm burden, lead time and calibration. Results: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with the extended input (vital signs, Glasgow Coma Scale, age, sex and 21 laboratory values) was 0.9428 (95% confidence interval 0.9102-0.9753) in the trial and 0.9587 (0.9548-0.9626) externally, and with the core (non-laboratory) input 0.9103 (0.8716-0.9490) and 0.9458 (0.9415-0.9500), above every comparator. For arrests with CPR, the external AUROC was 0.8697 (0.8538-0.8854) with the extended input and 0.8425 (0.8264-0.8591) with the core input, above the National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2), 0.7157 (0.6987-0.7319), and the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA), 0.7424 (0.7205-0.7631). At no greater alarm burden than NEWS2 ≥ 7 and SOFA ≥ 11, iCARS with the extended input detected 37.17 (35.75-38.65) and 30.66 (28.76-32.65) percentage points more of the points preceding an arrest, with median lead times within the 12 h window of 11.42 h and 11.50 h; the score was already above threshold when the window opened in 53.8% and 58.3% of admissions with an arrest, and first crossed it a median of 72.42 h and 80.84 h before the arrest. Conclusions: Evaluated unchanged, the approved model retained high discrimination externally, including for arrests with CPR, and detected more of the points preceding an arrest than conventional scores at no greater alarm burden. No operating threshold is proposed.

articles.title: Clinical, Functional, and Radiological Evaluation of Pulmonary Involvement in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis.
articles.abstract: Background: Pulmonary involvement is one of the most serious extra-articular manifestations of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), frequently remaining clinically silent until irreversible lung damage develops. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT)-detected pulmonary involvement in patients with RA; compare the clinical, laboratory, and pulmonary function characteristics of patients with and without pulmonary involvement; and identify factors associated with pulmonary abnormalities. Methods: In this single-center retrospective cross-sectional study, 141 patients fulfilling the 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for RA who had undergone thoracic HRCT were included. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, disease activity scores, pulmonary function tests, and HRCT findings were compared between patients with and without pulmonary involvement. Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of pulmonary involvement, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the diagnostic performance of serum uric acid. Results: HRCT identified pulmonary involvement in 33 of 141 patients (23.4%), with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia being the most common radiological pattern (39.4%), followed by usual interstitial pneumonia (24.2%). Patients with pulmonary involvement had significantly higher serum uric acid concentrations (5.65 ± 1.62 vs. 4.51 ± 1.31 mg/dL, p < 0.001), lower serum albumin levels (38.8 ± 4.9 vs. 40.9 ± 3.5 g/L, p = 0.008), higher platelet counts (p = 0.006), and lower forced vital capacity and predicted FEV1 values (p = 0.010 and p = 0.019, respectively). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, serum uric acid remained the only independent predictor of pulmonary involvement (odds ratio, 1.656; 95% confidence interval, 1.187-2.311; p = 0.003). ROC analysis demonstrated acceptable discriminatory performance for serum uric acid (AUC = 0.713), with an optimal cutoff value of >5 mg/dL yielding 68% sensitivity and 70% specificity. Conclusions: Nearly one-quarter of patients with RA demonstrated HRCT-detected pulmonary involvement despite having a similar prevalence of respiratory symptoms. Elevated serum uric acid was independently associated with pulmonary involvement and may represent an inexpensive, readily available biomarker to identify patients who may benefit from targeted pulmonary evaluation. These findings support the integration of simple laboratory markers with clinical assessment to facilitate earlier recognition of RA-associated pulmonary disease.

articles.title: The Potential of Large Language Models in Gynecologic Oncology Telephone Triage.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Nurse-led telephone triage, frequently guided by the United Kingdom Oncology Nursing Society (UKONS) tool, is a cornerstone of supportive oncology care, yet the appropriateness of triage decisions varies across settings. Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in medical communication but remain unvalidated for autonomous clinical decision-making, particularly in gynecologic oncology, where remote and telephone-based care pose distinct challenges. Methods and Materials: Twenty fictitious case vignettes representing common treatment-related toxicities in gynecologic oncology were developed. Three board-certified gynecologic consultants independently assigned UKONS Red-Amber-Green (RAG) triage categories, reaching unanimous consensus that served as the reference standard. Vignettes were submitted verbatim, as single-turn queries with no follow-up prompting, to three publicly available LLMs (OpenEvidence, ChatGPT, Google Gemini). LLM responses were mapped to RAG categories and compared descriptively against the reference standard, stratified by treatment type and platform. Results: All three LLMs achieved 100% concordance with the reference standard for all Red cases across both treatment groups, with no high-acuity case downgraded to self-care. Discrepancies clustered at lower-acuity boundaries. In the chemotherapy-alone group, errors were limited to omission of an explicit 24-h follow-up window for 1 Amber-rated complaints. In the combined group, all LLMs over-triaged intermediate-risk complaints toward immediate or same-day evaluation; low-risk complaints showed more variable over-triage. Conclusions: LLMs identified unambiguous emergent gynecologic oncology symptoms, preserving the UKONS safety floor, but showed relatively reduced precision and a conservative over-triage bias at lower-acuity margins, especially in the combined-therapy collective. These findings support a supervised, adjunctive role for LLMs, rather than autonomous deployment, pending prospective validation.

articles.title: Lactylation-Related Biomarkers in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: Association of Serum HMGN2 with Prevalent Heart Failure and Its Diagnostic Performance.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lactate and lactylation are associated with the development of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). This study aimed to identify potential lactylation-related biomarkers with diagnostic and prognostic value in patients with HFrEF. Methods: We identified the potential lactylation-related biomarkers for heart failure (HF) by integrating bioinformatics analysis with machine learning algorithms. A total of 251 patients with HFrEF and 210 adults without HF were enrolled to validate the diagnostic values of lactylation-related biomarkers at both the mRNA and protein levels. Results: Bioinformatics analysis and machine learning identified EIF4G1, HLTF, HMGN2, LSP1, and PPM1G as hub lactylation-related genes in patients with HF. In the external validation cohort, elevated serum high-mobility group nucleosomal-binding domain 2 (HMGN2) levels were significantly associated with HFrEF. Beyond its diagnostic utility in HFrEF, HMGN2 was associated with prevalent HFrEF (AUC 0.81, 95% CI 0.77-0.85). In exploratory 12-month follow-up, higher HMGN2 was associated with poor outcomes. Conclusions: HMGN2 is a lactylation-associated biomarker that is elevated in patients with HFrEF, associated with prevalent HFrEF, and shows promise for risk stratification with diagnostic discrimination.

articles.title: A 3D CBCT-Based Approach to Assessing Effective Radiation Penetration Depth in Intraoperative Electron Radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate characterization of treatment geometry is essential for intraoperative electron radiotherapy (IOeRT) treatment planning. Mobile cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) enables volumetric assessment of intraoperative anatomy beyond conventional point-based measurements. This study compared clinically applied distance measurement techniques with geometric distance descriptors retrospectively extracted from comprehensive three-dimensional CBCT datasets. Methods: Ninety-six patients receiving IOeRT as a tumor-bed boost during breast-conserving surgery were included. Manual CBCT measurements (mCBCT) were compared with mean (USavg) and minimum (USmin) ultrasound measurements per patient. Comprehensive 3D distance extraction was performed in 82 CBCT datasets using an approximated thoracic-wall surface as the geometric reference. Minimum and first-quartile distances were evaluated across the complete applicator cross-section and within a 1-cm-diameter inner disk around the central beam axis. Results: The mean paired difference between mCBCT and USavg was 0.3 mm and was not statistically significant, whereas mCBCT measurements exceeded USmin by an average of 1.5 mm. In the principal comparison, the minimum CBCT-derived distance within the inner disk was 1.4 mm smaller than mCBCT. Across the complete applicator area, minimum distances were 9.1-10.7 mm smaller than the clinical measurements. The first-quartile distance across all surface points was 1.4 mm smaller than mCBCT, whereas the corresponding inner-disk difference was not statistically significant after correction. Isodose-atlas-based dose-volume analysis indicated that a 1.5-mm change in assumed penetration depth could correspond to an approximately 7% change in the 90% isodose volume at shallow depths. Conclusions: Clinical CBCT and ultrasound measurements showed small group-level differences but substantial patient-level variability. Comprehensive 3D CBCT analysis revealed spatial variations in tissue depth not fully represented by the clinical measurements, highlighting the limitations of characterizing treatment geometry using a single distance. Although anatomical accuracy and patient-specific dosimetric consequences remain to be established, these findings support the potential of intraoperative 3D CBCT to advance IOeRT toward individualized, image-guided treatment planning.

articles.title: Per-Lesion Mask-Supervised Attention for Multi-Label Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Detection.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning models for diabetic retinopathy (DR) usually report a severity grade, and their attention maps explain that grade rather than individual lesions. We aimed to detect microaneurysms, hemorrhages, hard exudates and soft exudates (cotton-wool spots) separately, each with an attention map trained to fall on that lesion. Methods: An EfficientNet-B4 and Transformer encoder, pretrained on severity grades, feeds four lesion queries that each return a score and an attention map; a localization loss trains each map toward its lesion mask. We trained it on DDR and TJDR, tested it on their test sets and on two external sets (IDRiD and e-ophtha), and compared it with a U-Net. Results: The mean areas under the curve (AUCs) were 0.93-0.94 for hemorrhages, 0.90-0.96 for hard exudates and 0.81-0.90 for soft exudates; microaneurysms reached 0.91-0.96, except on DDR (0.58). We analyze this drop in detail. Attention ranked lesion pixels above the rest of the retina with an AUC-Judd of 0.948-0.996. Without the localization loss, detection was slightly lower, and attention moved to regions outside the lesions that still raised the prediction. The model detected lesions better than U-Net (mean AUC of 0.876 against 0.853) and, unlike the latter, also learned from images that have labels but no masks: with masks on half of the training images, detection and AUC-Judd were nearly unchanged. Conclusions: Supervising each lesion's attention with its own mask gives a per-lesion score and a map that falls on that lesion, without reducing detection.

articles.title: Galvanic Vestibular-Evoked Myogenic Potentials in Unilateral Vestibular Schwannoma: Paired-Ear Differences and Contralateral Abnormalities.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To characterize paired-ear vestibular-evoked myogenic potential (VEMP) response patterns and contralateral abnormalities in patients with MRI-confirmed unilateral vestibular schwannoma (VS). Methods: This exploratory retrospective paired-ear study included 24 patients with unilateral VS confirmed by contrast-enhanced MRI. Patients underwent pretreatment pure-tone audiometry, caloric testing, air-conducted sound cervical VEMP (ACS-cVEMP), bone-conducted vibration ocular VEMP (BCV-oVEMP), galvanic vestibular stimulation cervical VEMP (GVS-cVEMP), and GVS-oVEMP. Tumor-affected and contralateral non-tumor ears were compared using McNemar's and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Age was compared by contralateral VEMP status using Mann-Whitney U tests. All p values were unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Results: Hearing loss and caloric abnormalities were more frequent in tumor-affected ears (91.7% vs. 20.8% and 62.5% vs. 8.3%, respectively; both p < 0.001). Abnormality rates were higher in tumor-affected than contralateral non-tumor ears for ACS-cVEMP (83.3% vs. 45.8%; p = 0.022), GVS-cVEMP (70.8% vs. 20.8%; p = 0.002), and GVS-oVEMP (70.8% vs. 16.7%; p = 0.002), whereas the BCV-oVEMP difference was not significant (62.5% vs. 33.3%; p = 0.092). Tumor-affected ears showed prolonged GVS-cVEMP p13 latency (median, 12.47 vs. 11.35 ms; p = 0.008) and reduced amplitude (median, 59.02 vs. 66.24 μV; p = 0.044). Patients with contralateral ACS-cVEMP abnormalities were older than those with normal responses (median, 62 vs. 45 years; p = 0.001); age did not differ significantly by contralateral GVS-VEMP status. Conclusions: In this exploratory paired-ear study, GVS-cVEMP abnormalities were more frequent in tumor-affected ears, and the observed contralateral abnormality rate was numerically lower than that for ACS-cVEMP. GVS-cVEMP may complement conventional VEMPs when contralateral abnormalities complicate interpretation. These preliminary findings require validation in larger prospective controlled studies.

articles.title: CBCT-Based Assessment of Tooth Morphology and Dental Arch Dimensions Across Skeletal Class I, II, and III Malocclusions: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Three-dimensional data that evaluate tooth morphology and dental arch dimensions together across sagittal skeletal patterns are limited. This cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) study compared tooth morphology and dental arch dimensions among skeletal Class I, II, and III malocclusions and examined their relationships. Methods: This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 111 individuals (37 per group; 24 females and 13 males in each group), selected from archived CBCT records in reverse chronological order with sex-frequency matching. Skeletal class was based on the ANB angle. Crown length, root length, and mesiodistal width of the central incisors, canines, second premolars, and first molars, together with arch perimeter and intercanine, inter-second premolar, and intermolar widths, were measured. Groups were compared using patient-clustered Gaussian generalized estimating equations with Holm-adjusted contrasts and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction across 35 outcomes; 108 tooth-arch associations were adjusted for class, age, and sex. All analyses were exploratory. Results: Five of 35 outcomes showed nominal class effects (p < 0.05), mainly in the mandible (central incisor and canine crown lengths, arch perimeter, and intercanine width), but none remained significant after FDR correction (q ≥ 0.169). In exploratory contrasts, mandibular arch perimeter was greater in Class III than in Class I (2.20 mm; 95% CI 0.56-3.85). In the primary models, no mesiodistal width or root length differed nominally. Nine of 108 tooth-arch associations remained significant after FDR correction (standardized β 0.27-0.36), six involving premolar and molar mesiodistal widths. Conclusions: No difference in tooth morphology or arch dimensions among skeletal classes remained significant after multiplicity correction; the nominal mandibular findings are exploratory. The findings are descriptive, cannot establish causality, and do not support class-specific treatment recommendations.

articles.title: Serial Red Cell Distribution Width and Mortality After TAVR: An Observational Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Preprocedural red cell distribution width (RDW) is associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), but the prognostic relevance of serial measurements and native leaflet morphology remains uncertain. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 1369 patients who underwent native-valve TAVR from January 2019 to October 2023. The primary analysis evaluated baseline RDW-coefficient of variation (RDW-CV) and mortality in the overall cohort. Exploratory landmark analyses examined postprocedural RDW-CV changes among survivors with repeat measurements. Valve-disease phenotype and leaflet morphology were evaluated as potential effect modifiers. Results: During a median reverse Kaplan-Meier follow-up of 58.7 months, 196 patients died. Higher baseline RDW-CV was associated with mortality over all follow-up (adjusted HR per 1-SD increase, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.02-1.34; p = 0.022). After adjustment for baseline RDW-CV and clinical covariates, greater increases at 3 months (HR per window-specific 1-SD increase, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.20-1.94; p < 0.001) and 6 months (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.08-1.73; p = 0.009) were associated with subsequent mortality. Exploratory analysis suggested a stronger 6-month association in bicuspid than tricuspid valves (HR, 2.47 [95% CI, 1.65-3.69] vs. 1.02 [0.75-1.40]; interaction p = 0.002). Adding 6-month RDW-CV change increased the cross-validated 2-year AUC from 0.628 to 0.651. Conclusions: Baseline RDW-CV was associated with mortality after TAVR. Among patients with repeat testing, increases at 3 and 6 months were associated with subsequent mortality, with an exploratory stronger association in bicuspid aortic valve.
