Standardized prospective sampling is required to confirm these longitudinal findings.

articles.title: Tomographic Evaluation of Temporal Bone Pneumatisation with Sinus Variations.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Temporal bone pneumatisation and paranasal sinus variations have mostly been studied separately. This study evaluated temporal bone pneumatisation with frontal, ethmoid and sphenoid sinus variations using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and investigated relationships among these structures. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study (ethics approval no. 2025/58), 88 CBCT scans of patients aged ≥25 years were analysed. Temporal bone pneumatisation, frontal sinus size, International Frontal Sinus Anatomy Classification (IFAC) cells, ethmoid variants and sphenoid sinus pneumatisation were categorised using established classifications. Bilateral concordance and age-, sex- and inter-regional associations were tested with false discovery rate (FDR) correction, and exploratory Firth regression and multiple correspondence analysis were performed. Results: The sample comprised 49 females and 39 males (mean age 41.6 ± 13.3 years). Bilateral concordance was good for supra-bulla (κ = 0.76), supraorbital ethmoidal (κ = 0.61) and agger nasi cells (κ = 0.60) and moderate for temporal pneumatisation (κw = 0.56). The frontal sinus was larger on the left side (FDR-adjusted p = 0.002). No age-, sex- or inter-regional association survived FDR correction. In exploratory regression, male sex was associated with frontal septal cells (adjusted odds ratio [ORadj] = 3.75, 95% CI 1.36-11.15) and right supraorbital ethmoidal cells (ORadj = 3.48, 95% CI 1.35-9.62). Multiple correspondence analysis revealed no single dominant dimension. Conclusions: Temporal bone and paranasal sinus pneumatisation showed marked bilateral concordance, but no inter-regional association survived correction for multiple testing. The sex differences in frontal septal and supraorbital ethmoidal cells are hypothesis-generating and need confirmation in larger samples.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Colonoscopy-Sparing Potential of RAID-CRC Screen After a Positive Faecal Immunochemical Test.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Faecal immunochemical test (FIT)-based colorectal cancer (CRC) screening generates many colonoscopy referrals without advanced neoplasia. We evaluated RAID-CRC Screen, a qPCR-based faecal bacterial signature, as second-line triage after positive FIT in the Galician population-based screening programme. Methods: This cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study included participants with FIT ≥ 100 ng haemoglobin/mL and colonoscopy as reference standard. RAID-CRC Screen was analysed from residual FIT-buffer material. The primary analysis included evaluable assays and complete colonoscopy. An additional intention-to-diagnose analysis assigned non-evaluable results to colonoscopy referral. Comparisons with data-derived alternative FIT thresholds were exploratory. Results: Among 1291 participants in the primary analysis, 34 (2.6%) had CRC and 441 (34.2%) advanced neoplasia. RAID-CRC Screen was positive in 1087 (84.2%). Sensitivity was 94.1% (95% CI, 80.3-99.3%) for CRC and 87.5% (84.1-90.5%) for advanced neoplasia; specificities were 16.1% (95% CI, 14.1-18.2%) and 17.5% (95% CI, 15.0-20.3%), respectively. RAID-CRC Screen after FIT100 would avoid 204 colonoscopies (15.8%; 95% CI, 13.9-17.9%) while missing two CRCs and 55 advanced neoplasms. FIT118 alone would avoid 149 colonoscopies (11.5%), with CRC sensitivity of 100.0% (95% CI, 89.7-100.0%) and advanced neoplasia sensitivity of 92.3% (95% CI, 89.4-94.6%). In the intention-to-diagnose analysis (1312), including 21 non-evaluable results, colonoscopy reduction was 15.5% (95% CI, 13.6-17.6%), with the same two CRCs not referred. Conclusions: RAID-CRC Screen triage reduced modelled colonoscopy referrals at the cost of missed CRCs and advanced neoplasia. FIT118 alone avoided fewer colonoscopies while retaining all observed CRCs. These exploratory comparisons do not establish superiority or the safety of withholding colonoscopy.

articles.title: The Effectiveness of Mechanical Thrombectomy Following the Siriraj Stroke Fast Track Activation Protocol.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has become the standard treatment for ischemic stroke patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO). However, there is limited understanding of the factors influencing outcomes, particularly in the Thai population. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of MT following the Siriraj Stroke Fast Track Activation Protocol and to identify predictors of favorable outcomes. Methods: A single-center prospective cohort study enrolled 120 consecutive patients with LVO who underwent MT between April 2023 and August 2024. The primary outcome was favorable functional status (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 3 months. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors. Results: Among 120 patients (median age 68 years; 53% male), 57% achieved favorable outcomes at 3 months. Successful recanalization (modified Treatment in Cerebral Ischemia ≥ 2b) was achieved in 85%, with first-pass effect in 42%. The mortality rate was 7.5%, and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 3.3%. Multivariable analysis was restricted to pre- and intra-procedural variables and estimated by Firth's penalized-likelihood method. Independent predictors of favorable outcome were successful recanalization (aOR 19.51, 95% CI 2.47-274.05; p = 0.004), absence of diabetes mellitus (aOR 6.22, 95% CI 1.58-32.87; p = 0.008), lower baseline NIHSS (aOR 0.87 per point, 95% CI 0.76-0.96; p = 0.005), and red/mixed thrombus composition (aOR 3.06, 95% CI 1.01-9.96; p = 0.049). Younger age, higher baseline ASPECTS and a minimum intra-procedural diastolic blood pressure ≥ 55 mmHg showed consistent but non-significant associations. Post-procedural measures such as the 24 h NIHSS were deliberately excluded from the model because they lie on the causal pathway to the 3-month outcome. Conclusions: The outcomes of MT at Siriraj Hospital are comparable to those reported in international studies. Successful recanalization, absence of diabetes, lower baseline stroke severity and red/mixed thrombus composition were independently associated with favorable outcome. The thrombus-composition finding is novel in this population but should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation with immunohistochemical and digital-image analysis in larger cohorts. The protocol described here is resource-appropriate and may be transferable to other stroke centers in low- and middle-income settings.

articles.title: High Time for Pathology AI: Practical Considerations for Turning Potential into Practice.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and efficiency in anatomical pathology, but technical success alone does not establish clinical utility. In this Perspective, we examine practical requirements for translating computational pathology tools into routine practice, including prioritization of genuine clinical bottlenecks, representative datasets, independent validation, workflow integration, costs, clinician oversight, regulatory compliance, and post-deployment monitoring. We distinguish evidence from retrospective model evaluations, controlled reader studies, prospective workflow assessments, and economic simulations, recognizing that their conclusions are not interchangeable. We also propose a staged, decision-oriented framework through which laboratories can assess clinical need, select technologies, perform local validation, conduct prospective pilots, deploy with safeguards, and monitor performance throughout the AI lifecycle. Evidence from selected applications is encouraging, but effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and readiness for routine use vary by intended purpose and practice environment. Responsible adoption should therefore be guided by demonstrated clinical benefit, operational feasibility, and ongoing evaluation rather than algorithmic performance alone.

articles.title: MRI-Based Patterns of Meniscal Tears and Associated Intra-Articular Abnormalities in Patients at a Tertiary Care Center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Meniscal tears are common intra-articular knee injuries that arise from acute trauma or degenerative change and frequently coexist with ligamentous and chondral abnormalities. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) allows noninvasive characterization of tear location, morphology, and associated pathology, but MRI-based data from Saudi Arabia are scarce. Objective: To describe the MRI patterns of meniscal tears and associated intra-articular abnormalities and their distribution by age, sex, and mechanism of injury, in patients evaluated at a tertiary care center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, consecutive patients aged ≥15 years with meniscal tears reported on knee MRI at King Abdulaziz Medical City, Riyadh, between January 2020 and December 2023 were included. Data were extracted from original radiology reports and electronic medical records. Groups were compared using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests; unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and p-values were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR). Results: Of 496 patients (65.7% male; mean age 41.8 ± 13.2 years), 60.3% had a traumatic mechanism. The medial meniscus was involved in 415 patients (83.7%; isolated in 69.4%). Horizontal tears were the most frequently reported pattern (27.2%), followed by radial (19.6%) and root (19.4%) tears. Joint effusion (58.7%), anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear (36.1%), and cartilage loss (34.3%) were the most frequent associated findings. Traumatic cases were younger (median 34 vs. 51 years) and more often had isolated lateral meniscal, horizontal, vertical, bucket-handle, and complex tears and ACL tears (49.2% vs. 16.2%; OR 4.99, 95% CI 3.21-7.75), whereas degenerative cases more often had radial, root, and degenerative-pattern tears, cartilage loss (61.9% vs. 16.1%), and joint effusion. These associations remained significant after FDR adjustment. Surgical management was recorded in 67.1% of patients. Conclusions: In this hospital-based sample, meniscal tear patterns and associated MRI findings differed by age, sex, and mechanism of injury. Because the data derive from a single referral center and from original clinical reports, the findings describe a selected population, should not be extrapolated to the general Saudi population, and are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Interpreting Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra in a High-Risk Tuberculosis Referral Cohort in Taiwan: Treatment-Associated Culture Discordance and Rifampicin-Indeterminate Results.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Interpretation of positive and indeterminate rifampicin (RIF) calls from Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra (Ultra) in previously treated, high-risk populations is poorly characterised. Methods: We retrospectively analysed all 2271 Ultra records (2024) at Taiwan's National Reference Mycobacteriology Laboratory, a high-risk referral cohort, against referring-laboratory culture and phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing (pDST), with line-probe assay (LPA) as a reflex test and treatment history defined by referral indication. Results: Among 1662 culture-paired records, sensitivity was 91.7% and specificity 75.1%. Specificity was 92.7% in screening or risk-based referrals but 56.4% in previously or currently treated patients, who accounted for 84.8% of culture-negative Ultra-positive results. Positive predictive value fell from 89.3% (HIGH) to 36.2% (Trace). All 77 Trace results were RIF indeterminate (77 of 78 indeterminate calls). In 362 of 382 pDST-paired records with determinate calls, RIF sensitivity and specificity were 94.3% and 96.8%. Eight of 10 pDST-discordant resistance calls, none sequenced, were LPA-resistant. Reflex LPA was interpretable in 98.9% of resistance-detected records but in 19.2% of indeterminate records. Conclusions: Low specificity was concentrated among previously or currently treated patients, and indeterminate calls reflected Trace detection. LPA supported most pDST-discordant resistance calls, whose mutational basis remains unconfirmed. Stewardship should reflect the limited yield of reflex LPA in paucibacillary specimens.

articles.title: The Evaluation of Developmental Dysplasia of Hip from Pediatric Ultrasound Images by Key Point-Based Deep Learning.
articles.abstract: Background: Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is a common hip disorder in infants. Ultrasound is the primary imaging modality for infants younger than 6 months, but measurements using the Graf and Harcke methods depend on examiner experience. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a key point-based deep learning model for the automated measurement of the Graf α and β angles and femoral head coverage. Methods: A total of 300 standard-plane hip ultrasound images from 165 infants aged 0-6 months were retrospectively collected at a single tertiary center, and reference key points were determined by consensus of pediatric orthopedic surgeons. We developed a dual-branch network, named "DDH-KPNet," which combines a UNet++ convolutional branch and a transformer branch fused with attention modules. Performance was evaluated with fivefold cross-validation at three levels: accuracy of key point localization; intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); and DDH classification. Results: The experimental results demonstrated that Graf-based classification achieved accuracy = 0.903, sensitivity = 0.81, and specificity = 0.9497 (under 95% conference interval); Harcke classification achieved accuracy = 0.942, sensitivity = 0.888, and specificity = 0.968 (under 95% conference interval); and ICCs for α = 0.832, β = 0.728, and coverage = 0.923. Conclusions: The proposed model showed promising agreement with expert measurements under internal validation. Multicenter external validation and independent diagnostic analysis by different physicians are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Ultrasonographic Evaluation of Masseter Muscle Thickness and Fractal Dimension in Bruxist and Healthy Individuals.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to determine whether masseter muscle thickness and ultrasound-derived fractal dimension (FD) differ between patients with bruxism and healthy controls. Methods: Thirty patients with clinically assessed bruxism and 30 healthy volunteers (15 female, 15 male each) were included. Bruxism required a history of tooth grinding or clenching for at least one year plus at least one of three additional findings (tooth wear, masseter tenderness on palpation, morning jaw pain or headache); controls had none of these findings. Bilateral B-mode scans were acquired at rest and during maximum clenching under standardized settings. Thickness was measured with calipers, and FD was calculated by box-counting in ImageJ (version 1.54f) from three 100 × 100-pixel regions of interest per image. Intraobserver reliability was excellent for thickness (ICC = 0.967-0.980) and good for FD (ICC = 0.850-0.929). Results: Thickness was greater in bruxism patients on both sides and in both conditions (p < 0.001; bilateral mean at rest 12.95 ± 1.47 vs. 9.72 ± 1.78 mm). Bilateral mean FD was higher in bruxism patients during clenching (1.202 ± 0.027 vs. 1.182 ± 0.028; p = 0.008), and this difference remained significant after Holm correction across six FD comparisons. The resting difference (1.188 ± 0.026 vs. 1.171 ± 0.031; p = 0.029) was not robust to multiplicity correction or to exclusion of two controls whose regions of interest extended beyond the muscle. Conclusions: Clinically assessed bruxism was associated with greater masseter thickness in this sample. Bilateral mean FD was modestly higher during clenching; the resting FD difference was not robust. The reproducibility and clinical relevance of these texture measures require further study.

articles.title: From Anatomy to Pathology: How Well Can AI Interpret Static Point-of-Care Ultrasound Images?
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multimodal artificial intelligence may support point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) interpretation in emergency medicine, but its performance on static images and sensitivity to acquisition context remain uncertain. This study evaluated GPT-5.6 Sol and assessed whether probe-region information improves interpretation across view/plane, anatomy, and pathology domains. Methods: In this paired comparative in silico study, 92 educational ultrasound images from seven anatomical regions were assessed under standardized uninformed (image only) and informed (image plus probe-region code) prompting conditions. Two independent raters scored responses against textbook-based references in three domains: view/plane identification, anatomical structure identification, and pathological finding detection. Each domain was scored from 0 to 2. Disagreements were resolved by a third ultrasound expert, and fully correct responses were defined as domain scores of 2. The primary outcome was the total performance score (0-6). Secondary outcomes included domain-specific scores, fully correct response rates, and exploratory subgroup analyses. Wilcoxon signed-rank and McNemar tests assessed paired scores and fully correct rates, respectively. Results: Total performance was higher with informed prompting (median (interquartile range), 5 (4-6) versus 4 (2-5); p < 0.001). Interrater agreement was substantial to almost perfect across evaluation domains (quadratic-weighted κ = 0.750-1.000). Fully correct rates increased from 58.7% to 88.0% for view/plane identification and from 47.8% to 82.6% for anatomical structure identification (both p < 0.001). Pathological finding detection improved from 35.9% to 48.9% (p = 0.002). Among pathology-positive images, missed or incorrectly labeled pathology remained frequent (44.8%) despite informed prompting. Regional differences in total performance were significant only under uninformed prompting (p = 0.002). Conclusions: Probe-region information substantially improved view/plane and anatomical structure identification, but pathological finding detection remained comparatively weak. In static POCUS interpretation, improved anatomical recognition did not translate into reliable pathology detection. Persistent false-negative and false-positive errors do not support independent diagnostic use. Potential applications in POCUS education and anatomical labeling require further validation.

articles.title: Large Language Models Versus Clinicians in Predicting Recovery from Idiopathic Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early prognostication in idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL) remains difficult, and although the use of large language models (LLMs) in otolaryngology is being increasingly evaluated, data directly comparing their prognostic predictions with those of clinicians assessing the same patients remain limited. This study evaluated the zero-shot, role-prompted performance of three contemporary LLMs against a panel of board-certified otolaryngologists in forecasting SSNHL outcomes. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated 100 consecutive patients with idiopathic SSNHL and randomly selected 30 for a blinded observer comparison. In the primary cohort of 100 patients, recovery was classified as favorable recovery (complete/partial, n = 37, 37.0%) or poor outcome (slight/none, n = 63, 63.0%) based on functional audiometric utility. Identical de-identified multimodal case sets (n = 30; 9 favorable, 21 poor), including the baseline audiogram image, were independently graded for 1-month recovery likelihood (low/moderate/high) by three otolaryngologists and three zero-shot LLMs-ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol; OpenAI), Gemini (Gemini 3.1 Pro; Google), and Claude (Claude Opus 4.7; Anthropic), accessed through their publicly available web interfaces in July 2026-all blinded to outcomes; actual recovery was classified using the Siegel criteria. Results: In the primary cohort, multivariable logistic regression identified baseline pure-tone average (aOR = 0.957, 95% CI: 0.936-0.979, p = 0.0001) and admission delay (aOR = 0.797, 95% CI: 0.656-0.966, p = 0.0211) as significant independent predictors of recovery (model C-statistic = 0.834, Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.7925). In the sub-cohort (n = 30), Expert 2 achieved the highest overall diagnostic accuracy (86.7%, 95% CI: 70.3-94.7%; sensitivity 95.2%, specificity 66.7%). All three LLMs achieved identical overall accuracy (70.0%) that did not differ significantly from that of individual experts, although the study was not powered to establish equivalence, and all models remained below the best-performing expert (86.7%). Gemini achieved the highest specificity (77.8%, 95% CI: 45.3-93.7%) and the highest positive predictive value (87.5%, 95% CI: 64.0-96.5%) among all raters, and every case it rated as having low recovery potential failed to recover (10 of 10). Conclusions: Zero-shot, role-prompted LLMs predicted 1-month SSNHL outcome with 70.0% accuracy-not significantly different from that of individual experienced otolaryngologists, though the study was not powered for equivalence-and below the best-performing expert. Their reliable "rule-in" but poor "rule-out" pattern warrants prospective evaluation and does not yet support use in treatment decisions.

articles.title: Automatic Detection of Dental Implant Brands and Exposure Status Using Deep Learning on Periapical Radiographs.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dental implant technology has become the primary treatment modality for managing tooth loss in current clinical practice. Accurate identification of implant brands and their clinical exposure status have increasingly emerged as a critical issue in implant-related research and clinical diagnosis. Conventional approaches that rely on clinicians' experience are time-consuming and may lead to misclassification due to variations in image quality or subtle differences in implant design features across brands. Methods: This single-center study classified six categories combining two implant brands (3i and Xive) and three exposure statuses. A retrospective cohort of 497 patients (708 periapical radiographs, 928 implant instances) was partitioned using an 8:1:1 stratified ratio with strict patient-level independence. Following YOLOv8-based implant localization and ROI extraction, classification was evaluated across deep learning backbones using 5-fold cross-validation and compared against a panel of three dental specialists on a test set of 8 complex cases. Results: YOLOv8 achieved a precision of 99.39% and a sensitivity of 98.63% in the implant detection task. For the classification of implant brand and exposure status, EfficientNet-B3 achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 99.18 ± 0.85% (95% CI: [94.20%, 100.00%]) across 5-fold cross-validation, demonstrating competitive diagnostic performance alongside existing implant classification benchmarks in the literature. In a preliminary clinical feasibility assessment on representative cases, the framework demonstrated rapid algorithmic inference (mean inference time of 36.18 ms per image), providing instant decision-support potential alongside participating clinicians. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the technical feasibility and proof-of-concept of a deep learning framework for identifying dental implant brands and exposure status under robust internal validation. While offering preliminary decision-support potential, external validation on multi-center cohorts and prospective clinical trials across expanded implant systems remain necessary before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Interleukin-12 Is Associated with Rheumatoid Factor and Interferon-γ, but Not with Disease Activity, in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis.
articles.abstract: Background: IL-12 is a proinflammatory cytokine produced mainly by activated dendritic cells and macrophages that drives the differentiation of naïve T cells into Th1 cells and stimulates interferon-γ production by natural killer and T cells, thereby linking innate and adaptive immunity. Ultrasensitive quantification of IL-12 has not previously been performed in large rheumatoid arthritis (RA) cohorts, mainly due to the limited availability and high cost of these platforms. In the present study, we measured serum IL-12 using an ultrasensitive assay to systematically assess its relationship with key disease characteristics in a large, well-characterized cohort of patients with RA. Methods: A total of 216 patients with RA were recruited and underwent a comprehensive assessment of disease characteristics and disease activity. Lipid parameters and hematological markers were assessed, insulin resistance indices were calculated, and metabolic syndrome was defined according to established criteria. Arterial stiffness, carotid intima-media thickness, and plaque presence were evaluated through carotid ultrasonography. Serum IL-12 levels were quantified using Simoa (Single Molecule Array) technology. To examine the relationship between clinical and metabolic parameters and IL-12 concentrations, multivariable linear regression models were applied. Results: In multivariable analyses, serum IL-12 levels were independently associated with IFN-γ and rheumatoid factor positivity. However, no significant relationships were found between IL-12 and disease activity indices, acute-phase reactants, cardiovascular risk factors, subclinical atherosclerosis, lipid profile, glucose metabolism, or hematological parameters. Conclusions: Using an ultrasensitive assay, we found that serum IL-12 levels were associated with interferon-γ levels and rheumatoid factor positivity in patients with RA, supporting a role for IL-12 at the interface between cellular and humoral immunity. In contrast, circulating IL-12 did not appear to be a useful systemic biomarker of disease activity or of the cardiovascular and hematological comorbidities associated with RA.

articles.title: Development of Hybrid Deep Learning Systems Combining Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers for Medical Ultrasound Image Classification.
articles.abstract: Background: Accurate classification of thyroid nodule ultrasound images is clinically significant. This study evaluated whether hybrid architectures combining the local feature extraction of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with the global context modelling of vision transformers (ViTs) outperform each category in isolation. Methods: Two public datasets (6905 images; 3331 benign, 3574 malignant) were used. Eleven ImageNet-pretrained architectures were compared: CNN-based (ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B4, ConvNeXt), ViT-based (Swin Transformer, DeiT, PVTv2, XCiT) and hybrid (ConViT, CoaT, MobileViT, HuviT). Backbones were frozen and only the classification head was trained; HuviT's new projection and encoder remained frozen at random initialisation. Wilson and Newcombe 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were computed; explainability used gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Results: ConViT achieved the highest accuracy (83.30%; 95% CI 80.91-85.45) and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 89.94% (95% CI 87.8-91.7). ConvNeXt ranked second (82.63%) but had the highest ROC-AUC (90.02%; 95% CI 87.9-91.8); the intervals overlapped. HuviT reached 76.35%. Grad-CAM for a representative case highlighted lesion areas. Conclusions: While ConViT achieved the highest performance on threshold-based metrics, these findings suggest the potential of specific hybrid designs rather than establishing general superiority of hybrid architectures. Given the retrospective design and the partial association between image source and class label, prospective external validation is warranted.

articles.title: Decreased Circulating Glutamine and Myo-Inositol in Cervical Cancer: Exploratory NMR Metabolomics and Internal Discrimination Using Their Additive Feature (MQ).
articles.abstract: Background: Cervical cancer is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but circulating NMR metabolite signatures require rigorous statistical assessment before clinical interpretation. Methods: Serum metabolite concentrations were analyzed in 33 cervical cancer (CC) cases and 31 normal controls (NC). Group differences across 35 primary metabolites were assessed using Welch's t-test with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) control; Mann-Whitney tests were used as distribution-robust sensitivity analyses. Age-adjusted linear models with HC3 robust standard errors were fitted for each primary metabolite (primary analysis: raw concentrations; sensitivity analysis: log2-transformed concentrations), with FDR correction across the 35 models. MQ was defined as [glutamine] + [myo-inositol]. ROC discrimination was summarized using stratified-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and paired DeLong testing compared MQ with glutamine. Results: Glutamine (CC 229.7 ± 102.2 μM; NC 434.8 ± 123.8 μM) and myo-inositol (CC 18.3 ± 8.8 μM; NC 35.8 ± 11.0 μM) were lower in CC, and both remained significant after age adjustment and FDR correction. Within CC, serum glutamine was strongly inversely correlated with tumor length (Spearman ρ = -0.94, n = 31; exploratory, requires independent replication). Apparent ROC AUCs were 0.906 for glutamine, 0.889 for myo-inositol, and 0.919 for MQ. The paired DeLong comparison of MQ versus glutamine was not statistically significant (AUC difference 0.0132; approximate 95% CI -0.0031 to 0.0295; p = 0.113). Repeated cross-validation is reported as within-cohort resampling performance and not independent validation. Conclusions: The findings support lower circulating glutamine and myo-inositol in this cohort. MQ is an exploratory additive feature without demonstrated superiority over glutamine alone; external validation and adjustment for additional clinical confounders are required.

articles.title: Paranasal Sinus Fractures in Pediatric Head Trauma: A Retrospective CT-Based Analysis of Pattern Distribution, Mechanism Correlation and Associated Intracranial Injury.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pediatric paranasal sinus fractures are often reported within broader craniofacial trauma series. This retrospective cross-sectional descriptive study focused on fracture distribution across the four sinus groups, injury mechanisms, initial management, and associated traumatic intracranial hemorrhage. Methods: Written head CT reports and clinical records from a pediatric emergency hospital in Romania were reviewed retrospectively for 2021-2025. Thirty-eight patients with documented sinus fractures were included. Sinus involvement was coded by anatomical group, with bilateral involvement counted once per group. Traumatic intracranial hemorrhage was defined as hemorrhage documented on the index CT. Analyses were descriptive. Results: Median age was 13 years; 25 patients (65.8%) were male. Maxillary fractures occurred in 31/38 patients (81.6%), frontal fractures in 13 (34.2%), ethmoid fractures in 12 (31.6%), and sphenoid fractures in four patients (10.5%). Eighteen patients had isolated maxillary fractures, three had isolated frontal fractures, and 17 (44.7%) had multisinus fractures. Motor vehicle accidents accounted for 19 injuries (50.0%). Traumatic intracranial hemorrhage was documented in 10 patients (26.3%), including two of seven with posterior table involvement. Eight hemorrhage cases lacked posterior table fractures. Twenty patients received conservative management, 10 underwent other operative interventions, and eight were transferred; no sinus-specific operation was documented at the study institution. Among the 30 non-transferred patients, median hospital stay was six days. Conclusions: Maxillary involvement predominated in this selected pediatric sinus-fracture cohort. Traumatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred with both isolated and multisinus fractures and was usually documented without posterior table involvement. Report-based ascertainment, exclusions with unknown fracture status, and unavailable post-transfer outcomes limit interpretation. These findings support further descriptive investigation in larger cohorts with standardized image review.

articles.title: Who Can Truly Skip the Sentinel Node? A Paired Two-Stage Virtual Tumor-Board Study Among Patients Meeting the 2025 ASCO Clinicopathologic Criteria.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sentinel lymph-node biopsy (SLNB) may be omitted in selected patients with clinically node-negative, early-stage breast cancer; however, the extent to which nodal information still influences contemporary adjuvant-treatment planning remains uncertain. This study aimed to determine whether disclosure of SLNB pathology changed multidisciplinary systemic-treatment and/or radiotherapy recommendations among patients fulfilling study-defined criteria derived from the 2025 American Society of Clinical Oncology omission pathway. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, record-based paired decision-impact study, routine clinical records of consecutive postmenopausal women aged ≥ 50 years who underwent breast-conserving surgery and SLNB between 1 January 2015 and 30 June 2026 were reviewed after closure of the prespecified clinical-record window. Each anonymized case was assessed by a six-member virtual tumor board in two stages: first with SLNB pathology concealed and subsequently, after a six-week washout period, with nodal findings disclosed. The primary outcome was a definitive change in chemotherapy, CDK4/6-inhibitor, and/or radiotherapy recommendation. Paired transitions, interobserver agreement, decision confidence, and pre-SLNB factors associated with management-changing information were evaluated. Results: Among 412 eligible patients, occult sentinel-node deposits were identified in 46 (11.2%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 8.5-14.6%), including isolated tumor cells in seven, micrometastases in 13, and macrometastases in 26. Nodal disclosure produced at least one definitive management change in 28 patients (6.8%; 95% CI, 4.7-9.6%), corresponding to 14.7 SLNB procedures per management-changing recommendation. Twenty-six changes represented treatment escalation. Radiotherapy recommendations changed in 22 patients, CDK4/6-inhibitor recommendations in 13, and chemotherapy recommendations in seven, with overlap between domains. The expanded decision-impact endpoint was reached in 43 patients (10.4%; 95% CI, 7.8-13.8%). Management changed in 0.5% of patients with pN0 disease, none with isolated tumor cells, 46.2% with micrometastases, and 76.9% with macrometastases (p < 0.001). Increasing clinical tumor size was associated with management-changing information (adjusted odds ratio per 5 mm increase, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.07-2.37; p = 0.023). Conclusions: SLNB pathology left definitive adjuvant-treatment recommendations unchanged in more than 90% of selected patients but altered management in approximately one in 15, predominantly through radiotherapy-field selection and CDK4/6-inhibitor consideration. These findings support selective, multidisciplinary implementation of SLNB omission while emphasizing that decision changes do not necessarily represent proven oncological benefit.

articles.title: Incidental Detection of PSMA-Avid Thymic Squamous Cell Carcinoma on [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT During Initial Prostate Cancer Staging.
articles.abstract: A man in his 70s with biopsy-confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma underwent gallium-68-labeled prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-11 ([68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) for initial staging. In addition to intense PSMA uptake in the prostate (maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax], 15.3), PET/CT incidentally revealed a moderately PSMA-avid anterior mediastinal mass (SUVmax, 6.1). Contrast-enhanced chest CT showed a 6.4 cm heterogeneously enhancing anterior mediastinal mass suspicious for an invasive thymic malignancy, with possible invasion of the adjacent lung and pericardium. Multiple left pleural nodules raised concern for pleural metastases. The patient underwent total thymectomy, lung wedge resection, pericardial excision, and pleural nodule biopsies. Histopathology confirmed moderately differentiated thymic squamous cell carcinoma with lung and pericardial invasion and pleural metastasis (pT2N0M1a, TNM stage IVA; Masaoka-Koga stage IVa). Tumor-cell positivity for p40, CD5, CD117 (c-kit), and GLUT1, together with the histopathological and anatomical findings, supported the diagnosis. The patient subsequently completed four cycles of cisplatin, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide chemotherapy, with stable disease in the response assessment, while the concurrent prostate cancer was managed with androgen deprivation therapy. This case illustrates the importance of CT morphology and tissue confirmation when an atypically located PSMA-avid lesion is encountered during prostate cancer staging.

articles.title: Exploring the Interrelationship Among Bone Status Indices: A Structural Equation Modeling Approach Reveals the Role of Osteocalcin as a Marker of Overall Bone Turnover.
articles.abstract: Objective: Bone status indices (BSIs) are key tools to monitor cell metabolic activity but lack specificity for clinical use. By applying a new statistical approach, this study aimed at highlighting the association between osteocalcin (OC), a regulatory molecule of bone turnover, often considered a putative biomarker of bone formation, and bone resorption markers like the β-isomerized C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (β-CTX-I) and urinary lysil-pyridinoline (uLysPYD), also investigating on the impact of vitamin D, age, and sex on their levels. Methods: Path analysis within the Structural Equation Modeling framework was applied to investigate relationships among BSIs. This model hypothesized OC as the outcome variable, affected by the direct effect of β-CTX-I, uLysPYD and 25-hydroxy-vitamin D [25-(OH)D] and by two 25-(OH)D indirect effects, through β-CTX-I and uLysPYD. Results: OC showed positive association with bone resorption markers, also when the model was run separately for sex and age groups. 25-(OH)D negatively associated with each bone biomarker. Age represented an effect modifier for 25-(OH)D relationship with both OC and β-CTX-I: the main differences were observed between the youngest (18-45) and the oldest cohorts (56-65 and >75) in both OC and β-CTX-I relationships with 25-(OH)D, and 46-55 and 66-75 groups in β-CTX-I and 25-(OH)D relationship. Both indirect effects were negative; the main effect of 25-(OH)D on OC was exerted through β-CTX-I. Conclusions: Rather than index of osteoblast activity, OC behaves as an overall turnover marker and possibly associated with resorption in elderly. The osteoclast-mediated bone resorption could impact OC serum levels, as it impacts β-CTX-I.

articles.title: Total Ovarian Volume and Multidimensional Pain in Primary Dysmenorrhea: A Cross-Sectional Ultrasound Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The relationship between ovarian morphology and primary dysmenorrhea is poorly defined. We examined whether total ovarian volume (TOV) differs by dysmenorrhea status and is associated with multidimensional pain burden. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 118 nulliparous women aged 18-24 years, grouped by worst menstrual pain on a 0-10 visual analog scale (VAS ≥ 2, n = 76; control, n = 42). Pain was assessed with the Short-Form McGill Pain Questionnaire (SF-MPQ), and transabdominal ultrasonography was performed on cycle days 2-5. Results: Median TOV was higher with dysmenorrhea (17.04 [12.30-23.48] vs. 11.61 [9.00-15.72] cm3; p < 0.001). Sensory (17.0 [10.0-21.0] vs. 4.0 [1.0-8.0]), affective (4.0 [2.0-6.0] vs. 0.0 [0.0-2.0]), and total SF-MPQ scores (20.0 [13.2-27.0] vs. 4.5 [1.0-10.2]) were all higher (p < 0.001 for each). Each 5 cm3 increase in TOV was associated with higher odds of dysmenorrhea after adjustment for clinical covariates (odds ratio 1.764, 95% CI 1.270-2.681; p = 0.003), although discrimination was modest (area under the curve 0.718). The association was attenuated when restricted to women with bilateral ovarian volumes ≤ 10 cm3. Conclusions: Higher TOV accompanied greater multidimensional pain, but the association was not robust to exclusion of larger ovaries and requires external validation.

articles.title: Circulating Nucleosomes Respond to Moderate Aerobic Exercise: A Pilot Study in Healthy Individuals and Cancer Patients.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating nucleosomes containing H3.1 represent a distinct fraction of extracellular chromatin. Although strenuous exercise is known to increase circulating extracellular chromatin components, it remains unclear whether H3.1-containing nucleosomes also respond to moderate physiological stress and whether this response varies with the underlying biological condition. Methods: Sixteen healthy subjects and 13 subjects with cancer completed a standardized 5 km walking exercise. Venous blood samples were collected immediately before and after exercise, and circulating H3.1-containing nucleosomes were quantified in K2-EDTA plasma with an automated immunoassay. Within-group and between-group comparisons were performed using non-parametric tests. Relative exercise-induced changes and age-adjusted analyses were evaluated as sensitivity analyses. Results: Circulating H3.1-containing nucleosome concentrations increased significantly after exercise in both healthy subjects (p < 0.0001) and those with cancer (p = 0.001). Cancer patients displayed higher baseline concentrations (p = 0.0056), whereas post-exercise concentrations were comparable between groups (p = 0.840). The absolute exercise-induced increase was significantly higher in healthy subjects (p = 0.028). This difference was confirmed when the response was expressed relative to individual baseline concentrations (median increase: 124.7% [IQR 63.9-191.5%] vs. 36.5% [20.6-42.0%]; p = 0.0009) and persisted after age adjustment (p = 0.0046). Conclusions: Circulating H3.1-containing nucleosomes respond to moderate aerobic exercise, with distinct patterns in healthy subjects and those with cancer. These preliminary findings support further investigation of H3.1-containing nucleosomal chromatin as a dynamic marker of the biological response to exercise.

articles.title: Multi-Reference Evaluation of Deep Learning Tumour Segmentation in Multi-Sequence Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma MRI.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning segmentation of nasopharyngeal carcinoma is usually reported as one Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) against one reference mask, although multi-sequence MRI is often delineated separately on each sequence. We aimed to quantify how far the choice of reference changes reported performance, and to compare this with the disagreement between radiologists. Methods: We analysed a public dataset of 277 patient records with separately delineated T1-weighted, T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI, 30 of whom were annotated by two radiologists. Tumour volumes were compared without registration. Spatial agreement was measured after rigid registration, with the loss from transferring masks between acquisition grids estimated separately. nnU-Net models were scored against every reference, including the second radiologist's, in 102 held-out patient records. Results: Without registration, the sequence effect on tumour volume was 10.9%, against a reader effect of 5.7% (ratio 1.9, 95% CI 1.40 to 2.49). After rigid registration, per-sequence references agreed at a median DSC of 0.783, against 0.898 between radiologists; in the double-annotated patient records, the paired gap narrowed only from 0.129 to 0.083 (95% CI 0.063 to 0.111) when grid transfer was matched. One fixed set of predictions scored 0.726, 0.685 and 0.673, depending only on the reference (median per-patient reference spread 0.075), and switching the reference sequence moved scores 2.7 to 3.6 times as much as switching the radiologist. Conclusions: Part of the cross-sequence difference is a difference in what each sequence makes visible rather than annotation error, so a single-reference DSC on multi-sequence data depends on a rarely stated choice. Performance should be reported against every available reference and read against measured inter-reader agreement.

articles.title: Fusion of the Manubriosternal and Xiphisternal Junctions on Computed Tomography: A Probabilistic and Threshold-Based Approach to Age Assessment.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sternal fusion has been studied as an adult age indicator, but findings remain inconsistent, partly because variable fusion processes have been interpreted within deterministic frameworks. We reassessed manubriosternal and xiphisternal fusion on computed tomography (CT) using a probabilistic, threshold-based approach. Methods: Thoracic CT examinations of 512 individuals aged 30-65 years were retrospectively analysed. Manubriosternal fusion was classified on a three-stage ordinal scale and xiphisternal fusion dichotomously. Fusion was examined across five age bands (30-40, 40-50, 50-55, 55-60 and 60-65 years) and for age thresholds of 50, 55 and 60 years using sensitivity, specificity and likelihood ratios (LRs). Results: Manubriosternal fusion overlapped extensively across age bands, with a significant but weak association with age (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001; ε2 = 0.060). Xiphisternal fusion increased from 37.6% (30-40 years) to 77.3% (55-60 years) and plateaued at 75.7% (60-65 years; Mann-Whitney p < 0.001), leaving one quarter of 60-65-year-olds non-fused. Xiphisternal fusion increased the odds of being ≥50, ≥55 and ≥60 years old (odds ratios 3.15, 3.14 and 2.57), but its evidential value was modest (positive LRs 1.38-1.55; negative LRs 0.48-0.54). Adding manubriosternal stage improved discrimination for the ≥55-year threshold in an exploratory model (area under the curve 0.628 to 0.676; p = 0.002). Conclusions: CT-based sternal fusion is unsuitable for deterministic or standalone age estimation. Xiphisternal fusion provides only modest, supplementary information that may be combined with other indicators when CT is already available for clinical or postmortem purposes; it does not justify CT acquisition for age assessment.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Comorbidity in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: The "Excessive Daytime Sleepiness" Phenotype Versus Comorbid Insomnia and Sleep Apnea (COMISA).
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) and comorbid insomnia and sleep apnea (COMISA) are common clinical phenotypes of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). We compared their cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidity. Methods: Cross-sectional, single-center retrospective analysis of adults with polygraphy-confirmed OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥ 5 events/h). The EDS phenotype was defined as an Epworth Sleepiness Scale score ≥ 10 without insomnia (n = 54), and COMISA as OSA with clinically reported insomnia (n = 45). Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with phenotype. Results: OSA severity and the prevalence of any cardiovascular disease (90.7% vs. 86.7%) were similar. In the adjusted model, higher BMI (aOR 0.92 per kg/m2) and cardiac arrhythmias (aOR 0.20) were associated with lower odds of COMISA, and dyslipidemia with higher odds (aOR 2.51). Conclusions: Both phenotypes carry a high cardiovascular burden, but they seem to differ in metabolic profile: severe obesity and an arrhythmic tendency in sleepy OSA, and dyslipidemia in COMISA.

articles.title: Quantitative 3-Dimensional Characterization of Aortic and Carotid Artery Tortuosity in Mucopolysaccharidosis Type IVa: An Exploratory Comparative Imaging Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Vascular involvement has been described in mucopolysaccharidosis type IVa (MPS IVa), but the morphology of the aorta and carotid arteries has not been comprehensively characterized. This study aimed to quantitatively assess aortic and carotid artery tortuosity and kinking using contrast-enhanced three-dimensional (3D) magnetic resonance (MR) angiography. Methods: In this retrospective exploratory comparative imaging study, six patients with confirmed MPS IVa underwent clinically indicated 3D MR angiography of the aorta and supraaortic vessels; two were excluded due to motion artifacts, leaving four patients for analysis. Two radiologists independently assessed vascular kinking and tortuosity. For comparison, 12 age- and sex-matched polytrauma patients without documented vascular abnormalities were retrospectively evaluated using computed tomography angiography. Results: All four patients with MPS IVa showed multiple kinking sites of the descending aorta and increased tortuosity of the common and internal carotid arteries. Aortic tortuosity indices ranged from 2.01 to 2.68. Carotid tortuosity indices were also increased, particularly in the internal carotid arteries. Compared with controls, all assessed tortuosity indices were consistently higher in patients with MPS IVa (exploratory p = 0.001). Despite multiple aortic kinking sites, no marked anatomical luminal narrowing was observed. Conclusions: This exploratory study provides quantitative evidence of differences in aortic and carotid geometry between a small, highly selected MPS IVa cohort and external imaging controls. Larger studies using harmonized imaging protocols and longitudinal follow-up are needed to assess prevalence, disease-specific causation and clinical significance of these findings.

articles.title: Effect of the Measurement Interface on Maximal Expiratory Pressure During Voluntary Cough in Young Adults.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To determine whether there are differences between a nozzle and an oronasal mask in the measurement of maximal expiratory pressure (MEP) during a voluntary cough maneuver in young university students. Methods: Forty university students aged 20-25 years were recruited, comprising 20 males and 20 females. Forced vital capacity and MEP were measured during a voluntary cough maneuver. All participants were assessed using both interfaces. The order of the interfaces used to measure MEP during the voluntary cough maneuver was randomized, once the order was determined, the evaluations were conducted on two separate days: one for the nozzle and another for the oronasal mask. Subsequently, participants were asked to report their perception of air leakage and comfort associated with each device. Results: There was no significant main effect of the interface on MEP after adjusting for gender, peak expiratory flow (PEF), and body mass index (BMI) (F(1.36) = 3.285; p = 0.078; η2p = 0.084). There was a significant interaction between interface and BMI (F(1,36) = 6.391; p = 0.016; η2p = 0.151). Gender and PEF were significantly associated with MEP (gender: F(1,36) = 16.698; p < 0.001; η2p = 0.317; PEF: F(1,36) = 8.985; p = 0.005; η2p = 0.200). Conclusions: In young adults, the measurement interface alone did not significantly alter MEP. The relationship between BMI and MEP varied according to the interface used, as evidenced by the interface × BMI interaction; gender and PEF were significantly associated with MEP.

articles.title: DUET-Net: A Deformable CNN-Transformer with Calibrated Dual Uncertainty for Brain Tumor MRI Classification.
articles.abstract: Background: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a primary modality for brain tumor diagnosis and treatment planning, making accurate automated classification critically important. However, existing deep learning approaches face limitations in prediction reliability, generalization across imaging domains, and calibrated confidence estimation. To address these gaps, we introduce DUET-Net, a hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that integrates six complementary architectural innovations. Methods: First, a multiscale depthwise fusion (MSDF) module aggregates multi-receptive-field context from a single 2D MRI slice using parallel depthwise convolutions at three kernel sizes. Second, domain-adaptive batch normalization (DABN) with input-conditioned mixture weights maintains domain-specific statistics while sharing affine parameters, enabling sample-adaptive generalization across imaging sources. Third, an enhanced convolutional block attention module (CBAM) introduces deformable spatial offsets to adaptively attend to irregular tumor borders. Fourth, a deformable cross-scale attention (DCSA) module combines per-scale learnable spatial offsets with adaptive cross-scale weighting for geometry-aware multi-resolution fusion. Fifth, a hierarchical Vision Transformer encoder coupled with Monte Carlo dropout and a heteroscedastic aleatoric head enables dual uncertainty estimation grounded in the Kendall-Gal framework. Sixth, post-hoc temperature calibration and Grad-CAM++ provide trustworthy confidence scores and visual interpretability. Results: The proposed model achieves 99.51% accuracy on the Kaggle dataset, 95.27% on the Figshare dataset, and 99.89% on the Mendeley dataset with an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.0142. With approximately 48 M parameters and 6.66 GFLOPs, DUET-Net sustains 52.41 FPS and is the only compared method to provide calibrated uncertainty estimation. Ablation, cross-dataset, and uncertainty-formulation comparison studies further validate the reliability of the framework. Conclusions: The potential of our proposed net as a promising approach for reliable computer-assisted brain tumor classification, although further external and prospective clinical validation is necessary before deployment.

articles.title: Admission Prognostic Scores and Endoscopic Findings in Relation to the Two Components of Five-Day Treatment Failure in Acute Variceal Bleeding: An Exploratory Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Five-day treatment failure after acute variceal bleeding combines failure of bleeding control and early rebleeding, which may reflect different clinical processes. We explored whether admission scores and endoscopic findings relate similarly to these components. Methods: All 303 consecutive admissions treated with band ligation at a tertiary centre during 2021-2025 were analysed. Six scores were compared using paired AUROCs and Holm adjustment. Results: Failure occurred in 31 admissions (10.2%): 15 failures of primary haemostasis and 17 rebleeds, with one admission meeting both components. Point estimates of discrimination were higher for rebleeding for all six scores (differences 0.123-0.236), but intervals were wide, and no formal between-component test was performed. No comparison among the six scores using the primary score definitions survived the Holm adjustment for the composite or either component; this does not establish equivalence. Active bleeding at endoscopy was associated with failure of primary haemostasis (odds ratio 4.52, 95% CI 1.40-14.53), whereas its association with rebleeding was uncertain (1.07, 0.40-2.90). Red wale markings showed no clear association. Conclusions: This exploratory pattern suggests that the components may capture different clinical processes, a hypothesis requiring prospective confirmation in a larger cohort. Non-standardised outcome classification, uncertain follow-up after transfer, intervening TIPS and sensitivity to recorded versus recomputed scores limit inference.

articles.title: Indocyanine Green and Technetium-99m: CT-Guided Marking of Lung Nodules Before Robotic-Assisted Lung Resection.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: For stage I non-small cell lung cancer, surgery remains the cornerstone of treatment and the use of minimally invasive techniques is desirable. The lack of tactile feedback in RATS is a well-known drawback of this approach, so precise identification of the disease is crucial for performing lung resection. Methods: We present our retrospective case history, accounting for 83 patients, which were divided into two groups based on marking technique: 99mTc-MAA (99mTechnetium Albumin Macroaggregates) only (Tech group) (22 cases, 26.5%) and 99mTc-MAA + Indocyanine Green (Tech + ICG group) (61 cases, 73.49%). Results: In the Tech group, there were 11 males (50%) ad 11 females (50%), the median nodule diameter was 21.5 mm (IQR 16), and the median distance of the nodule from the visceral pleura was 18 mm (IQR 21). Eighteen out of 22 nodules (81.82%) were subsolid. Three conversions were reported, all due to failure to identify the nodule (13.63%). The mean operative time was 111.6 ± 45.6 min. The histopathological examination resulted in 13 lung adenocarcinomas, one squamous cell carcinoma, two minimally invasive lung adenocarcinomas, two lung adenocarcinomas in situ, three metastases from another tumor, and one benign nodule. In the Tech + ICG group, there were 27 males (44.26%) and 34 females (55.73%), the median nodule diameter was 18 mm (IQR 14), and the median distance of the nodule from the visceral pleura was 24 mm (IQR 15). Forty-six out of 61 nodules were subsolid (75.4%). Four conversions were reported, due to failure in nodule identification (6.55%). The operative time was 105.6 ± 36.8 min. The histopathological examination resulted in 12 lung adenocarcinomas, seven squamous cell carcinomas, nine minimally invasive lung adenocarcinomas, 12 lung adenocarcinomas in situ, one typical carcinoid, seven atypical adenomatous hyperplasias, seven metastases from another tumor, and six benign nodules. The two groups are homogeneous in terms of median nodule diameter (p = 0.676), the median distance from visceral pleura (p = 0.114), SUV max (p = 0.894), operative time (p = 0.512), and nodule characteristics (solid vs. subsolid) (p = 0.724). The conversion rate was lower in the Tech + ICG group (6.55% vs. 13.63%), but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.375). Conclusions: Both techniques appear to be safe and reproducible. Further standardized studies are needed to validate and confirm the results obtained from our case series.

articles.title: Neurofibromatosis Type 1: Clinical and Molecular Characterization in a Romanian Cohort of 80 Patients.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is an autosomal dominant tumor-predisposition disorder with age-dependent manifestations and marked clinical variability. This study characterized clinical observations and documented molecular findings in a Romanian regional referral cohort. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 80 patients referred between 2017 and 2025 because of a family history of NF1 or suggestive clinical signs. Available next-generation sequencing (NGS) and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) results were reviewed, and variants were classified according to ACMG/AMP criteria. Results: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic NF1 variants were reported in 15/80 patients (18.75%): 13/66 children (19.7%) and 2/14 adults (14.3%). Five sequence variants and ten copy-number deletions were identified. Clinical observations included pigmentary, neurodevelopmental, skeletal, dysmorphic, and tumor-related findings. Testing availability and clinical documentation were heterogeneous. Conclusions: The detected molecular spectrum included both sequence and dosage variants. Uneven assay availability limits estimation of the incremental yield of combined testing. Complete diagnostic documentation and age-appropriate follow-up are important for interpreting molecular findings and supporting family counseling.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted ACR TI-RADS and Bethesda-like Risk Prediction for Indeterminate Thyroid Nodules: A Retrospective Proof-of-Concept Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cytologically indeterminate thyroid nodules (Bethesda III-IV) remain a diagnostic challenge. We evaluated the TRAICK (version 1.9.4; TRAICK, Istanbul, Türkiye) artificial intelligence (AI) system, which generates an American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS) category and an imaging-derived Bethesda-like risk category from gray-scale ultrasound images. Methods: This retrospective proof-of-concept study included 52 surgically resected nodules with Bethesda III (n = 29) or IV (n = 23) cytology, with histopathology of the index nodule as the reference standard. The two TRAICK outputs were analyzed separately, and the ACR TI-RADS output was compared with two radiologists using the McNemar and DeLong tests. Results: Twenty-three nodules (44.2%) were malignant on index-nodule histopathology. The TRAICK ACR TI-RADS output had an accuracy of 71.2% (95% CI 57.7-81.7) and an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.762 (0.640-0.884). Its AUC did not differ significantly from that of Radiologist 1 (0.762 vs. 0.777, p = 0.783); specificity was higher (65.5% vs. 37.9%, p = 0.021), whereas sensitivity was lower without a statistically significant difference (78.3% vs. 91.3%, p = 0.250). Compared with Radiologist 2, the TRAICK ACR TI-RADS output had higher accuracy (71.2% vs. 51.9%, p = 0.013), specificity (65.5% vs. 24.1%, p < 0.001), and AUC (0.762 vs. 0.629, p = 0.042). The Bethesda-like output had an AUC of 0.822 (0.707-0.938), with a sensitivity of 60.9% and specificity of 86.2% at the V-VI threshold. In sensitivity analyses, the AUC of the ACR TI-RADS output did not differ significantly from that of Radiologist 1, whereas its AUC advantage over Radiologist 2 was not statistically significant when low-risk neoplasms were classified as malignant. Conclusions: In this small, selected surgical cohort, the TRAICK ACR TI-RADS output showed discrimination that did not differ significantly from that of the more accurate of two experienced radiologists, with higher specificity, and its Bethesda-like output showed promising discrimination. These findings support further study of TRAICK as a complementary aid for preoperative decision-making; independent prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Diagnostic and Clinical Utility of Novel Anti-PAD4 Antibodies in Anti-CCP2-Negative and Anti-CCP2-Positive Rheumatoid Arthritis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains challenging, particularly in anti-CCP2-negative disease. Novel biomarkers, including anti-peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) autoantibodies, have emerged as promising tools for improving diagnostic accuracy in RA patients. The aim of this study was to analyze the performance of the first clinically validated anti-PAD4 assay. Methods: A total of 192 well-characterized RA patients and 383 controls were included in this study and tested for anti-CCP2, RF IgA, and RF IgM (all Phadia, Thermo Fisher) as well as anti-PAD4 IgA and anti-PAD4 IgG by ELISA (laboratory developed test, Exagen, Inc., Vista, CA, USA). Results for the anti-PAD4 IgG ELISA for 143 patients were used for method comparison with a particle-based multi-analyte technology (PMAT, Inova Diagnostics, San Diego, CA, USA). Results: ELISA and PMAT showed moderate-to-good agreement for anti-PAD4 IgG (rho = 0.66; Passing-Bablok slope 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.92; kappa = 0.67). Anti-PAD4 IgG was significantly correlated with anti-PAD4 IgA (rho = 0.47) and weakly correlated with RF IgM (rho = 0.29), RF IgA (rho = 0.28), and anti-CCP2 (rho = 0.22) (all p < 0.001). The PAD4 IgG and IgA ELISAs were validated in the RA population, yielding sensitivities/specificities of 31.8%/92.7% for anti-PAD4 IgG, 18.8%/93.7% for anti-PAD4 IgA, 43.2%/91.1% for RF IgM, 23.4%/96.1% for RF IgA, and 42.2%/99.2% for anti-CCP2, respectively. Anti-CCP2 IgG achieved the highest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.86), followed by RF IgA (AUC = 0.69) and RF IgM (AUC = 0.67). Anti-PAD4 IgG and anti-PAD4 IgA showed modest discrimination (AUC = 0.55 and 0.52, respectively). Among the biomarkers evaluated, anti-CCP2 demonstrated the strongest association with RA (OR = 110.27), followed by RF IgM (OR = 7.40), RF IgA (OR = 7.14), anti-PAD4 IgG (OR = 5.92), and anti-PAD4 IgA (OR = 3.48) (all q < 0.001). In the anti-CCP2-negative population, the strongest association was found for anti-PAD4 IgG (OR = 2.87, q = 0.005), followed by RF IgM (OR = 2.20, p = 0.024). After adjustment for anti-CCP2, RF, age, and sex, anti-PAD4 IgG remained independently associated with RA (OR = 2.69, p = 0.003), with a small gain in discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.02-0.04). Conclusions: Our study established comparability between methods and shows that anti-PAD4 provides modest but statistically significant diagnostic information in the anti-CCP2-negative RA population, independent of anti-CCP2 and RF, in the anti-CCP2-negative RA population, where conventional markers are uninformative.

articles.title: MLFRNet: Multi-Scale Local Feature Refinement Network Using Multi-Scale Depthwise Convolution for HER2 Score Classification.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2) is a key biomarker for selecting treatment strategies in breast cancer patients. In routine pathology workflows, HER2 assessment is performed by pathologists through examination of immunohistochemistry (IHC)-stained sections under a microscope. Manual IHC assessment requires expert interpretation and can be subject to inter-observer variability, which motivates the study of computer-assisted analysis in digital pathology. Methods: MLFRNet uses a ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone with a Multi-scale Local Feature Refinement (MLFR) module that integrates Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), a multi-scale depthwise convolution block (MSB), and a residual refinement block (RB). ECA reweights channel representations without dimensionality reduction, after which MSB applies parallel depthwise convolutions with 3 × 3, 5 × 5, and 7 × 7 kernels to capture complementary spatial contexts. The resulting representation is further processed by RB before classification. Comprehensive experiments were conducted on the HER2-IHC-40× dataset across three prespecified stochastic runs. Results: The mean test accuracy was 96.10 ± 0.22% and the macro-averaged F1-score was 95.30 ± 0.23%. Conclusions: Because the public release does not provide patient or whole-slide identifiers, patient-level and slide-level independence of the partitions could not be independently verified. The reported results should therefore be interpreted as an exploratory patch-level benchmark rather than as patient-level or clinically validated HER2 scoring performance.

articles.title: Calibration-Aware Heterogeneous Multimodal Ensemble for Multi-Class Skin Lesion Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Background: Reliable classification of skin lesions is essential for early melanoma detection; however, substantial visual overlap among lesion types and pronounced class imbalance continue to limit the performance and reliability of existing automated systems. These challenges motivate the integration of complementary visual representations with clinical metadata to improve discrimination across lesion classes. Methods: This study introduces a calibrated multimodal ensemble learning framework for skin lesion classification. The proposed framework combines visual features extracted from Swin Transformer, EVA-02, and CoAtNet architectures with patient age and anatomical region information. A two-stage adaptive temperature scaling is applied to calibrate the predicted probabilities of the ensemble. Results: Experimental evaluation on the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC 2019) dataset demonstrates strong classification performance, achieving a macro-F1 score of 0.91 and a macro-AUC of 0.99. The framework further showed robust generalization on the official ISIC 2019 benchmark set, attaining a balanced accuracy of 0.65. The external validation on the PH2 dataset yielded a macro-F1 score of 0.93 and an ROC-AUC of 0.96. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that combining heterogeneous visual representations, clinical metadata, and calibration-aware ensemble learning provides a robust and trustworthy solution for skin lesion classification and computer-aided dermatological diagnosis.

articles.title: The Effect of the Prognostic Nutritional Index and Triglyceride-Glucose Index for Predicting Mortality in Patients with Stroke.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Stroke is an acute condition in which impaired cerebral perfusion causes focal or global neurological dysfunction. Serious complications are a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in patients with stroke. Malnutrition is common in this population, and nutritional markers, including the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), may be useful for early risk assessment of stroke-associated infections. Insulin resistance (IR) is also an emerging risk factor for stroke and has been associated with poor prognosis through various metabolic and inflammatory pathways. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index has been proposed as a reliable surrogate marker of IR. Various biochemical and clinical parameters are used to assess prognosis in patients with stroke. We investigated the prognostic value of the TyG index and PNI for mortality and early mortality, defined as death within the first 30 days, in these patients. Methods: After application of the exclusion criteria, 415 patients with stroke were included. Demographic characteristics, including age and sex, and comorbidities were reviewed. Complete blood count, biochemical parameters, C-reactive protein, blood gas measurements, and lactate levels were recorded. Brain computed tomography and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging findings were reviewed to classify patients into ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke subgroups. Patients were grouped as survivors or nonsurvivors, and deaths within the first 30 days were classified as early mortality. PNI and TyG index values were calculated using the following formulas: PNI = 10 × serum albumin (g/dL) + 0.005 × total lymphocyte count (cells/mm3); TyG index = ln [fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) × fasting blood glucose (mg/dL)/2]. Results: Of the 415 patients included, 389 (93.7%) had ischemic stroke and 26 (6.3%) had hemorrhagic stroke. The median age was 74 years (IQR, 65.0-81.0), and the sex distribution was balanced: 207 patients (49.9%) were women and 208 (50.1%) were men. The PNI was lower in nonsurvivors than in survivors in the overall stroke cohort (ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke combined; 40.86 ± 8.02 vs. 46.88 ± 6.85, p < 0.001), the ischemic stroke subgroup (41.12 ± 8.77 vs. 46.82 ± 6.83, p = 0.001), and the hemorrhagic stroke subgroup (39.79 ± 3.79 vs. 48.17 ± 7.32, p = 0.006). The PNI was also lower in patients who died within the first 30 days than in survivors in the overall cohort (41.86 ± 8.42 vs. 46.88 ± 6.85, p < 0.001), the ischemic stroke subgroup (42.46 ± 8.90 vs. 46.82 ± 6.83, p = 0.002), and the hemorrhagic stroke subgroup (38.60 ± 4.35 vs. 48.17 ± 7.32, p = 0.012). Conclusions: Biomarkers calculated using simple hematological parameters have a significant impact on mortality and early mortality in stroke patients (both ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke). When we examined the effects of these TyG and PNI markers on mortality in stroke patients in our study, we observed that the PNI had a significant impact on mortality. Although our findings suggest that the PNI independently predicts mortality or could guide risk assessment in the emergency department, we consider this an exploratory observation, as stroke severity measures-such as the NIHSS-and relevant treatment data were not included in our analyses. However, we believe that single-point TyG values do not carry sufficient significance regarding mortality; therefore, future research should take into account cumulative, repeated TyG measurements obtained during patient follow-up.

articles.title: Beyond Cause of Death: Translating Medico-Legal Autopsy Evidence into Risk Mitigation, Organizational Learning, and Institutional Adoption.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Although medico-legal autopsy remains an important source of postmortem evidence for clarifying causes and circumstances of death, identifying diagnostic discrepancies, and evaluating adverse clinical outcomes, its relevance may extend well beyond individual case resolution. Evidence generated after death can contribute to healthcare risk management, organizational learning, and institutional decision-making, yet the mechanisms through which these benefits acquire broader system value remain insufficiently understood. This study therefore examined relationships among medico-legal risk mitigation, financial risk mitigation, organizational learning capability, perceived system value, and institutional adoption intention. Methods: A cross-sectional survey of 1035 professionals working in healthcare, forensic medicine, pathology, legal, and administrative settings in Serbia was analyzed using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, structural equation modeling, and bootstrap mediation analysis. Results: Greater medico-legal risk mitigation was associated with both financial risk mitigation and perceived system value, whereas financial risk mitigation and organizational learning capability independently contributed to perceived system value. In turn, perceived system value showed the strongest direct relationship with institutional adoption intention. Mediation analyses further identified an indirect learning pathway and a sequential mechanism linking medico-legal risk mitigation with institutional adoption through financial risk mitigation and perceived system value. Conclusions: These findings position postmortem evidence as a potential source of diagnostic and organizational intelligence rather than solely as the endpoint of retrospective investigation. Its broader institutional relevance depends on the extent to which evidence generated through autopsy can be translated into risk mitigation, organizational learning, and recognized system value that supports systematic integration into healthcare practice.

articles.title: First-Trimester Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index, APRI and FIB-4 Scores in Women Who Later Develop Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy: Association with the Disease and with Perinatal Outcomes in a Retrospective Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Objective: To examine whether the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), AST-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) score, derived from routine first-trimester tests, are associated with subsequent intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) and, within ICP, with adverse perinatal outcomes. Materials and Methods: This retrospective case-control study included 115 women with ICP and 64 controls with normal liver tests. Indices were derived from 11- to 14-week values. The two primary hypotheses concerned APRI and SII (Bonferroni α = 0.025); all other analyses were exploratory, with false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment. Within ICP, the co-primary outcomes were a composite of preterm birth, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, fetal distress, neonatal intensive care admission or 1-min Apgar score < 7, and the same composite excluding preterm birth, because delivery timing was protocol-driven by bile acids. Results: APRI (AUC 0.786; 95% CI 0.718-0.852; p < 0.001) and SII (AUC 0.615; 0.530-0.697; p = 0.011) were higher in women who later developed ICP; FIB-4 was not. ALT alone discriminated better (AUC 0.895; DeLong p = 0.003), APRI and SII added no discrimination beyond ALT (AUC 0.904; p = 0.465), and when cases were restricted to the transaminase range of controls (ALT ≤ 31 U/L), the AUC of APRI fell to 0.644. Within ICP, no index demonstrated an association with either composite outcome (all FDR-adjusted q > 0.15), although power was only ~45% for an AUC of 0.60. Bile acids were associated with the composite excluding preterm birth (AUC 0.681; adjusted OR 1.43 per 10 µmol/L; 1.16-1.76); the stronger association with the full composite (AUC 0.754) is partly definitional. Conclusions: First-trimester APRI and SII carry a group-level signal in women who later develop ICP, but this signal largely reflects transaminases and is inflated by control selection. The indices did not demonstrate an association with perinatal outcomes, although small effects cannot be excluded; surveillance and delivery timing should continue to rely on bile acids.

articles.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-Generated Simplifications of Shoulder MRI Reports: Assessments by Orthopedic Surgeons and Non-Healthcare Volunteers.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To evaluate ChatGPT-generated (GPT-5) simplifications of shoulder MRI reports from the perspectives of orthopedic surgeons and non-healthcare volunteers. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, 100 de-identified shoulder MRI reports issued between June 2024 and June 2025 were simplified with ChatGPT in February 2026 using a standardized prompt. Between 10 March and 10 April 2026, three orthopedic surgeons independently rated each simplified text against the original report for accuracy, completeness, understandability, and misleading potential on a 5-point Likert scale (higher scores indicating better ratings). In a second arm, 100 adult non-healthcare volunteers each reviewed one simplified report and completed a six-item questionnaire on perceived clarity, comprehensibility, usefulness, and appropriateness. Results: Median expert scores were 5.0 in all domains, and all three raters assigned scores ≥ 4 in 86-98% of reports. Gwet's AC2 ranged from 0.93 to 0.98, whereas Krippendorff's α ranged from -0.02 to 0.05. Among volunteers, agreement ranged from 47% for understanding report terms to 80% for the appropriateness of the text. Health literacy correlated positively with most items (r = 0.329-0.429, p ≤ 0.001), and age correlated negatively with understanding report terms (r = -0.352, p < 0.001). Conclusions: The simplified reports were rated favorably by orthopedic surgeons and were perceived as useful by non-healthcare volunteers. However, the study was limited by its single-center design, the use of a single model and prompt, the absence of a comparison with the original reports in the volunteer arm, and the reliance on self-reported rather than objectively tested comprehension; therefore, it does not demonstrate improved patient comprehension or clinical safety. Such texts should supplement, not replace, the original report and physician consultation.

articles.title: Aspects of Dental Occlusion in Young University Students with Temporomandibular Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Temporomandibular dysfunction (TMD) has a multifactorial aetiology, and the contribution of dental occlusion remains controversial.
