The objectives of the study were to estimate the proportion of students at the Faculty of Dentistry in Craiova with Fonseca Anamnestic Index (FAI) scores suggestive of TMD-related manifestations and to highlight possible associations between dental occlusion and FAI scores in a selected subset. Methods: A total of 106 students completed the Romanian version of the FAI. Three participants declined further participation after completing the questionnaire and before FAI scoring; their responses were not scored. The remaining 103 questionnaires were included in the FAI analysis. Following the screening, a study group of 20 students was selected from the upper end of the recorded score distribution, and a control group of 20 was selected from the lower end; 17 controls scored zero and three scored five. Static and dynamic occlusal parameters were assessed with T-Scan III where valid recordings were available. Between-group comparisons and Spearman correlations were performed, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate adjustment within defined exploratory test families. Results: The study showed that 43 of 103 students (41.75%) had FAI scores suggestive of TMD-related manifestations after the discrepant totals had been reconciled with the source questionnaires. In the selected groups, maximum intercuspation occlusion time (p < 0.001; q = 0.015), protrusive disclusion time (p = 0.003; q = 0.020), and active premature contacts during right and left lateral excursions (both p = 0.002; q = 0.015) differed after adjustment. Conclusions: Occlusal assessment with the T-Scan III System showed that differences between the selected study and control groups were more evident for dynamic parameters than for static occlusal-force distribution. The FAI does not establish a clinical TMD diagnosis, and the exploratory cross-sectional design does not support causal or therapeutic conclusions.

articles.title: FetalSegNet: Automatic Segmentation of the Fetus and Sub-Anatomical Structures in Prenatal Ultrasound Images Using Hybrid Deep Learning Models.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Automatic segmentation of fetal anatomical structures in prenatal ultrasound images is challenging because of low tissue contrast, noise caused by speckles, anatomical variability and the fact that structures are only partially visible within individual image frames. This study has developed and evaluated FetalSegNet, a multi-label deep learning framework that can simultaneously perform segmentation of the fetus and selected sub-anatomical structures, including the head, arms, legs and heart. Methods: A dataset comprising 3321 prenatal ultrasound images obtained from 217 patients was created, with pixel-level annotations generated under expert supervision. FetalSegNet was implemented using four hybrid encoder-decoder configurations that combine EfficientNetV2-M and MaxViT-S encoders with UNet++ and Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) decoders. Performance was evaluated on an unseen test set using Dice score, intersection over union (IoU), precision, recall, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) and average symmetric surface distance (ASSD). The presence of anatomical structures was also assessed using classification metrics, while HiResCAM was used to examine the spatial relevance of model activations. Results: Among the FetalSegNet configurations, the EfficientNetV2-M-UNet++ model achieved the highest overall segmentation performance, with a Dice (DSC) score of 0.9232, IoU of 0.8746, HD95 of 4.23 mm, and ASSD of 1.02 mm. Class-specific results indicated better performance in segmentation for the head and fetus, whereas the leg and heart classes showed comparatively poorer and more inconsistent results. The models also achieved high F1-scores and a high level of accuracy in assessing the presence of anatomical structures. HiResCAM analyses showed that model activations were predominantly concentrated within the corresponding anatomical regions. Conclusions: FetalSegNet provides a unified, multi-label framework for simultaneously segmenting the fetus and multiple sub-anatomical structures in prenatal ultrasound images. By combining a hybrid deep-learning architecture with independent output-mask channels, comprehensive boundary-based evaluation, and activation-based interpretability analysis, the framework offers an integrated strategy for fetal anatomical segmentation. These findings support further investigation of FetalSegNet for automated and interpretable analysis of prenatal ultrasound images.

articles.title: Histoanatomic and Quantitative Substaging of Lamina Propria Invasion in pT1 Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma: Associations with Recurrence and Progression.
articles.abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate lamina propria invasion in pT1 bladder urothelial carcinoma using different substaging methods and to compare the relationships of these methods with recurrence and progression. Methods: In 140 retrospectively evaluated cases of pT1 urothelial carcinoma, muscularis mucosae-based histoanatomic substaging, maximum invasion depth, maximum horizontal invasion width, number of invasive foci, and T1m/T1e-based micrometric classifications were examined. Results: Recurrence was detected in 55 patients (39.3%) and progression in 30 patients (21.4%). No significant difference was found among the histoanatomic substaging groups with respect to recurrence rates (p = 0.884), whereas the progression rate was markedly higher in the pT1c group compared with the pT1a and pT1b groups (52.2%; p < 0.001). In the logistic regression analysis adjusted for age and tumor number, pT1c was independently associated with progression compared with pT1a (OR 6.999; 95% CI 2.328-21.044; p = 0.001). Maximum invasion depth and maximum horizontal invasion width were also significantly higher in cases that developed progression and retained their independent associations with progression in the adjusted models. For each 1 mm increase, the OR was 1.209 (95% CI 1.063-1.375; p = 0.004) for maximum invasion depth and 1.084 (95% CI 1.007-1.167; p = 0.033) for maximum horizontal invasion width. An increasing trend in progression toward T1e was observed in the T1m/T1e classifications, but this did not reach significance in the adjusted models. Conclusions: Our findings support that both pT1c invasion extending beyond the muscularis mucosae and continuous quantitative invasion measurements can provide prognostic information in assessing progression risk in pT1 bladder urothelial carcinoma.

articles.title: Neural Representation of the Coding of Language and Speech in Children with Congenital Toxoplasmosis.
articles.abstract: Purpose: Children diagnosed with congenital toxoplasmosis (CT) are at increased risk of central auditory nervous system dysfunction, potentially affecting their hearing skills and language development, even in the absence of direct hearing loss. This study therefore explored whether electrophysiological measures of language and speech were affected in children with CT. Method: This prospective longitudinal cohort study recruited 13 children diagnosed with CT (the CT group) and 25 typically developing children (control group). Participants underwent frequency-following response (FFR) recording at three developmental stages: stage 1 (S1) covering the first to third month of life; stage 2 (S2) spanning the sixth to tenth month; and finally stage 3 (S3) from 4 to 6 years, although by then losses to follow-up were severe (>50%). During S3, language and speech development assessments were also conducted. Results: Logistic regression between FFR components and expressive language assessments showed no significant differences, although statistical power was compromised by the small number of remaining children. There was no significant interaction between the FFR components across the stages or between groups (p > 0.05). Main-effect analyses revealed that children with congenital toxoplasmosis exhibited significantly prolonged latencies relative to controls for waves A (β = 0.38 ms, 95% CI [0.11, 0.65], p = 0.008), F (β = 0.46 ms, 95% CI [0.01, 0.91], p = 0.048), and O (β = 0.87 ms, 95% CI [0.40, 1.34], p < 0.001). Conclusions: Our findings indicate that children diagnosed with CT exhibit prolonged latencies of waves A, F, and O and reduced slope values in the FFR, suggesting impairments in neural speech sound coding from the first months of life into early childhood, independent of the assessment stage. Although FFR latencies did not predict expressive language outcomes, all children in the CT group assessed at S3 presented language and/or speech alterations, which suggests a possible association between congenital toxoplasmosis and speech development. Given the small number of children assessed at this stage, this is a preliminary finding that warrants further investigation in larger longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Establishment of Reference Intervals for Lithium Heparin Plasma Potassium in Adults.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: In current Chinese clinical practice, the reference interval established for serum potassium is routinely applied to both routine biochemical testing conducted with serum separator tubes and emergency biochemical testing using lithium heparin plasma. This study aimed to establish a plasma-specific reference interval for potassium via the indirect ion-selective electrode (ISE) method, in compliance with the Chinese national health industry standard WS/T 402-2024. Methods: A total of 296 paired plasma and serum samples were collected from health examination participants at the Chinese PLA General Hospital. Potassium concentrations were measured using the ISE module of the Roche cobas 8000 modular analyzer series. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Bland-Altman analysis were used to compare the two specimen types, and reference intervals for plasma potassium were determined using the nonparametric method. Results: Serum potassium concentrations were significantly higher than plasma potassium levels (median difference: 0.23 mmol/L; Z = -13.96; p < 0.001). Statistical analysis indicated that plasma potassium reference intervals should be stratified by sex. The reference interval for plasma potassium was 3.21-4.72 mmol/L in adult males and 3.21-4.51 mmol/L in adult females. Conclusions: Plasma and serum potassium levels exhibit a systematic bias. Retrospective analysis shows that applying the serum-derived reference interval to plasma potassium results in reclassification of 16.97% of emergency plasma potassium measurements. The sex-specific plasma potassium reference intervals established in this study offer a more reliable basis for interpreting plasma potassium results in emergency and perioperative settings.

articles.title: A Patch-Based Attention Framework for Automated Diabetic Retinopathy Severity Grading Using Fundus Images.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Automated diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity grading from fundus images is a challenging task due to the high resolution of retinal images and the spatially sparse nature of pathological lesions. Methods: In this study, we propose a patch-based attention framework for DR severity grading that exploits localized information while avoiding aggressive global downsampling. Each fundus image is partitioned into non-overlapping patches, which are processed using a shared ResNet-18 encoder to extract patch-level feature representations. An attention-based aggregation mechanism then assigns adaptive importance weights to the extracted features and produces an image-level representation for severity classification. The proposed framework is evaluated on the APTOS 2019 dataset. Results: An analysis of different patch configurations identifies 25 patches as the best-performing setting, achieving a multi-class accuracy of 0.852, compared with 0.817 for the whole-image baseline. A controlled ablation using the same effective input resolution further shows that attention-based aggregation achieves the highest accuracy and F1-score among the evaluated whole-image and patch-based aggregation configurations. The model also achieves a binary DR/No-DR accuracy of 0.986. Attention visualizations provide qualitative insight into the regions contributing to model predictions. Conclusions: These results demonstrate the potential of attention-guided patch-based feature learning for accurate and interpretable diabetic retinopathy severity grading.

articles.title: Developing an Algorithm to Quantify Dermatomyositis-Associated Calcinosis Using Infrared Images.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adult and Juvenile Dermatomyositis (DM/JDM)-associated calcinosis varies in its clinical presentations. Current modalities such as physician exam and CT imaging do not fully document calcinosis burden. As a result, this paper examines infrared imaging, which measures skin temperature, as a supplementary modality to assess calcinosis activity. Methods: Fifteen patients (3 DM and 12 JDM) who fulfilled probable or definite Bohan and Peter criteria for DM/JDM and with previously documented calcinosis were included. IR scans of target body regions were obtained in a temperature-controlled and humidity-monitored room. We developed an algorithm to assess calcinosis by measuring local temperature variations in IR scans. Body regions were determined to be calcinosis-positive if the algorithm identified at least 15% of the body region as suspected calcinosis. Results: Twenty-nine out of ninety body regions were designated calcinosis-positive. The average suspected calcinosis areas ranged from 8.6 to 14.2%, and left and right extremity averages were within 0.6% area of each other. Agreement between the IR algorithm and physician exam was variable, as the algorithm simultaneously detected regions that overlapped with physician-marked areas and regions outside of physician-marked boundaries. Conclusions: IR imaging appears to identify areas of calcinosis activity in DM/JDM and presents many promising advantages to warrant future study. Its integration with structural imaging modalities will enable a more comprehensive assessment of calcinosis.

articles.title: Incremental Diagnostic Value of Zero-Echo-Time Magnetic Resonance Imaging for Osseous Cervical Neural Foraminal Stenosis: A Retrospective Multireader Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Conventional cervical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) depicts cortical bone poorly, whereas computed tomography (CT) adds radiation exposure. We evaluated whether adding zero-echo-time (ZTE) imaging improves detection of CT-defined grade ≥2 foraminal stenosis. Methods: This single-centre retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 81 consecutive eligible patients evaluated between October 2024 and June 2025 who underwent cervical MRI and CT within 14 days. Two blinded musculoskeletal radiologists graded 810 foramina from C2-C3 through C6-C7 using conventional MRI and MRI + ZTE. A study-specific scale incorporated narrowing, nerve-root morphology, and surrounding fat appearances. Consensus CT grading was the reference standard; grade ≥2 defined a positive foramen. Paired differences were assessed with patient-clustered bootstrap resampling. Results: Mean age was 48.9 ± 13.6 years; 55 patients were women. CT identified grade ≥2 stenosis in 150/810 foramina (18.5%). Adding ZTE increased sensitivity from 68.7% to 87.3% for Reader 1 and from 17.3% to 35.3% for Reader 2. Sensitivity differences were 18.7 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], 10.6-27.1) and 18.0 percentage points (95% CI, 6.6-30.3), respectively. Specificity increased from 90.5% to 96.8% and from 96.7% to 97.6%, respectively. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve increased by 0.115 (95% CI, 0.076-0.164) and 0.121 (95% CI, 0.061-0.184). Binary interreader agreement increased numerically from κ = 0.25 to κ = 0.41. Conclusions: Adding ZTE improved detection of CT-defined grade ≥2 foraminal stenosis, although sensitivity remained low for one reader. Effects on CT use, management decisions, and clinical outcomes require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: A Modular Diabetic Retinopathy Analysis Framework for Lesion Segmentation and Severity Grading: Cross-Dataset External Validation from APTOS to Messidor-2.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: High in-domain accuracy of diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading models does not guarantee a similar performance for a new population. We quantify how an APTOS-trained grader degrades on an independent cohort and examine why. Methods: A modular framework combines a ResNet-34 U-Net for lesion segmentation (IDRiD) with an EfficientNet-B0 severity grader (APTOS 2019), optionally fused with lesion-derived and frequency features. The grader was evaluated zero-shot on Messidor-2 (n=1744) with bootstrap confidence intervals, four training seeds, referable-DR analysis, a discrimination-versus-calibration decomposition, a paired preprocessing ablation, and a duplicate audit. Results: Quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) fell from 0.873 (95% CI 0.831-0.909) on the APTOS test set to 0.455 (0.400-0.507) on Messidor-2; across four seeds the external QWK was 0.410±0.057. Referable-DR sensitivity fell from 92.7% to 35.0% (specificity 93.9% and 96.6%) and the AUC from 0.984 to 0.795, indicating both a loss of discrimination and a calibration shift; recalibrating thresholds with target labels (cross-validated) raised QWK only to 0.583. Omitting CLAHE reduced QWK to 0.326 (paired difference 0.129, 0.089-0.171). Thirty-three APTOS test images duplicated in the training or validation data changed QWK marginally (0.866). Lesion-feature fusion did not significantly improve grading. The segmentation Dice on lesion-containing patches was 0.51-0.68, whereas the per-image Dice was 0.21-0.61. Conclusions: In-domain agreement is a poor proxy for external performance; multi-seed reporting, explicit calibration analysis, and preprocessing control are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Exploratory Clinicopathological Associations Between Prespecified Clinical-Structural Domains and Synovial Tissue Findings in End-Stage Knee Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: Background: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a heterogeneous whole-joint disease. This exploratory clinicopathological study evaluated associations between four prespecified continuous clinical and structural domains and synovial tissue findings in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for primary end-stage knee OA. Methods: This prospective single-center study included 79 patients undergoing cemented TKA. Standardized inflammatory, metabolic/lipomatous, osteocartilaginous/remodeling, and mechanical domain scores were evaluated against suprapatellar histopathological and intraoperative macroscopic synovial outcomes. Associations were examined using Spearman correlations and age- and sex-adjusted regression models with false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction. Results: Low-grade synovitis was present in 63.3% of knees and high-grade synovitis in 31.6%. Unadjusted analyses showed weak correlations between the inflammatory domain and macroscopic synovitis (ρ = 0.24, p = 0.032) and between the metabolic/lipomatous domain and synovial lipomatosis severity (ρ = 0.23, p = 0.042). Adjusted estimates were β = 0.24 (p = 0.043) for inflammatory domain-Krenn synovitis, β = 0.23 (p = 0.050) for inflammatory domain-macroscopic synovitis, and OR = 1.57 (p = 0.044) for metabolic/lipomatous domain-lipomatosis severity. No associations were observed for the osteocartilaginous/remodeling or mechanical domains. None of the six prespecified associations remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Conclusions: End-stage knee OA showed substantial synovial heterogeneity, but no prespecified domain-tissue association remained significant after multiple-testing correction. The evaluated domains should therefore be considered exploratory clinicostructural constructs rather than validated biological or diagnostic classifications. Further multicenter longitudinal studies integrating imaging, molecular biomarkers, and tissue assessment are needed.

articles.title: Ultrasound Echotexture Analysis as a Diagnostic Adjunct for Naja atra Envenomation Versus Cellulitis in Acute Limb Swelling.
articles.abstract: Objectives:Naja atra (N. atra) envenomation and cellulitis frequently present with overlapping clinical features of acutely swollen extremities, creating a diagnostic dilemma during the early clinical course of acute limb swelling. This study investigated whether ultrasound imaging with echotexture analysis can effectively differentiate these two conditions. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study conducted at Taichung Veterans General Hospital included 115 ultrasound images from 84 patients categorized into three groups: confirmed N. atra envenomation (n = 45), confirmed non-snakebite cellulitis (n = 40), and controls (n = 30). Gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) features including contrast, correlation, energy, and homogeneity, along with the grayscale value and the power Doppler vascularity-to-ROI ratio, were quantitatively computed from ultrasound images. Group comparisons used generalized estimating equations to account for multiple images from the same patient, with Bonferroni correction for pairwise comparisons. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results: Significant differences among the three groups were found for contrast (p < 0.001), correlation (p < 0.001), homogeneity (p = 0.005), and the vascularity-to-ROI ratio (p < 0.001). In pairwise comparisons between N. atra envenomation and cellulitis, contrast was significantly higher (0.273 ± 0.068 versus 0.230 ± 0.040, p = 0.001) and homogeneity was lower (0.878 ± 0.020 versus 0.890 ± 0.017, p = 0.004) in the N. atra group. ROC curve analysis for discriminating N. atra envenomation from cellulitis yielded an Area Under the Curve of 0.707 (95% confidence interval, 0.591-0.824) for contrast and 0.684 (95% confidence interval, 0.568-0.800) for homogeneity. At an optimal cutoff of ≥0.243, contrast achieved 73.3% sensitivity and 70.0% specificity. Conclusions: Echotexture analysis, specifically contrast and homogeneity, may differentiate N. atra envenomation from cellulitis. These parameters may reflect the heterogeneous tissue destruction induced by venom compared to the diffuse inflammation seen in cellulitis. These proof-of-concept findings require validation in larger prospective cohorts before clinical application.

articles.title: Association Between Radiographic Haglund Morphology and MRI-Measured Achilles Tendon Rupture Location: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Achilles tendon ruptures usually occur proximal to the calcaneal insertion. Whether posterosuperior calcaneal prominence is associated with rupture location remains uncertain. We examined the association between radiographic Haglund morphology and MRI-measured rupture-to-insertion distance. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, adults treated for acute Achilles tendon rupture from January 2015 to December 2025 were assessed. Rupture distance was measured on sagittal MRI. Two blinded orthopaedic surgeons measured bump height and the bump-calcaneus ratio on standard lateral ankle radiographs; radiographic Haglund morphology required both thresholds (≥4.0 mm and ≥7.5%, respectively). We compared groups with the Mann-Whitney U test and bootstrap confidence intervals and used median regression adjusted for age, sex, sport-related mechanism, and comorbidity. Results: Of 292 screened patients, 106 were included; 28 (26.4%) met the radiographic criteria. The cohort included 27 women (25.5%) and had a median age of 41.5 years. Interobserver ICC(2,1) values were 0.9976-0.9994, with complete agreement in threshold-derived classification (κ = 1.000). Median rupture distance was 1.60 cm (IQR, 1.49-2.58) with Haglund morphology versus 4.85 cm (IQR, 3.51-5.55) without it. The unadjusted median difference was -3.25 cm (95% CI, -3.40 to -2.68; p < 0.001); the adjusted association was -2.89 cm (95% CI, -3.61 to -2.17; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Radiographic Haglund morphology was associated with more distal Achilles tendon rupture in this selected rupture cohort. The retrospective design and exclusion of 113 patients with incomplete records limit generalizability; the study does not establish causality or whether morphology increases rupture risk.

articles.title: HIV-PrivFed: Privacy-Utility-Fairness-Aware Federated Learning for HIV Risk Stratification and Testing Prioritization Under Non-IID Clinical Heterogeneity.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: HIV screening from routinely collected behavioral data could help to prioritize testing across clinics that cannot centralize sensitive records; however, the utility, privacy, and client-level fairness of federated models on real non-IID data are poorly characterized. Methods: Using Sialon-II, a cohort of men who have sex with men in 13 European cities (13 natural clients; horizontal federated learning), we benchmarked ten conventional classifiers and a centralized residual MLP, compared local-only, FedAvg, and FedProx baselines, and evaluated HIV-PrivFed, a differentially private FedProx-based algorithm with client-by-client Rényi accounting and client-level fairness auditing (fairness is audited, not enforced); secure aggregation overhead was benchmarked in simulation. Results: The best conventional model reached an AUROC of 0.696 (AUPRC 0.235), statistically indistinguishable from logistic regression on the original partition. Federated learning exceeded local-only learning (AUROC 0.607 versus 0.565). Achieved worst-client privacy budgets (ε = 22.1-224.1) were far looser than the nominal targets and give no meaningful guarantee; accuracy was retained at these budgets (AUROC 0.629-0.650) but fell to 0.553 and 0.524 at ε=8 and 4. Client-level estimates were highly uncertain. Conclusions: Useful accuracy and a meaningful privacy guarantee did not coexist in this small-cohort setting; larger cohorts and external validation are needed before deployment.

articles.title: Overt and Occult Hepatitis B in Hemodialysis Patients: Insights from High-Sensitivity Testing and Genetic Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Occult hepatitis B infection (OBI) remains a diagnostic challenge, particularly in hemodialysis (HD) patients, who are vulnerable to HBV infection due to immune dysfunction and repeated exposure. Methods: We evaluated the prevalence and molecular characteristics of OBI among 874 HD patients in St. Petersburg, Russia, using high-sensitivity nested real-time PCR targeting the S and X genes. Results: HBV DNA was detected in 3.7% (32/874), as reflected in subcategories: overt CHB in 2.1% (18/874) and OBI in 1.6% (14/874). Genotype D predominated (93.8%), with subgenotypes D2 (56.3%), D1 (25.0%), and D3 (12.5%) present. OBI patients had low viral loads (6.0-148.3 IU/mL), whereas CHB patients showed high viremia (7843-64,870,000 IU/mL). Immune escape mutations were significantly more frequent in OBI (92.9%) than CHB (16.7%; p < 0.0001), with A128V being most common (31.3%). Core mutations were nearly universal (93.7%). Drug resistance mutations were found in 6.3% of cases without prior antiviral therapy. Seronegative infections (i.e., negative for anti-HBc IgG and anti-HBs IgG) were common, comprising 77.8% of CHB and 14.3% of OBI cases. Anti-HBc prevalence increased with dialysis vintage (3.8% to 43.1%, p < 0.0001), while anti-HBs declined with age (rs = -0.85, p = 0.0001). Conclusions: In conclusion, OBI affects 1.6% of HD patients in this cohort, with immune escape mutations as a key molecular driver of the occult phenotype. These findings suggest that HBV DNA screening may warrant consideration in HD patients, as serological results alone are inadequate for ruling out occult infection.

articles.title: Red Cell Phenotype Modifies the Association Between Free Triiodothyronine and Erythrocyte Count: A Cross-Sectional Study of 3673 Adults in a Hemoglobinopathy-Endemic Region of Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Thyroid hormone regulates erythropoiesis, but most population studies have used thyrotropin (TSH) alone and have not examined whether the erythroid association differs by red cell phenotype. We examined this in a population where inherited microcytosis and iron deficiency are both common. Methods: We analyzed 3871 adults of both sexes with paired free triiodothyronine (FT3), free thyroxine, TSH, and complete blood count from three hospitals in Jazan, Saudi Arabia (3673 with FT3 within the reference interval formed the primary analysis). All three analytes were entered simultaneously in models adjusted for age and sex; mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) were pre-specified comparison (negative control) outcomes; red cell discriminant indices were used to assign a normocytic, acquired microcytic, or presumed inherited-trait pattern, which was compared against linked ferritin and transferrin saturation. Results: FT3 was associated with erythrocyte count (standardized β 0.097, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.066-0.128, p < 0.001) and hemoglobin (+2.7 g/L per pmol/L); TSH was not (p = 0.547). The erythrocyte count association was present in normocytic (β 0.101) and acquired microcytic records (β 0.099) but absent in the presumed trait pattern (β -0.017; interaction p = 0.002) and remained absent under a stricter trait definition, whereas the hemoglobin association did not differ by phenotype (interaction p = 0.639). FT3 was unrelated to iron status, and the association survived adjustment for ferritin and restriction to same-episode iron measurements. In an exploratory comparison, both associations were strongest in iron-replete normocytic patients (hemoglobin +3.6 g/L per pmol/L, p < 0.001) and attenuated in measured iron deficiency. Conclusions: FT3, not TSH, was associated with erythrocyte count and hemoglobin. The count association was absent in the index-defined trait pattern, in which erythrocyte number is already high, and both associations were blunted where iron was limited. These observations are consistent with, but do not demonstrate, a limit on the marrow's count response, since erythropoietic activity was not measured; they are hypothesis-generating and require replication with confirmed hemoglobin genotype, measured iron status, and reticulocyte or erythropoietin data.

articles.title: Explainable Rhythm-Resolved EEG for Retrospective Comparison of Psychiatric-Service Adults with Recorded Violent Offences and Non-Clinical Controls.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examines whether rhythm-resolved EEG features separate two retrospective groups and whether those features can be traced to explicit rhythms and sensors. The groups are psychiatric-service adults with recorded violent offences and non-clinical controls; the design does not compare offenders with non-offenders. Methods: We analysed 2554 non-overlapping 15 s EEG epochs from 95 adults (51 controls; 44 recorded-offence participants). RhythmFluxPat generated 9216 rank-transition features. CWImRMR selected 352 features with full-cohort labels, and classifier selection was nested within 95 participant-held-out leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) folds. Results: Classifier-nested tkNN classified 2392/2554 epochs (93.66%) and 93/95 participants (97.89%), and an independent check reproduced both confusion matrices. A nested support-vector machine (SVM) gave similar values (94.71% of epochs; 93/95 participants). In the comparative evaluation of four feature selectors, CWImRMR remained the best branch (93.85%), and a 44-feature subset reached 91.11%. DRLobish linked the selected features to delta and beta-to-gamma routes in the recorded-offence-assigned panel and to theta and alpha-to-theta routes in the control-assigned panel. Conclusions: RhythmFluxPat provides traceable rank-persistence and rank-exchange coordinates. The reported accuracies are optimistic internal estimates. Fully nested replication with matched psychiatric controls is required before any claim of generalisation or biomarker validity.

articles.title: Regional Corneal Densitometry Changes and Endothelial Stability After Cruciate-Pattern Nd:YAG Laser Posterior Capsulotomy: A Retrospective Self-Controlled Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Nd:YAG laser posterior capsulotomy may be followed by subtle corneal optical changes. We evaluated regional corneal densitometry (CD) and endothelial parameters after standardized cruciate-pattern capsulotomy. Methods: In this retrospective, self-controlled study, 51 eyes of 51 pseudophakic patients with clinically significant posterior capsule opacification underwent capsulotomy by a single surgeon. Scheimpflug CD was assessed in the anterior, central, posterior, and full-thickness cornea across 0-2, 2-6, 6-10, and 10-12 mm zones. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure (IOP), pachymetry, keratometry, aberrometry, and specular microscopy were evaluated before treatment and at postoperative week 1 and month 1. Results: CD increased in the 0-2, 2-6, and 6-10 mm zones of the anterior and central layers, while the 10-12 mm zone showed no statistically significant time-related difference. The largest reported effect was in central-layer CD at 0-2 mm (d = 0.52). BCVA improved (decimal values, 0.32 ± 0.18 to 0.81 ± 0.13; p < 0.001). Endothelial cell density (ECD) and hexagonality showed no statistically significant time effects (p = 0.720 and p = 0.290); coefficient of variation decreased (p = 0.003), an isolated finding of uncertain clinical significance. IOP differed between week 1 and month 1 (15.0 ± 3.14 vs. 16.4 ± 2.73 mmHg) but both means were within the conventional physiological range and measurements were affected by the postoperative medication schedule. Corneal thickness, keratometric indices, and aberrations showed no significant time effects. Conclusions: Central and paracentral backscatter increases were detectable over one month without a statistically demonstrable deterioration in the measured endothelial or corneal structural indices. These findings do not establish endothelial equivalence or the clinical superiority of a capsulotomy pattern; controlled studies with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: Sequential Application of the Birmingham Atypical Cartilage Tumor Imaging Protocol and Radiological Aggressiveness Score in Long-Bone Intramedullary Cartilage Tumors: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: The Birmingham Atypical Cartilage Tumor Imaging Protocol (BACTIP) addresses referral triage, whereas the Radiological Aggressiveness Score (RAS) estimates resection-grade histology. We evaluated their sequential application in a selected tertiary-center cohort. Methods: This retrospective study included 99 patients during 2001-2025, combining consecutive eligible surgical chondrosarcomas with a nonconsecutive enchondroma sample. Groups comprised lesions outside BACTIP referral categories, referral-category lesions with RAS < 4, and referral-category lesions with RAS ≥ 4. Diagnostic performance for resection-grade disease (grade 2, grade 3, or dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma) and exploratory, unadjusted oncologic outcomes were assessed. Results: All 47 resection-grade tumors met BACTIP referral criteria (sensitivity 100%; 95% CI, 92.4-100%). Requiring RAS ≥ 4 increased whole-cohort specificity from 69.2% to 94.2% and reduced sensitivity to 91.5% (95% CI, 80.1-96.6%). RAS positivity alone and sequential classification identified identical patients. Four grade 2 tumors were RAS-negative despite BACTIP category 3 classification, and grade 2 sensitivity was 78.9% (15/19). Excluding dedifferentiated tumors, sensitivity was 83.3% (20/24). Oncologic events were concentrated in the referral/RAS-positive group, and global log-rank comparisons were significant for all three endpoints (p < 0.001). Conclusions: BACTIP may structure referral assessment, while RAS may further characterize imaging aggressiveness in lesions meeting referral criteria. The four RAS-negative grade 2 tumors underscore the importance of maintaining specialist referral when BACTIP referral criteria are met, even when RAS suggests lower imaging aggressiveness. Neither tool replaces clinical assessment, histopathological correlation, or multidisciplinary review. This selected cohort does not establish safe nonreferral, independent prognostic value, or improved management or outcomes. Prospective validation in the intended referral population is required.

articles.title: Classification of Surface Electromyography Recordings from Young and Older Adults Using CWT Scalograms: A Window-Level Proof-of-Concept Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Age-related changes in skeletal muscle involve alterations in both muscle structure and neuromuscular function. Surface electromyography (sEMG) provides a non-invasive method for assessing muscle electrical activity. This study aimed to investigate whether time-frequency representations of sEMG signals combined with deep learning could classify recordings obtained from healthy young and older adults, without assuming that the discriminative features necessarily reflect age-related neuromuscular changes. Methods: sEMG signals were experimentally collected from 60 healthy adults, including 30 young and 30 older adults. The resulting continuous wavelet transform (CWT) scalogram images were randomly divided into training and test sets at the image-window level using an 80:20 ratio. Consequently, windows from the same participant could appear in both sets. Signals were filtered, segmented into overlapping windows, and converted into CWT scalogram images for classification using ResNet-18. Results: At the window level, the CWT-ResNet model achieved an accuracy of 78.98%, an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.8589, a sensitivity of 71.34%, a specificity of 85.06%, and a balanced accuracy of 78.20%. Muscle-specific analyses showed window-level classification accuracies ranging from 78.57% to 79.89% across all three muscle sites. However, the observed classification performance may have been influenced by differences in movement timing, active and resting periods, anthropometric characteristics, and participant overlap between the training and test sets. These potential influences were not isolated through additional control analyses. Conclusions: CWT-based time-frequency representations of sEMG combined with ResNet-18 demonstrated preliminary feasibility for classifying sEMG recordings obtained from young and older adults under the revised preprocessing and image-window-level evaluation conditions. The findings do not establish that the model specifically detects age-related neuromuscular changes. Participant-independent validation and analyses controlling for task execution and anthropometric characteristics are required.

articles.title: Electrocardiographic Features in Patients with Neuromuscular Diseases: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: Neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) are a group of progressive hereditary disorders frequently associated with significant cardiac involvement, which can represent a primary cause of mortality. This study aims to characterize the electrocardiographic findings in patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), Becker Muscular Dystrophy (BMD), and Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1 (DM1). Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 131 ECGs from 74 patients (28 DMD, 24 BMD, 22 DM1) followed in the Department of Clinical and Experimental Medicine of the University of Messina, Italy. None of the enrolled patients had clinically manifest heart failure. Electrocardiographic and echocardiographic data were collected, and each ECG finding was considered present if documented in at least one ECG during follow-up. In the DM1 group, an exploratory analysis of the 12-lead P-wave voltage sum (ΣP) and of its ratio to the QRS voltage sum (ΣQRS) was performed and compared with DMD and BMD patients and healthy controls. Results: In DMD patients, the most common findings were deep Q waves (57.1%), negative T waves in the lateral leads (39.3%), and complete and incomplete right bundle branch block (RBBB) (25.0% each). In BMD, incomplete RBBB (27.3%), U waves (27.3%) and left atrial enlargement (23.8%) were prevalent, and 3 patients (12.5%) had a pacemaker. In DM1, atrial fibrillation (18.2%), PR interval prolongation (38.9% of patients in sinus rhythm) and early repolarization (42.9%) were frequent. Mean ΣP and ΣP/ΣQRS values were lower in DM1 patients than in DMD and BMD patients and healthy controls. Conclusions: This study confirms many previously described ECG abnormalities in NMDs and highlights disease-specific patterns. The finding of deep Q waves in DMD may reflect inferolateral fibrosis. Notably, the reduced P-wave voltage in DM1 patients is a novel, hypothesis-generating observation that may reflect atrial myopathy; its value as a predictor of atrial arrhythmias requires prospective validation. These findings underscore the critical role of routine ECG surveillance in the management of patients with NMDs.

articles.title: Clinical, Hereditary, and Lifestyle Factors Associated with Cardiovascular Disease in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Diabetes mellitus and cardiovascular disease (CVD) constitute a dual epidemic in Saudi Arabia. This study examined the associations of cardiometabolic conditions, behavioural risk factors, and family history with cardiovascular disease among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Methods: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted on 423 adults with self-reported physician-diagnosed T2DM drawn from a community-based survey in the Jazan region, Saudi Arabia. Sociodemographic, anthropometric, behavioural, dietary, and clinical variables were assessed using a validated WHO STEPwise-based questionnaire. CVD status was determined through self-reported physician diagnosis. Bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression with Firth penalisation were used to identify factors associated with CVD, with a reduced model as a sensitivity analysis. Results: Participants had a mean age of 48 ± 15 years; 60% were male, and 98% were Saudi nationals. The prevalence of self-reported CVD was 9.7%. Family history of CVD showed the strongest association (OR = 14.57; 95% CI: 5.88-40.90; p < 0.001), followed by diagnosed dyslipidaemia (OR = 5.19; 95% CI: 1.91-14.22; p = 0.001) and diagnosed hypertension (OR = 4.71; 95% CI: 1.86-13.16; p < 0.001). Regular whole-grain consumption (OR = 0.30; 95% CI: 0.11-0.75; p = 0.010) and a monthly income of 5000-9999 SAR (OR = 0.23; 95% CI: 0.05-0.89; p = 0.032) were associated with lower odds of CVD; all five associations persisted in a reduced model. Body mass index, physical inactivity, and smoking were not significantly associated with CVD after adjustment. Conclusions: In this exploratory analysis of adults with T2DM, CVD was strongly associated with family history of CVD, hypertension, and dyslipidaemia, and inversely associated with whole-grain intake. Given the cross-sectional design, self-reported measures, and wide confidence intervals, these associations do not establish causality and require prospective confirmation; family history of CVD may nonetheless help prioritise patients for cardiovascular risk assessment.

articles.title: Multiscale Peritumoral Ultrasound Machine Learning Scores and Pathological Response to Neoadjuvant Therapy in Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Peritumoral ultrasound may capture tissue characteristics relevant to treatment sensitivity. In this study, we examined whether malignancy-related prediction scores (PS) were associated with pathological response to neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer. Methods: Support vector machine classifiers were developed for 1, 3, 5, and 7 mm peritumoral regions using 1716 pathologically confirmed lesions. We assessed PS against postoperative Miller-Payne (MP) grade in 132 patients who completed neoadjuvant therapy and surgery. Ordinal logistic regression examined overall associations, interactions with hormone receptor (HR) status and Ki67, and treatment-stratified associations adjusted for both. Holm correction addressed multiple testing. The 7 mm classifier was refitted using 1584 patients outside the response cohort while retaining the originally selected features. Results: Higher 7 mm PS was associated with lower MP grade overall (odds ratio [OR] per 0.1-unit increase, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66-0.95; Holm-adjusted p = 0.048). HR and Ki67 interactions remained significant at 1 mm (adjusted p = 0.049 and 0.036, respectively). In 60 complete cases receiving chemotherapy plus anti-HER2 therapy, the original 7 mm PS was associated with MP grade after adjustment (OR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.42-0.85; adjusted p = 0.037). The refitted PS showed an attenuated association in these patients (OR, 0.709; 95% CI, 0.526-0.955; raw p = 0.0239; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0478). Associations in the original classifier test subsets (n = 22-26) were not significant after correction. Conclusions: The 7 mm score may complement HR and Ki67 for response assessment during chemotherapy plus anti-HER2 therapy. Interactions at 1 mm suggest variation with molecular characteristics. These findings warrant independent validation.

articles.title: Subject-Specific Cardiovascular Signatures Revealed by Arterial Pulse Signals in Patients with Heart Diseases-Part I: General Cases.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluates whether cardiovascular (CV) parameters derived from noninvasive arterial pulse signals can capture subject-specific physiological characteristics and longitudinal changes in patients with diverse heart diseases. Method: Arterial pulse signals at the radial artery (RA) and carotid artery (CA) of each patient were successfully recorded from all 18 patients using micro-fabricated tactile sensors. Signal quality was screened before analysis, and the accepted signals were analyzed using a single-degree-of-freedom time-frequency (SDOF-TF) framework. Key CV parameters, including time-based indices-heart rate (HR), heart rate variability (HRV), respiration rate (RR), and respiration modulation (RM), as well as harmonic amplitudes and normalized arterial pulse waveform (APW)-were extracted from measurements at rest and post-exercise across three rehabilitation visits in 18 patients with heterogeneous CV conditions. Longitudinal changes in CV parameters within subjects and variability between subjects were assessed. Results: Compared with a healthy reference, the patients exhibited heterogeneous CV profiles, with lower HRV in all patients except one with AF, who showed elevated HRV, and generally reduced post-exercise CV responses. Higher-order harmonic amplitudes were attenuated at the RA, while CA-derived APW measurements showed greater sensitivity to systolic upstroke slope. Marked inter-subject variability was evident in at-rest CV parameters and 5-min post-exercise responses. Longitudinal CV responses varied across rehabilitation visits, potentially reflecting multiple contributing factors. Conclusions: The 100% pulse acquisition rate supports the feasibility of the tactile sensor technology for pulse measurement, and the combined sensor technology and SDOF-TF framework enable quantitative characterization of shared and individualized CV patterns in cardiac patients and their post-exercise recovery, including time-based indices, harmonic signatures, site-specific differences, and interactions among CV parameters. These findings warrant further investigation in larger cohorts with appropriate physiological reference measurements.

articles.title: Transdiscal Versus Cement-Augmented Pedicle Screw Fixation for Thoracolumbar Fractures in Patients with Diffuse Idiopathic Skeletal Hyperostosis (DISH).
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rigid internal fixation and early mobilization using pedicle screws have become a standard treatment option for vertebral fractures in patients with diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis. Poor bone quality and a long lever arm may result in a high rate of screw loosening, screw pullout, and implant failure in these patients. Therefore, researchers have developed various techniques to enhance fixation strength, including cement-augmented fenestrated pedicle screw (CAFPS) and transdiscal screw (TDS) fixation. This study compared the clinical and radiological outcomes of CAFPS and TDS fixation techniques for treating diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH)-associated thoracolumbar vertebral fractures. This study compared the clinical and radiological outcomes of CAFPS and TDS fixation techniques for DISH-associated thoracolumbar vertebral fractures. Methods: Retrospective comparative cohort study. An evaluation was conducted of patients who underwent posterior instrumentation for vertebral fractures accompanied by DISH, using CAFPS or TDS techniques, at our hospital between August 2019 and March 2025. We assessed preoperative, operative, and postoperative data, outcomes, and radiographic parameters. Results: We included 40 patients; 11 received CAFPS, and 29 received TDS fixation. Operative time (104 ± 19.6 min vs. 115 ± 29.4 min, p = 0.32), blood loss (87.7 ± 69.4 mL vs. 88.3 ± 64.8 mL, p = 0.95), and bone union rate (100% vs. 89.7%, p = 0.27) did not differ significantly. The incidence of screw loosening number was higher in the TDS group (5.68% vs. 13.4%, p = 0.049). However, patient-level analysis showed no difference (4/11 vs. 7/29, p = 0.455). Neither group had implant backouts, failures, or reoperations. Conclusions: Transdiscal screws and transdiscal and cement-augmented pedicle screws are useful techniques for treating thoracolumbar vertebral fractures in patients with DISH. These techniques can reduce the level of fixation in vulnerable patient populations.

articles.title: Do Non-Invasive Fibrosis Indices Reflect Interstitial Lung Disease and Pulmonary Function in Systemic Sclerosis?
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a major manifestation of systemic sclerosis (SSc). The Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) and aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) are indirect hepatic fibrosis indices of uncertain pulmonary relevance. We compared these indices by documented ILD status and explored associations with pulmonary function and historical forced vital capacity (FVC) changes. Methods: This retrospective observational study included 102 patients with SSc (61 with ILD, 41 without ILD). Indices were calculated from the last eligible laboratory assessment; ILD was classified using available high-resolution computed tomography records. Patients with relevant hepatic and laboratory confounders were excluded. Pulmonary associations were explored within SSc-ILD, including a sensitivity analysis restricted to ≤12 months between laboratory and follow-up pulmonary function testing. Results: Neither index differed significantly by ILD status (FIB-4, p = 0.91; APRI, p = 0.06). In logistic models adjusted for age and diffuse cutaneous phenotype, FIB-4 showed a borderline inverse association with documented ILD status only after adjustment for age and and diffuse cutaneous phenotype (adjusted odds ratio 0.247, 95% confidence interval 0.062-0.988; p = 0.048), whereas APRI did not (p = 0.064). Within SSc-ILD, neither index correlated significantly with FVC % predicted, diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) % predicted, forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) % predicted, or historical FVC changes. FIB-4 correlated inversely with absolute FVC (ρ = -0.53, p < 0.001), but this association was not significant after age and sex adjustment (p = 0.40). The absolute-FVC correlation persisted within the ≤12-month subgroup. Conclusions: Findings do not consistently support these indices as stand-alone indicators of SSc pulmonary involvement; prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Enhancing Machine Learning Performance for ALS Classification Using Feature Selection Technique.
articles.abstract: Background: Electromyogram (EMG) is considered for the diagnosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). We investigated how frequently an initial electrophysiological evaluation is performed in ALS patients. Objective: We aimed to identify ALS cases using the feature selection algorithm (FSA). A pattern of feature involvement was expected in the early phase of ALS based on the typical consistent involvement of a few particular muscles in the late stages. Methods: We used a clinical and EMG dataset of 36 patients (21 ALS patients and 15 healthy) for analysis. The present approach used a Random Forest (RF)-based machine learning (ML) algorithm for the prediction of ALS patients. The goal of this study was to determine how feature selection techniques can enhance machine learning algorithms that can be used in real-time applications. Findings: The experimental findings demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed model. This work demonstrates how machine learning models can offer important predictive insights in ALS, improving knowledge of disease dynamics and aiding patient care. According to the comparison results, the RF model utilizing the feature selection algorithm demonstrated a positive improvement, and the accuracy of the RF model with and without the feature selection technique was found to be 87.50% and 75%, respectively. Conclusions: The algorithm improved the model accuracy from 75% to 87.50%, resulting in an absolute increase of 12.5 percentage points in classification accuracy. This study found that fibrillation, positive sharp waves (PSW), and fasciculation features were high-yielding in EMG of ALS cases.

articles.title: Vessel-Specific Quantitative Plaque Characteristics on Coronary CT Angiography for Prediction of FFR-Defined Myocardial Ischemia.
articles.abstract: Objectives: To determine whether quantitative coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) plaque characteristics associated with fractional flow reserve (FFR)-defined ischemia vary among coronary arteries and whether they improve prediction when added to conventional clinical and stenosis information. Methods: This retrospective study included 204 patients and 289 vessels (161 left anterior descending [LAD], 55 left circumflex [LCX], and 73 right coronary artery [RCA] vessels) evaluated by CCTA and invasive FFR. Plaque characteristics were quantified using semi-automated software. Predictors were selected separately by vessel using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) for LAD and RCA and Boruta-XGBoost for LCX. Model evaluation incorporated five-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. Incremental performance was assessed by adding selected plaque features to Model 1, which comprised clinical variables and severe stenosis (≥70%). Results: FFR-defined ischemia (FFR ≤ 0.80) was identified in 90 LAD, 24 LCX, and 37 RCA vessels. Ischemic vessels had longer lesions, smaller minimum luminal area, greater stenosis, and higher plaque burden. Vessel-specific plaque models yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.755 (95% CI: 0.682-0.826), 0.789 (95% CI: 0.656-0.905), and 0.775 (95% CI: 0.661-0.877) for LAD, LCX, and RCA, respectively. In a separate incremental analysis, compared with Model 1, Model 2 improved AUC in LAD (0.613 to 0.755; net reclassification improvement (NRI) = 0.736; integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) = 0.163) and RCA (0.489 to 0.767; NRI = 0.955; IDI = 0.276), with smaller gains in LCX (0.617 to 0.754; NRI = 0.651; IDI = 0.169). Conclusions: Quantitative CCTA plaque characteristics showed potentially vessel-dependent associations with FFR-defined ischemia. Incorporating selected plaque features into clinical and stenosis-based models improved discrimination in the LAD and RCA. These exploratory findings require validation in larger, independent cohorts.

articles.title: Serum TLR2, TLR4, TLR2/TLR4 Ratio, and ESM1 in Sepsis: A Single-Center Prospective Observational Study of Diagnostic and Prognostic Associations.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sepsis remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality, and reliable diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers are needed. This study investigated the diagnostic and prognostic associations of endothelial cell-specific molecule-1 (ESM1), toll-like receptor (TLR)2, TLR4, and the TLR2/TLR4 ratio in sepsis. Methods: In this single-center prospective observational study, serum biomarker levels were measured in 60 patients with sepsis and 23 ambulatory controls and analyzed for associations with the presence of sepsis and in-hospital mortality. Demographic characteristics and comorbidities were comparable between groups. Results: No significant differences were observed in ESM1, TLR4, or the TLR2/TLR4 ratio between groups (p > 0.05). TLR2 levels were lower in patients with sepsis than in controls (median [IQR]: 0.551 [1.508] vs. 1.394 [8.606], respectively; p = 0.056), without reaching statistical significance. Receiver operating characteristic analysis yielded an AUC of 0.636 (p = 0.080) for TLR2, with 91.7% sensitivity and 47.8% specificity at a cut-off of ≤3.2129. In-hospital mortality occurred in 36.7% of patients. Serum creatinine levels were higher in non-survivors than survivors (median: 2.30 vs. 0.89 mg/dL; p = 0.039), whereas no significant associations with mortality were observed for demographic characteristics, clinical findings, other laboratory parameters, or biomarker levels. Conclusions: TLR2 levels were numerically lower in sepsis, but the difference was not statistically significant. Its diagnostic utility requires validation against non-infectious systemic inflammation in clinically relevant control populations. No significant diagnostic or prognostic associations were detected for ESM1, TLR4, or the TLR2/TLR4 ratio in this cohort.

articles.title: A Deep Learning Framework with Qualitative Post Hoc Explanation for Dry Eye Detection and Tear Film Lipid Layer Pattern Classification Using Anterior-Segment and Tearscope Imaging.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dry eye disease (DED) is assessed by combining patient-reported symptoms with ocular surface findings. We evaluated a deep learning strategy with qualitative post hoc explanation in two independent ophthalmic imaging tasks: DED-versus-healthy classification from anterior segment slit lamp images; and four-class recognition of tear film lipid layer (TFLL) interference patterns in Tearscope images using the Guillon categories. Methods: ResNet backbones were modified by adding parallel expansion channels while keeping the ImageNet-initialized channels frozen. The added channels were He-normal initialized and trained at 1 × 10-4, with the MLP classification head trained at 1 × 10-3. Latin hypercube sampling was used for hyperparameter selection within the development data. We used Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ only for post hoc interpretation. We evaluated ShECS slit lamp images (n = 434) and VOPTICAL-Is Tearscope images (n = 406). Results: Under the original evaluations, ResNet-101×3 achieved the highest scores among the evaluated configurations on both tasks. On ShECS, accuracy was 74% (95% CI: 0.63-0.82), with precision 0.80, recall 0.90, and F1-score 0.85 for the DED (positive) class, and AUC 0.80. On VOPTICAL-Is, the original image-level evaluation yielded four-class TFLL accuracy of 90% (95% CI: 0.82-0.95), with macro precision 0.89, macro recall 0.90, and macro F14 0.89, and a macro one-versus-rest AUC of 0.98. Conclusions: These preliminary proof-of-concept results support further evaluation of the combined channel-expansion and differential-training strategy, together with qualitative post hoc explanation methods for ophthalmic image classification. Because VOPTICAL-Is contains only healthy-subject images and has no documented subject identifiers in the accessed release (group-code overlap between the development and held-out subsets was observed, and subject overlap cannot be excluded), the second task represents image-level TFLL pattern classification rather than clinical DED-subtype diagnosis. A separate code-grouped sensitivity analysis with a frozen ResNet-50 feature extractor yielded 0.59 held-out accuracy (macro one-versus-rest AUC 0.85). Because this grouped run did not re-run the 0.90 ResNet-101×3 configuration, the numerical difference cannot be attributed solely to partitioning, or interpreted as a direct measurement of subject-level leakage; rather, it demonstrates sensitivity to group-aware partitioning. The original image-level estimates should therefore be treated as exploratory and not as evidence of subject-level generalization. A controlled 2 × 2 factorial ablation (channel width × trainability policy) on the same code-grouped partition, executed as a TensorFlow/Keras ResNet-50 reconstruction with three seeds per cell, indicated descriptively that unfreezing the final convolutional stage was associated with higher accuracy and macro F1 (e.g., standard width: accuracy 0.556 vs. 0.469), whereas the effect of widening was small and inconsistent across metrics and policies. These descriptive summaries involve no significance testing and do not measure subject-level leakage. External clinical validation of identified cohorts is needed before routine use.

articles.title: Non-Endoscopic Screening for Barrett's Esophagus Using a DNA Methylation-Based Assay: Real-World Experience in 11,991 Patients.
articles.abstract: Background: Barrett's esophagus (BE), defined by specialized intestinal metaplasia (SIM), is the recognized precursor to esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). Despite established screening guidelines for high-risk populations, uptake of endoscopic screening remains low. We report the results of early commercial use of a non-endoscopic BE screening strategy, EsoGuard® (EG), a molecular biomarker assay performed on esophageal cell samples collected via a companion swallowable balloon capsule device (EsoCheck®, EC). Methods: We retrospectively analyzed the feasibility and tolerability of EG/EC as a non-endoscopic approach to BE evaluation in patients tested from January 2023 through June 2024. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate risk factors associated with positive EG results. Results: Among 11,991 patients tested, 11,355 (94.7%) had successful cell collection with the EC device, with procedures averaging less than 2 minutes and no device-related adverse events reported. Over 95% of surveyed patients would recommend the test to others. Overall, 93.1% (10,566/11,355) of collected samples had binary EG results, among which 17.8% had positive assay results suggesting the presence of BE. Positivity rates increased with age, with age > 50 years as the strongest individual predictor of a positive EG result. Conclusions: These data represent the largest real-world experience with EG and EC to date, demonstrating high tolerability and no reported device-related adverse events. The findings support the feasibility of large-scale implementation and suggest that EG/EC use may improve access to guideline-recommended BE screening across diverse healthcare settings.

articles.title: Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide Falls Progressively During Treated Exacerbations of COPD and Is Discordant with Blood Eosinophil Counts.
articles.abstract: Background: The behavior of fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) during treated COPD exacerbations and its agreement with blood eosinophil counts are poorly characterized. Objectives: To describe serial FeNO trajectories across hospitalized COPD exacerbations (AECOPDs), assess concordance between FeNO and blood eosinophils, and test whether these can predict length of stay (LOS). Methods: Prospective cohort of patients hospitalized for AECOPD. FeNO was measured on admission, on day 2 and at discharge; blood eosinophils and post-bronchodilator spirometry on admission and before discharge; and arterial blood gases on admission and on day 2. The admission measurements preceded the first dose of corticosteroid. All patients received guideline-directed treatment, including systemic corticosteroids. Results: Most patients were male (94.7%), with a mean age of 71.7 ± 8.3 years. FeNO fell from 16 (IQR 10-25) ppb on admission to 13.5 (7-20) ppb on day 2 and 9 (6-18) ppb at discharge (p < 0.001). Blood eosinophils fell from 60 (20-150) to 0 (0-40) cells/µL (p < 0.001), and FEV1 increased from 38% to 45% predicted (p < 0.001). Agreement between biomarkers on admission was poor (ρ = 0.21, p = 0.07; κ = 0.08, 95% CI -0.15 to +0.30), and 31 patients (40.8%) were classified differently by the two markers. Admission FeNO (ρ = 0.03, p = 0.79), ΔFeNO (ρ = -0.12, p = 0.31), and admission eosinophils (ρ = -0.08, p = 0.49) were not associated with LOS. Of the patients who were type-2-high on admission (FeNO ≥ 20 ppb), 57% had fallen below that threshold by day 2 and 62% by discharge (71% and 71%, respectively, at ≥25 ppb). Over the admission-to-discharge interval, the changes in the two markers were unrelated once each was adjusted for its own admission value (partial ρ = 0.05, p = 0.73), and there was no agreement on the direction of change (κ = 0.03). Conclusions: FeNO progressively declines during treated AECOPD, alongside a fall in the blood eosinophil count, so that the type-2 label assigned on admission is no longer valid for most patients 48 h later. FeNO and blood eosinophils identified largely non-overlapping patients, and no biomarker predicted length of stay.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prediction of Midpalatal Suture Maturation from Cervical Vertebral Maturation Assessed on Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs: Development of a Combined Diagnostic Model.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the association between cervical vertebral maturation (CVM) and midpalatal suture (MPS) maturation and developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted model for predicting MPS stage from lateral cephalometric radiographs and clinical variables. Methods: CVM and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-defined MPS stages were assessed in 250 individuals. Their association was examined using Spearman correlation and multivariable ordinal logistic regression incorporating CVM stage, chronological age, and sex. A separate dataset of 1448 cephalograms was used to develop and evaluate a YOLOv11 model for automated CVM classification. The combined-model cohort comprised 325 patients, including the initial 250 and 75 additional patients, divided into training (n = 260) and held-out internal test (n = 65) subsets. The combined model was trained using reference CVM stage, chronological age, and sex and evaluated on the held-out test set using AI-predicted CVM stage in place of reference CVM. Results: CVM and MPS stages were strongly correlated (r = 0.749, p < 0.001). CVM stage and age were significantly associated with MPS stage, whereas sex was not (Nagelkerke R2 = 0.716). YOLOv11 correctly detected and classified 277/344 reference regions (80.5%). On the held-out test set, the combined model achieved 69.2% five-class accuracy (45/65; 95% CI: 57.2-79.1%) and 92.3% binary accuracy for A-C versus D-E. Repeated nested cross-validation across 325 patients yielded 58.3% mean accuracy with reference CVM, compared with 58.8% for reference CVM alone. Substituting AI-CVM only during evaluation in the 65-patient subset yielded 55.7% mean accuracy. Conclusions: The proposed AI-assisted model remains exploratory, with automated-input evaluation limited to 65 patients. The added predictive value of age and sex beyond CVM staging alone remains unproven. Its performance does not establish the ability to predict expansion success or justify replacing clinically indicated CBCT. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Clinical Significance of Severe and Borderline Umbilical Acidemia: Arterial pH, Lactate, Base Excess and Apgar Score Dynamics in Early Neonatal Risk Stratification.
articles.abstract: Background: While Apgar score is still the cornerstone of perinatal assessment, umbilical cord blood acid-base analysis provides objective information on fetal acid-base status at birth. Guidelines recommend cord blood gas evaluation in selected high-risk cases of low Apgar scores. However, newborns with severe and borderline acidemia may have temporarily reassuring Apgar scores despite biochemical evidence of metabolic stress. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of severe and borderline umbilical acidemia, especially in the case of pH 7.19-7.10 values as a gray zone, and to assess whether lactate, base excess and metabolic burden score improve neonatal risk stratification. Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of 1.989 newborns with available (routine) umbilical cord arterial blood gas parameters and 1 and 5 min Apgar scores. Severe and borderline acidemia were defined as arterial pH < 7.10 and 7.19-7.10, respectively. Arterial pH, lactate and base excess parameters were assessed, along with 1 and 5 min Apgar scores and early perinatal outcomes including the need for neonatal intensive care unit admission and CPAP requirement. Results: Close observation or NICU admission was associated with lower pH, higher lactate, and more negative base excess with a higher metabolic burden score. Among newborns with arterial pH < 7.20 (n = 299), ROC analysis showed lactate with the highest discriminative performance for close observation or NICU admission (AUC 0.783), followed by metabolic burden score (AUC 0.759). Both lactate and the metabolic burden score outperformed the pH risk alone. Although Apgar scores were statistically lower among admitted newborns, median 5 min Apgar values remained clinically reassuring. Conclusions: Severe and borderline umbilical arterial acidemia may identify neonates requiring closer observation. Integrating lactate, base excess, metabolic burden score and Apgar score dynamics may improve early risk stratification to discover perinatal hypoxia, with identification of newborns requiring close postnatal observation.

articles.title: FDNet: A Lightweight Feature-Dominated U-Net for Hippocampus Segmentation in Brain MRI.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hippocampus segmentation in brain MRI is challenging because the structure is small, irregularly shaped, and poorly contrasted against surrounding tissue. Increasingly complex U-Net variants improve accuracy at computational cost. We investigated whether modifying the relative contribution of encoder features within skip connections can improve performance without additional attention or gating modules. Methods: We propose FDNet, a lightweight feature-dominated U-Net that concatenates multiple identical copies of encoder feature maps with the corresponding decoder features. Three variants (FDNetX2, FDNetX3, and FDNetX4) were evaluated on sagittal MRI slices from ADNI, the Medical Segmentation Decathlon, and IBSR using five-fold cross-validation, assessed with overlap metrics and per-slice false-positive/false-negative counts. To address potential subject-level leakage in the slice-level evaluation, a subject-grouped assessment with a fixed held-out test set was additionally conducted on ADNI, with re-implemented baselines and nnU-Net v2. Results: Under the slice-level protocol, FDNet achieved Dice coefficients of 0.9339 on ADNI, 0.9470 on Decathlon, and 0.9477 on IBSR, outperforming re-implemented U-Net, Attention U-Net, and SegNet baselines with substantially fewer parameters. Under the subject-grouped protocol, the best FDNet variant reached a held-out test Dice of 0.9050 versus 0.9019 for nnU-Net. All variants significantly outperformed the three baselines after Holm correction (adjusted p < 0.0001); their advantage over nnU-Net was not significant. Conclusions: Repeated encoder features within skip connections can provide competitive hippocampus segmentation with a relatively small parameter budget. Because all results come from curated research datasets without external or cross-dataset validation, they indicate competitive performance under the evaluated conditions rather than clinical readiness.

articles.title: Interpretable RR Interval-Based ECG Rhythm Abnormality Detection: Cross-Dataset Evaluation, Feature Explainability, and Feature-Level Sensitivity Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Interpretable ECG rhythm classification remains challenging because of variability in recording conditions, patient characteristics, and annotation practices across datasets. Although deep learning models can achieve high classification performance, their limited interpretability and sensitivity to domain shift can restrict their applicability in real-world clinical settings. This study investigates an interpretable and computationally efficient framework for ECG rhythm abnormality detection using statistical descriptors of RR interval variability. Methods: Mean RR, SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, and heart rate features were extracted from ECG recordings to characterize beat-to-beat temporal variability. A Random Forest classifier was employed for binary rhythm classification using the PhysioNet/CinC 2017 dataset, followed by cross-dataset testing on the ECG-SDS dataset, which consists of synthetic ECG recordings. Same-dataset evaluation was additionally performed on ECG-SDS to establish a same-dataset performance benchmark. Feature ablation and feature-level sensitivity analyses using controlled Gaussian perturbations were conducted to examine feature contribution and classifier sensitivity to perturbations in the extracted feature representation. Multi-class experiments were also performed by incorporating atrial fibrillation and sinus tachy-brady rhythms. Results: In binary cross-dataset evaluation, the proposed framework achieved an accuracy of 78.6%, abnormal rhythm recall of 74.2%, and ROC-AUC of 0.836 on ECG-SDS. The same-dataset ECG-SDS evaluation achieved an accuracy of 93% and ROC-AUC of 0.89. Ten-fold stratified cross-validation yielded a mean accuracy of 92.20% ± 2.63% and mean AUC of 0.8880 ± 0.0477. Feature ablation showed only modest performance changes when individual descriptors were removed. The exploratory same-dataset multi-class evaluation on ECG-SDS achieved an accuracy of 91.67%. Conclusions: The results demonstrate that compact RR interval statistical descriptors can provide an interpretable and computationally efficient representation for ECG rhythm classification. The reduction in performance during cross-dataset testing may reflect dataset shift and differences in model configuration. These cross-dataset results should be interpreted as a technical assessment of transferability rather than as validation in an independent clinical population. Further validation using independent real-world clinical ECG datasets is required before conclusions regarding clinical generalizability or screening applications can be drawn.

articles.title: When Users Log Mood After Assessment: Temporal-Lag, Discriminant Validity, and the Simplicity Paradox of Single-Label Ecological Momentary Mood Tracking in a Saudi Arabic-Language Digital Mental Health Cohort-A Diagnostic-Accuracy Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Digital mental health platforms increasingly deploy self-directed single-label mood tracking as an ecological momentary assessment (EMA) tool, often framed as a screening indicator for depression or anxiety. Whether such naturalistic mood logs accurately detect screening-positive PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores has not been tested at scale against validated Arabic-language reference-standard instruments. Objectives: To evaluate, retrospectively, how accurately naturalistic single-label Arabic mood tracking detects screening-positive scores on the validated Arabic PHQ-9 and Arabic GAD-7 administered on the same platform, and to characterise the convergent-validity signal on continuous scores. Methods: This was a retrospective linked-records study of a Saudi Arabic-language commercial digital mental health platform. From 25,555 adult mood-logging users (aged 18 years or older), we assembled three intersection cohorts: depression (n = 4236), anxiety (n = 2449), and both-scales (n = 1825). Nine Arabic mood labels were categorised a priori as negative, positive, or neutral. Operating characteristics with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were computed for four primary indices; thirteen comparator specifications and four machine-learning models were compared against the best-performing index. AUC differences were evaluated with a DeLong-equivalent bootstrap test. Reporting followed STARD. Results: The best-performing index (proportion of negative logs) yielded an AUC of 0.624 (95% CI 0.604-0.642) for screening-positive detection of depression and 0.652 (0.629-0.676) for anxiety, both below the conventional 0.80 benchmark for a clinically useful screening test. Youden-optimal sensitivity and specificity were 0.522 (0.506-0.538) and 0.712 (0.679-0.741) for depression and 0.569 (0.547-0.589) and 0.706 (0.670-0.743) for anxiety. Positive likelihood ratios of 1.81 and 1.93 fell below the 2-5 range that is conventionally associated with even small clinically meaningful shifts in post-test probability. Spearman correlations with continuous scores were modest but stable across bootstrap resamples (ρ = 0.232 for depression, 0.268 for anxiety; both p < 0.001). Three structural findings emerged. First, a temporal-sequencing pattern was observed: median lag was +19 days for depression and +25 days for anxiety, with 80.9% and 79.4% of mood logs recorded on or after scale completion, respectively; among users with mood logs recorded before scale completion, AUC was 0.586 (0.554-0.618) for depression and 0.605 (0.569-0.641) for anxiety. Second, genuine discriminant validity was found for the depression-specific composite (Steiger's Z = 2.82, p = 0.005) but not for the anxiety-specific single label (Z = 0.32, p = 0.75), reflecting a 2.24% anxiety-label prevalence on this platform. Third, we observed a simplicity-paradox pattern in which added composite complexity either failed to raise cross-validated AUC or destroyed discriminant validity. Conclusions: On this platform, single-label Arabic mood tracking shows a modest but statistically reliable retrospective association with screening-positive status on the validated Arabic PHQ-9 and Arabic GAD-7 that does not reach the conventional 0.80 AUC benchmark for a clinically useful screening test; it should not substitute for these validated instruments. It is best treated as a longitudinal engagement and self-monitoring indicator rather than a stand-alone screening tool.

articles.title: Traumatic Cataract Following Accidental HIFU Exposure of the Upper Eyelid: A Rare Ocular Complication-Case Report.
articles.abstract: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) is increasingly used for noninvasive facial tightening, but inadvertent exposure of the periocular region may injure ocular structures.
