We present a 34-year-old woman who developed sudden visual deterioration approximately 30 min after facial HIFU when the applicator accidentally moved onto the right upper eyelid. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), measured using Snellen charts, was 0.2 in decimal scale in the right eye and 1.0 in the left eye, with intraocular pressure of 17 and 14 mmHg, respectively. Slit-lamp examination revealed a slightly dilated, sluggish pupil and dense inferior lens opacity with a rosette-shaped opacity involving the posterior lens, while the eyelid skin and cornea remained intact. Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) and ultrasound biomicroscopy showed no capsular rupture; ultrasound biomicroscopy additionally demonstrated separation of cortical lens material from the posterior capsule. BCVA progressively decreased to 0.04 before cataract surgery. Phacoemulsification with implantation of a non-diffractive spiral intraocular lens was performed two months after the HIFU exposure. On postoperative day 1, uncorrected visual acuity was 1.0 at distance and 0.5 at near, with intraocular pressure of 16 mmHg, and these findings remained stable during six months of follow-up. Posterior segment OCT and visual field testing showed no clinically relevant abnormalities. The images illustrate a characteristic pattern of traumatic cataract following inadvertent periocular HIFU exposure and the multimodal imaging used for diagnosis and follow-up. This case emphasizes that lens injury may occur despite an intact cornea and eyelid and supports strict avoidance of direct HIFU application to the eyelids, together with appropriate ocular protection.

articles.title: Comparative Radiomics Analysis of Trabecular Bone Surrounding Dental Implants on Panoramic Radiographs in Smokers and Non-Smokers.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Smoking is associated with adverse dental implant outcomes, but early smoking-related changes in peri-implant trabecular bone texture remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated longitudinal changes in panoramic radiomics features around dental implants in active smokers and non-smokers. Methods: This retrospective study included 47 patients and 110 implant sites, with 55 implant sites per group. Panoramic radiographs obtained at 0-7 days (T0), 4-6 weeks (T1), and 10-14 weeks (T2) after implant placement were analyzed. Twenty-eight first-order gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) and gray-level run length matrix (GLRLM) features were extracted; features with intraclass correlation coefficients ≥ 0.75 were included in mixed repeated-measures analyses. Results: Twenty-six features met the reliability threshold. Following BH-FDR correction across the 26 group-by-time interaction tests, significant interactions remained for GLCM Contrast (adjusted p = 0.010) and GLRLM Short Run Emphasis (SRE; adjusted p = 0.033). The Entropy interaction did not remain statistically significant after correction (adjusted p = 0.075). Contrast increased in smokers but remained relatively stable in non-smokers, whereas SRE decreased in smokers and increased in non-smokers. Conclusions: Smoking status was associated with divergent early peri-implant radiographic texture trajectories, particularly for Contrast and SRE. These findings indicate quantitative imaging differences rather than direct evidence of impaired osseointegration and warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Association and Discrimination of Urinary System Stone Disease Using Anthropometric Indices, Lifestyle Behaviors, and Artificial Intelligence: A Multicenter Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Urinary system stone disease is common and highly recurrent, and body mass index (BMI) poorly reflects the central adiposity linked to stone risk. We compared BMI with five next-generation anthropometric indices (A Body Shape Index [ABSI], Body Roundness Index [BRI], Waist-to-Height Ratio [WtHR], Conicity Index [ConI], Waist-to-Hip Ratio [WHR]) for their association with stone disease, and developed a hybrid autoencoder-based artificial intelligence model integrating anthropometric, clinical, and lifestyle data. Methods: This multicenter case-control study included 1195 participants (562 stone cases, 633 controls) from six centers in Turkey. Thirty-one variables were grouped into three subgroups (basic measurements, derived indices, clinical/lifestyle data), each processed by a separate autoencoder; combined features were classified with XGBoost, Cubic SVM, Fine KNN, and logistic regression. Each index's independent association was assessed by quartile-based logistic regression, and discriminative power by ROC/AUC. Results: BMI showed no between-group difference (p = 0.919) or discriminative power (AUC = 0.498). ABSI, BRI, WtHR, ConI, and WHR were all significantly higher in the stone group, showed positive trends across quartiles after full adjustment (all p-trend ≤ 0.001), and outperformed BMI (AUC 0.547-0.564); associations were strongest for ConI (aOR = 2.62) and ABSI (aOR = 2.57). The hybrid AI model performed best with XGBoost (77% accuracy), followed by Fine KNN (71%), logistic regression (69%), and Cubic SVM (68%). Conclusions: Unlike BMI, next-generation indices reflecting central adiposity are independently and consistently associated with stone disease, and a multivariable AI model combining anthropometric, clinical, and lifestyle data reached 77% accuracy in separating stone patients from controls on a single test split. These findings are a hypothesis-generating risk-stratification signal that requires external validation, and they do not support clinical screening.

articles.title: MTEP: A Matched Temporal Evaluation Protocol for Cognitive Fatigue Detection from In-Task Self-Reports.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Fatigue models are often trained on labels that participants produce, by an action, while the sensors record. We aimed to certify that an evaluation design's estimates reflect the state rather than the report. Methods: We present MTEP, a matched temporal evaluation protocol delivering label and feature separation, participant-level generalisation, within-recording position balance and report-independence, meaning that no window used to predict a report overlaps the act producing it. We certify report-independence by lead displacement and position balance with linear and nonlinear models, calibrate both certificates with injected effects of known amplitude and shape, compare four evaluation designs on corpora of known truth, and apply MTEP to CogBeacon and CL-Drive. Results: On corpora of known truth, MTEP returned the correct verdict in 78 of 80 cases against 58-62 for designs in current use, which concluded that a detector works in 16-19 of 20 corpora containing only the reporting act (MTEP: 1 of 20). The report-independence certificate had a specificity of 39/40 and detected an act-borne component of 0.05 local standard deviations in 30/40 replicates; the nonlinear position certificate detected imbalances the linear test missed (10/10 vs. 0/10). On CogBeacon, MTEP certified at a lead of one round, with pooled ROC-AUC 0.659 carried by task performance. Our model exceeded every published single-classifier accuracy on the same EEG features and protocols, yet a sensor-free clock matched or exceeded published accuracies on both corpora. Conclusions: Report-independence is a distinct requirement that existing designs do not imply; it can be checked from the collection protocol and certified on the evaluation sample.

articles.title: Five Multimodal AI Configurations Versus Anaesthesiologists for Pecto-Intercostal Block Classification in an Archived-Image Reader Study of a Prospective CABG Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We compared five general-purpose multimodal AI configurations with anaesthesiologists classifying sonographic pecto-intercostal fascial plane block spread. Methods: This archived-image reader study used a prospective cohort of 120 ASA III adults undergoing isolated coronary artery bypass grafting at one centre. In June 2026, five free AI configurations and three experts classified identical sets of 8-10 left-sided frames. Direct binary comparisons used each expert's labels in 115 block recipients; five no-block controls were separate. The senior expert reviewed expert labels before setting the final reference, precluding independent expert-AI accuracy comparison. Reference-conditioned balanced accuracy was defined as mean sensitivity and specificity. Results: Direct balanced agreement was 42.3-53.9% for four configurations and 55.4-64.9% for Kimi K2.6. AI asserted spread in 17/25 no-block classifications; all 20 human classifications indicated absence. Final-reference balanced accuracy was 76.9-91.9% for experts and 44.6-66.9% for AI, conditional on the expert-informed reference. Pain analyses were exploratory. Conclusions: Direct comparisons establish neither anatomical accuracy nor independent expert superiority. Limitations include one centre, operator and ultrasound system; selected frames; free access; no raw AI outputs, reproducible a priori power calculation or non-recruitment-day eligibility log.

articles.title: Chronic Post-Traumatic Organized Hematoma of the Brachial Artery: The Role of Multimodal Ultrasound.
articles.abstract: Chronic post-traumatic organized hematoma of the upper extremity is uncommon and may mimic a soft-tissue mass or a pseudoaneurysm when predominantly thrombosed. We report a 60-year-old woman with progressive right upper-arm swelling and finger numbness 30 years after blunt trauma. CT angiography demonstrated a low-attenuation mass along the brachial-ulnar arterial course with tortuous vessels along its margin. Gray-scale ultrasound demonstrated a large heterogeneous, predominantly hypoechoic lesion adjacent to the brachial artery, while conventional color Doppler provided limited vascular information. Superb microvascular imaging (SMI) detected sparse intralesional and perilesional arterial flow, and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) further demonstrated partial microbubble filling supplied by small arterial branches arising from the brachial artery. These findings initially raised the possibility of a chronic partially thrombosed pseudoaneurysm; however, no pseudoaneurysmal neck or characteristic to-and-fro flow was identified. The lesion was therefore considered most consistent with a chronic post-traumatic organized hematoma with neovascularization supplied by small brachial artery branches. Ultrasound-guided biopsy revealed organized fibrous tissue with hemorrhage and sparse inflammatory cells, supporting an organizing hematoma and excluding malignancy. This case underscores the diagnostic challenge of chronic post-traumatic organized hematoma and highlights the role of comprehensive ultrasound, particularly SMI and CEUS, in characterizing vascularity and informing clinical decisions.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Triage and Diagnostic Support for Gastric Biopsies: A Multi-Centre Prospective Evaluation Across NHS Wales.
articles.abstract: Background: Histopathology workforce shortages and operational backlogs severely delay gastric cancer reporting. This multi-centre prospective evaluation assessed the diagnostic accuracy, clinical safety-net utility, and workflow triaging efficiency of an artificial intelligence (AI) platform for gastric biopsies across NHS Wales. Methods: A prospective cohort of 848 consecutive gastric biopsy cases across three NHS Health Boards was processed using a commercial AI platform. Diagnostic performance was evaluated against standard-of-care clinical reference diagnoses. Post-analytic cross-tabulation simulated dynamic AI-driven worklist prioritisation to quantify triage safety, false-positive alerts, and turnaround time impact across urgent and routine pathways. Results: For gastric malignancies (n = 40), the AI platform achieved a sensitivity of 100.0% (95% CI: 91.2-100.0%; AUC 0.986) and a specificity of 97.2% (95% CI: 95.8-98.1%). Sensitivities for low-grade dysplasia/adenoma (n = 12) and gastric intestinal metaplasia (n = 98) were 100.0% and 94.9%, respectively. The AI review functioned as a parallel safety net, capturing eight primary lesions missed during routine human evaluation, including one occult adenocarcinoma. In workflow simulation, the platform correctly prioritised 100.0% of cancers, including 6 cancers hidden within routine backlogs, and 97.2% (106/109) of high-risk non-cancer precursors, with false-positive alerts in 4.6% (39/848) of all cases. Conclusions: AI-assisted gastric pathology review demonstrates exceptional diagnostic accuracy, acts as a reliable clinical support tool, and enables effective risk-stratified triage. Deploying AI triage in public healthcare infrastructure offers a scalable solution with the potential to reduce diagnostic backlogs and accelerate treatment for high-risk oncology patients.

articles.title: Prospective Evaluation of Super-Resolution Ultrasound for Differentiating Benign and Malignant Small Breast Nodules.
articles.abstract: Objective: The objectives of this study were to identify key super-resolution ultrasound (SR US) microvascular parameters via cluster analysis and evaluate their value in differentiating benign from malignant breast nodules of size ≤2 cm, and to assess the added value of integrating conventional US features. Methods: This study screened 481 breast nodules by conventional and SR US; 123 nodules of size ≤2 cm were included. Spearman hierarchical clustering, within-cluster principal component analysis, and iterative variance inflation factor elimination selected core parameters. With histopathology as the reference, five models were built: conventional US morphological features (M1), quantitative SR US (M2), M2 plus enlarged enhancement area and penetrating vessels (M3), Model 1 plus enlarged enhancement area and penetrating vessels (M4), and all features (M5). Performance was compared by AUCs and the DeLong test, with bootstrap optimism correction, Hosmer-Lemeshow calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: Five parameters were retained: vascular density (VD), fractal dimension (FD), mean intensity (Mean Inten), standard deviation of velocity (Std Vel), and minimum velocity (Min Vel). The AUCs for M1-M5 were 0.702, 0.752, 0.820, 0.793, and 0.852, and their sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value (%) were 50.0/82.2/65.8/70.6, 58.0/82.2/69.0/74.1, 86.0/65.8/63.2/87.3, 80.0/69.9/64.5/83.6, and 88.0/71.2/67.7/89.7, respectively; M5 performed best (AUC 0.852; sensitivity 88.0%, specificity 71.2%, PPV 67.7%, NPV 89.7%). The bootstrap-corrected AUCs were 0.684, 0.716, 0.779, 0.732 and 0.799; calibration was adequate and DCA confirmed a net benefit for SR US models. Conclusions: VD, FD, Mean Inten, Std Vel, and Min Vel differentiate benign from malignant breast nodules of size ≤ 2 cm. SR US outperforms conventional US, and integrating morphologic features further improves discrimination.

articles.title: Mitigating Text Dominance in Medical Vision-Language Learning for Long-Tailed Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medical vision-language learning integrates radiographic images and textual information for chest X-ray (CXR) classification. However, in long-tailed multi-label CXR classification, modality imbalance can cause models to rely disproportionately on radiology reports while underutilizing visual information. This study investigates text dominance and proposes a modality-balanced framework to strengthen visual representation while preserving multimodal performance. Methods: Experiments used MIMIC-CXR with patient-level training, validation, and test splits of 32,942, 4024, and 3955 paired samples, respectively. Swin-Tiny and PubMedBERT served as visual and textual encoders. The proposed framework combines adaptive gated fusion, Asymmetric Loss (ASL), and training-time modality dropout. It was compared with Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) concatenation, ASL concatenation, gated fusion, and cross-attention fusion. Results: The BCE baseline achieved a Macro AUROC of 0.9957 under Image + Text evaluation and 0.5804 under Image-Only evaluation, while Text-Only evaluation yielded 0.9955, indicating substantial modality disparity. Other alternatives achieved Image-Only Macro AUROC values of 0.5610-0.5720. The proposed framework improved Image-Only Macro AUROC to 0.7697 and Macro PR-AUC from 0.1814 to 0.3428 while maintaining an Image + Text Macro AUROC of 0.9958. The modality-dominance gap decreased from 0.4151 to 0.2260, a 45.6% reduction in performance disparity. Grad-CAM and Integrated Gradients provided insights into visual evidence and textual attribution, revealing reliance on explicit disease-related terminology in reports. Conclusions: These findings suggest that combining adaptive gated fusion, ASL, and modality dropout can improve Image-Only performance while preserving multimodal discrimination in long-tailed multi-label CXR classification.

articles.title: Comparing Lightweight Models for Physician-Consensus Pharyngitis Classification from Primary-Care Smartphone Images.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Smartphone-acquired throat images could support accessible pharyngitis assessment, but the performance and computational efficiency of lightweight models on such images require further evaluation. This study compared five lightweight models for predicting physician-consensus bacterial versus nonbacterial labels from smartphone throat images. Methods: We analyzed PGUPharyngitis, a public dataset of smartphone throat images collected in general practice. The final cohort comprised 635 patients, of whom 105 (16.5%) had bacterial physician-consensus labels. The reference outcome was physician consensus based on images and clinical information rather than microbiological testing. Five ImageNet-pretrained lightweight classifiers-four convolutional neural networks (CNNs; MobileNetV3-Small, EfficientNet-B0, ShuffleNetV2, and YOLO26n-cls) and one CNN-Transformer hybrid (MobileViT-XS)-were fine-tuned using patient-level five-fold cross-validation. Performance was assessed using area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), alongside computational efficiency. Device-only and clinical-variable logistic-regression models provided non-image comparisons. Results: Mean PR-AUC across folds ranged from 0.317 to 0.372 and AUROC from 0.663 to 0.708, with no clearly superior architecture. Bacterial-label prevalence differed by acquisition device (Samsung 9.2% versus Xiaomi 26.9%); the device-only and clinical-variable comparators achieved AUROCs of 0.650 and 0.598, respectively. At validation-selected high-sensitivity thresholds, the models flagged 65-78% of patients, with positive predictive values of only 19-22%. All models contained fewer than five million parameters, making them compact candidates for future evaluation on resource-constrained devices. Conclusions: Lightweight models showed moderate performance against physician-consensus labels. However, acquisition device was associated with the reference labels, image-model AUROCs were not clearly distinguishable from that of the device-only comparator, and device-related confounding cannot be excluded. Because performance was measured against these labels and positive predictive values were low, the findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy or clinical applicability, which require validation against microbiological reference standards in independent clinical cohorts.

articles.title: A Comparative Study of Breast Tumors Before and After Neoadjuvant Therapy.
articles.abstract: Background: Pathological response after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer varies substantially across immunohistochemical surrogate subtypes. This study aimed to compare pretreatment biopsy features with post-treatment surgical pathology findings and to explore baseline predictors of favorable pathological response. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed female patients with invasive breast carcinoma treated with neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery at a single institution between January 2020 and December 2024. Pretreatment histological features, stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, tumor cellularity, necrosis, in situ component, lymphovascular/perineural invasion, and immunohistochemical surrogate subtype were compared with post-treatment findings. Residual disease was assessed using the Residual Cancer Burden system, and vital status was analyzed as an exploratory outcome. Results: The analytical dataset included 146 breast carcinoma records. RCB-0, RCB-I, RCB-II, and RCB-III were observed in 20, 14, 64, and 46 of 144 evaluable records, respectively, and pCR was identified in 18/142 evaluable records. Tumor cellularity decreased significantly after therapy, whereas stromal TILs and tumor necrosis did not change significantly. Favorable pathological response and pCR were more frequent in HER2-positive and triple-negative tumors than in luminal tumors. In univariable Firth regression, higher baseline stromal TILs and HER2-positive/triple-negative subtype were associated with increased odds of RCB 0/I and pCR, and both associations persisted in multivariable models adjusted for age and grade. Nineteen patients (13.0%) deceased; crude mortality increased across RCB classes (0%, 14.3%, 7.8% and 26.1% for RCB-0 to RCB-III; p = 0.008), with no deaths among patients achieving pCR. Conclusions: In conclusion, favorable pathological response after neoadjuvant therapy was uncommon in this cohort and was observed mainly in HER2-positive and triple-negative tumors. Baseline stromal TILs and immunohistochemical surrogate subtype showed exploratory associations with response, supporting their further evaluation in larger, treatment-stratified cohorts with formal survival follow-up.

articles.title: Quantitative CT Analysis of Nasal Septal Body and Inferior Turbinate Morphology in Allergic Rhinitis: Structural-Airway Relationships.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is characterized by dynamic mucosal congestion, yet the nasal septal body (NSB), inferior turbinate (IT), and adjacent airway passages have rarely been assessed together. We evaluated whether AR is associated with a multilevel structural-airway pattern while limiting confounding by marked septal deviation. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 301 adults with septal deviation < 8° (163 patients with clinically diagnosed AR and 138 participants in a clinically defined non-AR comparison group). Coronal computed tomography measurements included total transverse NSB width, dominant IT width, and adjacent airway widths. Between-group differences were evaluated using effect sizes and multivariable regression adjusted for age, sex, and septal deviation angle. Correlation, interaction, and sensitivity analyses assessed structure-airway relationships. Results: Patients with AR had greater NSB width (11.92 ± 1.81 vs. 10.80 ± 1.89 mm; Hedges' g = 0.605) and dominant IT width (12.78 ± 1.69 vs. 10.41 ± 1.83 mm; g = 1.350), together with smaller adjacent airway widths. All four primary comparisons remained significant after Holm correction and adjustment (all p < 0.001). The NSB-IT correlation (rho = 0.257) was attenuated after adjustment for AR (partial rho = 0.089; q = 0.124), whereas inverse structure-airway associations persisted. A significant AR-status × IT-width interaction was observed for medial airway width (interaction q = 0.030). Conclusions: At the time of CT, patients with AR had greater NSB and IT widths and smaller corresponding regional airway dimensions, with a larger between-group morphometric difference at the IT level. These findings support a multilevel anatomical view of the nasal airway in AR, in which the NSB and IT are best interpreted together with their adjacent airway spaces rather than as isolated structures. Their clinical relevance, however, requires validation against symptoms and objective airflow measures.

articles.title: Automated Intracranial Hemorrhage Segmentation in CT Images Using Attention U-Net with Deep Supervision and Test-Time Augmentation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Intracranial hemorrhage is a life-threatening condition that requires rapid and accurate diagnosis using computed tomography (CT). Manual segmentation is time-consuming and subject to interobserver variability, motivating the development of automated segmentation methods. This study proposes an enhanced Attention U-Net for intracranial hemorrhage segmentation using the RSNA Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection dataset, in which only 1082 of 20,154 images have pixel-level annotations. The proposed architecture integrates attention gates, deep supervision, cosine annealing, and test-time augmentation. An ablation study was also conducted to evaluate the contribution of each component. Methods: The proposed Attention U-Net and a baseline U-Net were trained and evaluated using identical experimental protocols. Performance was assessed on an independent test set using the Dice score, IoU, sensitivity, and precision. To evaluate the reproducibility of the performance advantage across datasets, both architectures were additionally trained and evaluated under identical protocols on the independent Brain Hemorrhage Segmentation Dataset (BHSD), comprising 2961 annotated axial slices derived from 192 CT volumes. The BHSD test set consisted of 621 slices. Results: On the independent RSNA test set, the proposed Attention U-Net achieved a Dice score of 0.7965 (±0.0814), outperforming the baseline U-Net (0.7683 ± 0.0906). The proposed model also achieved an IoU of 0.6689, sensitivity of 0.8094, and precision of 0.7966. On the BHSD test set, the Attention U-Net again outperformed the baseline U-Net, achieving a Dice score of 0.5676 versus 0.5063, sensitivity of 0.5350 versus 0.5138, and IoU of 0.4408 versus 0.3924. Thus, the proposed architecture demonstrated a consistent relative performance advantage across both independent datasets, although absolute performance was lower on BHSD than on RSNA. Conclusions: The findings demonstrate that incorporating attention mechanisms, multiscale supervision, and inference-time enhancement can improve intracranial hemorrhage segmentation performance. The consistent improvement over the baseline U-Net across two independent datasets further supports the effectiveness and cross-dataset robustness of the proposed architecture. The results also highlight the potential of semi-supervised learning to leverage the large volume of unlabeled CT data available in intracranial hemorrhage datasets.

articles.title: Diagnosis Prediction of Lumbar Spinal Canal Stenosis by Plain Radiography Using Discriminative Radiographic Features.
articles.abstract: Purpose: To investigate whether widely available lumbar spine radiography can predict lumbar spinal canal stenosis (LSCS). Methods: This retrospective, single-center cross-sectional study included patients who underwent both lumbar spine radiography and magnetic resonance imaging. Correlations between radiographic and MRI parameters and their associations with LSCS were analyzed with adjustment for age and sex. The predictive performance of machine learning algorithms was evaluated with nested cross-validation. Results: Among 201 subjects, 104 had L4/5 LSCS and 97 did not; the LSCS group was 18 years older. After adjustment for age and sex, static spondylolisthesis (aOR 5.62, p < 0.001), average disc height (aOR 1.23, p = 0.021), and dynamic lordotic angle (aOR 0.96, p = 0.011) remained significant predictors, and adding radiographic parameters to age and sex increased the AUC from 0.85 to 0.91 (p = 0.007). Static spondylolisthesis remained significant in an age- and sex-matched subset (aOR 4.81). In nested cross-validation, machine learning models combining radiographic parameters with age and sex achieved an accuracy of 80.7% (sensitivity 82.9%, specificity 78.4%, AUC 0.87), compared with 76.2% for radiographic parameters alone. Conclusions: Lumbar spine radiography provides information on LSCS that is additional to age. Radiographic signs reflecting the stabilization phase of spinal degeneration, particularly static spondylolisthesis and decreased dynamic lordosis, were the most robust predictors. External validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Temporal Lactate Kinetics and Tissue Lactate Burden in Experimental Skeletal Muscle Ischemia-Reperfusion: Associations with Inflammation, Cellular Injury, and Oxidative Stress.
articles.abstract: Background: Skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) induces metabolic, inflammatory, and oxidative disturbances that may persist after restoration of blood flow. This study evaluated circulating lactate kinetics together with tissue lactate, inflammatory, cellular injury, and oxidative markers following experimental skeletal muscle I/R. Methods: Animals subjected to skeletal muscle I/R were compared with vascular I/R, bone fracture, sham, and control groups. Circulating lactate, PO2, glucose, hematocrit, and calculated oxygen saturation were assessed immediately after ischemia, approximately 15 min after reperfusion, and approximately 2 h after reperfusion. Tissue and plasma lactate, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), interleukin-6 (IL-6), malondialdehyde (MDA), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) were also evaluated. Results: In the skeletal muscle I/R group, circulating lactate decreased from 2.19 ± 0.67 mmol/L immediately after ischemia to 1.44 ± 0.84 mmol/L during early reperfusion, before rising to 3.33 ± 1.15 mmol/L at approximately 2 h (Friedman p < 0.001), resulting in a negative lactate clearance. This biphasic pattern contrasted with the progressive decline in lactate observed in the vascular I/R and bone fracture groups. Tissue lactate was markedly elevated (11.96 ± 1.27 mmol/L) and showed positive correlations with MDA (ρ = 0.802), IL-6 (ρ = 0.741), and LDH (ρ = 0.671), all p < 0.001. Conclusions: Skeletal muscle I/R was characterized by a late increase in circulating lactate together with elevated tissue lactate and biochemical evidence of inflammatory activation, cellular injury, and oxidative stress. Serial lactate assessment may provide complementary information on post-ischemic metabolic recovery, although further validation is required.

articles.title: Clinical Performance of a Fully Integrated Sample-to-Answer Multiplex PCR Respiratory Panel: A Multicenter Evaluation Using Prospective, Archived and Contrived Nasopharyngeal Specimens.
articles.abstract: Background: Most syndromic respiratory PCR panels process one specimen per cartridge and instrument module. Objectives: We evaluated the agreement of a fully integrated, batch-capable sample-to-answer 22-target respiratory panel with BioFire FilmArray Respiratory Panel 2.1. Methods: Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected prospectively from symptomatic individuals aged ≥ 2 years at three US clinical sites between December 2025 and May 2026. Investigational and comparator testing were performed in separate, mutually blinded CLIA-certified laboratories; discordant specimens were retested with a third molecular assay, reported descriptively. Archived (n = 240) and contrived (n = 200) specimens for low-prevalence targets were analyzed separately. Positive and negative percent agreement (PPA, NPA) were reported with Wilson score 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results: Of 1501 participants enrolled, 1482 specimens yielded paired valid results; final invalid rates after repeat testing were 0.07% and 0.13%, respectively. Twelve targets met all prespecified prospective acceptance criteria (PPA 91.5-100%). Seven targets had PPA point estimates of 90.0-100% but lower 95% CI bounds below 80%, and three had no prospective positives. NPA was 99.6-100% for all 22 targets. Conclusions: The system showed high agreement with the comparator for targets well represented in prospective specimens. For the remaining ten targets, prospective evidence was insufficient to confirm the acceptance criteria; archived and contrived results provide supportive evidence of detection but do not change this prospective classification.

articles.title: Lean Mass Index Adjustment of eGFR Strengthens Associations with Cardiometabolic Risk Factors.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Serum creatinine (SCr)-based estimates of glomerular filtration rate (eGFRSCr) are influenced by muscle mass. This study investigated whether normalizing SCr to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA)-derived lean mass index (LMI) alters associations with cardiometabolic phenotypes. Methods: We analyzed 11,141 adults (mean age 46.0 ± 17.2 years) from the Austrian LEAD (Lung, hEart, sociAl, boDy) cohort. SCr was normalized to sex- and age-specific LMI reference values to calculate LMI-adjusted eGFR (eGFRLMISCr) within individuals. Associations with prevalent cardiometabolic conditions were compared using age- and sex-adjusted logistic regression with paired bootstrap resampling. Annualized eGFR change was compared in 7487 participants with complete follow-up measurements. Results: The estimates were closely correlated (R2 = 0.897), but LMI adjustment changed GFR-category assignment in both directions. Higher eGFRLMISCr was positively associated with prevalent dyslipidemia, hypertension, pre-diabetes, diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity. Differences in annualized change depended on age and sex, with lower LMI-adjusted slopes in women, particularly at younger ages, and higher slopes in men. Conclusion: LMI adjustment influences eGFR slopes in a sex- and age-specific manner and changes both filtration function category assignment and associations with cardiometabolic phenotypes. As these associations may partly reflect the direct incorporation of body composition into the estimate, our findings will require validation against measured GFR or an independent filtration marker.

articles.title: DenseGated-MSNet: A Multi-Sequence Gated Fusion Network for Multiple Sclerosis Classification from Brain MRI.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays a central role in its diagnosis and monitoring. Because different MRI sequences provide complementary information about MS-related pathology, jointly exploiting multiple sequences may improve automated classification. However, many existing automated MS classification studies rely on limited sequence information, are not consistently evaluated under subject-independent protocols, and are constrained by the scarcity of publicly available multi-sequence datasets organized at the subject level. Methods: To address these gaps, we collected and publicly released a new multi-sequence brain MRI dataset and proposed DenseGated-MSNet, a novel end-to-end multi-input deep learning model for MS versus non-MS classification. DenseGated-MSNet processes each co-acquired MRI sequence in parallel through an independent sequence-specific DenseNet-121 branch and integrates the resulting representations through a proposed input-dependent gated feature-level fusion mechanism. Under a strict subject-independent evaluation protocol, the model configuration was determined on a subject-independent development set, and the performance of the final model was internally evaluated using five-fold subject-independent cross-validation on the same cohort at the image and subject levels. Results: In internal five-fold subject-independent cross-validation, DenseGated-MSNet achieved a pooled subject-level accuracy of 90.57% (95% CI: 86.44-93.53%) and an AUC of 0.947 (95% CI: 0.918-0.976). The learned gate values also provided sequence-level modulation information, indicating how strongly each MRI sequence was weighted during multi-sequence integration. Conclusions: Overall, these findings suggest that DenseGated-MSNet can effectively integrate complementary information from multiple MRI sequences for discriminating established MS from selected non-MS controls, while providing sequence-level modulation information. Together with the released dataset, the proposed framework provides a reproducible basis for future subject-independent MS classification studies.

articles.title: DBS Direct Elution and Multiplex Digital PCR for SMN1 and SMN2 Copy-Number and CFTR Variant Detection: Development and Validation of a Molecular Screening Workflow.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Scalable molecular workflows may facilitate carrier screening for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and cystic fibrosis (CF). This study aimed to develop and validate a dried blood spot (DBS)-based multiplex digital PCR (dPCR) workflow for SMN1 and SMN2 copy-number analysis and targeted detection of CFTR p.Phe508del. Methods: The workflow combined direct DNA elution with multiplex dPCR. Analytical validation used 50 previously characterized samples, with multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) and Sanger sequencing as reference methods. The workflow was subsequently applied to 1670 women from Crete and Ikaria, Greece, followed by targeted testing of 10 partners. Results: All 50 directly eluted samples amplified successfully. dPCR showed complete agreement with reference methods. Repeatability coefficients of variation were below 5%. Copy-number classification performance estimates are apparent, as thresholds were derived and evaluated in the same small validation cohort. Among 1670 women screened, 34 (2.04%) were identified as SMN1 carriers and 20 (1.20%) as CFTR p.Phe508del carriers. Partner testing identified two carrier couples. Conclusions: The DBS-based multiplex dPCR workflow demonstrated complete analytical concordance with reference methods in this preliminary validation and was implemented in a population screening cohort. Its targeted scope leaves residual carrier risk, requiring appropriate counseling. Larger independent validation and formal throughput and cost assessments are needed before routine implementation.

articles.title: YOLO11m-Based Artificial Intelligence Versus Orthopaedic Physician Panels for Arthroscopy-Referenced Three-Category MRI Classification of the Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff: A Multi-Reader Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) may support rotator cuff MRI interpretation; however, its performance relative to clinicians at different experience levels remains uncertain. We compared a locked YOLO11m-based model with prespecified orthopaedic physician panels using arthroscopy as the reference standard. Methods: This retrospective single-centre study included a separate 300-patient model-development dataset and an arthroscopy-referenced reader cohort of 258 patients (60 intact cuffs, 86 partial-thickness tears, and 112 full-thickness tears). Twelve blinded physicians were assigned to four three-reader experience panels, and panel diagnoses were defined by a two-of-three majority. Paired accuracy comparisons used exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment. Results: AI achieved 0.841 overall accuracy (95% CI, 0.792-0.881). The senior-specialist panel had numerically higher accuracy (0.911), but the difference from AI was not statistically significant after adjustment (Holm p = 0.060); the junior-specialist panel also did not differ from AI (0.822; Holm p = 0.649). AI showed higher paired accuracy than the senior-resident (0.729; Holm p = 0.005) and junior-resident panels (0.671; Holm p < 0.001). Partial-thickness tears had the lowest AI sensitivity (0.709). Conclusions: In this restricted-cine, three-category benchmark, AI outperformed both resident panels, whereas neither specialist panel comparison reached the adjusted significance threshold. These findings do not establish equivalence to specialists or benefit from AI-assisted reading.

articles.title: Sinonasal Anatomic Variations Across Vertical Skeletal Patterns in Skeletal Class I Adults: A Retrospective Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Vertical skeletal morphology may influence maxillofacial dimensions, but its relationship with discrete sinonasal anatomic variations remains uncertain. This study compared the prevalence of paranasal sinus and nasal cavity variations among adults with hypodivergent, hyperdivergent, and normodivergent skeletal patterns. Methods: Faculty archives spanning 2016-2025 were screened. Eighty-seven untreated adults with a skeletal Class I relationship were included and categorized according to their vertical skeletal pattern as follows: 27 hypodivergent, 26 hyperdivergent, and 34 normodivergent. All cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) examinations were acquired using a single NewTom 5G unit with 0.25 mm isotropic voxels. Nasal septal deviation and septal spur were evaluated per participant; 22 additional variants were evaluated bilaterally. Side-level comparisons used binary logistic generalized estimating equations with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Results: Age (p = 0.5072), nasal septal deviation (p = 0.2247), and septal spur (p = 0.9294) did not differ significantly among groups. The paradoxical middle turbinate showed a nominal group effect (Wald χ2 = 6.199, p = 0.0451), but the association was no longer significant after false discovery rate correction (q = 0.4642). No other estimable side-level group or within-group right-left comparison was significant. Conclusions: No statistically significant associations were detected between vertical skeletal pattern and sinonasal anatomical variations in this sample of skeletal Class I adults. However, small-to-moderate associations cannot be excluded, particularly for rare variants. The nominal finding for the paradoxical middle turbinate requires confirmation in larger, prospectively defined cohorts.

articles.title: Systemic Redox Biomarkers in Diabetic Retinopathy: Comparative Evaluation of Thiol-Disulfide Homeostasis, Ischemia-Modified Albumin, and Superoxide Dismutase.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Oxidative stress is implicated in diabetic retinal injury, but systemic redox biomarkers in diabetic retinopathy remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to evaluate systemic thiol-disulfide homeostasis (TDH), ischemia-modified albumin (IMA), and serum and urinary superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity in patients with diabetic retinopathy (DRP), diabetic individuals without retinopathy, and healthy controls. Methods: This cross-sectional comparative study included 31 patients with treatment-naïve DRP, 31 diabetic patients without retinopathy, and 45 healthy controls. Serum native thiol, total thiol, disulfide, IMA, and serum and urinary SOD activities were measured at a single study visit and compared among groups. Results: Serum native thiol, total thiol, and disulfide concentrations differed among the three groups (all overall p ≤ 0.001). Compared with diabetic patients without retinopathy, patients with DRP had lower native thiol concentrations after Bonferroni correction (p = 0.011); the difference in total thiol did not meet the corrected significance threshold (p = 0.029). Both diabetic groups had lower disulfide concentrations than healthy controls. IMA concentrations and serum and urinary SOD activities did not differ significantly among groups (all p > 0.05). Of the 31 patients with DRP, 15 had diabetic macular edema (DME), whereas 16 did not have DME. No statistically significant differences in the measured redox biomarkers were detected between patients with and without DME. Conclusions: Lower serum native thiol concentrations were associated with diabetic retinopathy in this cross-sectional cohort, whereas IMA and serum and urinary SOD activities showed no significant between-group differences. These findings suggest that circulating thiol status warrants further investigation in larger, longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Factors Affecting Time to First Treatment in Early-Stage Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Most patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) are diagnosed at an early stage, but the time to first treatment (TTFT) varies widely. We aimed to identify clinical and routine laboratory factors associated with TTFT. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 103 patients with Rai stage I-II CLL followed at a tertiary center between 2005 and 2025. TTFT was the primary endpoint, and overall survival (OS) the secondary endpoint; Kaplan-Meier, competing-risk, and Cox regression analyses were performed. Results: Median age was 71 years; 78 patients (75.7%) had Binet stage B disease. During a median follow-up of 125.8 months, 66 patients (64.1%) received treatment (median TTFT, 38.1 months). Only 1 of 25 Binet stage A patients required treatment, versus 65 of 78 Binet stage B patients (median TTFT, 20.2 months; p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, Binet stage B (hazard ratio [HR] 34.8, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.8-252.4) and a higher absolute lymphocyte count (ALC; HR 1.33 per doubling, 95% CI 1.10-1.61) were independently associated with a shorter TTFT, whereas age, sex, lactate dehydrogenase, and β2-microglobulin were not. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio added no information beyond ALC. No factor was independently associated with OS. Conclusions: In this tertiary referral cohort of Rai stage I-II CLL without Rai stage 0 patients, Binet stage and lymphocyte count, available from a physical examination and a complete blood count, identified patients likely to need treatment soon and may guide follow-up when molecular markers are unavailable. These findings should not be extrapolated to all patients with asymptomatic early-stage CLL.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Diagnostic Accuracy of Different Imaging Modalities in Patients with Pathologic Nipple Discharge.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of different imaging modalities in patients with pathologic nipple discharge. Methods: This is a single-centre retrospective analysis of patients with pathologic nipple discharge. All performed imaging modalities were reviewed for their sensitivity and specificity in correctly diagnosing malignancy, as well as lesions with uncertain malignant potential (B3). Results: Of 388 patients, pathology or follow-up confirmed 41 cases of malignancy (15 breast cancer, 26 ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS)), 151 cases of B3 lesions, and 196 benign cases. The combination of ultrasound and mammography/tomosynthesis achieved a sensitivity of 82.5% (95% CI 68.1-91.3) and a specificity of 83.5% (77.4-88.2) for the detection of malignancy. For the classification of B3 lesions as suspicious (BI-RADS 4/5), the sensitivity and specificity were 33.8% (26.7-41.7) and 83.5% (77.4-88.2), respectively. Ductography demonstrated a sensitivity of 89.3% (72.8-96.3) and a specificity of 13.3% (8.2-20.8) for malignancy, while MRI showed a sensitivity of 71.4% (45.4-88.3) and a specificity of 90.0% (76.9-96.0). In classifying B3 lesions as suspicious, ductography reached a sensitivity of 94.8% (89.7-97.5) and a specificity of 13.3% (8.2-20.8), compared to 75.9% (57.9-87.8) and 90.0% (76.9-96.0), respectively, for MRI. Conclusions: While the combination of ultrasound and mammography/tomosynthesis correctly classified 82.5% of breast malignancies associated with pathologic nipple discharge as suspicious, their sensitivity for classifying B3 lesions as suspicious was only moderate (33.8%). In patients with negative or inconclusive conventional imaging but persistent clinical suspicion, MRI may be considered as an additional diagnostic tool, whereas ductography, given its low specificity, is of limited value for assessing lesion dignity and may primarily serve to localize the affected duct prior to surgery. Further research is needed to determine which diagnostic modality provides the greatest benefit in specific cases.

articles.title: Chronological Magnetic Resonance Angiography Demonstration of Spontaneous Posterior Cerebral Artery Recanalization: Unmasking Cardioembolic Stroke and Postprandial Atrial Fibrillation Mislabeled as Dumping Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and post-gastrectomy dumping syndrome share overlapping symptoms, such as palpitations, dizziness, and chest discomfort, making them clinically difficult to distinguish. We report a case where anchoring bias led both the patient and clinicians to misattribute postprandial symptoms to dumping syndrome, until a cardioembolic stroke unmasked latent AF. A 63-year-old man with a history of distal gastrectomy performed 5 years prior developed postprandial palpitations, chest discomfort, and dizziness triggered by rapid eating or cold drinks. A prior facility had empirically attributed these episodes to dumping syndrome without cardiac evaluation. Initial electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm. The next day, he developed acute diplopia and ptosis due to left oculomotor nerve palsy. Brain MRI demonstrated a left medial midbrain infarction, and MR angiography (MRA) showed 99% stenosis of the left P1 segment. Transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated left atrial enlargement and decreased left atrial appendage flow velocity with spontaneous echo contrast. Continuous electrocardiographic telemetry post-dinner captured paroxysmal AF, unmasking the arrhythmia. His CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED scores were calculated as 3 and 2, respectively. He was treated with anticoagulants and discharged with mild sequelae (modified Rankin Scale score 1). Follow-up MRA at 3 months showed complete recanalization of the P1 segment. This chronological MRA sequence provided visual proof differentiating cardioembolism from fixed intracranial atherosclerosis.

articles.title: Agreement, Reliability, and Feasibility of Melbourne Rapid Fields Tablet Perimetry Compared with Humphrey Field Analyzer in Glaucoma.
articles.abstract: Objectives: We aimed to evaluate the agreement, test-retest reliability, test duration, and patient acceptability of Melbourne Rapid Fields (MRF) tablet perimetry compared with Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA) 24-2 SITA-Standard perimetry in glaucoma patients. Methods: This cross-sectional study evaluated 64 eyes of 64 patients with primary or secondary glaucoma. Participants underwent both HFA and MRF perimetry in a non-randomized sequence. Agreement was analyzed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Test-retest reliability of MRF was evaluated in 47 participants after 4 weeks. Acceptability was assessed via questionnaires. Results: MRF demonstrated comparable reliability indices to HFA (p > 0.05), although these findings do not establish equivalent clinical reliability due to differences in platform-specific definitions. MRF demonstrated excellent test-retest reliability for MD (ICC 0.993), PD (ICC 0.992), and VC (ICC 0.992; all p < 0.001). Compared with HFA, MRF produced significantly less negative MD (-6.27 ± 5.55 vs. -8.32 ± 5.47 dB, p < 0.001) and higher PSD/PD (7.48 ± 3.26 vs. 6.33 ± 4.11 dB, p < 0.001), while VFI/VC did not differ significantly (p = 0.808). Overall agreement was good-to-excellent MD (ICC 0.949), PSD/PD (ICC 0.880), and VFI/VC (ICC 0.930). However, exploratory severity-stratified Bland-Altman analysis suggested greater variability in moderate and severe glaucoma. MRF was significantly faster than HFA (4.22 ± 0.81 vs. 5.46 ± 1.33 min, p < 0.001). All patients reported it was easy and comfortable. Conclusions: MRF provides excellent test-retest reliability, shorter testing duration, and high patient acceptability. While overall agreement is high, systematic differences and greater advanced-stage variability prevent direct interchangeability with HFA. Instead, MRF serves as a practical, complementary platform for accessible, frequent testing.

articles.title: Ultrasonographic and Shear Wave Elastographic Assessment of the Mentalis Muscle: Associations with Mandibular Symphysis and Craniofacial Morphology.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the ultrasonographic thickness and shear wave elastography (SWE)-derived stiffness of the mentalis muscle across different sagittal skeletal patterns and to investigate their relationships with mandibular symphysis morphology and cephalometric variables. Methods: Forty-eight adults aged 18-35 years were classified according to ANB angle into Class I, Class II, and Class III groups, with 16 participants in each group. Mentalis muscle thickness and stiffness were assessed bilaterally at lateral, intermediate, and medial regions using ultrasonography and SWE. Cephalometric skeletal, dental, soft-tissue, and symphyseal measurements were evaluated. Group comparisons were performed using one-way ANOVA or Welch's ANOVA, as appropriate, and within-group associations were assessed using Pearson correlation analysis with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction applied separately to elastography and muscle-thickness correlation families. Results: Mentalis muscle thickness did not differ significantly among the skeletal groups. Right intermediate elastography was the only ultrasonographic parameter showing a significant overall intergroup difference (p = 0.011, η2 = 0.182), with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons showing significantly higher values in Class II than in Class I (adjusted p = 0.012). After FDR correction, selected associations between elastographic stiffness and skeletal, dental, or soft-tissue variables remained significant, whereas no muscle-thickness correlations remained significant. These associations varied across skeletal groups and were considered exploratory. Conclusions: Resting ultrasonographic characteristics of the mentalis muscle showed no consistent association with mandibular symphysis morphology across sagittal skeletal patterns. Mentalis muscle thickness was comparable among the groups, whereas elastographic stiffness demonstrated only a limited and region-specific between-group difference. Selected associations with skeletal and soft-tissue variables were observed; however, these exploratory findings should not be interpreted as evidence of skeletal-class-specific biological mechanisms. Larger studies incorporating functional assessments of the perioral musculature are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: TOLLIP and MUC5B Genetic Variants Influence the Circulating KL6, SPD, and HE4 Levels in Interstitial Lung Abnormalities.
articles.abstract: Background: Interstitial lung abnormalities (ILAs) are alterations of lung parenchyma found in approximately 5% of individuals older than 60 years. There is growing interest in identifying early biomarkers that may facilitate diagnosis and predict disease progression. Given ILA's biological complexity, a multidimensional approach integrating genetic susceptibility and immune dysregulation is warranted. Methods: We studied 87 ILA subjects and 74 subjects without changes on high-resolution computed tomography and without respiratory symptoms. We also classified ILA subjects by progression status during 5 years of follow-up: 20 progressed, and 67 did not. This study evaluated demographic characteristics, circulating soluble proteins (KL6, SPD, and HE4), T cell polarization (Th1/Th2 balance), and selected gene polymorphisms (TERT, MUC5B, FAM13A, TOLLIP, and DSP). Results: Patients with ILA were predominantly male and showed significant abnormalities in pulmonary function tests; they had higher circulating SP-D levels (78 ± 44 versus 43 ± 31 ng/mL, p < 0.0001). Genetic variants significantly influence circulating levels; the median KL6 levels were higher in patients and controls carrying the TOLLIP rs5743890 TT genotype (0.27 ng/mL [0.01-0.71 ng/mL]) than in those with the TC genotype (0.01 ng/mL [0.00-0.19 ng/mL]). The SPD levels according to the MUC5B rs35705950 genotypes were lower in controls and patients carrying the common genotype GG (48.66 ng/mL [27.49-80.40 ng/mL] and 56.91 ng/mL [32.23-90.22 ng/mL]) than subjects with GT + TT genotypes (83.09 ng/mL [56.52-139.72 ng/mL], and 93.70 ng/mL [57.77-154.38 ng/mL]) and HE4 levels were different when the patients and controls carrying the MUC5B rs35705950 GG (2.43 pmol/mL [1.56-3.22 pmol/mL], and 2.43 pmol/mL [1.65-3.29 pmol/mL]) were compared to those with the GT genotype (1.56 pmol/mL [1.21-1.97 pmol/mL], and 1.48 pmol/mL [1.08-2.09 pmol/mL]). No difference emerged when we divided ILAs by progression. The Th1/Th2 ratio does not differ between ILAs and controls, even after polyclonal stimulation. Conclusions: Our findings provide relevant insight into the relationship between genetic background and circulating levels.

articles.title: Comprehensive Analysis of Next-Generation Sequencing and ARMS-PCR for Detecting EGFR S768 Mutations in Chinese Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients.
articles.abstract: Background: Accurate detection of mutations at the EGFR S768 site is crucial for selecting appropriate treatment regimens for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study compared Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) and amplification refractory mutation system polymerase chain reaction (ARMS-PCR) for detecting EGFR S768 mutations in Chinese NSCLC patients. Methods: This study retrospectively analyzed 20,731 molecular pathology tests (8345 by NGS and 12,386 by ARMS-PCR). Results: The detection rate of EGFR S768 variants was significantly lower by ARMS-PCR than by NGS (0.40% vs. 1.15%, p < 0.001). The variants detected by ARMS-PCR were predominantly S768I, whereas NGS identified a broader spectrum, including S768I, S768_D770dup, S768_V769delinsIL, and S768_V769insLDS. Furthermore, the EGFR S768I mutation frequently co-occurred with other EGFR mutations, while insertion mutations at or near the EGFR S768 site rarely coexisted with other EGFR mutations (95.08% vs. 3.03%, p < 0.001). Notably, three cases with S768_V769delinsIL or V769_D770insSVV detected by NGS were identified as S768I by ARMS-PCR, which potentially affected the selection of patients' treatment plans. The sequence variations such as c.2307_2308insAGCGTGGTG, c.2303_2305delinsTCT, and c.2303_2305delinsTTT may be the reasons for the inconsistency between ARMS-PCR and NGS, due to possible non-specific primer binding. However, this remains a hypothesis based on sequence comparison and requires further experimental validation. Conclusions: Complex mutations or insertions around EGFR S768 site may cause discordant results between ARMS-PCR and NGS. NGS was recommended to confirm the EGFR S768 variants when the patient experiences rapid disease progression during treatment with EGFR S768I-directed targeted therapy.

articles.title: The Need for Device-Specific Training Before Handheld Ultrasound Use: Agreement and Repeatability of Simulated Aortic Aneurysm Diameter Measurements by Senior Sonography Students on a Familiar Conventional and an Unfamiliar Handheld System.
articles.abstract: Background: Ultrasound measurement of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) diameter guides screening and surveillance, but whether students' measurement competence on a conventional system transfers to an unfamiliar handheld device has rarely been assessed. Methods: Twenty-seven senior sonography students made three anteroposterior outer-to-outer measurements of two water-filled balloons embedded in gelatin (reference diameters 3.53 and 5.88 cm, calculated from the circumference before embedding), first on the familiar cart-based conventional system and then, in a fixed, non-randomised order, on a handheld system with which they had no prior hands-on experience. The primary outcomes were bias against the calculated reference, with equivalence testing (±5%), and the paired between-system difference, with Bland-Altman analysis; repeatability was assessed with repeatability coefficients. Results: Conventional measurements were equivalent to the calculated reference within ±5% (bias -0.09 cm, 95% CI -0.16 to -0.02; +0.07 cm, 95% CI -0.05 to +0.19). Handheld measurements were higher (+0.17 and +0.33 cm; both p < 0.001) and failed equivalence; the mean between-system difference was +0.26 cm (95% CI 0.18-0.34), without proportional bias. Single-reading repeatability coefficients were 0.31-0.67 cm. Conclusions: Students' conventional-system measurements agreed closely with the calculated reference, although this reference was not verified after embedding. Because device type was confounded with operator inexperience and with a fixed testing order, which introduces an unquantifiable learning or fatigue effect, the 0.26 cm value is an observed between-system difference under the study conditions and cannot be attributed to the handheld device itself. Measurement competence did not transfer automatically to a new device, underlining the critical need for device-specific training before handheld systems are used for aortic measurement. These implications are educational and technical; phantom findings do not support clinical surveillance recommendations without confirmation in patients.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of the Veno-Arterial Carbon Dioxide Difference in COVID-19-Associated Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: In acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, hyperventilation and alterations in oxygenation can influence CO2 kinetics via the Haldane effect, potentially modifying the venous-to-arterial carbon dioxide partial pressure gradient (PvaCO2) irrespective of tissue perfusion, thereby complicating its prognostic significance. This study assessed the predictive importance of PvaCO2 in critically ill patients experiencing acute respiratory failure linked to COVID-19. Methods: This retrospective bicentric study included critically ill patients with hypoxemic COVID-19 (PaO2/FiO2 < 300 mmHg) admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) during the first and second waves of the Belgium epidemic, with at least one PvaCO2 assessment within 5 days of admission. PvaCO2 was assessed early after ICU admission using paired arterial and central venous blood gases. The highest daily value was registered. The first registered value was considered as a baseline. The primary outcome was ICU death within 28 days. Results: Among 300 ICU admissions, 136 patients met inclusion criteria, with PvaCO2 measured within 48 h in 76%. Median PaO2/FiO2 was 123 (79-176) mmHg, with no significant differences in baseline severity between patients with normal or abnormal PvaCO2. Lactate levels were generally normal, and inotrope use was uncommon. Early abnormal PvaCO2 was not significantly associated with ICU death within 28 days in the competing-risk analysis (sHR 1.69, 95% CI 0.86-3.33; p = 0.13), while complementary Bayesian analysis indicated an 89.7% posterior probability of increased hazard. When stratified by hypoxemia severity-severe (PaO2/FiO2 ≤ 100 mmHg), moderate (>100-200 mmHg), and mild (>200 mmHg)-a stronger exploratory signal related to ICU mortality was observed in moderate hypoxemia; however, the formal interaction did not reach statistical significance (Pinteraction = 0.075). Conclusions: Early PvaCO2 was not significantly associated with ICU death within 28 days in patients with predominantly hypoxemic respiratory failure without major baseline circulatory shock. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested that its association with outcome may vary according to arterial and central venous oxygenation. This hypothesis warrants targeted evaluation in future prospective studies.

articles.title: Decoding the Prognosis of Sepsis-Induced Acute Lung Injury: Machine Learning Model Development and SHAP Interpretability Analysis Based on Critical Care Databases.
articles.abstract: Background: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (SI-ALI) has high morbidity and mortality. Early prognosis prediction is critical, but traditional scoring systems lack dynamic, interpretable, and personalized capabilities. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting mortality in SI-ALI. Methods: Data from the MIMIC-IV database (training/internal validation) and from the eICU-CRD database (external validation) were analyzed. The Lasso regression model with cross-validation was utilized for the identification of the key features. Subsequently, a series of predicted models were formulated utilizing six distinct machine learning algorithms, and the performance of the models was evaluated using various analytical tools. SHAP values were employed to interpret the machine learning models. Results: Among 7250 patients, eight key indicators were identified. The GBDT model achieved an internal AUC of 0.801 (95% CI: 0.775-0.827), accuracy 0.730, sensitivity 0.692, and specificity 0.739. External validation showed an AUC of 0.681 (95% CI: 0.650-0.708), accuracy 0.601, sensitivity 0.686, and specificity 0.574. However, precision, F1, and MCC were modest, indicating limited predictive accuracy. SHAP identified urine output, respiratory rate, BUN, PLR, lactate, INR, age, and anion gap as the most influential variables. Conclusions: The GBDT model showed modest discriminative ability and limited generalizability. It should be considered an exploratory tool requiring further prospective multicenter validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Evaluation of Functional Activity of Ciliated Epithelium in Patients with Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
articles.abstract: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a heterogeneous recessive disorder of cilia that leads to respiratory tract disorders and organ laterality defects. Objectives: This study was designed to diagnose PCD in patients using various methods: genetic, immunofluorescence, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and assessment of ciliary beat frequency (CBF) in ALI cultures. Methods: The study included (n = 35) patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia and (n = 10) healthy controls (HC). The diagnosis of PCD was established using molecular genetic analysis: WES, TEM, immunofluorescence staining of ALI-culture, and high-speed videomicroscopy. Ciliogenesis of ciliated epithelial cells was performed in patients with PCD and HC to improve the diagnosis of PCD. Results: Genetic sequencing was conducted for all patients and variants in 17 genes were found. All variants were known. A comparison of CBF assessment in PCD patients and HC using high-speed videomicroscopy showed that the CBF in PCD patient nasal cells was significantly reduced (p < 0.0001), with sensitivity of 91% and specificity of 89.2%. CBF was independent of age and showed no statistical difference between adults and children. Conclusions: The diagnosis of PCD was confirmed in all patients using various diagnostic methods, including the assessment of CBF of ALI culture. The creation of databases of ALI cultures, combined with genotypic and structural abnormalities, is necessary both for diagnosis and, in the future, for use as models in the development of targeted therapies and for assessing their effectiveness.

articles.title: MALDI-TOF/MS Serum Spectral Profiling for Breast Cancer Discrimination Using Direct and ACN-Assisted Workflows: A Retrospective Proof-of-Concept Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Serum matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF/MS) profiling may complement breast cancer (BrC) assessment, but retrospective studies are vulnerable to demographic and batch confounding. We evaluated direct-serum (Workflow A) and acetonitrile (ACN)-assisted (Workflow B) profiling. Methods: Workflow A analyzed 60 archived sera (30 BrC, 30 controls) with sample-level nested 10-fold cross-validation and L2-regularized logistic regression. Workflow B included 40 sample groups (20 BrC, 20 negative/comparator; approximately four spots/sample); replicates were aggregated before repeated sample-level five-fold cross-validation and batch/source diagnostics. Results: Workflow A yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.932, but groups were not age matched (52 vs. 45 years; standardized mean difference approximately 1.03), precluding cancer-specific interpretation independent of age. Workflow B yielded a mean AUC of 0.978 ± 0.007 and a balanced accuracy of 0.968, but negative/comparator batch/date classification reached an AUC of 0.970, and cross-batch transfer was asymmetric (1.00 vs. 0.64); five comparator sera were commercially sourced. Conclusions: Workflow A provides preliminary group-discrimination evidence but remains age-confounded. Workflow B demonstrates strong apparent internal discrimination under substantial batch/source confounding and is best viewed as an analytical stress test, not independent validation. Candidate m/z signals remain unidentified; age-matched, batch-balanced external validation and orthogonal molecular identification are required before cancer-specific or biomarker claims.

articles.title: Exploring NS5A Protein of Hepatitis C Virus Through Computational Deep Learning Models and Phylogenetic Analysis for Sequence Variability.
articles.abstract: Background: Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) remains a global health threat, causing severe liver diseases such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Protein sequences are essential for exploring genetic variability and improving detection. This study presents a generative LSTM model, AI-VNA, for generating and analyzing NS5A protein sequences to enhance understanding of sequence diversity and improve predictive modeling. Methods: The AI-VNA model was trained on curated NS5A protein sequences and evaluated against baseline models including CNN, 1D-CNN, GRU, and Simple RNN. Generated sequences were validated using BLAST (version 2.16.0) to assess biological relevance. Additional analyses included a sequence similarity heatmap, phylogenetic clustering using UPGMA, and statistical comparison of sequence similarities via the Mann-Whitney U test. Results: AI-VNA achieved 98.56% accuracy, outperforming other models and demonstrating strong capability in modeling sequence patterns. BLAST validation showed an average query coverage of 82%, an average E-value of 1 × 10-155, and 96.68% identity to known NS5A proteins. The sequence similarity heatmap revealed notable variability among the generated sequences. Phylogenetic analysis showed distinct clustering patterns, indicating both conservation and diversity. A box plot comparing similarity scores of predicted and database sequences showed significant variation (p = 0.01221; Cliff's Delta = 0.291, small effect). Conclusions: These findings highlight the AI-VNA model's ability to generate evolutionarily relevant and diverse NS5A protein sequences, supporting its potential for improving HCV sequence analysis and aiding in diagnostic and therapeutic developments.

articles.title: Elasticity per Thickness Index for Breast Sonoelastography: Quantitative Analysis of Implant- and Clinically Related Peri-Implant Capsular Formation.
articles.abstract: Background: Peri-implant capsular formation remains a multifactorial process influenced by implant characteristics and patient-specific tissue responses. Ultrasound with shear-wave elastography offers evaluation of the biomechanical properties of both the capsule and surrounding breast tissues. Elastographic assessment does not distinguish intrinsic stiffness from the amount of fibrotic tissue. We introduced the Elasticity per Thickness Index (ETI) as an exploratory measure of capsular stiffness related to capsule thickness. Methods: This prospective study assessed peri-implant capsules and adjacent breast tissue compartments using B-mode ultrasound and shear-wave elastography over more than two years of follow-up. Capsular stiffness, thickness, and the exploratory Elasticity per Thickness Index (ETI; kPa/mm) were compared across implant characteristics, and their associations with clinical variables were analyzed. Results: Significant postoperative increases in stiffness were found across multiple native tissue compartments. Breast tissues remained on average stiffer than preoperatively throughout follow-up. Implant type or shape (F and M series, L3, MP EU, HP EU; anatomical vs. round) showed no association with stiffness changes, although round implants tended to yield higher fascial stiffness (p = 0.080). The ETI was independent of implant shape (p = 0.430). Higher-profile implants showed a nominally higher ETI than medium-profile implants (39.1 ± 13.4 vs. 31.9 ± 13.4 kPa/mm; unadjusted p = 0.050), which should be interpreted as an exploratory finding. The ETI was not significantly associated with implant profile after accounting for bilateral clustering (p = 0.455). Capsular stiffness was inversely associated with time from surgery to assessment (Rs = -0.329, p = 0.013), although this cross-sectional association does not demonstrate longitudinal softening. Conclusions: At the postoperative assessment, the peri-implant capsule showed a mean stiffness of 15.52 ± 3.81 kPa. The ETI may provide a complementary thickness-related description of capsular stiffness, although its reliability and clinical relevance require further validation. No robust association between implant profile and the ETI was identified after accounting for bilateral clustering.

articles.title: An Explainable Multi-Model Ensemble for Brain Hemorrhage Detection and Subtype Classification Using 34,366 NCCT Images.
articles.abstract: Background: Brain hemorrhage is a critical neurological emergency and it is essential to quickly and accurately identify the type of bleeding if treatment is to be properly guided and patient outcomes are to be improved. Even though non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is still the main imaging technique used for the initial evaluation, diagnostic difficulties continue due to overlapping radiological patterns and the limitations involved in manual interpretation. The purpose of this study was to create and validate an ensemble deep learning approach for the automated multi-class classification of brain hemorrhage subtypes based on NCCT images. Methods: Transfer learning was applied using three convolutional neural network architectures such as InceptionV3, Xception, and InceptionResNetV2. The models were trained independently and combined using an unweighted soft-voting strategy. The framework was evaluated on 34,366 NCCT images belonging to six diagnostic categories: EDH, SDH, SAH, IPH, IVH, and normal findings. Results: Xception achieved the highest performance among the individual models, whereas the ensemble produced the best overall results. Using the final test-set results, the ensemble achieved an accuracy of 95.35%, with macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score of approximately 95%. Grad-CAM visualizations showed that the model frequently attended to anatomically plausible regions associated with the predicted hemorrhage categories. Conclusions: The findings suggest that combining complementary CNN architectures may improve internal test-set performance for six-class NCCT image classification. However, because the study used an image-level split from a single public dataset without external validation, the proposed framework should be considered a research-stage decision-support approach rather than a clinically validated diagnostic system.

articles.title: Temporal Analysis of the Associations Between Radiological Imaging Prevalence and Life Expectancy at Birth and Mortality.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to analyze the temporal associations between radiological imaging prevalence and life expectancy at birth and mortality. Methods: The study used the Türkiye Ministry of Health Statistics Yearbook, World Health Organization (WHO) and World Bank data to analyze radiological imaging counts, female life expectancy at birth, and female mortality levels for Turkey between 2015 and 2023. The widest date range from both datasets was selected for the analysis. Because the Ministry of Health Statistics provides the widest date range for radiological imaging as 2015-2023, the research dataset was limited to this date range. Results: There was no direct relationship between radiologic imaging and life expectancy at birth or female mortality (p > 0.05). Year-controlled partial correlation analysis results showed that life expectancy at birth was significantly correlated with CT imaging numbers (r = -0.854; p < 0.01). MR, CT, ultrasound, Doppler, ECO and mammography had no significant association with female life expectancy at birth (p > 0.05). Similarly, associations between MR, CT, ultrasound, Doppler, ECO and mammography and female mortality were statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) Conclusions: In the study, no univariate association reached p < 0.05; the single nominal finding for CT is negative and unstable, and the analysis is exploratory.

articles.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Fontan-Associated Liver Disease: The Role of Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
articles.abstract: Background: Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) develops as a consequence of chronic systemic venous congestion, which alters hepatic hemodynamics and promotes sinusoidal congestion, inflammation, and fibrosis. Our objective was to evaluate liver changes using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in patients with a Fontan circuit. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study including patients who underwent the Fontan procedure between January 2005 and December 2019 and were evaluated using T1, T2 and apparent diffusion coefficient mapping. Patients were classified into two groups: none-to-mild FALD (≤5 points) and moderate-to-severe FALD (≥6 points). FALD severity was characterized, and logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association between the variables of interest and the outcome. The discriminative performance of quantitative MRI parameters was also assessed using ROC curves. Results: Thirty-nine patients were included, with a median age at surgery of 9.3 years (IQR 5.9-10.8); 61.5% (n = 24) were female. The most frequent diagnosis was tricuspid atresia (51.3%, n = 20), and the Fontan procedures were mainly performed using an extracardiac conduit (97.4%, n = 38). No factors were significantly associated with moderate-to-severe FALD. T1 mapping of segment I demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (AUC = 0.771; 95% CI: 0.500-1.000), with a cutoff value of >734 ms, yielding a sensitivity of 83.3% (95% CI: 43.65-99.15) and a specificity of 75% (95% CI: 57.89-86.75). Conclusions: After 10 years of follow-up, 15% had moderate-to-severe FALD. T1 mapping of segment I demonstrated the highest discriminative performance, with a sensitivity greater than 80% for identifying moderate-to-severe FALD.

articles.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models for Emergency Triage in Urology: A Multi-Model Study.
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the triage accuracy, response quality, safety, and repeatability of widely used large language models (LLMs) in urologic emergencies and to examine their potential clinical utility and risks. Methods: We developed 50 standardized clinical vignettes covering 10 categories of urologic emergencies, including testicular torsion, acute urinary retention, and Fournier gangrene.
