The set comprised high-risk vignettes requiring immediate emergency care, borderline vignettes, and atypical vignettes containing misleading cues. Six commercially available LLMs-Kimi 3.0, DeepSeek V4, Qwen 3.8-MAX, GPT-5.6 Sol (ChatGPT), Claude Opus 4.8, and Ant Afu (AQ)-were evaluated in Chinese-language interactions. Each vignette was submitted three times in independent conversations. Two urologists with more than 10 years of clinical experience assessed triage accuracy using a three-level reference standard (immediate emergency department [ED] evaluation, routine outpatient evaluation, or home observation). They also rated response quality across eight dimensions using a 5-point Likert scale and evaluated medical-error severity (0-3), response stability, and Chinese readability. Overall differences were assessed using the Friedman test, followed by pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm adjustment. Results: A total of 900 responses were generated. Overall three-class accuracy was 89.11%, and the macro-averaged F1 score was 85.73%. Qwen achieved the highest accuracy (94.00%), whereas Claude achieved the lowest (80.67%). However, none of the pairwise comparisons between models reached statistical significance after Holm adjustment. All models generally recognized scenarios requiring immediate ED evaluation, but their ability to distinguish routine outpatient evaluation from home observation varied substantially. Mean content-quality scores ranged from 3.68 to 4.15; AQ achieved the highest overall score (4.15 ± 0.49), whereas DeepSeek achieved the lowest (3.68 ± 0.48). Clinically relevant errors occurred in 12.3% of responses, including major errors in 6.2% and dangerous errors in 3.1%. Three-run exact triage agreement ranged from 78% to 96%. Readability performance varied by metric, with no single model consistently outperforming the others. Conclusions: The six LLMs demonstrated some ability to perform three-level triage of urologic emergencies, supporting further investigation of their potential clinical applications. Nevertheless, important limitations remained in the management of borderline cases, response stability, and safety; some responses included potentially dangerous self-management instructions or could delay care for high-risk patients. Integration with authoritative guidelines, structured risk warnings, and human review will be necessary to improve clinical safety and reliability.

articles.title: Scapular Osteoid Osteoma: An Extremely Rare Case with an Atypical Clinical Presentation.
articles.abstract: Osteoid osteoma (OO) is a benign osteoblastic tumor that rarely occurs in the scapula and may present with atypical clinical and imaging findings. A 25-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of right shoulder pain without nocturnal pain. Radiographs revealed a well-defined osteolytic lesion with internal calcification and surrounding osteosclerosis in the scapular body. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a 15-mm lesion containing an 11-mm coarse calcification, whereas magnetic resonance imaging showed surrounding bone marrow edema. The differential diagnosis included OO and osteomyelitis. Surgery was performed for pain relief and definitive diagnosis. Histopathological examination revealed immature woven bone trabeculae within a fibrovascular stroma, with prominent osteoblastic rimming and minimal cytologic atypia, confirming the diagnosis of OO. The patient remained asymptomatic at the 1-year follow-up, and radiographs showed no evidence of local recurrence. OO of the scapular body is extremely rare and may present without the characteristic nocturnal pain. CT is particularly useful for identifying the nidus, whereas histopathological examination remains important for definitive diagnosis.

articles.title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model (CNN-GRU) with MRMR for EEG-Based Depression Detection.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent mental health disorder for which objective and reliable diagnostic approaches remain an active area of research. Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising non-invasive modality for identifying neural activity patterns associated with depression, while advances in deep learning have enabled effective analysis of complex EEG signals. Methods: In this study, we propose a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and gated recurrent units (GRUs) for temporal modeling of EEG signals. The spatial and temporal features extracted by the CNN and GRU components were concatenated into a 120-dimensional representation, after which minimum redundancy maximum relevance (mRMR) feature selection was applied to reduce redundancy and retain the 30 most informative features before classification. The proposed framework was evaluated using the publicly available MODMA EEG dataset, and its performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results: Across 30 independent simulation runs, the CNN-GRU-mRMR framework achieved a mean classification accuracy of 96.74%, exceeding the performance of the comparison methods evaluated in this study. The model also demonstrated high precision, recall, and F1-score, indicating strong classification performance within the evaluated dataset. Conclusions: These findings suggest that integrating spatial and temporal feature learning with mRMR-based feature selection can improve EEG-based depression classification. Further validation using larger, more diverse, and independent clinical datasets is needed to establish the generalizability of the framework and evaluate its potential utility for objective EEG-based depression assessment.

articles.title: Corneal Biomechanical and Tomographic Signatures for Keratoconus.
articles.abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to identify tomographic and biomechanical biomarkers that differentiate mild/moderate from advanced/severe keratoconus (KCN) based on the ABCD classification. The secondary objective was to assess the diagnostic performance of previously reported biomarkers for distinguishing KCN from KCN-free controls and to compare classifications derived from cohort-specific and previously established cutoff values, evaluating their consistency and potential generalizability in the Romanian KCN population. Methods: Adult patients who presented to the Oculens Clinic between 1 January 2024 and 1 September 2025 for clinical care were eligible for enrolment in this observational study. Diagnosis of KCN was made following current practice, and all participants underwent ophthalmologic examination followed by corneal tomography and biomechanical measurements. Results: Forty-four subjects with KCN and 38 controls, with a median age of 26.5 years. Patients with mild/moderate KCN (23 patients) were similar in terms of age and sex to those with advanced/severe KCN (21 patients). The values of Kmax showed the best performance in terms of AUC (0.908, 95%CI = [0.824 to 0.992], Se = 76.19 [52.83 to 91.78], Sp = 86.96 [66.41 to 97.22], cutoff = 54.15), with an excellent discriminatory ability in the identification of patients with mild/moderate KCN compared to advanced/severe KCN. Low TL values indicate advanced/severe disease, with the highest values of true positives (18), true negatives (22), and the smallest value of false negatives (3) but with a moderate AUC (0.880 [0.755 to 1.0]). The performances of previously reported cutoff values on the Romanian cohort were tested in 44 patients with KCN and 38 KCN-free individuals. The discriminatory abilities of the previously reported indices, except for KI and BAD-D which were overfitted, were retained in the current cohort, and all exhibited excellent (AUC lower bounds higher than 0.9) or good (AUC lower bounds higher than 0.8) discriminatory performances. The agreement between the current cutoff values and the classification generated by the previously reported cutoff values is sustained by almost perfect agreement in the classification as KCN or KCN-free (Cohen's kappa values ≥ 0.81, and raw agreement ≥ 90%). Conclusions: Our findings support further evaluation of Kmax and corneal thinnest location as markers of keratoconus severity and as potential tools for disease detection. The high concordance observed between classification based on cohort-specific and previously established thresholds suggests consistent performance of these biomarkers within the study population. These parameters may represent promising tools for the management of patients with keratoconus, pending further validation.

articles.title: Diagnosis and Treatment Strategies of Eosinophilic Esophagitis: A Nationwide Survey.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is an increasingly recognized chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease of the esophagus. Data on the real-world diagnosis and management practices among gastroenterologists in Israel is scarce. This study aimed to describe current diagnostic and treatment practice patterns for eosinophilic esophagitis among Israeli gastroenterologists, and to identify areas of concordance with, and variability relative to, international recommendations. Methods: A nationwide, cross-sectional, internet-based survey was conducted among gastroenterologists from the Israeli Gastroenterology Association (IGA) and the Israeli Society of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition between February and April 2024. We used a structured 28-item questionnaire covering physician demographics, diagnostic practices and treatment strategies of EoE. Responses were analyzed for the entire cohort and compared across subgroups based on physician characteristics. Results: Of the 540 eligible gastroenterologists, 114 (22%) completed the survey. Almost all responders (97%) would obtain esophageal biopsies in the case of dysphagia even without typical endoscopic findings. Similarly, 94% of the responders would obtain esophageal biopsies in the case of typical endoscopic findings even without dysphagia. About 86 (75%) were familiar with the Endoscopic Reference Score (EREFS) system. Proton pump inhibitors were the most prescribed first-line treatment (92%), followed by dietary interventions (40%) and topical steroids (17%). As compared with adult gastroenterologists, pediatric gastroenterologists were more likely to obtain biopsies, use the EREFS and initiate treatment before histologic confirmation was obtained. Overall, practices showed broad concordance with international recommendations (>75% of respondents). Conclusions: In this cross-sectional survey, it was demonstrated that diagnostic and treatment practices for EoE among Israeli gastroenterologists were broadly concordant with international recommendations. However, several areas of inconsistency across different provider subgroups were identified. These gaps can be managed through educational programs that will improve standardization of management in EoE.

articles.title: Time-of-Day-Associated Variation in Serum CO2 Patient-Result Distribution and Its Impact on PBRTQC Performance.
articles.abstract: Background: Patient-based real-time quality control (PBRTQC) is now widely used in clinical labs, yet the impact of time-dependent variation on its performance remains understudied, particularly with regard to serum carbon dioxide (CO2). This study explores how time-of-day-associated variation in the serum CO2 patient-result distribution affects PBRTQC outcomes and clinical acidosis classification, and an optimization strategy is evaluated. Methods: We analyzed 168,957 serum CO2 results collected over one year (2025) using three biochemical analyzers. Moving average-based PBRTQC was compared between peak (10:00-13:00) and off-peak periods, using either conventional unified limits or time-stratified separate limits. Results: Serum CO2 patient-result distribution shifted significantly toward higher values during the peak period (23.6 vs. 23.0 mmol/L, p < 0.001). A unified control strategy led to a marked rise in false-positive rates (0.955% vs. 0.062%). In a simulated category-transition analysis, 92 of 1212 samples (7.59%) were reclassified, of which 88 were acidosis-to-normal shifts. The time-stratified model reduced peak false positives to 0.069% while maintaining efficient detection of error. Conclusions: Time-of-day-associated variation in the distribution of patients' serum CO2 impairs PBRTQC specificity during peak hours. Time-stratified control limits reduce false-positive rates while maintaining error detection, offering a practical solution for reliable serum CO2 monitoring. These findings should be interpreted as descriptive, given the cross-sectional design and the potential influence of patient case mix.

articles.title: Design of a PSO-Optimized VGG19 Convolutional Neural Network for Automatic Breast Cancer Image Classification.
articles.abstract: Background: Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2) overexpression is detected in approximately 25-30% of malignant breast cancer cases and is intrinsically associated with aggressive tumor progression. Reliable assessment of HER2 status is critical for selecting optimal targeted therapies; however, conventional immunohistochemistry (HER2 SISH) evaluation predominantly relies on visual inspection, a process that is highly subjective and susceptible to inter-observer variability. To mitigate diagnostic inconsistencies, this study proposes an automated classification framework leveraging a VGG19 convolutional neural network, fundamentally enhanced via Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for rigorous hyperparameter tuning. The model development and evaluation in this study were performed using a purely synthetic image dataset. Methods: The PSO algorithm is systematically employed to optimize critical training parameters, facilitating an efficient exploration of the complex search space and significantly improving the stability of the learning process. Experimental evaluations conducted on these purely synthetic high-resolution histopathology images demonstrate that the proposed PSO-VGG19 framework substantially outperforms baseline architectures, including MobileNet. Results: Specifically, the optimized system achieves a classification accuracy of 98.10%, sensitivity of 98.11%, specificity of 99.37%, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 99.66%. Conclusions: These empirical results demonstrate that integrating metaheuristic optimization with deep learning architectures yields robust computational performance for HER2 patch-level classification, serving as a foundational computational proof-of-concept for future digital pathology research.

articles.title: Benchmarking Open-Source Large Language Models for Breast Ultrasound Report Processing: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: General-purpose large language models (LLMs) may support medical reporting, but their role in breast ultrasound (BUS) workflows remains uncertain. We evaluated locally deployable open-source LLMs for BUS report quality control, BI-RADS reasoning, and clinical decision support tasks under physician supervision using retrospective, multicenter reports from real-world clinical practice. We further characterized their relative strengths, limitations, and potential assistive roles compared with proprietary models and ultrasound physicians. Methods: We built a multicenter benchmark of 1173 task-specific Chinese BUS reports from three tertiary hospitals. Seven tasks covered report quality control, BI-RADS reasoning and clinical decision support. We evaluated 24 open-source LLMs, 20 proprietary LLMs and six ultrasound physicians. Tasks 1-5 used reference-standard classification metrics. Tasks 6-7 used blinded expert ratings on five-point Likert scales. Results: Open-source LLMs did not differ significantly from proprietary LLMs in basic error detection, findings-impression inconsistency detection, treatment response assessment or follow-up recommendation generation. They performed worse in terminology non-standardization detection, single-modality BI-RADS categorization and multimodal BI-RADS categorization. Mean accuracies were 0.3775 vs. 0.4563, 0.4121 vs. 0.4920 and 0.6149 vs. 0.7178, respectively. In the 210-case human-evaluation subset, physicians outperformed LLMs in basic error detection, findings-impression inconsistency detection, single-modality BI-RADS categorization and multimodal BI-RADS categorization. LLMs received higher expert-rated scores for treatment response assessment and follow-up recommendation generation. Terminology non-standardization detection showed mixed results across physician seniority and model group. Among open-source LLMs, reasoning-capable models outperformed non-reasoning models in six of seven tasks. The latest open-source release period showed higher composite performance, although substantial model-level heterogeneity remained. Conclusions: Open-source LLMs may support selected BUS report-processing tasks, especially longitudinal summarization and recommendation drafting. Their weaker performance in terminology non-standardization detection and BI-RADS reasoning indicates persistent limits in specialized diagnostic reasoning. Clinical deployment should remain physician-supervised and should include local validation, version control, and task-specific model selection.

articles.title: Large-Scale Evaluation of IgM and IgG Lateral Flow Assays for Rapid Diagnosis of Human Brucellosis.
articles.abstract: Background: Human brucellosis is a major occupational hazard in India, especially among veterinary healthcare workers due to frequent contact with livestock. This study evaluated in-house standardized IgM and IgG-based lateral flow assays (LFAs) against a Rose Bengal Plate Test (RBPT) and a Serum Agglutination Test (SAT). Methods: A total of 1356 serum samples (392 veterinary doctors and 964 paraveterinary staff) were sourced for evaluation of the tests across Karnataka, India. The results were analyzed for performance metrics {DSe (Diagnostic Sensitivity), DSp (Diagnostic Specificity), PPV (Positive Predictive Value), NPV (Negative Predictive Value), accuracy, and kappa with 95% CI} through chi-square and regression analyses. Results: Overall seropositivity was 7.67% (104/1356; 95% CI: 6.31-9.22) by RBPT, 3.47% (47/1356; 95% CI: 2.56-4.58) by SAT, 2.95% (40/1356; 95% CI: 2.12-4.00) by IgM_LFA, and 6.34% (86/1356; 95% CI: 5.10-7.77) by IgG_LFA. The RBPT vs. IgM and IgG_LFA showed a DSe of 85.3% (74.6-92.7) and 82.69% (74.03-89.41), respectively. Compared with SAT, IgM_LFA and IgG_LFA demonstrated high DSe values of 95.35% (84.2-99.4) and 96.55% (88.1-99.6), respectively. Seroprevalence was higher among paraveterinary staff (8.71%, CI 95%: 7.20-10.90) than veterinary doctors (5.10%, CI 95%: 3.14-7.77), higher in males (8.30%, CI 95%: 6.77-10.04) than females (4.02%, CI 95%: 2.44-9.05) and higher in individuals aged >55 years (9.09%, CI 95%: 5.64-13.69) compared to other age groups. Regression analysis yielded coefficients of 62.90% (p = 0.0107) for veterinarians and 87.89% (p = 0.0001) for paraveterinarians. Conclusions: This integrated field evaluation confirms improvement in brucellosis detection and emphasizes the need for field-applicable diagnostic tools.

articles.title: From Non-Advanced Disease to Mast Cell Leukemia: Diagnostic, Morphologic, and Molecular Heterogeneity of Systemic Mastocytosis in a Single-Center Real-World Series.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Systemic mastocytosis (SM) is a heterogeneous clonal mast-cell neoplasm requiring integrated clinical, biochemical, morphological, immunophenotypic, and molecular assessment. This study aimed to characterize the diagnostic and biological heterogeneity of SM across different disease phenotypes. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed six patients with SM diagnosed and managed between 2018 and 2022 at a single center. Clinical presentations, organ involvement, serum tryptase concentrations, bone marrow morphology, immunophenotypic and molecular findings, treatment, and outcomes were analyzed. Results: The cohort included four males and two females aged 16-86 years. Cutaneous manifestations occurred in five patients and frequently preceded diagnosis. All patients had bone marrow involvement, with variable mast-cell infiltration and aberrant CD25 and/or CD2 expression. Serum tryptase concentrations ranged from 15.8 to 348 μg/L. The highest concentration occurred in Patient 5, who had a FIP1L1::PDGFRA-positive myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and prominent systemic mast-cell involvement. In contrast, Patient 6, diagnosed with mast cell leukemia, had a tryptase concentration of 28.5 μg/L despite extensive marrow and peripheral blood involvement. KIT mutations were detected in five patients, while Patient 6 tested negative. Conclusions: This series highlights the marked clinical and biological heterogeneity of SM and the potential discordance between serum tryptase concentrations, mast-cell burden, molecular findings, and disease aggressiveness. Accurate diagnosis and disease characterization require an integrated multidisciplinary approach.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Objectives: To validate a deep learning-based algorithm for automated detection, segmentation, and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid on optical coherence tomography (OCT) across multiple retinal diseases. Methods: In this retrospective validation study, spectral-domain OCT volume scans from eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), and macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) were analyzed. Automated segmentation was performed using the fluid analyzer on Skopix by NetraMind Innovations, a deep learning-based framework trained to identify intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), pigment epithelial detachment (PED), and subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM). Automated segmentations were reviewed and manually corrected by two masked experienced retina graders, with discrepancies adjudicated by a senior retina specialist. Scan-level detection performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient (AC1). Spatial segmentation agreement across all B-scans was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Quantitative agreement between automated and manually corrected fluid volumes was evaluated using correlation and Bland-Altman analyses. Inter-grader reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: A total of 98 OCT volumes comprising 31 nAMD, 25 DME, and 42 MacTel eyes were included. In nAMD, IRF detection demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.8%, specificity of 83.0%, and AUC of 0.876, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.4%, specificity of 96.7%, and AUC of 0.901. In DME, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were 99.6%, 97.3%, and 0.989 for IRF and 98.4%, 96.4%, and 0.978 for SRF, respectively. In MacTel, IRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 87.3%, specificity of 95.1%, and AUC of 0.927, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.8%, specificity of 98.4%, and AUC of 0.929. Segmentation agreement between automated and manually corrected annotations was high across disease groups, with Dice coefficients of 0.829 and 0.922 for IRF and SRF in nAMD, 0.858 and 0.941 in DME, and 0.908 and 0.97 in MacTel, respectively. Automated fluid volumes demonstrated strong correlations with manually corrected measurements, with minimal systematic bias on Bland-Altman analysis. Conclusions: The automated segmentation algorithm demonstrated strong validation performance for the detection and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid across nAMD, DME, and MacTel. High segmentation agreement, particularly for IRF and SRF, and strong volumetric agreement with expert-corrected measurements support the potential use of automated OCT fluid quantification in clinical practice and research.

articles.title: Feature-Based Fusion of Angiography Videos and Blood Parameters for Fractional Flow Reserve (FFR) Prediction.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Estimating fractional flow reserve (FFR) non-invasively in intermediate coronary artery disease remains challenging because anatomical stenosis severity does not consistently correlate with functional ischemia. While conventional image-based models typically assume simplified fluid dynamics, functional flow may also be influenced by blood cellular properties. We evaluated a multimodal neural network framework that conditions angiographic representations on hemorheological surrogate parameters derived directly from routine complete blood count (CBC) data. Methods: Retrospective data from 179 patients (256 left anterior descending [LAD] videos) with matched invasive FFR were analyzed. To incorporate cellular flow tendencies without specialized assays, routine CBC parameters were configured into a 5-parameter Blood Fluidity Model (BFM) comprising gender, baseline mean platelet volume (MPV), and three engineered surrogate metrics: Erythrocyte Fragility Index (red blood cell distribution width [RDW] × mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration [MCHC]), Cell-Free Hemoglobin Index (hemoglobin [HGB]-(hematocrit [HCT]/3)), and Erythrocyte-Platelet Volume Balance (HCT/plateletcrit [PCT]). A Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) architecture was used to modulate three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D-CNN) spatiotemporal features extracted from angiography videos. Evaluation relied on patient-grouped 5-fold cross-validation and an independent test set (36 patients). Results: On the independent test set, the video-only baseline showed limited predictive utility (area under curve [AUC]: 0.482). The multimodal (angiography video features modulated by BFM) FiLM model improved upon angiography video-only, BFM-only (AUC: 0.599), and video late-fusion with BFM baselines (AUC: 0.521), achieving an AUC of 0.621, a balanced accuracy of 0.590, and a statistically significant correlation with invasive FFR (rs = 0.246, p = 0.003). Engineered hemorheological surrogates outperformed raw hematological inputs (all blood parameters only: AUC: 0.601. Multimodal Late Fusion AUC: 0.478. Multimodal FiLM AUC: 0.570). Conclusions: Integrating novel CBC-derived biophysical parameters alongside angiographic sequences demonstrates the feasibility of combining blood rheology and vessel geometry into a single computational framework. While observed performance gains remain modest, this approach illustrates the potential of leveraging routine laboratory data to support non-invasive physiological evaluation without incurring additional procedural burden.

articles.title: Histopathological Spectrum of the Human Appendix with Aging and Adiposity: A Forensic Autopsy Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Histological variation in the vermiform appendix in forensic autopsy populations remains incompletely characterized. This study evaluated age- and adiposity-related histopathological patterns and their potential medico-legal relevance. Methods: This prospective cross-sectional study included 101 consecutive adult forensic autopsy cases. Appendiceal specimens were assessed semi-quantitatively for lymphoid nodules, fibrosis, luminal narrowing, and submucosal adipose accumulation, with morphometric assessment of the submucosa-to-muscularis propria ratio. Associations with age and adiposity measures were examined using correlation analyses and multivariable ordinal regression. Postmortem interval (PMI) and natural versus non-natural cause of death were evaluated in sensitivity analyses. Results: Advancing age was associated with lower lymphoid nodule scores (ρ = -0.301, p = 0.002) and higher fibrosis (ρ = 0.403, p < 0.001), luminal-status (ρ = 0.228, p = 0.022), and submucosal-adipose-accumulation scores (ρ = 0.302, p = 0.002). In adjusted models, age remained associated with lower lymphoid scores (OR = 0.971, 95% CI 0.951-0.992) and higher submucosal adipose accumulation (OR = 1.027, 95% CI 1.007-1.048), while fibrosis showed threshold-specific age associations (ORs = 1.039 and 1.087; 95% CIs 1.013-1.065 and 1.050-1.125). Unadjusted associations between adiposity measures and histopathological outcomes were modest. Greater abdominal subcutaneous fat thickness was associated with higher luminal-status (OR = 1.212, 95% CI 1.027-1.431) and submucosal-adipose-accumulation scores (OR = 1.203, 95% CI 1.022-1.416) after adjustment for age and sex. In the three-level luminal sensitivity model, the age estimate was essentially unchanged after adding PMI, and PMI was not significant. After additional adjustment for cause of death, age associations with fibrosis and submucosal adipose accumulation remained significant, whereas those with lymphoid nodule score and luminal status did not. Conclusions: Age showed the most consistent associations with appendiceal histological variation, particularly fibrosis and submucosal adipose accumulation. Adiposity-related associations were modest and measure-dependent. These findings provide descriptive forensic context but do not establish diagnostic thresholds or causality.

articles.title: Recurrent Acute Liver Failure as the First Manifestation of ARCN1-Associated Disorder Caused by a Terminal Exon Frameshift Variant.
articles.abstract: Background: ARCN1-related syndrome (short stature-micrognathia syndrome, SSMG; OMIM #617164) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the ARCN1 gene, which encodes the δ-COP (COPD) subunit of the COPI coatomer complex. The condition is classically characterized by intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), short stature with rhizomelic shortening, microcephaly, micrognathia, facial dysmorphism, and global developmental delay. Methods: Clinical examination, blood tests and genetic analysis were performed. Whole-exome sequencing and Sanger analysis were conducted, followed by bioinformatics analysis and ACMG-based variant interpretation to identify and characterize the pathogenic variant. Results: We report a male proband with a previously undescribed variant in the ARCN1 gene, presenting with an atypical phenotype. Notably, the patient lacked the classical syndromic features, including short stature, microcephaly, IUGR, and developmental delay. The predominant clinical manifestation was transient hepatic dysfunction occurring during febrile episodes, which resolved between acute events. On physical examination, rhizomelic shortening and dysmorphic facial features, including mild micrognathia, were found. Overall, identified symptoms were mild in severity, which may be associated with the variant's location within the gene. Conclusions: We describe a novel likely pathogenic variant in the ARCN1 gene associated with a mild phenotype of SSMG. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of ARCN1-related syndrome and highlights the importance of considering this diagnosis in patients with unexplained recurrent liver injury, even in the absence of classical syndromic features.

articles.title: Systemic Inflammatory Biomarkers and Unsupervised Phenotyping of Surgical Pleurodesis Outcomes in Malignant Pleural Effusion: A Retrospective Single-Centre Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Pleurodesis is widely used to control malignant pleural effusion (MPE), but reliable pre-procedural predictors of success remain lacking. We assessed whether routinely available systemic inflammatory biomarkers predict short-term pleurodesis outcome and explored multidimensional inflammatory phenotypes. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included 144 patients who underwent pleurodesis for MPE between January 2021 and August 2025. Pre-procedural systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. K-means clustering, principal component analysis, and uniform manifold approximation and projection were used for exploratory phenotyping. Results: Complete success occurred in 100 patients (69.4%), failure in 35 (24.3%), and partial response in 9 (6.3%). None of the biomarkers discriminated success from failure (AUC: SII, 0.471; NLR, 0.409; PLR, 0.490; CRP, 0.544). Three exploratory clusters showed crude success rates of 88.9%, 72.3%, and 61.5%, respectively, but substantial overlap and lack of external validation precluded clinical interpretation. Conclusions: Single pre-procedural systemic inflammatory biomarkers should not be used alone to select patients for pleurodesis. Prospective multicenter studies integrating systemic markers with pleural biology and mechanical factors are warranted.

articles.title: Reducing Benign Breast Biopsies in Women Aged 35 Years or Younger Using a Clinician-AI-Age Triage Strategy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Symptomatic breast services face increasing diagnostic demand, while younger women with benign-appearing ultrasound lesions frequently undergo biopsy despite a low prevalence of malignancy. This study evaluated whether a rule-based clinical decision algorithm combining patient age, clinician ultrasound assessment and artificial intelligence (AI) decision support could identify a subgroup in whom biopsy might be avoided without excluding malignancy from the biopsy pathway. Methods: A retrospective analysis was performed using prospectively collected service-evaluation data from 240 patients (254 lesions) attending a large NHS breast unit between May and December 2025. Clinician ultrasound assessment, KOIOS DS Breast AI output and histopathology were recorded. Lesions in women aged ≤ 35 years were eligible for biopsy avoidance when clinician assessment was U2 or U3 and the KOIOS AI assessment was BI-RADS 2. Histopathology was the reference standard. Secondary analyses compared clinician and AI diagnostic performance. An illustrative five-year budget impact analysis was undertaken from the NHS provider perspective. Results: Among 151 lesions in women aged ≤ 35 years, 146 were benign and five were malignant. The algorithm would have classified 87 lesions for biopsy avoidance (57.6%; 95% CI, 49.3-65.6%). Of these, 67 (77.0%) had a clinician U3 classification. All 87 were benign on histopathology (100%; 95% CI, 95.8-100%), while all five malignant lesions remained in the biopsy pathway. Clinician assessment showed higher specificity than AI (99.1% vs. 75.7%), whereas AI showed higher sensitivity (96.9% vs. 81.3%). Avoidance of 87 biopsies was associated with approximately £85,000 in gross cost offsets during the evaluation period in the illustrative economic model. Conclusions: The AI-supported clinical decision algorithm could substantially reduce benign biopsy activity in younger women while maintaining cancer detection in this cohort. The small number of malignancies, single-centre design and biopsy population mean that prospective multicentre validation is required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: The "Heat-and-Cold" Strategy: Combining Intercostal Nerve Cryoablation for Analgesia After Uniportal VATS Pleurectomy and Hyperthermic Intrathoracic Chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: We report interesting images from a 54-year-old woman with recurrent B2 thymoma associated with myasthenia gravis, treated using a minimally invasive uniportal VATS pleurectomy combined with hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy (HITHOC). Preoperative imaging identified two hypermetabolic pleural lesions. Complete resection was achieved, followed by cisplatin-based HITHOC. Postoperative pain was managed by a multimodal approach combining erector spinae plane block and intercostal nerve cryoablation, resulting in a VAS score of two on the first postoperative day, decreasing to zero subsequently, and with no opioid requirement to control pain. The patient experienced an uneventful recovery and rapid discharge. This case highlights the feasibility and safety, with favourable outcomes in this patient. Larger and comparative series are needed to confirm the potential advantages of combining minimally invasive surgery with advanced analgesic strategies in complex thoracic oncology.

articles.title: Differential Plasma MMP-3 Levels in H1N1 and COVID-19 Pneumonia.
articles.abstract: Background: Matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) participates in extracellular matrix remodeling and lung injury, yet its behavior across different viral pneumonias remains unclear. We compared circulating MMP-3 levels in patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and H1N1 pneumonia and evaluated their relationships with clinical severity. Methods: This retrospective study included hospitalized patients with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 or H1N1 infection. Plasma MMP-3 concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Clinical severity was assessed using the arterial oxygen partial pressure to fractional inspired oxygen ratio (PaO2/FiO2), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score, and hospital length of stay. Between-group comparisons and correlation analyses were performed among 109 patients, including 57 with H1N1 and 52 with COVID-19. Results: Plasma MMP-3 concentrations were higher in patients with H1N1 than COVID-19. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated excellent discriminatory ability of MMP-3 for differentiating H1N1 from COVID-19 pneumonia with an optimal cutoff value of 4.601 ng/mL. Higher MMP-3 levels were associated with lower bicarbonate levels in both cohorts, although the association reached statistical significance only in patients with H1N1. Conclusions: The circulating MMP-3 differs substantially between H1N1 and COVID-19 pneumonia and is substantially higher in H1N1 patients.

articles.title: MRI-Derived Muscle Composition and Visceral Adiposity in Relation to Mortality and Vascular Outcomes in MASLD.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a cardiometabolic phenotype rather than a single-pathway liver disorder, yet prognostic work tends to privilege liver fat over the rest of body composition. We examined which magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived compartment, including hepatic, abdominal adipose, or skeletal muscle, best explained risk within MASLD. Methods: We investigated 24,976 UK Biobank adults with abdominal MRI, including 10,490 with MASLD, 2577 with MASLD with increased alcohol intake, and 11,909 without steatotic liver disease. Five MRI parameters were examined: proton density fat fraction (PDFF), visceral adipose tissue (VAT), abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue (ASAT), muscle fat infiltration (MFI), and thigh fat-free muscle volume (FFMV). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, incident cardiovascular disease, and incident cerebrovascular disease. Cox models jointly included all five MRI variables and adjusted for demographic, metabolic, and biochemical covariates. Results: Within MASLD, liver PDFF was not independently associated with all-cause mortality or cerebrovascular disease after multivariable adjustment, whereas an inverse association was observed with cardiovascular disease. By contrast, higher MFI was associated with all-cause mortality and cerebrovascular disease, whereas greater FFMV was associated with lower cardiovascular risk. VAT showed an independent association with cardiovascular disease, whereas ASAT had no significance. Clustering identified a lean-sarcopenic phenotype with higher mortality and cerebrovascular risk than a balanced reference phenotype. Conclusions: MRI-derived body-composition parameters showed outcome-specific associations with clinical outcomes in MASLD. Muscle-related measures were particularly associated with all-cause mortality and cerebrovascular disease, whereas visceral adiposity and muscle volume contributed to cardiovascular risk. These findings support the potential value of integrated body-composition assessment rather than reliance on hepatic steatosis alone, although further validation is needed to establish its incremental clinical utility.

articles.title: Does the Quantum Layer Help? A Leakage-Aware Benchmark of Hybrid Quantum-Classical Models for Brain Tumor MRI Classification.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hybrid quantum-classical neural networks are reported to classify brain tumors on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) accurately, but these reports rarely control for data leakage or test whether the quantum circuit contributes. We examined both issues. Methods: We audited version 2 of the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI Dataset (7200 images) with mirror- and rotation-invariant duplicate detection and by matching every image to its source collections, which recovered patient identities for 4846 tumor images. A variational quantum circuit (VQC) was compared with size-matched, deeper and Fourier-surrogate classical controls using frozen features, end-to-end fine-tuning and training from scratch, all under patient-grouped five-fold cross-validation. Results: Of the 1600 test images, 1269 (79%) had a copy in the training partition, and 915 of the 917 figshare-derived test images shared a patient with it. On frozen features, a six-qubit VQC head was 6.0 percentage points (pp) less accurate than its classical control (95% confidence interval -6.8 to -5.2) and less accurate than a classical surrogate of its own function class. With fine-tuning, it stayed within about 1 pp of its control but was 0.7 pp less accurate (-1.2 to -0.1) after convergence-based training; a hybrid network trained from scratch was 8.3 pp less accurate than its control. Patient-grouped evaluation lowered accuracy by 3-8 pp relative to our earlier duplicate-grouped evaluation, and 76 glioma test images from another source remained poorly recognized. Conclusions: The quantum layer added cost but no accuracy, and leakage and provenance mattered more than the classifier head.

articles.title: From Stage to Systems: Integrating Standard Laboratory Markers into Bladder Cancer Prognostic Models.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Bladder cancer (BC) remains a globally prevalent malignancy with significant clinical heterogeneity. While the TNM staging system is the diagnostic standard, its ability to provide individualized, comprehensive prognostic insights is limited. This study evaluates whether integrating routine laboratory markers into machine learning (ML) frameworks can enhance mortality risk prediction beyond traditional staging. Methods: Routine electronic health records from 337 adult patients with confirmed BC (2010-2023) were analyzed. Six ML architectures were evaluated for mortality risk prediction: logistic regression (GLM), elastic net logistic regression (GLMNET), generalized additive models (GAM), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), gradient boosting machines (GBM), and support vector machines (SVM). Results: All models demonstrated stable performance, with the SVM achieving the highest pooled AUC (0.679, 95% CI 0.57-0.77). Feature importance analyses identified tumor grade and routine blood markers, specifically platelet count, bicarbonate (CO2), and random glucose, as the highest-ranking predictors, demonstrating a greater relative feature weight than individual traditional anatomical staging parameters within the models. Conclusions: Integrating standard hematologic and metabolic panels into ML models offers a potential, cost-effective avenue to augment risk stratification, warranting further external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Beyond the Segmental Code: Anatomic Diversity and Surgical Pathways in Left Atrial Appendage Isomerism with the {A,L,I} Combination.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Left atrial appendage isomerism (LAAI) is associated with substantial variation in venous connections and intracardiac anatomy. A subgroup of LAAI patients has L-loop ventricular topology together with a particular great artery relationship-a combination that corresponds historically to Van Praagh's {A,L,I} segmental notation-but this subgroup has not been separately characterized. We aimed to describe the anatomical spectrum, rhythm and conduction abnormalities, biventricular repair eligibility, and surgical pathways in this subgroup. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 15 patients with LAAI, L-loop ventricular topology, and a specific great artery relationship (aorta left-sided, pulmonary artery right-sided)-a combination corresponding historically to Van Praagh's {A,L,I} notation-evaluated between January 2010 and December 2025. Diagnosis was confirmed independently by echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography in all patients. Anatomical suitability for biventricular repair was determined by multidisciplinary consensus. Results: Median age at presentation was 3.0 months, and median follow-up was 31.0 months. An interrupted inferior vena cava was present in all patients. The great artery relationship was aorta left-posterior/pulmonary artery right-anterior in 12 patients, aorta left-anterior/pulmonary artery right-posterior in 2, and side-by-side in 1. Ventriculoarterial connection was concordant in 8 patients, double-outlet right ventricle in 6, and double-outlet left ventricle in 1. A common atrioventricular valve was present in 7 patients. Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction was present in 7 patients. Arrhythmia was documented in 6 patients, and 2 required permanent pacemaker implantation. Ten patients (66.7%) were considered anatomically eligible for biventricular repair; repair had been completed in 4, 2 had received interim palliation, and 4 remained awaiting surgery. The remaining 4 patients followed a single-ventricle pathway. One death was confirmed, and 2 patients were lost to follow-up. Conclusions: Within LAAI, the coexistence of L-loop ventricular topology and a specific great artery relationship was associated with ventriculoarterial concordance in most patients, which may support biventricular repair. Anatomical eligibility for repair, however, did not always translate into completed repair. Larger, multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Longitudinal Quantitative Pupillometry and Its Association with the Best Documented Level of Consciousness During ICU Hospitalization: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Quantitative pupillometry objectively assesses neurological status and has demonstrated prognostic value after cardiac arrest. Nonetheless, it remains unclear whether longitudinal changes in quantitative pupillary parameters are associated with concurrent trajectories of consciousness recovery during the acute phase of intensive care unit (ICU) hospitalization in comatose patients with heterogeneous underlying etiologies. We investigated associations between longitudinal quantitative pupillary trajectories and recovery of consciousness. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 126 adult ICU patients with Glasgow Coma Scale scores ≤8 who underwent serial constriction velocity (CV) and percentage change in pupil diameter (%CH) measurements during the first 5 ICU days. Neurological outcomes were classified into Good (minimally conscious state or better) and Bad (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome or coma) groups. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using generalized linear mixed models. Results: The Good outcome group consistently had higher CV and %CH than the Bad outcome group. Generalized linear mixed models showed significant group and time effects on bilateral CV and %CH, with significant group-by-time interactions only for bilateral %CH. %CH continued increasing in the Good outcome group but plateaued after Day 3 in the Bad outcome group. Conclusions: Serial quantitative pupillometry revealed a concurrent longitudinal association between changes in quantitative pupillary parameters and neurological status in a heterogeneous cohort of comatose ICU patients. These findings suggest that longitudinal assessment of quantitative pupillary parameters may complement multimodal neurological evaluations by providing objective information reflecting the ongoing process of consciousness recovery and dynamic changes in neurological status during the acute phase.

articles.title: Texture Fusion and Extreme Learning Machine for Interstitial Lung Disease Classification in HRCT Images.
articles.abstract: Background: Accurate classification of interstitial lung disease (ILD) patterns in HRCT images remains challenging due to overlapping textures across disease types. We propose a computer-aided diagnosis pipeline for classifying five lung tissue classes from HRCT images: ground glass, micronodule, emphysema, fibrosis, and normal. Methods: The method applies a multi-stage texture-enhancement pre-processing step (separating coarse/fine, high/low-contrast, and directional image components) followed by extraction of nine texture, gradient and gradient-orientation descriptors (LBP, RGLBP, BDIP, bilateral, CDF, SDLGFFO, SSGSM, HOG, and gradient orientation). All nine descriptors were evaluated individually, together with one fused configuration, a combination of four of the nine (LBP, RGLBP, BDIP, and HOG), which gave the highest accuracy. Feature dimensionality is reduced using PCA guided by an eigenvalue-based estimator, and classification is performed with an extreme learning machine (ELM), with SVM (RBF kernel) used as a comparison baseline. Results: On a dataset of 5000 HRCT images (1000 per class; 500 train/500 test per class), the fused four-dimensional representation, classified with ELM (without kernel), achieved 92% accuracy-the best result among 46 configurations compared directly on the held-out test set and therefore a test-set-optimized figure rather than an independently validated estimate of generalization performance-outperforming individual descriptors and alternative dimensionality-reduction methods (LLE, Kernel LDA, Laplacian Eigenmaps, Nyström, Random Fourier). Conclusions: The proposed pipeline combines a multi-stage texture-enhancement step with multi-descriptor fusion; the enhancement step is intended to improve the separability of subtle ILD texture patterns, but its individual contribution has not been verified, as an enhanced-versus-unenhanced ablation was not performed.

articles.title: Calibration- and Workload-Aware Machine Learning for PTSD-Focused Triage in Children Referred Following Sexual Abuse.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early identification of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) after childhood sexual abuse may support timely assessment, but triage requires evaluation of calibration, missed cases, and referral workload. This study assessed whether routinely recorded information could support prioritization for PTSD-focused assessment. Methods: This retrospective single-center study evaluated classification of post-event diagnostic outcomes documented by a specialist child and adolescent psychiatrist in 311 forensic referral records. DSM-5 diagnoses were grouped as PTSD versus no recorded post-event psychiatric diagnosis (n = 218; PTSD = 106) and PTSD versus other non-PTSD clinical outcomes (n = 199; PTSD = 106). Five models were compared. Within each evaluation design, preprocessing, model selection, sigmoid calibration, and threshold derivation were confined to the development partition; each pipeline was applied unchanged to held-out or chronologically later records. Results: Histogram-based gradient boosting yielded a held-out ROC-AUC of 0.6190 (95% CI, 0.4472-0.7853) and PR-AUC of 0.6578 in the primary formulation. Its threshold flagged 36 of 44 records and captured 18 of 21 PTSD cases (sensitivity, 0.8571; specificity, 0.2174). LightGBM yielded a ROC-AUC of 0.6441 (95% CI, 0.4475-0.8125) and PR-AUC of 0.6805 in the secondary formulation. Its threshold flagged 30 of 40 records and captured 18 of 21 PTSD cases (sensitivity, 0.8571; specificity, 0.3684). Calibration reduced Brier scores to 0.2537 and 0.2401, but the calibrated primary model remained slightly worse than the prevalence-only reference (Brier skill score, -0.0165; calibration slope, 0.4276). Temporal ROC-AUC values were 0.6358 and 0.6767, with high workloads. Conclusions: Routinely recorded information provided modest discrimination, and high case capture required assessment of most records. External validation, prospective workflow evaluation, and local recalibration are required before clinical use.

articles.title: Lateral Tibial Slope on Pre-Reconstruction MRI in ACL Graft Rerupture: Association, Discriminative Performance, and Measurement Reliability.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the association between lateral tibial slope (LTS), measured using the Hudek method on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before primary anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction, and ACL graft rerupture, and assessed the discriminative performance and reliability. Methods: This retrospective comparative study included 23 patients with definite ACL graft rerupture and 46 controls without rerupture after at least two years of follow-up. LTS was independently measured twice, four weeks apart, by a radiologist and an orthopedic surgeon blinded to group allocation and clinical outcomes. Reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), interobserver agreement using Bland-Altman analysis, and discriminative performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Age-adjusted associations with rerupture were evaluated using logistic regression. Results: LTS was significantly higher in the rerupture group in both measurement rounds for both observers (all p ≤ 0.009). Intraobserver repeatability was excellent for the radiologist (ICC = 0.985) and good for the orthopedic surgeon (ICC = 0.852), while interobserver agreement was moderate (ICC = 0.547 for mean measurements). The orthopedic surgeon measured LTS 0.85° higher on average. The area under the ROC curve was 0.794 (95% CI, 0.678-0.910) for the radiologist and 0.700 (95% CI, 0.563-0.837) for the orthopedic surgeon. Exploratory thresholds of ≥4.3° and ≥5.4° showed sensitivities of 60.9% and 43.5% and specificities of 93.5% and 91.3%, respectively. After age adjustment, each 1° increase in LTS was associated with 1.682-fold and 1.412-fold higher odds of rerupture (both p ≤ 0.003). Conclusions: Higher LTS before primary ACL reconstruction was associated with graft rerupture, including after age adjustment. Observer-related differences may influence absolute measurements and derived thresholds. Given their high specificity but limited sensitivity, these exploratory thresholds should not be considered validated clinical decision cutoffs.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Multimodal Artificial Intelligence in Differentiating Ocular Surface Squamous Neoplasia from Benign Lesions: A Retrospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ocular surface squamous neoplasia (OSSN), comprising conjunctival intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and invasive squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), can be difficult to distinguish from benign ocular surface lesions. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multimodal vision-language model in differentiating OSSN from selected benign lesions using standardized clinical and imaging inputs. Methods: In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 90 histopathologically confirmed lesions (20 CIN, 20 invasive SCC, 20 pterygia, 20 pseudopterygia, and 10 conjunctival papillomas) from a single tertiary center were evaluated with ChatGPT-4o (OpenAI) under three predefined conditions: expert-structured text, image-only, and combined multimodal input. The model was required to select a single diagnosis from predefined categories. Histopathology was the reference standard; agreement with expert clinical consensus was assessed separately. Scenario authors and consensus raters were blinded to histopathology. Results: In the multimodal condition, diagnostic accuracy was 78.9% (71/90; 95% CI, 69.4-86.0%), sensitivity 82.5% (95% CI, 68.1-91.3%), specificity 76.0% (95% CI, 62.6-85.7%), positive predictive value 73.3%, negative predictive value 84.4%, positive likelihood ratio 3.44 and negative likelihood ratio 0.23; false-negative and false-positive rates were 17.5% and 24.0%. Agreement with expert consensus was moderate (κ = 0.58). Accuracy was 60.0% (54/90; 95% CI, 49.7-69.5%) with expert-structured text alone and 70.0% (63/90; 95% CI, 59.9-78.5%) with images alone; because case-level paired predictions were not retained, between-condition differences were assessed descriptively only. Conclusions: In this single-center, diagnostically enriched cohort, a multimodal vision-language model showed measurable but imperfect diagnostic performance under standardized experimental conditions. These exploratory findings do not support autonomous clinical use; prospective external validation across broader lesion spectra and real-world clinical pathways is required.

articles.title: Tissue miR-143 and miR-29b Expression as Prognostic Biomarkers in Patients with Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Receiving Adjuvant Chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) carries one of the worst prognoses among solid tumors, and biomarkers that complement standard pathological variables in patients undergoing resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy are still lacking. Here, we examined whether tumor expression of 10 selected microRNAs (miRNAs) is associated with recurrence patterns and survival in this clinical setting. Methods: Fifty patients with resected PDAC who received adjuvant chemotherapy at a single institution (2012-2022) were studied retrospectively. Expression of let-7c, miR-10b, miR-27a, miR-29b, miR-31, miR-34a, miR-142, miR-143, miR-17-5p, and miR-200c was measured by quantitative real-time PCR in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor tissue, with adjacent non-tumor pancreatic tissue available for 21 patients. Associations with local recurrence, metastasis, disease-free survival (DFS), and overall survival (OS) were assessed by logistic regression and Cox regression, with miRNA expression dichotomized at the median. Results: Seven miRNAs (let-7c, miR-27a, miR-29b, miR-31, miR-34a, miR-143, miR-200c) were downregulated in tumor tissue and miR-10b was upregulated (all p < 0.05). Higher tumor expression of miR-143 was associated with local recurrence, while higher miR-29b expression was associated with shorter disease-free survival. Adenosquamous histology was independently associated with shorter DFS and OS. Conclusions: Higher tumor expression of miR-143 and miR-29b was associated with local recurrence and shorter disease-free survival, respectively. These exploratory associations require validation in larger independent cohorts.

articles.title: CD138-Positive Plasma Cells in the Endometrium of Women with a Caesarean Scar Defect.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study seeks to assess the prevalence of CD138-positive plasma cells in endometrial biopsies from women undergoing surgery for symptomatic caesarean scar defect (CSD) and examine associations with niche morphology, defect size, symptoms, and surgical approach. Study design: In this prospective single-centre study, women undergoing surgery for symptomatic CSD between January 2024 and June 2026 were included if an endometrial biopsy had been assessed for CD138. Plasma-cell counts were categorised as negative (0 cells/HPF), borderline (1-4 cells/HPF), or elevated (≥5 cells/HPF). Preoperative niche morphology was assessed by transvaginal ultrasound. Associations with CD138 status were tested using Mann-Whitney U and Fisher's exact tests and multivariable logistic regression. Results: Of 235 surgically treated women, 196 had an assessable CD138 result. CD138 positivity was present in 26 (13.3%); 19 (9.7%) had 1-4 cells and seven (3.6%) > 4 cells. CD138 status was not associated with defect size, uterine position, inclusion cysts, concomitant peritoneal endometriosis, surgical approach, or any recorded symptom. The absence of associations persisted after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions: Endometrial CD138-positive plasma cells were present in a minority of women with symptomatic CSD and did not reflect defect morphology, severity, or symptom burden. Routine CD138 testing cannot be justified on the basis of niche subtype or defect size.

articles.title: Nutritional Impact and Symptom Profile Associated with 5-Fluorouracil and Capecitabine in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: An Observational Study Using the PG-SGA.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Colorectal cancer and its chemotherapeutic treatment may be associated with gastrointestinal toxicity and nutritional deterioration. This study evaluated the association between exposure to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) or capecitabine and eating-related symptoms and nutritional status. Methods: We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study of 91 patients with colorectal cancer receiving active chemotherapy. Clinical, anthropometric, and treatment-related variables were collected. Nutritional status was assessed using the Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA), and body composition was evaluated by multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis. Associations between exposure to 5-FU or capecitabine and symptomatic and nutritional variables were analyzed. Results: Ninety valid observations were available for the pharmacological analysis. Loss of appetite was more frequent among patients treated with 5-FU than among those not exposed to 5-FU (31.6% vs. 11.5%; p = 0.006), as was nausea (26.3% vs. 5.8%; p = 0.037). Among patients treated with capecitabine, diarrhea was less frequent than among those not exposed to capecitabine (23.5% vs. 51.3%; p = 0.048). Conclusions: Exposure to 5-FU and capecitabine was associated with distinct symptom profiles that may be clinically relevant to nutritional status. Multidimensional nutritional assessment using the PG-SGA may facilitate the early identification of nutritional risk during chemotherapy. However, the observational and cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; therefore, these findings require confirmation in prospective, longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Continuous Near-Infrared Spectroscopy as a Real-Time Monitor of Intravenous Thrombolysis in Acute Ischaemic Stroke: A Prospective Observational Emergency Department Study.
articles.abstract: Background. Intravenous (IV) thrombolysis is the standard of care for acute ischaemic stroke (AIS), yet there is still no objective bedside tool for monitoring the brain continuously during the infusion. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) provides non-invasive, continuous measurement of regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO2). We evaluated whether bilateral frontal NIRS, and in particular the absolute interhemispheric difference in rSO2 (ΔNIRS), tracks the clinical trajectory of patients receiving IV alteplase in the emergency department (ED). Methods. A prospective observational cohort study was conducted in the ED of a tertiary university hospital. Consecutive adults receiving IV alteplase for AIS were screened, and those enrolled underwent continuous bilateral frontal NIRS monitoring. Bilateral rSO2, ΔNIRS, vital signs, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) were recorded at baseline and at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60 and 120 min after the start of the infusion. Patients were classified by clinical trajectory during monitoring as improvement, no change, or deterioration. Results. Forty-one patients were analyzed (26 female, 63.4%; mean age 73.6 ± 14.8 years); 15 (36.6%) improved, 21 (51.2%) showed no change and 5 (12.2%) deteriorated. In the whole cohort, absolute rSO2 rose only slightly in the affected hemisphere and did not change in the unaffected hemisphere. However, affected-hemisphere rSO2 rose significantly in the improvement group (median 59 to 67; p = 0.001) and fell significantly in the deterioration group (p = 0.015). ΔNIRS narrowed from a median of 4 (IQR 3-9) at baseline to 1 (IQR 0-5) at 120 min in the improvement group (p = 0.034) and did not change significantly in the other groups. The two patients with acute complications desaturated bilaterally. NIHSS correlated strongly and inversely with GCS at every time point (ρ = -0.74 to -0.84; all p < 0.001). Conclusions. During IV thrombolysis in the ED, continuous bilateral frontal NIRS tracked the clinical trajectory. Because recanalisation and reperfusion were not assessed independently, what NIRS paralleled was the clinical course, not reperfusion itself. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant larger studies that validate ΔNIRS against perfusion or vascular imaging.

articles.title: Current Diagnostic Practices for Sacroiliac Joint Pain Among Interventional Pain Physicians: Results of an Exploratory Practice Survey.
articles.abstract: Background: Sacroiliac (SI) joint pain contributes to chronic axial low back pain, but diagnosis remains challenging because no single historical feature, physical examination maneuver, imaging finding, or injection response is universally accepted as definitive. Although guidelines recommend multimodal assessment, less is known about how interventional pain physicians diagnose SI joint pain in real-world practice. Objective: We aim to describe self-reported diagnostic practices for suspected SI joint-mediated pain among interventional pain physicians. Study Design: Exploratory cross-sectional survey. Methods: An anonymous, voluntary SurveyMonkey questionnaire was distributed between 1 January 2026, and 20 June 2026, to physicians practicing interventional pain medicine through academic institutional email distribution, professional contacts, and social media platforms. The present analysis focused on survey items related to physician specialty, practice setting, diagnostic approach, discordance between history and physical examination, use of diagnostic injections, estimated prevalence of SI joint pain, and management when SI joint and lumbar facet pain coexist. Results: Forty-eight physicians initiated the survey, although some respondents skipped individual items; therefore, item-level response totals ranged from 47 to 48. Respondents were predominantly anesthesiologists (72.3%) and most commonly practiced in academic medical centers (58.3%). All incorporated history and physical examination into their primary diagnostic approach, and 62.5% also included diagnostic injection. A single diagnostic injection was reported by 59.6%, whereas 27.7% routinely used two or more. Conclusion: Respondents reported multimodal clinical assessment with variation in diagnostic injection strategies. This small, self-selected sample describes practice patterns and does not establish national consensus, diagnostic standards, or population prevalence.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Contrast-Enhanced Computed Tomography in Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: The Added Value of Combining CT with CA-125.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Preoperative prediction of retroperitoneal lymph node (LN) metastasis in epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) may inform surgical planning and counselling. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) for pathological LN metastasis and explored whether adding serum CA-125 to CT findings improves prediction. Methods: This single-centre retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 97 patients with invasive EOC who underwent primary (n = 81) or interval (n = 16) cytoreductive surgery with histopathological LN assessment (2022-2025) and CT within two months before surgery. Pelvic and para-aortic CT findings were compared with histopathology at the patient and regional levels. A logistic model combining these CT findings with log2-transformed CA-125 was compared with the CT-only model using a likelihood-ratio test and was internally validated by bootstrapping. Results: Pathological LN metastasis was present in 31 patients (32.0%). At the patient level, CT had a sensitivity of 58% and a specificity of 67%; a short-axis threshold of >10 mm increased specificity to 94% (sensitivity 23%). Adding CA-125 to the CT model improved model fit (likelihood-ratio p = 0.019) and discrimination (optimism-corrected area under the curve 0.63 vs. 0.70), with acceptable calibration (corrected slope 0.86). The association of CA-125 with LN metastasis was attenuated after adjustment for high-grade serous histology (adjusted odds ratio per doubling 1.18, 95% confidence interval 0.98-1.43) and was not evident in patients with stage III-IV disease. Conclusions: CT has limited sensitivity for LN metastasis in EOC, although enlarged nodes are highly specific. CA-125 may add information to CT findings, but this largely reflects differences in disease extent and histology. These preliminary findings require prospective, externally validated studies before any clinical application.

articles.title: Intraoperative Correlates of Electrode Array Insertion Dynamics and Electrophysiological Parameters Under SmartNav-Guided Cochlear Implantation: An Exploratory Single-Centre Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Real-time intraoperative navigation systems such as SmartNav (Cochlear Ltd., Sydney, Australia) provide objective feedback on electrode array insertion during cochlear implantation, yet it remains unclear whether the parameters they record vary across the device- and patient-level factors a surgeon selects between. This study compared intraoperative insertion dynamics and electrophysiological parameters across electrode array design (CI622 slim-straight versus CI632 slim-modiolar), surgical approach (round window versus cochleostomy), and patient age (children versus adults). Methods: Twenty-nine consecutive implantations in 26 patients (three children implanted bilaterally) performed with SmartNav monitoring were analysed. Insertion angle, insertion speed, total insertion time, the number of contacts (of 22) with in-range impedance, and the number of contacts (of 22) with a measurable neural response telemetry (NRT) response were extracted from device logs and operative records; insertion kinetics were available for 22 of 29 implantations. Distributions were non-normal, so comparisons used the Mann-Whitney U test with rank-biserial effect sizes, Fisher's exact test, Kruskal-Wallis test, and Spearman correlation. Exploratory multivariable regression, Brown-Forsythe variance testing, bootstrap effect sizes, and outlier-inclusive and one-ear-per-patient sensitivity analyses were additionally applied; no correction for multiple comparisons was made. Results: The CI632 array was advanced faster per electrode than the CI622 (median 0.33 versus 0.56 s/electrode; n = 5 versus 16; p = 0.015; rank-biserial r = -0.75; bootstrap 95% CI -1.00 to -0.38), but the difference was not significant when one implausible outlying value was retained (p = 0.113). Impedance and NRT status were modestly correlated (ρ = 0.388, p = 0.037, uncorrected) and unchanged after adjustment for age band (partial ρ = 0.389), but were not significant in the one-ear-per-patient analysis. The study was unable to detect a difference between age groups or between surgical approaches (five cochleostomies versus 24 round window insertions) in any parameter, and impedance status varied minimally across all strata. Conclusions: Within the limits of a small, unbalanced cohort, SmartNav-derived parameters did not differ detectably across patient age or surgical approach. The data suggest that electrode array design is associated with per-electrode insertion pacing, an observation that depends on a single excluded data point and requires confirmation. The impedance-NRT association is exploratory, is consistent with a chance finding once multiplicity is considered, and should not yet be regarded as an intraoperative integrity signal. No clinical outcome was linked to the intraoperative parameters, so no inference about the clinical superiority of either array or approach can be drawn.

articles.title: Multispecimen Genomic Profiling Reveals Inter-Specimen Heterogeneity and Supports Ascites as a Complementary Biospecimen in Pseudomyxoma Peritonei.
articles.abstract: Background: Pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) is a rare peritoneal malignancy with limited genomic data across different biospecimen types. The extent to which ascites and plasma reflect tissue-detected genomic alterations remains incompletely characterized. This study compared genomic profiles across tumor tissue, ascites, and plasma and explored KRAS-defined molecular features in PMP. Methods: Sixty patients with pathologically confirmed PMP were retrospectively included. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) data were available from tumor tissue in 57 patients, ascites in 40, and plasma in 28, with overlapping specimen availability. Cross-specimen genomic concordance was evaluated in 37 patients with matched tissue-ascites samples, including 28 patients with matched tissue, ascites, and plasma. Exploratory analyses were performed to characterize genomic and pathway-level features across KRAS-defined subgroups. Results: In tumor tissue, KRAS (66.7%), GNAS (31.6%), and TP53 (21.1%) were the most frequently altered genes. Among 28 patients with matched tissue, ascites, and plasma, patient-level concordance was 35.7%. At the mutation level, ascites showed higher tissue-referenced positive percentage agreement (PPA) than plasma (93.1% vs. 36.2%). In the expanded cohort of 37 matched tissue-ascites pairs, ascites achieved a tissue-referenced PPA of 94.2% and revealed additional alterations not detected in the corresponding tissue samples. Exploratory KRAS mutation stratification identified G12D (35.0%), G12X (32.5%), and KRAS-wild-type (wt) (17.5%) tumors as the predominant subgroups. KRAS-mutant tumors harbored more detected genomic alterations and potentially clinically actionable alterations than KRAS-wt tumors. Wnt and PI3K pathway alterations were more commonly observed in the G12D and G12X subgroups, respectively, whereas canonical oncogenic pathway alterations were less frequent in KRAS-wt tumors. Conclusions: PMP exhibits substantial genomic heterogeneity across patients and biospecimen types. Ascites cfDNA showed high concordance with tissue and captured additional genomic alterations, suggesting that ascitic fluid may serve as a complementary source for molecular profiling in PMP. KRAS-defined subgroups exhibited distinct genomic characteristics, although their clinical relevance requires further validation in larger, well-characterized cohorts.

articles.title: Photon-Counting Detector CT Enables Quantification of Dorsal Root Ganglion Enlargement in Radiculopathy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dorsal root ganglion (DRG) enlargement in radiculopathy reflects inflammatory nerve root responses and correlates with symptom severity. While DRG enlargement can be detected by MRI, it is unclear whether photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) acquired during routine periradicular therapy (PRT) enables detection and quantification of DRG volumetric changes in lumbosacral radiculopathy. Methods: This retrospective study included 28 selected patients with unilateral L5 or S1 radiculopathy undergoing PCD-CT-guided PRT followed by confirmed therapeutic response. Three independent blinded readers segmented DRGs on low-dose planning acquisitions. Affected and contralateral DRG volumes were compared using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results: Affected DRGs exceeded contralateral volumes in 26 of 28 patients (92.9%). Median symptomatic DRG volume was 341.1 mm3 versus 282.3 mm3 contralaterally (p < 0.001). Median DRG enlargement was +24.0%. The result was consistent across L5 and S1 radiculopathy levels. Inter-reader agreements were high (median Dice similarity coefficients 0.78-0.85, median volumetric similarities 0.93-0.95). Conclusions: PCD-CT enables visualization and quantification of DRG volumetric changes on routine therapeutic imaging of selected patients, extracting biological information from procedural acquisitions. This establishes PCD-CT for investigating nerve pathophysiology and extends CT-based neuroradiological research into biological questions previously limited to MRI.

articles.title: Effect of Image Enhancement Filters on the Detection of Periapical Radiolucent Lesions on Panoramic Radiographs: A Multi-Reader Multi-Case Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Panoramic radiography is widely used in dental practice, but its two-dimensional projection geometry and anatomical superimposition can obscure periapical radiolucent lesions, particularly in the maxillary anterior region and for novice observers. Methods: This retrospective multi-reader, multi-case study aimed to evaluate the effects of unsharp mask and Gaussian blur filters on the diagnostic performance and interobserver agreement of novice observers in detecting periapical radiolucent lesions on panoramic radiographs. Twenty final-year dental students evaluated 56 panoramic radiographs (28 lesion-positive and 28 lesion-free cases; 224 maxillary anterior teeth) under three imaging conditions (original, unsharp mask, and Gaussian blur). Observers scored lesion presence using a five-point confidence scale. Diagnostic performance (AUC, sensitivity, and specificity) was compared using the Dorfman-Berbaum-Metz/Obuchowski-Rockette multi-reader, multi-case method. Interobserver agreement was assessed using quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: Imaging condition significantly affected AUC, sensitivity, and specificity (all p ≤ 0.003). Compared with original images, unsharp mask significantly improved sensitivity (78.2% vs. 52.5%), specificity (90.2% vs. 83.2%), and AUC (0.876 vs. 0.737) (all p < 0.05), with the highest interobserver agreement (ICC = 0.951; κ = 0.476). Gaussian blur significantly reduced sensitivity (40.2%) and AUC (0.655) compared with original images (both p < 0.001). Conclusions: Unsharp mask filtering was associated with improved diagnostic performance and interobserver agreement among novice observers, whereas Gaussian blur was associated with reduced lesion detection performance. These findings suggest that unsharp mask filtering may have potential as an adjunct to radiographic interpretation training.

articles.title: Inflammatory and Nutritional Biomarkers for Overall Survival in Gastric Adenocarcinoma: Comparative Performance and Exploratory Temporal Patterns.
articles.abstract: Background: Inflammatory and nutritional biomarkers are associated with survival in gastric cancer; however, their incremental prognostic value beyond routinely available clinical factors and the stability of their associations over time remain uncertain.
