We compared six routinely available biomarkers within a common clinically adjusted framework and evaluated their associations with overall survival (OS), model performance, temporal variation, and internal robustness. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 255 patients with gastric adenocarcinoma. A prespecified parsimonious Cox model comprising age, sex, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, and metastatic disease at diagnosis served as the clinical reference model. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score were added separately. Model fit and discrimination, multiple-testing-adjusted associations, time-varying effects, bootstrap internal validation, and influence-diagnostic sensitivity analyses were assessed. Results: During follow-up, 227 patients (89.0%) died. Median OS was 11.66 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 9.63-13.47), and reverse Kaplan-Meier median follow-up was 88.51 months (95% CI, 69.72-110.59). After adjustment for the prespecified clinical factors, higher NLR, PLR, and SII were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher LMR, PNI, and HALP were associated with lower mortality; all associations remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (q ≤ 0.007). The clinical model had a C-index of 0.678. Biomarker addition yielded C-indices ranging from 0.682 to 0.695, with the largest numerical increase observed for PNI (ΔC-index, +0.017). The HALP-extended model yielded the numerically lowest Akaike information criterion. Exploratory time-specific estimates suggested stronger biomarker-mortality associations during early follow-up, although the interaction tests did not remain significant after multiplicity correction. Bootstrap-corrected C-indices were 0.689 for PNI, 0.686 for HALP, and 0.682 for SII, with low optimism and successful convergence of all 1000 resamples. Influence-diagnostic sensitivity analyses preserved the direction and statistical significance of these associations. Conclusions: Inflammatory and nutritional biomarkers provided additional prognostic information beyond the prespecified clinical factors. Although all six biomarkers remained associated with OS when evaluated separately, their incremental contribution to overall discrimination was modest. PNI and HALP yielded the most favorable numerical model-performance estimates; however, the absolute differences were modest, and formal paired bootstrap comparisons identified no significant differences between the biomarker-extended models. External and longitudinal validation is required before routine prognostic implementation.

articles.title: Malignancy-Associated Secondary EGJOO (Pseudoachalasia) Due to Infiltrative Gastric Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Pseudoachalasia is an uncommon condition that clinically, radiographically, and manometrically mimics primary achalasia and is most frequently caused by a malignancy involving the gastroesophageal junction or gastric cardia. Distinguishing pseudoachalasia from a primary motility disorder remains challenging because conventional investigations may initially appear reassuring. We present a patient with progressive dysphagia and weight loss whose initial EGD was interpreted as showing no definite mucosal abnormality and whose HREM demonstrated a manometric pattern consistent with EGJOO. Progressive symptoms prompted repeat endoscopy and EUS; these revealed distinct abnormalities of the proximal gastric wall; targeted biopsies confirmed poorly differentiated gastric adenocarcinoma. Although the initial endoscopic examination showed no evident abnormality, HREM cannot visualize or histologically characterize tissue; therefore, it cannot exclude a structural or malignant etiology. This case illustrates that progressive symptoms should prompt re-evaluation.

articles.title: Factors Associated with the Accuracy of Sonographic Fetal Weight Estimation: A Study of 1262 Vietnamese Pregnancies.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sonographic estimated fetal weight (EFW) guides many obstetric decisions. We examined maternal, fetal and sonographic factors associated with EFW error using the Hadlock II, Hadlock III and Shinozuka formulas. Methods: This is a retrospective cross-sectional study of 1262 singleton pregnancies at 30-41 weeks scanned within 3 days before delivery. Accuracy was assessed by mean percentage error (MPE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), successful estimation rate (SER; error ≤ 10%), Bland-Altman analysis with regression-based limits of agreement and Deming regression. Formulas were compared with paired tests. Each factor's contribution was measured as the decrease in Nagelkerke R2 (ΔR2) in multivariable logistic regression; factor × formula interactions were tested with generalised estimating equations (GEE). Results: MAPE was 5.44%, 5.64% and 5.75% and SER 86.2%, 84.2% and 84.5% for Hadlock II, Hadlock III and Shinozuka, respectively; differences between formulas were small (ΔMAPE ≤ 0.31 percentage points). Against birth weight, all three overestimated small and underestimated large fetuses (Deming slopes 0.79-0.85). Birth weight was the strongest correlate of SER (decrease in Nagelkerke R2, 0.052-0.129) and, in the main analysis, the only factor whose effect differed between formulas (p < 0.001); other factors reduced Nagelkerke R2 by <0.02. Sensitivity was 42-66% for the 89 neonates < 2500 g and 18-38% for the 39 neonates ≥ 4000 g; positive predictive values were 78-82% and 88-100%, respectively, the latter based on 8-16 estimates (lower 95% confidence limits, 47-74%). Conclusions: EFW error was mainly associated with fetal size; this pattern, partly due to regression towards the mean, cannot be used as a bedside correction. Other characteristics showed little additional association with accuracy. The differences between the formulas were small, their clinical relevance is unclear, and none is recommended over the others. An EFW of 2500-2999 g does not exclude low birth weight, and an EFW of 3500-3999 g does not exclude a neonate of ≥4000 g.

articles.title: Evaluation of Trabecular Bone Microarchitecture for Zygomatic Implants: A Cone Beam Computed Tomography Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Zygomatic implants are commonly used to rehabilitate atrophic maxillae and maxillary defects, offering quicker prosthesis placement than bone grafting, but their placement requires technical precision due to the complexity of the zygomatic region. Trabecular bone quality is a key determinant of implant stability, yet data on the zygomatic bone's microarchitecture remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare trabecular bone microarchitectural features of the zygomatic bone with three reference sites (first molar region, mandibular condyle, and angle of mandible) using cone beam computed tomography (CBCT). Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study screened 847 archived CBCT scans from the Ankara University Faculty of Dentistry, of which 99 systemically healthy patients aged 20-30 years were included. Trabecular bone microstructural parameters, including tissue volume, bone volume, percent bone volume, trabecular thickness, trabecular number, trabecular separation, and fractal dimension, were assessed using CTAn software at the zygomatic bone, first molar region, mandibular condyle, and angle of mandible. Results: The zygomatic bone exhibited significantly higher tissue and bone volumes than the other regions but lower percent bone volume and trabecular number; trabecular thickness and separation were greatest in the zygomatic bone, while fractal dimension values were lowest. When pooled across the four regions, significant right-left differences were also observed, with higher tissue volume and pore space on the right side. Conclusions: These findings provide baseline reference data on the zygomatic bone's trabecular structure in a young, systemically healthy population. Further clinical studies in patient groups more representative of typical zygomatic implant candidates, including both older individuals with age-related maxillary atrophy and younger patients with trauma- or pathology-related bone loss, are needed to confirm the relevance of these findings to implant predictability and safety.

articles.title: Associations Between the Chippaux-Smirak Index and Clinical Foot Assessments in Young Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The Chippaux-Smirak Index (CSI) measures relative midfoot plantar contact, whereas the six-item Foot Posture Index (FPI-6), navicular drop test (NDT), and resting calcaneal stance position (RCSP) assess static foot posture, change in navicular height, and calcaneal alignment, respectively. This study examined associations among these measures, agreement between CSI and FPI-6 classifications, and measurement reliability in young adults. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 350 young adults, with both feet assessed (700 feet). Two orthotists independently measured CSI, FPI-6, NDT, and RCSP. Generalised estimating equation models accounted for correlations between feet and were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and foot side. Agreement was assessed using exact percentage agreement and linear weighted Cohen's kappa, and reliability using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Results: After adjustment, each increase of 10 percentage points in CSI was associated with a 2.141-point-higher FPI-6 total score, a 2.660 mm greater navicular drop, and an RCSP that was 3.240° more valgus (all p < 0.001). CSI and grouped FPI-6 classifications agreed for 82.9% of feet (linear weighted κ = 0.664, 95% CI 0.595-0.727). Single-measure interrater ICCs ranged from 0.644 for NDT to 0.884 for CSI. Digital remeasurement of CSI demonstrated excellent intrarater reliability (ICC(A,1) = 0.989). Conclusions: Higher CSI values were associated with a more pronated static foot posture, greater navicular drop, and a more valgus RCSP. Incomplete agreement between CSI and FPI-6 classifications indicates that these methods provide related but distinct information and should be interpreted according to the specific foot characteristic assessed.

articles.title: Immune Microenvironment Heterogeneity in Breast Cancer: Stromal Lymphocytic Patterns Across Molecular and Clinicopathologic Subtypes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) have emerged as important indicators of tumour-host immune interaction in breast cancer, with increasing prognostic and predictive significance across molecular subtypes. However, most available evidence is derived from Western populations and focuses predominantly on quantitative stromal TIL assessment, while data regarding morphologic stromal immune architecture in Asian populations remain limited. This study evaluated stromal lymphocytic infiltration patterns and their association with molecular and clinicopathologic characteristics in an Indian cohort of invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. Methods: This retrospective observational pathology-based study included 231 female patients diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma at Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Aligarh Muslim University, India, between 2009 and 2014. Stromal lymphocytic infiltration was assessed on haematoxylin and eosin-stained sections using a semi-quantitative four-tier scoring system adapted from Guo et al. with whole-section assessment at ×100 magnification by two pathologists. Associations with tumour grade, tumour size, lymph node status, and molecular subtype were assessed using exact and ordinal tests with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. Results: Luminal breast carcinoma was the most common molecular subtype (59.3%), followed by HER2-positive tumours (22.5%) and triple-negative breast cancer (18.2%). Sparse stromal lymphocytic infiltration (score 1) represented the most frequent pattern overall (46.8%). Significant associations were identified between stromal lymphocytic infiltration and molecular subtype, tumour grade, and lymph node status (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001, p = 0.044 and p = 0.044, respectively). Triple-negative and HER2-positive tumours demonstrated higher proportions of moderate-to-dense (score 2-3) infiltration than luminal tumours (40.5% and 48.1% vs. 16.8%). Score 2-3 infiltration was more frequent in Grade III tumours (51.2%) and, conversely, in lymph node-negative than in lymph node-positive tumours (40.8% vs. 21.9%). No statistically significant association was observed between stromal lymphocytic infiltration and tumour size (Holm-adjusted p = 0.071). Conclusions: Stromal lymphocytic infiltration patterns demonstrate substantial heterogeneity across breast cancer molecular subtypes and are associated with molecular subtype and histologic grade, whereas higher infiltration was more frequent in lymph node-negative tumours. These descriptive associations suggest that stromal immune patterns vary with tumour phenotype rather than tumour size. Semi-quantitative morphologic stromal lymphocyte assessment on routine histopathology is inexpensive and feasible in resource-limited settings; its reproducibility and prognostic value require validation.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Radiofrequency Echographic Multi Spectrometry Compared with Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry: A Real-World Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Radiofrequency Echographic Multi-Spectrometry (REMS) is an ultrasound-based technique for the assessment of bone mineral density (BMD) that has been proposed as an alternative to dual-energy X ray absorptiometry (DXA) for the diagnosis of osteoporosis. Although previous studies have reported high diagnostic concordance between REMS and DXA, evidence from real-world settings remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance and agreement between REMS and DXA in a clinical population undergoing BMD assessment. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, 145 subjects undergoing BMD evaluation were assessed with both REMS and DXA. Complete paired examinations were available for 142 patients at the lumbar spine and 134 at the femoral neck. DXA was used as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance of REMS was evaluated by calculating sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Agreement between REMS and DXA diagnostic classifications was assessed using linearly weighted Cohen's kappa. Mean REMS and DXA measurements were compared using paired Student's t-tests, whereas agreement between continuous BMD measurements was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to evaluate the discriminative performance of REMS T-scores. Results: At the lumbar spine, REMS showed a sensitivity of 50.0% (95% CI: 37.5-62.5), specificity of 65.5% (95% CI: 54.8-74.8), PPV of 50.0% (95% CI: 37.5-62.5), and NPV of 65.5% (95% CI: 54.8-74.8). At the femoral neck, sensitivity was 40.0% (95% CI: 28.1-53.2), specificity 70.9% (95% CI: 60.1-79.7), PPV 48.9% (95% CI: 35.0-63.0), and NPV 62.9% (95% CI: 52.5-72.2). ROC analysis showed limited discriminatory performance for DXA-defined osteoporosis, with AUC values of 0.610 at the lumbar spine and 0.623 at the femoral neck. Linearly weighted Cohen's kappa values were 0.225 and 0.183, respectively, indicating limited agreement in diagnostic classification. No statistically significant differences in mean BMD or T-score values were detected between the two techniques. Conclusions: In this real-world retrospective cohort, REMS and DXA showed no statistically significant differences in mean BMD or T-score values, but agreement in individual diagnostic classification was limited. These results suggest that REMS may have a complementary role alongside DXA rather than serving as a standalone screening method for DXA-defined osteoporosis in this cohort. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the clinical significance of REMS-DXA discordant cases and their relationship with fracture risk.

articles.title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Histogram Analysis of Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma of the Head and Neck: Correlation with Histological Grade and Exploratory Survival Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: In this study, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of a whole-tumor histogram analysis of apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values derived from diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) for predicting adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) histological grade and solid-component status. Methods: This retrospective study included 168 patients with primary head and neck ACC who underwent preoperative 3.0 T MRI with DWI, randomly allocated with stratification by grade to a derivation cohort (n = 107) and an internal validation cohort (n = 61). Whole-tumor ADC histogram features were extracted and reduced through correlation analysis, and the two most discriminative features were combined in a logistic regression model. Overall survival was explored using Cox regression. Results: ADC10 alone (the 10th percentile of ADC) had areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.821 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.727-0.899) and 0.780 (95% CI 0.643-0.895) for grade III in the derivation and validation cohorts, and 0.743 and 0.709 for solid-component status; adding the low-ADC volume did not improve discrimination (DeLong p ≥ 0.468). The model output was associated with overall survival in the pooled cohort (hazard ratio per standard deviation, 1.627) but not in the validation cohort or after adjustment for grade. Conclusions: ADC10 showed promising discrimination of grade III ACC in internal validation, with no gain from adding the low-ADC volume; the prognostic value is unconfirmed, and multicenter external validation is warranted.

articles.title: Subject-Specific Cardiovascular Signatures Revealed by Arterial Pulse Signals in Patients with Heart Diseases-Part II: Special Cases.
articles.abstract: Aim: This study evaluates whether cardiovascular (CV) parameters derived from noninvasive arterial pulse signals can reveal subject-specific characteristics in patients with atypical CV dynamics. Methods: Seven special-case patients-including a heart transplant (HTx) recipient and individuals with bradycardia (low heart rate, HR), low dicrotic notch (DN), and intermittent arterial pulse waveform (APW) variations-were analyzed across three visits over the cardiac rehabilitation (CR) period. Radial artery (RA) and carotid artery (CA) signals, acquired using micro-fabricated tactile sensors, were processed using a single-degree-of-freedom time-frequency (SDOF-TF) framework to extract multiple CV parameters. The analysis focused on descriptive characterization of subject-specific CV patterns in individual patients. Results: The patients exhibited highly heterogeneous CV profiles. Individuals with low HR exhibited relatively limited post-exercise HR changes. Individuals with low DN morphology exhibited elevated lower-order harmonic amplitudes. Individuals with intermittent APW variations exhibited cyclic changes in APW morphology at rest and during post-exercise recovery. Although CV patterns at rest differed across individuals, post-exercise assessment revealed more distinctive individual-specific differences, including differences between individuals within the same phenotype-based case subset. Across all patients and visits, RA measurements provided more stable and interpretable subject-specific CV patterns, whereas CA measurements were more susceptible to motion artifacts (MA) and sensor noise. For individuals with intermittent APW variations, the CA signals exhibited extremely poor signal quality, limiting their suitability for physiological interpretation. Conclusions: The SDOF-TF framework enabled the characterization of subject-specific, multi-parameter CV dynamics in these seven special cases. The findings illustrate the potential value of arterial pulse analysis for the individualized characterization of atypical CV dynamics. Future studies involving larger patient cohorts are needed to further investigate these findings and establish their clinical utility.

articles.title: Incidence of Adenomyosis in Hysterectomy Specimens Performed for Benign Uterine Pathologies: A Six-Year Retrospective Analysis from a Tertiary Center in Romania.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adenomyosis is a common yet frequently underdiagnosed cause of gynecological morbidity, and its definitive diagnosis still relies on histopathological examination of hysterectomy specimens. We aimed to determine the histopathological prevalence of adenomyosis in hysterectomy specimens removed for benign indications, characterize preoperative referral diagnoses and concurrent histopathological findings, and compare our results with the contemporary literature. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 430 consecutive abdominal hysterectomies performed for benign gynecological indications at a tertiary referral center in Iasi, Romania, between January 2019 and October 2024. Adenomyosis was defined histopathologically. An "incidental" finding was defined as the absence of adenomyosis in the preoperative referral diagnosis, without re-review of the original ultrasound reports. We report prevalence and the incidental rate with Wilson-score 95% confidence intervals (CIs); we used the chi-square test with Yates continuity correction for categorical comparisons and calculated odds ratios (ORs), with correction for multiple comparisons. Results: Adenomyosis was identified in 188 of 430 specimens (43.7%; 95% CI 39.1-48.4%), of which 186 (98.9%; 95% CI 96.2-99.7%) were incidental; adenomyosis was recorded in the referral diagnosis in only 2 cases (1.1%). Endometrial hyperplasia was the only co-finding significantly associated with adenomyosis (OR 2.30; 95% CI 1.48-3.55; p = 0.0002), an unadjusted univariate association that remained significant after multiple-comparison adjustment (adjusted p = 0.0014). No referral diagnosis discriminated adenomyosis status; leiomyoma was frequent in both groups (75.5% vs. 69.0%; not significant). Mean age was 50.0 ± 7.6 years, with no between-group difference (p = 0.112). Conclusions: Approximately two in five women undergoing hysterectomy for benign disease have adenomyosis, and it is rarely suspected preoperatively. Because this study did not test whether structured sonographic assessment improves detection, prospective evaluation of the revised 2022 Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) criteria with imaging-histopathology correlation is warranted.

articles.title: Good Enough to Sequence: Fluorometry-Guided Salvage of Low-Volume and Compromised Paediatric DNA in Custom Amplicon Next-Generation Sequencing.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Amplicon-based next-generation sequencing (NGS) is widely used in clinical practice, yet few studies address the impact of fluorometric quality control and of low-volume or compromised paediatric samples on library quantification and sequencing metrics. We reframe this question around a practical goal: whether sub-optimal paediatric DNA can be reliably salvaged for custom-panel amplicon NGS. Materials and Methods: Data from 314 paediatric samples sequenced on 16 custom-designed amplicon panels (Ion Torrent S5) were analysed retrospectively by Qubit input quantity (Group A ≥ 10 ng/µL; Group B < 10 ng/µL) and Nanoquant A260/280 quality (Group C 1.7-1.9; Group D < 1.7 or >1.9), and compared against post-library quantification, mean depth, and ten coverage QC parameters. Method agreement (Bland-Altman, proportional-bias regression), effect sizes (Cliff's δ), panel-adjusted mixed-effects models and ROC/logistic prediction of library failure were added. Results: Median input was 59.75 ng/µL by Nanoquant and 28.25 ng/µL by Qubit (p < 0.0001); median A260/280 was 1.86. Nanoquant overestimated DNA ~2.1-fold, but Bland-Altman analysis revealed wide, concentration-dependent limits of agreement (mean ratio 2.17×; 95% LoA 0.57-8.33×; proportional-bias p < 0.0001), indicating that no single correction factor is reliable. Group A comprised 91.7% (288/314) and Group B 8.3% (26/314); Group C 75.2% (236/314) and Group D 24.8% (78/314). Median post-library Qubit and mean depth were 1254 vs. 552 ng/mL (p < 0.0001) and 848× vs. 1352× (p = 0.025) for A vs. B, and 1254 vs. 1026 ng/mL (p = 0.049) and 745× vs. 1297× (p < 0.0001) for C vs. D. The higher depth in quantity Group B lost significance after adjusting for panel (mixed-model p = 0.083), identifying it as confounding. Input DNA predicted library failure (<300 ng/mL), with an ROC AUC of 0.79 and an exploratory empirical optimal threshold of ≈21 ng/µL (derived and tested in the same cohort; 14 failure events). None of the ten coverage QC parameters differed across groups. Discussion and Conclusions: Qubit quality control is strongly recommended because Nanoquant inflates readings ~2.1-fold, with no dependable correction factor. Low-volume or compromised paediatric DNA (<10 ng/µL and/or A260/280 outside 1.7-1.9) can be salvaged for amplicon NGS with defined protocol adaptations, with only ~19-23% of the worst-case samples failing library QC and comparable coverage in a small, concentration-matched representative subset (n = 5 per group) that was underpowered for formal equivalence testing. An empirical input threshold of ≈20 ng/µL, roughly double the manufacturer's minimum, best protects against library failure.

articles.title: Syphilis/HIV Early Rapid Response (SHIVER): Community-Driven Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) Across Diverse Sites in Saskatchewan, Canada.
articles.abstract: Background: Saskatchewan faces a growing public health challenge, with outbreaks of infectious syphilis and a continued increase in new HIV diagnoses. Rural, remote, and underserved populations experience disproportionate burdens due to barriers to timely testing, diagnosis, treatment, and linkage to care. The Syphilis/HIV Early Rapid Response (SHIVER) project implemented an innovative point-of-care testing (POCT) and treatment model to improve access to rapid diagnosis, immediate treatment, and care for individuals in inner-city, rural, remote, and underserved communities across Saskatchewan, Canada. Methods: Individuals aged ≥16 years were offered POCT for syphilis and/or HIV based on non-random criteria. Standard serology was collected according to provincial guidelines. Participants with a positive syphilis POCT result were offered immediate treatment, when appropriate, and follow-up testing. Those with a positive HIV POCT received counselling, confirmatory testing, and expedited linkage to care. Results: Between February 2023 and November 2024, 1797 participants were enrolled. Syphilis POCT was completed by 1781 participants, including 319 (17.9%) first-time testers. HIV POCT was completed by 1387 participants, including 141 (10.2%) first-time testers. The program achieved a diagnostic yield of 16.45% for syphilis and 3.39% for HIV. Integrating dual POCT in a single encounter increased testing opportunity, improved case detection, and minimized procedural burden for participants. Conclusions: This flexible POCT model successfully expanded access to testing, immediate treatment, and timely linkage to care for populations at the highest risk of syphilis and HIV. Its emphasis on community partnerships and culturally safe service delivery supports a scalable model that can improve access to infectious disease care in underserved communities. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05863117) Date of Registration: 19 April 2023.

articles.title: Application of High-Frequency Ultrasound (48 MHz) in Imaging and Evaluating the Effectiveness of Microneedling in Reducing Striae Distensae-A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Striae distensae (stretch marks) are atrophic skin lesions. Microneedling stimulates collagen remodeling, and high-frequency ultrasonography (HFUS) allows for the evaluation of these tissue changes. Objective: To assess the effectiveness of microneedling in reducing abdominal striae distensae using photographic and HFUS imaging. Methods: Ten women underwent three microneedling treatments at 6-8 week intervals. Skin structure was evaluated before and after the therapy using HFUS and photography. Results: Ultrasound imaging revealed pronounced structural tissue remodeling and a visible reduction in lesion visibility across the cohort. However, quantitative ultrasound shifts did not reach statistical significance in this pilot sample (n = 10), indicating that these findings represent observational trend data. In seven patients, a more homogeneous and ordered collagen structure was observed (increased medium echogenicity), while three showed the opposite trend. Visually, all subjects experienced shallower stretch marks, improved skin texture, evened color, and observational improvement. Conclusions: High-frequency ultrasonography suggests that microneedling is a safe and promising method for tissue remodeling and the clinical reduction of striae distensae.

articles.title: Mechanical Versus Kinematic Alignment in Total Knee Arthroplasty: Relationship Between Postoperative Alignment and Short-Term Functional Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mechanical alignment (MA) has traditionally been the reference alignment strategy in total knee arthroplasty (TKA), whereas kinematic alignment (KA) has emerged as an individualized alternative intended to approximate patient-specific knee anatomy. However, the relationship between postoperative mechanical-axis alignment and functional recovery remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to compare short-term functional outcomes and postoperative mechanical-axis alignment between MA and KA following primary TKA and to investigate the relationship between measured postoperative alignment parameters and functional outcomes. Methods: This single-center retrospective comparative cohort study included 120 patients who underwent primary unilateral TKA for end-stage knee osteoarthritis (KOA) between January 2022 and December 2024; 51 underwent MA and 69 underwent KA. Radiographic assessment included the hip-knee-ankle (HKA) angle, mechanical-axis deviation (MAD), residual varus deformity, and radiographic knee extension deficit. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC), and the Knee Society Score (KSS). Preoperative, postoperative, and change-from-baseline (Δ) functional scores were evaluated. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to assess associations between alignment strategy and postoperative functional outcomes after adjustment for baseline functional scores and relevant covariates. Associations between postoperative radiographic parameters and functional outcomes were additionally assessed. Results: Both alignment groups demonstrated substantial preoperative-to-postoperative functional improvement. MA achieved postoperative HKA alignment closer to the neutral mechanical axis than KA (179.63 ± 1.23° vs. 178.24 ± 2.32°; p < 0.001; FDR-adjusted p < 0.001). Absolute HKA deviation from neutral was lower with MA (0.97 ± 0.83° vs. 2.42 ± 1.62°; FDR-adjusted p < 0.001), as was postoperative absolute MAD (5.19 ± 4.53 mm vs. 7.86 ± 6.76 mm; p = 0.011; FDR-adjusted p = 0.018). KA was associated with a higher unadjusted postoperative KOOS score than MA (84.04 ± 12.33 vs. 77.12 ± 15.65; p = 0.010), whereas postoperative WOMAC (p = 0.206) and KSS (p = 0.843) did not differ significantly between groups. Between-group differences in change from baseline were not statistically significant for KOOS (p = 0.227), WOMAC (p = 0.130), or KSS (p = 0.427). After multivariable adjustment, no statistically significant between-group associations were observed for postoperative KOOS (adjusted β = 2.42; 95% CI, -0.93 to 5.77; p = 0.155), WOMAC (adjusted β = -2.80; 95% CI, -6.73 to 1.14; p = 0.162), or KSS (adjusted β = 1.09; 95% CI, -2.05 to 4.24; p = 0.492). Associations between the postoperative radiographic parameters and functional outcomes were negligible to weak, with none remaining statistically significant after FDR correction. Conclusions: Both MA and KA were associated with substantial short-term functional improvement, with no significant between-group differences in the magnitude of improvement from baseline. MA achieved postoperative alignment closer to the neutral mechanical axis, while the higher unadjusted postoperative KOOS score observed with KA was not statistically significant after adjustment for baseline characteristics and potential confounders. No significant postoperative differences in WOMAC or KSS were observed. The generally weak associations between measured postoperative mechanical-axis parameters and functional outcomes suggest that mechanical-axis alignment alone may not adequately explain short-term functional recovery. Because patient-specific coronal alignment parameters and achievement of the individualized KA target were not quantitatively assessed, the present findings cannot determine whether restoration of patient-specific anatomy was associated with functional outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical Presentation and Targeted Genetic Evaluation of Familial Isolated Pituitary Adenomas: A Single-Center Case Series.
articles.abstract: Background: Familial isolated pituitary adenomas (FIPA) are characterized by considerable clinical and genetic heterogeneity. Although germline pathogenic variants in AIP account for a subset of cases, most FIPA families remain genetically unexplained. We aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, tumor phenotype, treatment outcomes, and targeted genetic evaluation of FIPA families from a tertiary endocrine referral center. Methods: We retrospectively identified FIPA families among patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) evaluated at a tertiary endocrine referral center between 2019 and 2024. FIPA was defined as PitNETs occurring in at least two related individuals without clinical features suggestive of syndromic endocrine disease. Clinical, radiological, histopathological, and genetic data were analyzed. Results: Among 1068 patients with PitNETs, seven FIPA families were retrospectively identified (0.66% of the source cohort), comprising 20 affected individuals. Index cases included four women and three men, with a mean age at diagnosis of 37.1 ± 17.3 years. Somatotroph PitNETs predominated among index cases (5/7), whereas nonfunctioning PitNETs were more frequent among affected relatives (9/13). Six of seven index tumors were macroadenomas, and cavernous sinus invasion was present in two. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in AIP or MEN1 were identified by Sanger sequencing, and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) detected no copy number alterations involving AIP, MEN1, or CDKN1B. Conclusions: This series highlights the clinical heterogeneity of FIPA and the differing tumor spectrum between index cases and affected relatives. The absence of pathogenic variants identified by targeted genetic testing further illustrates the genetic heterogeneity of familial pituitary tumor predisposition.

articles.title: Preprocedural Serum Albumin and Early Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury After Elective Carotid Artery Stenting: Incremental Prognostic Information Beyond the PCI-Derived Mehran Score.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We assessed whether preprocedural serum albumin adds prognostic information to the PCI-derived Mehran score for early contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after elective carotid artery stenting (CAS). Methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort included 121 consecutive elective patients (January 2020-April 2026). The primary model combined the reconstructed Mehran score with albumin < 3.5 g/dL, a conventional threshold fixed in advance. Because the score uses actual contrast volume, the combined model applies only after CAS. The outcome used KDIGO serum creatinine thresholds (≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5 times baseline) from routine second-day testing. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results: Early CA-AKI occurred in 32 patients (26.4%). Adjusted odds ratios were 1.35 per Mehran point (95% CI 1.13-1.60) and 11.68 for albumin < 3.5 g/dL (95% CI 4.14-32.97). AUC increased from 0.768 to 0.865 (95% CI 0.794-0.937; likelihood ratio χ2 = 24.58, p < 0.001). Corrected AUC, calibration slope, and Brier score were 0.860, 0.96, and 0.132. In exploratory decision curves (20% threshold), corrected net benefit was 0.168 for the combined model and 0.133 for Mehran alone. Conclusions: Low preprocedural albumin added prognostic information to the PCI-derived score and may help select patients for closer renal surveillance after CAS. External validation and prospective impact studies are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Third-Trimester Cerebroplacental Ratio and Preceding Fetal Growth in Appropriate-for-Gestational-Age Fetuses: Limited Individual-Level Information in a Longitudinal Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) is mainly a contemporaneous hemodynamic and prognostic marker but has also been proposed as a marker of impaired growth velocity. We quantified how much third-trimester CPR constrains an individual fetus's preceding measured growth. Methods: In a retrospective single-center cohort, conditional estimated fetal weight growth (cEFW) was derived in 920 singleton pregnancies and analyzed in 760 fetuses appropriate for gestational age (AGA) at the third-trimester scan (median 32.9 weeks), with umbilical and middle cerebral artery Doppler measurements obtained during the same examination. Quantile regression estimated the conditional/unconditional 10th-90th percentile width of cEFW (width ratio) by within-cohort CPR z-score. Results: Each 1 SD increase in CPR corresponded to 0.100 SD higher cEFW (95% CI 0.040-0.160); the AUC for cEFW ≤ -1 SD was 0.553 (0.479-0.619). Point-estimate width ratios ranged from 0.968 to 1.194 between CPR z -2 and +1, with wide intervals at low CPR. The modeled probability of cEFW ≤ -1 SD was 14.4% (8.5-22.1) at z -2 and 10.5% (8.4-12.9) at z 0. Without AGA restriction (n = 878), the association was stronger (AUC 0.615), but point-estimate width ratios likewise showed no narrowing at low CPR. Conclusions: In AGA fetuses scanned mainly at 31-34 weeks, CPR provided limited individual-level information about preceding measured growth in terms of central 80% width, discrimination and lower-tail probabilities; at very low CPR, meaningful narrowing cannot be excluded. Prognostic value for perinatal outcome was not assessed.

articles.title: Explainable Classification Models for Identifying Elevated Gastrointestinal Symptom Burden in Honduran Communities: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gastrointestinal symptoms are a common reason for primary-care consultation, yet specialist assessment is often inaccessible in rural Central America. We evaluated whether explainable models using inexpensive demographic and lifestyle data can identify community residents aged 12 to 49 years with concurrently elevated gastrointestinal symptom burden. Methods: This was a cross-sectional survey of 1838 residents from 85 communities in five Honduran departments. Elevated symptom burden was defined as at least two of four indicators: recent abdominal pain, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux, and post-prandial bloating. Model A used eight demographic and lifestyle predictors; Model B added self-reported previous digestive diagnosis. Logistic regression was compared with six machine-learning classifiers under repeated nested five-fold and ten-fold cross-validation and community-grouped cross-validation. Discrimination, calibration, paired differences, community-level uncertainty, decision curves, SHAP explainability and subgroup performance were assessed. Results: Elevated symptom burden affected 840/1838 participants (45.7%, 95% CI 43.4 to 48.0). Model A showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.663, 95% CI 0.639 to 0.688), while Model B improved performance (AUROC 0.726, 95% CI 0.702 to 0.748) with good calibration (slope 0.955). No flexible learner outperformed logistic regression; the paired AUROC difference with gradient boosting was 0.001 (95% CI -0.008 to 0.010). Within strata of previous diagnosis, discrimination was only 0.621 to 0.643. Model B provided net benefit above screen-all and screen-none strategies at thresholds above approximately 0.25, but reaching 80% sensitivity required flagging 66% of participants. Conclusions: Low-cost information can identify concurrently elevated gastrointestinal symptom burden with moderate accuracy. A parsimonious, well-calibrated logistic regression model performed comparably to more complex methods and is a reasonable candidate for community-based identification of current burden, not for forecasting risk. Prospective external validation and age-specific thresholds are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Comparison of Perioperative Risk Assessment Tools for Major Postoperative Complications After Radical Cystectomy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To compare the discriminatory performance of commonly used perioperative risk assessment tools, including the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status Classification, Estimation of Physiologic Ability and Surgical Stress (E-PASS), Surgical Outcome Risk Tool (SORT), and modified 5-item Frailty Index (mFI-5), for major postoperative complications after radical cystectomy. Methods: This retrospective observational study included 193 patients who underwent open radical cystectomy for bladder cancer between January 2017 and January 2025. Major postoperative complications were defined as Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher. The discriminatory performance of ASA, E-PASS Comprehensive Risk Score (CRS), SORT, and mFI-5 was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Pairwise comparisons of the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) were performed using the DeLong test. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations with major complications, and exploratory analyses examined secondary postoperative outcomes. Results: Major postoperative complications occurred in 58 (30.1%) patients. The numerical AUC was highest for E-PASS CRS (0.618, 95% CI 0.536-0.701), followed by SORT (AUC 0.610, 95% CI 0.525-0.694), ASA (AUC 0.595, 95% CI 0.509-0.680) and mFI-5 (AUC 0.578, 95% CI 0.489-0.668). However, pairwise DeLong tests showed no statistically significant difference in discrimination between E-PASS CRS and SORT, or any of the other scores tested. In univariable analysis, high E-PASS CRS, high SORT score and mFI-5 ≥ 2 were significantly associated with major complications, while ASA classification was not. When all scores were entered into the multivariable model at the same time, none of the scores remained statistically significant. Conclusions: All of the risk assessment tools evaluated in this study demonstrated poor discriminatory ability for major postoperative complications following radical cystectomy. Although E-PASS CRS had the highest numeric AUC, its discrimination was not statistically better than the other scores analyzed. Existing risk tools may help with perioperative risk stratification but should not be used as stand-alone prediction models for major postoperative morbidity after radical cystectomy.

articles.title: Performance of Conventional Approaches Compared to Novel Blood Volume-, Angiogenesis-, and Tumor Hypoxia-Based Approaches to Diagnosing Tumor Recurrence on MRI After Radiation Therapy of Brain Metastases.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Differentiating tumor recurrence (TR) from radiation necrosis (RN) remains a significant challenge in the post-radiation management of brain metastases due to their overlapping clinical and radiographic features. Existing imaging techniques often lack the sensitivity and specificity necessary for accurate differentiation. This study evaluates the performance of a novel suite of imaging biomarkers characterizing microvasculature, blood flow dynamics, and tumor oxygen utilization in distinguishing TR from RN, compared with established cerebral blood volume (CBV) measures. Methods: This retrospective study included 119 symptomatic patients with metastatic brain lesions, 7-15 months post-radiotherapy. The training cohort (n = 96, 182 lesions) spanned June 2013 to May 2018, while a separate test cohort (n = 23, 23 lesions) was collected from January 2023 to December 2024. Lesions were classified as TR or RN based on expert consensus, pathology, and long-term follow-up. Eleven imaging biomarkers were assessed in the historical cohort and nine shared biomarkers were evaluated across cohorts, including both standard and novel biomarkers. Standard biomarkers included the Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC), corrected and non-corrected Cerebral Blood Volume (cCBV and ncCBV), and the Relative Amplitude of the Peak (rRHP). Novel biomarkers included Arterial Input Function Delay (Delay), Capillary Transit Time Heterogeneity (CTH and CTH Max), Oxygen Extraction Fraction (OEF), Relative Extravasation Correction (rLeakage), Relative Cerebral Metabolic Rate of Oxygen (rCMRO2), and Coefficient of Variance (COV). For each biomarker, a region of interest was selected from the lesion parenchyma, and a lesion-to-control parenchyma ratio was calculated. Biomarkers were evaluated for their ability to differentiate TR from RN, using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for univariate analyses and random forest modeling to identify optimal biomarker combinations. Bivariate analyses modeled lesion and control parenchyma as independent variables for each biomarker and compared AUCs for models in both cohorts. Results: In the training cohort, novel biomarkers, including Delay (AUC = 0.994), CTH (AUC = 1.000), CTH Max (AUC = 1.000), OEF (AUC = 0.991), rCMRO2 (AUC = 1.000), and Coefficient of Variance (AUC = 0.993), had higher observed AUC values than cCBV (AUC = 0.930) and ncCBV (AUC = 0.786). In the test cohort, the novel biomarkers did not demonstrate a consistent advantage over cCBV or ncCBV. The random forest model identified an optimal combination of five biomarkers (cCBV, ncCBV, Delay, OEF, and COV) with an AUC of 0.964. Among these, Delay had the highest feature importance, while ncCBV contributed the least. Conclusions: Novel imaging biomarkers demonstrated high discrimination in the training cohort, but this performance was not reproduced in the independent test cohort. The random forest analysis identified a combination of conventional and novel biomarkers with a reported AUC of 0.964. These findings support further investigation of their potential complementary diagnostic value but remain exploratory and require validation in larger prospective multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Prevalence and Morphometric Features of the Canalis Sinuosus and Its Accessory Canals in Turkish Adult Patients: A Single-Center Cross-Sectional CBCT Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The canalis sinuosus (CS) and its accessory canals (ACs) are neurovascular canals of the anterior maxilla at risk during surgery. We examined their prevalence, side distribution, diameter, localization, and course on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and explored associations with age and sex. Methods: Two observers independently read CBCT images of 603 adults from a single center. Canals were recorded only if they measured at least 0.5 mm, and ACs only if their continuity with the CS could be traced. Age, sex, and side were examined with generalized estimating equations and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Results: The CS was present in 53.2% of patients, bilaterally in 97.5% of them. ACs were seen in 59.5% of CS-positive patients (31.7% overall). Most ended in the lateral incisor region (26.5%) and ran straight vertically (63.4%). In exploratory analyses, age was associated with the presence of both canals (q = 0.040), whereas sex and side showed no significant association; the CS was wider in men (β = 0.227 mm; q < 0.001). Conclusions: At least one AC was present in 31.7% of patients, and 43.4% of ACs ended at lateral incisor or canine sites. When CBCT is available before anterior maxillary surgery, the planned site should be examined for these canals; demographic associations need confirmation.

articles.title: Anatomical Structures as Graph Nodes: Representation Before Architecture in Paediatric Brain Tumour Localisation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Paediatric brain tumour cohorts are small, and deep networks trained directly on volumetric MRI often perform poorly on them. The usual response is a larger architecture. The contribution of the anatomical representation itself has not been isolated as an experimental factor, so it is not known how much of the difficulty is architectural and how much is representational. This study addresses that gap, using supratentorial/infratentorial tumour localisation as a task defined entirely by anatomical geometry. Methods: In 108 paediatric patients with multi-sequence MRI and manual annotation of the tumour and eight anatomical structures, the task, the cohort and the subject-grouped five-fold cross-validation assignment were held fixed while the representation of the input was varied: 3D convolutional networks on raw volumes, the same networks given coordinate and craniocaudal-profile priors, a geometric rule with no fitted parameters, and a patient-level graph whose nodes are anatomical structures, read out by logistic regression or by a graph attention network. All anatomy downstream of the landmarks was predicted out of fold. Comparisons were patient-paired, with bootstrap intervals and Holm-corrected McNemar tests. Results: Balanced accuracy rose from 0.522 on raw voxels to 0.652 with explicit spatial priors, 0.681 for the parameter-free geometric rule, 0.775 for a five-feature linear readout of the graph and 0.838 for the graph attention network; the same decision layer given manual masks reached 0.918. Only the graph attention network exceeded the strongest convolutional baseline significantly (+0.187, Holm-adjusted p = 0.009). Automated segmentation was associated with a 0.143 gap, driven by spatial mislocalisation rather than by missed tumours. Conclusions: For this geometrically defined task and cohort size, representing anatomical structure explicitly was more effective than learning the same geometry from voxels.

articles.title: Plasma 8-Hydroxy-2'-Deoxyguanosine Levels in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a complex metabolic disorder characterized not only by impaired carbohydrate metabolism but also by alterations in lipid and protein metabolism. Hyperglycaemia in T2DM can promote the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), leading to oxidative stress. 8-Hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) is a biomarker of oxidative DNA damage commonly used to investigate oxidative stress. Methods: In this cross-sectional analytical observational study, patients diagnosed with T2DM and healthy controls were enrolled. Plasma 8-OHdG concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Associations between 8-OHdG concentrations and age, fasting blood glucose, and lipid profile parameters were evaluated. These associations were further explored in patient subgroups defined according to glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) levels. Results: Patients with T2DM had higher plasma 8-OHdG concentrations than healthy controls (Cohen's d = 1.092; 95% CI, 0.646-1.532; p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, the between-group difference was attenuated, with an adjusted mean difference of 28.84 ng/mL (95% CI, 0.278-57.41; p = 0.048). In the overall cohort, statistically significant correlations were identified between 8-OHdG levels and age (ρ = 0.379; 95% CI, 0.164-0.556; p < 0.001), fasting blood glucose (ρ = 0.266; 95% CI, 0.059-0.474; p = 0.011), and triglycerides (ρ = 0.376, 95% CI, 0.178-0.554; p < 0.001). Stratification of patients according to HbA1c levels revealed no statistically significant differences in 8-OHdG concentrations among the subgroups. Furthermore, none of the correlations examined within these subgroups remained statistically significant after adjustment for multiple testing. Conclusions: Plasma 8-OHdG concentrations were higher in patients with T2DM than in healthy controls, although the magnitude of the between-group difference was attenuated after adjustment for age. In the overall study population, 8-OHdG concentrations were associated with age, fasting blood glucose, and triglyceride concentrations. These findings suggest that 8-OHdG levels may be associated with demographic and metabolic factors. Given the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted as causal. Further prospective studies with larger cohorts are needed to evaluate the potential clinical relevance of plasma 8-OHdG measurement in T2DM.

articles.title: Development and evaluation of a microcapsule-based phantom simulating intra- and extracellular water diffusion.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop a microcapsule-based phantom that simulates intra- and extracellular diffusion and to evaluate its microstructural validity using time-dependent diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics and limited spectrally edited diffusion (IMPULSED) modeling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Microcapsules with undecane cores and melamine resin membranes were fabricated in three diameter ranges and dispersed at different concentrations within an octane gel to create phantoms with controlled microstructure. DWI was performed using pulsed gradient spin-echo and oscillating gradient spin-echo research sequences with effective diffusion times of 5.8, 10.2, and 51.1 ms. Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), relative ADC (rADC), and incremental area under the curve (iAUC) were calculated. Microstructural parameters, including diameter, intracellular volume fraction (fin), intracellular diffusivity (Din), extracellular diffusivity (Dex), and cellularity were estimated using the IMPULSED model. Group differences were assessed using one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test. Pearson's correlation analysis was conducted to evaluate correlations between theoretical and estimated microstructural parameters. Reproducibility was assessed with Bland-Altman analysis according to repeated imaging of independently fabricated phantoms. RESULTS: ADC significantly decreased with increasing diffusion time in all microcapsule phantoms (p < 0.001), whereas reference materials showed no time dependence. Higher microcapsule density resulted in lower ADC and higher rADC and iAUC. IMPULSED-derived diameters closely matched theoretical values (r = 0.992). Estimated fin and cellularity strongly correlated with theoretical values (r = 0.940 and 0.910). Reproducibility was good for ADC and IMPULSED-derived parameters. CONCLUSION: This microcapsule-based phantom reproduces diffusion time-dependent restriction and enables quantitative validation of time-dependent DWI and IMPULSED-derived microstructural metrics. KEY POINTS: Question Validation of time-dependent diffusion MRI and microstructural models requires phantoms that reproduce both intra- and extracellular water diffusion under controlled conditions. Findings The microcapsule-based phantom reproduced diffusion-time-dependent restriction, and MRI-estimated diameters strongly correlated with theoretical diameters across tested conditions, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.992. Relevance Statement The microcapsule-based phantom provides controlled intra- and extracellular diffusion environments for technical validation and standardization of quantitative MRI methods designed to characterize tissue microstructure.

articles.title: Deep learning denoising and deep learning-augmented contrast enhancement improve ultra-high-resolution photon-counting-detector CCTA image quality.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Ultrahigh-resolution (UHR) coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) using a photon-counting detector (PCD) provides excellent spatial resolution but is limited by increased image noise. We evaluated whether deep learning (DL)-based denoising and contrast enhancement can further improve UHR-CCTA image quality. MATERIALS AND METHODS: UHR-CCTA scans from 25 patients with coronary artery disease were retrospectively analyzed. Images were reconstructed at 0.2-mm slice thickness without and with quantum iterative reconstruction (QIR, Qoff-Q4), and subsequently processed using a DL tool for denoising and increasing iodine contrast enhancement. Subjective image quality (sharpness, noise, vessel wall delineation, and overall quality) was assessed by three radiologists using a 5-point Likert scale. Objective analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and coronary wall sharpness. Differences between image sets were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: DL-based CCTA demonstrated significantly superior subjective image quality across all parameters compared to standard reconstructions, with an overall median image quality ([interquartile interval, IQR]: 4 [3-5] versus 2 [2-3], p < 0.001). SNR and CNR were significantly higher for DL-based CCTA across all QIR levels (all p < 0.001). The highest values were observed for DL-based CCTAQ4 versus UHR-CCTAQ4 (SNR: 258.0 ± 147.5 versus 145.2 ± 50.1; CNR: 25.8 ± 17.1 versus 11.1 ± 4.5; both p < 0.001). Coronary wall sharpness was improved for DL-based CCTA for Q1-4 (all p < 0.027). CONCLUSION: DL-based denoising and iodine contrast enhancement effectively reduce noise and improve anatomic detail in UHR-CCTA, providing incremental value beyond vendor-specific reconstruction, particularly at high QIR strength levels. KEY POINTS: Question Deep learning reduces noise and enhances contrast in ultrahigh-resolution coronary CT angiography. Findings Image quality improves beyond standard iterative reconstruction methods, and vessel wall sharpness and diagnostic clarity significantly increase. Relevance statement This study aimed to determine at which levels of vendor-specific iterative reconstruction, DL-based denoising and contrast enhancement perform best in UHR CCTA, providing a foundation for future investigations on how these technical improvements may translate into diagnostic benefits.

articles.title: Image quality and artefact reduction for tantalum clips in ocular proton therapy using photon-counting CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Tantalum fiducials ("clips") used in intraocular proton therapy generate strong artefacts in conventional computed tomography, limiting the visibility of tumours and anatomical structures. This study investigated the potential of photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) for reducing tantalum-related artefacts. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two phantom models containing tantalum clips were examined using a photon-counting CT system and two conventional CT scanners with energy-integrating detectors (EICT). Reconstruction parameters, including tube voltage, image resolution, reconstruction kernel, virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI), and iterative metal artefact reduction (iMAR), were systematically optimised. Image quality was evaluated using objective metrics assessing homogeneity, noise, contrast, structural similarity, and artefact volume, complemented by a blinded subjective observer study. Correlations between objective and subjective results were analysed using Spearman's rank correlation. RESULTS: Objectively, PCCT showed no significant advantage over the modern EICT scanner but significantly outperformed the older-generation EICT therapy simulator. In contrast, blinded observers consistently preferred PCCT images. iMAR was the dominant factor influencing image quality. VMI alone did not yield relevant improvements. High-energy VMI (110 keV) combined with iMAR achieved the best subjective ratings. Higher spatial resolution due to smaller voxel sizes showed no clinically relevant benefit for artefact reduction. Soft reconstruction kernels provided the best balance between artefact suppression and image noise. Objective rankings correlated strongly with subjective assessments. CONCLUSION: PCCT combined with iMAR improves subjective image quality in intraocular proton therapy and reduces the perceived severity of tantalum artefacts. Nevertheless, tantalum remains a major challenge in image-guided proton therapy, requiring further optimisation of imaging and reconstruction strategies. KEY POINTS: Question Photon-counting CT may improve visualisation of tantalum clips and reduce metal artefacts in ocular proton therapy planning compared with conventional CT systems. Findings Photon-counting CT achieved the highest subjective image quality ratings, while iterative metal artefact reduction remained the dominant factor influencing artefact suppression. Relevance statement Photon-counting CT combined with iterative metal artefact reduction can improve visualisation of tantalum clips and surrounding anatomy in ocular proton therapy planning and may support more reliable tumour localisation despite limited objective differences compared with state-of-the-art conventional CT.

Rapid Infrarenal Aortic Rupture During Persistent Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Bacteraemia: Serial CT Evolution and Staged Endovascular Treatment-A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Persistent Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia can seed an atherosclerotic aorta. Early CT may show only wall thickening and periaortic inflammation, mimicking a degenerative penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) when no ulcer crater is visible. Case Presentation: An 80-year-old woman (BMI 19.5 kg/m2) presented with hypogastric and lumbar pain. Multiphasic CT showed a calcified infrarenal aorta with periaortic inflammation but no haemorrhage. Blood cultures obtained on two occasions confirmed persistent methicillin-susceptible S. aureus bacteraemia. Interval CT angiography showed an enhancing circumferential cuff and a small anterior contrast focus without a definite ulcer crater. Eight days after the initial CT, hypotension developed; CT angiography showed focal aortic wall disruption, active extravasation, and a large retroperitoneal haematoma. Emergency aorto-bi-iliac EVAR controlled the bleeding. An inferior mesenteric artery-fed type II endoleak filled the fresh rupture cavity and was treated by coil embolisation via mesenteric collaterals. One-month CTA showed a patent graft without endoleak. At six weeks, the patient remained clinically well with healed wounds and no need for further vascular intervention. CRP fell from 148.1 mg/L on postoperative day 5 to 49.4 mg/L at six weeks and 24.2 mg/L at approximately 12 weeks; the next outpatient review was scheduled in three months, although microbiological clearance remained undocumented. Conclusions: Serial imaging and persistent MSSA bacteraemia support probable infective aortitis with focal wall disruption; an infected degenerative PAU remains possible. Persistent bacteraemia, focal pain, and a progressive periaortic cuff should prompt early vascular review and short-interval imaging.

articles.title: Longitudinal Instrumental Assessment and Management of Dysphagia in a Child with Distal Trisomy 13q: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Children with rare neurogenetic disorders may present with complex feeding and swallowing impairments requiring repeated assessment and individualized management. In severe pediatric dysphagia, instrumental evaluation is particularly important for identifying aspiration, characterizing swallowing abnormalities, and informing decisions regarding oral feeding. Case Presentation: We report the longitudinal assessment and management of dysphagia in a 6-year-old girl with genetically confirmed distal trisomy 13q who presented with severe feeding difficulties and prolonged gastrostomy-tube dependence. Serial clinical evaluations and modified barium swallow studies (MBSS), performed between 18 months and six years of age, documented persistent oropharyngeal dysphagia involving both oral and pharyngeal phases. Earlier examinations demonstrated aspiration across tested consistencies, including silent aspiration. Management included structured swallowing therapy, controlled oral trials, texture modification, and continued enteral nutritional support, with feeding recommendations informed by clinical and instrumental reassessments. At 5 years and 10 months, aspiration persisted with thin liquids, although no aspiration was observed with thickened liquids or purees during the assessed trials. At six years of age, no aspiration was observed under the tested conditions, although deep laryngeal penetration and other pharyngeal swallowing abnormalities persisted. These findings supported cautious progression of oral intake while gastrostomy feeding remained necessary. Conclusions: This case highlights the value of longitudinal instrumental swallowing assessment in guiding individualized feeding decisions in children with complex neurodevelopmental disorders. Although swallowing findings changed over time, persistent airway protection abnormalities and differences in assessment conditions underscore the need for cautious interpretation and continued multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Metachronous Gastric Metastasis of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Mimicking Early Gastric Cancer and Detected on Esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Background: Although extrahepatic metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is common in the lungs and bones, metachronous gastric metastasis of HCC, which is initially detected in the form of multiple small gastric polyps, is extremely rare. Case presentation: A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with HCC by abdominal computed tomography (CT), but the patient received only intermittent treatment. After 15 months, esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed multiple 0.3-0.6 cm sessile polyps in the midbody and distal body of the stomach; these findings were not documented in the report of the previous examination. Microscopically, the stomach biopsy specimen revealed tumor cells with prominent nuclear atypia arranged in trabecular and solid patterns and infiltrating the gastric mucosa. However, no signs of glandular intraepithelial neoplasia were found in the gastric mucosa. Immunohistochemically, the tumor was positive for HepPar-1 and glypican-3 and negative for SALL4, cytokeratin-7, and cytokeratin-20, consistent with the immunophenotype of the primary HCC. Therefore, the gastric polyps were diagnosed as metachronous gastric metastasis of HCC. The patient was administered sorafenib, but follow-up CT showed radiological disease progression. He died 3 months after being diagnosed with metachronous gastric metastasis of HCC. Conclusions: Based on our experience, this rare case might help clinicians and pathologists avoid misdiagnosing gastric metastasis of HCC as primary gastric adenocarcinoma with hepatoid differentiation and prevent inappropriate treatment. In patients with HCC, biopsy of newly detected gastric polyps should be considered even when they appear benign on endoscopy, to exclude metastatic involvement.

articles.title: Bilateral Subareolar Epidermal Inclusion Cysts of the Breast After Prior Surgery for Mastitis: Differing Sonographic Appearances of Ruptured and Unruptured Cysts.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: An epidermal inclusion cyst (EIC) of the breast is an uncommon benign lesion, and bilateral subareolar involvement is exceptionally rare. Because a ruptured EIC can mimic malignancy or a primary infection, recognition of its imaging spectrum is clinically important. Case Presentation: A woman in her 40s presented with bilateral palpable subareolar masses and bloody, purulent nipple discharge, which had developed gradually over several months, ten years after bilateral surgery for mastitis. Mammography showed a right subareolar focal asymmetry with nipple-areolar thickening and a left circumscribed hyperdense mass. Sonography demonstrated a right mass with a preserved lamellated "onion-ring" pattern that proved unruptured at excision, and a left heterogeneously hypoechoic mass with small cystic changes that proved ruptured, with microabscess and hemorrhage; both masses were avascular on color Doppler, and the left mass showed focally high stiffness (peak 214.7 kPa) on shear-wave elastography. Surgical excision confirmed bilateral EIC. Conclusions: The coexistence of ruptured and unruptured cysts in one patient illustrates their differing sonographic appearances. Recognizing the onion-ring sign and integrating multiparametric ultrasound help distinguish benign EICs from malignancy or infection, while underscoring the need for histologic confirmation.

articles.title: Fulminant Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Myocarditis Presenting with Complete Atrioventricular Block After Combined Nivolumab and Ipilimumab Therapy: An Autopsy-Confirmed Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis is a rare but potentially fatal immune-related adverse event that may present with conduction abnormalities, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, and sudden cardiac death. The risk is increased with combined programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) blockade. We report a fatal case of fulminant ICI-associated myocarditis following combined nivolumab and ipilimumab therapy. Case Presentation: A 79-year-old man with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma developed progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea 14 days after his first and only cycle of nivolumab and ipilimumab. Electrocardiography revealed complete atrioventricular block. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin T increased from 2575 to 11,327 pg/mL, whereas creatine kinase initially decreased from 8690 U/L before rising again. Coronary angiography excluded obstructive coronary artery disease. Temporary transvenous pacing was followed by permanent pacemaker implantation. Despite intensive care, the patient developed progressive hemodynamic deterioration requiring vasopressor support and ultimately fatal cardiorespiratory collapse. ICI-associated myocarditis was not recognized during life; therefore, no myocarditis-directed diagnostic work-up or immunosuppressive treatment was initiated. Post-mortem examination demonstrated pronounced diffuse lymphohistiocytic myocarditis involving both atria and ventricles. ICI-associated myocarditis was identified as the cause of death, with a concomitant retroperitoneal abscess with pancreatic fistulation considered an aggravating condition. Conclusions: Complete atrioventricular block accompanied by a marked dynamic troponin increase should raise suspicion of ICI-associated myocarditis, particularly after exclusion of obstructive coronary artery disease. In this case, the diagnosis was established only post mortem. Earlier recognition of this clinical constellation may facilitate timely myocarditis-directed diagnostic evaluation and treatment.

Comment on Fındık et al. Comparative Evaluation of Clinical and Immunonutritional Risk Scores for Predicting Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury in Emergency Patients. Diagnostics 2025, 15, 2842.
articles.abstract: We read with interest the study by Fındık et al. comparing clinical and immunonutritional scores for predicting contrast-associated acute kidney injury in emergency department patients. The topic is clinically relevant, and comparative evaluation of practical risk tools may contribute to early identification of vulnerable patients. However, several methodological issues require clarification. Most importantly, the model presented as the Pre-CT AKI score differs substantially from the original score developed by Pattharanitima et al. in terms of its variables, thresholds, point assignments, total range, and risk classification. The definition of contrast-associated acute kidney injury also does not fully correspond to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria. In addition, the stated score range is inconsistent with the sum of the reported components, and discrepancies are present in the reported cohort sizes and receiver operating characteristic results. These issues may affect reproducibility and limit interpretation of the reported predictive performance as an external validation of the original Pre-CT AKI score.
